## MESTBYFILE.1 Windows ME refuses a standby or hibernation with a file open on a Stor98 drive: read, nothing to build (2026-11-15)

Branch `w50-mestby` from `3.5.1.0` at `a5c3d2950`; one commit, `5d4219c50` (Stor98 `docs/PLAN.md`,
phase 4, "Windows Me with a file open", and a pointer from phase 0.0's "not tested" line), reviewed, merged as
`1bc9076b4`. Nothing in a driver, INF or tool changes, so there was no gated build.

**Answer: inherent to ME, so recorded and nothing built; the reason is Windows ME's own rule rather than a
choice of ours.** ME refuses a
standby or a hibernation while any file is open on a disk behind a SCSI miniport. Stor98 is one such
miniport, and ME's own in-box AMD SCSI miniport is refused the same way. Nothing in Stor98 or xhcicm is
asked or answers: the refusal is made above the miniport, before any request reaches it. It does not depend
on the tunnel. It was not a recorded design choice: Stor98's PLAN listed ME standby and hibernation as not
tested. As soon as the file is closed, the same session sleeps and resumes, and the drive works afterwards.
Which component of Windows makes the refusal was not identified (no closed code was read).

**The message** (title "Power Management", buttons Close and Help): "Your computer cannot hibernate or
standby because the Stor98 Storage Controller for NVMe SSDs cannot enter into a low-power state." It is the
same for a standby and a hibernation. The device name is the adapter's Device Manager description, which is
the `DeviceDesc` of Stor98's 9x INF. With the AMD adapter the same box says "the AMD PCI SCSI Controller".
The text is not in this tree. It is shown by Windows' power management after `SetSuspendState`, which still
returns 1. Help opened an empty Help and Support page.

**Vehicles.** QEMU `asm4242-20261110-docks`, every guest with one vCPU on TCG. ME runs on the `pc` machine.
The bases are copies of task 50.6's, rebased into `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\mestby\bme` and `b98` and kept read-only:
- `medock-50`: ME, a PCI Express tunnel port and the dock (a USB4 device router with a PCIe switch and its
  own NVMe). The package is 50.6's build `01e98447d`, release flavour.
- `mei-50`: ME, the SHPC tunnel bridge and the ASM2464 enclosure.
- `medock`: the same dock with `3.4.3.0`.
- `q98dock-50`: 98 SE on q35 with the dock.

Every leg started on a fresh overlay. "R" means the release `xhcicm.sys` as installed (`acf8fb60...`). "Q"
means the qemu flavour copied over (`cc9143b5...`, checked with `fc /b`). The leg helper is `C98.EXE`, built
from `E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\mestby\m98\m98.c` (50.6's helper plus these commands):
- `keepv`: a writer that appends a 4 KiB block every 5 s through a held write-through handle, then
  compares every block after it closes.
- `holdr`: holds `TESTDATA.BIN` open for reading only, with nothing written.
- `seteject`: writes `XhciCmSafeEject`.
- `devstat`: lists every devnode's status through CFGMGR32.

In each leg the file is opened before the sleep is asked. A standby that happens is woken after 20 s. A
hibernation ends with QEMU exiting, and a cold start of the same disk resumes the image.

| Leg | ME vehicle, flavour | What | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| x1 | dock, R | file open for writing (16 bytes written, handle held) | standby **refused** (the message, `x1-refused1.png`); hibernation **refused**, same message; the drive written and compared afterwards |
| x3 | dock, R | nothing open (files on the volume, an Explorer window on E:\) | standby **passes**, woken; hibernation **passes** (image written in 18 s), resumed; files compared after each |
| x2, x6 | dock, R / Q | file open, `XhciCmSafeEject` 0 (Q log `cm.safe.eject=0`, no `cm.reenum.9x.removable`: xhcicm marked nothing) | standby and hibernation **refused** |
| x7, x8 | dock, R | file open, QEMU's ACPI root-bus hot-plug off, with and without `XhciCmSafeEject` 0 | **refused** |
| x4 | dock, R (the Q copy did not take) | file open | **refused** |
| x5 | plain NVMe hot-added at 00:03.0 (no tunnel; Stor98 by ME's wizard) | file open | standby and hibernation **refused**, the same message |
| x12 / x13 | dock, Q + Stor98 debug-port test image | file open / nothing open | x12 refused, x13 passes. In neither does Stor98 log any SRB or `HwAdapterState` between the last idle write and the attempt (no SHUTDOWN, FLUSH or adapter-state call). xhcicm logs its own suspend, then `u4.sleep.cancel` in the refused case: ME had begun and backed out |
| x15 | dock, R + Stor98 test image with `CachesData` FALSE (`fc` checked) | file open | **refused**: `CachesData` is not the trigger |
| x16 | dock, R | file written and closed, then held open for reading only | standby and hibernation **refused** |
| x20 | dock, R | one session: `TESTDATA.BIN` held read-only (nothing written), standby asked, then the file closed, standby asked again, then a hibernation | held: **refused**; closed: standby **passes**, woken, files compared; hibernation **passes**, resumed, files compared |
| x18 | dock, `3.4.3.0` base, R | file open | **refused** (as 50.6's m3b) |
| x19 | SHPC bridge + ASM2464 enclosure, R | file open | **refused** |
| x22 | dock, R | an MS-DOS Prompt with E: as its current drive, no file open | standby **passes**; files compared after the wake |
| x14 | USB stick (QEMU `usb-storage` on the xHCI, xhci98 + ME's own USB storage), plugged after the start | file open | standby **passes**; the held file's bytes compared OK after the wake, a new file written and compared |
| x23 | a second IDE disk (ME's IDE driver) | file open | standby **passes**; held file OK, new file compared |
| x26 | AMD Am53C974 (QEMU `am53c974`) hot-added at 00:03.0, ME's in-box "AMD PCI SCSI Controller", its disk E: | file open | standby and hibernation **refused**: "... because the AMD PCI SCSI Controller cannot enter into a low-power state." |
| x28 | the same AMD adapter | nothing open | standby **passes**, files compared after the wake |

98 SE (`q98dock-50`, R, leg x17, `keepv` writer): the standby is **not refused**. After the wake each write
through the held handle fails (error 31), and the drive is gone. The 50.6 legs k1, k2, k3b and k1L read the
same. This is record 21 section 6.1.5 item 9, "as read". 98 SE offers no hibernation on these vehicles
(run-49.md, "49.12 (continued)").

**What rules out the other causes.**
- `DN_REMOVABLE` (0x4000): `devstat` shows it on nearly every devnode of these ME guests, the IDE
  controller and the NHI included. The Stor98 devnode reads `0x19886ACE` in every configuration, and
  xhcicm's mark being off changed nothing.
- The tunnel: the plain root-bus NVMe is refused too.
- What Stor98 declares: no call reaches the miniport at the attempt, `CachesData` makes no difference, and
  ME's own SCSI miniport is refused the same way.
- Dirty data or the access mode: a read-only handle with nothing written is enough.

The one thing that decides is a handle held open on a disk behind a SCSI miniport.

**Could Stor98 avoid it?** Not from the miniport. The 9x miniport interface has no power entry point: the
Windows 98 DDK's `HW_INITIALIZATION_DATA` has `HwAdapterState` only. ME's in-box miniport is refused alike.
The ways left are a helper VxD that answers or overrides Windows' power query for the devnode (PLAN 0.12
chose no helper VxD), or another driver model. Neither is a small change, and overriding the refusal would
also take away what it gives on ME: on 98 SE, which does not refuse, the held-file drive is lost at the
wake.

**Not read.**
- Which Windows component makes the refusal.
- Real hardware (the bench).
- 98 SE hibernation.
- A Q-flavour log for x4 (its copy did not take; it is a release reading).
- Inbox comparators that did not run: the 53C810 (ME's "Symbios 8100S") installs and stays at problem 10;
  the 53C895A has no ME driver; the Am53C974 and DC-390 hang ME at the logo when present at power-on, which
  is why the AMD adapter was hot-added.

Voids:
- x2's tail (the leg script was edited while it ran; its two readings came before that).
- x9, x10, x11, x21, x24, x25, x27 (the comparators above).
- x14's first start (a USB disk present at power-on hung at "Booting from Hard Disk").

Evidence: `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\mestby\x<n>\` (`leg-*.txt`, `serial-*.log`, `debugcon-*.log`, `*-refused*.png`,
`pids.txt`), every QEMU start and stop in `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\mestby\pids.txt`. Leg scripts are in
`E:\xhci98-vm\p50\mestby\tools\` (`lmx*.sh`, `lpair.sh`, `lgen*.sh`, `ldk.sh`). The helper and the test
images' builds are in `E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\mestby\` (`m98\`, `sdbg.log`; the debug-port image
`4ef26369...`, the `CachesData` FALSE image `bced900b...`, not tracked; the source edit reverted at once).

## 50.20 A UAS drive cycled at each start of Speccy, HWiNFO and HWMonitor on an Intel 7 Series controller: the readings so far (2026-11-15)

Reading of field reports from one computer, then emulator legs. The fix's design was reviewed and revised
several times and is not yet settled; nothing is built. The computer: XP x64, an Intel 7 Series xHCI
(`8086:1E31`), a SanDisk UAS drive (`0781:55A9`, four streams on its status, data-in and data-out endpoints), `3.5.0.0`.

The reports, all from one computer:
- Nine quick saves from two boots (line interrupt, then `XhciInterruptMode` 4), taken after Speccy 1.32, HWiNFO and
  HWMonitor were run.
- Four earlier quick saves from the HWMonitor sessions ("A monitoring program on XP x64 ..." above).
- The user saw:
  - the drive disconnect and reconnect at each program start;
  - a "Delayed Write Failed" balloon for a browser profile file on the drive;
  - an Application Error "...could not be read ... 0xc0000098" (STATUS_FILE_INVALID, an in-page error from a file on
    the removed volume).

### What each start does (the stream trace captures, record 17 4.12.9)

Speccy's start, capture 2 (`034046`) and capture 3 (`034530`):

1. Two pass-through commands with data-in, on streams 1 and 2, are each answered CHECK CONDITION with 18 bytes of
   sense: a 34-byte SENSE IU, status event `0D0000FE` against `0D000110` for GOOD.
2. Each refusal's data-in TD is cancelled.
3. **The first cancel.** Its Stop Endpoint's Stopped event (`1B`, Stopped - Length Invalid) names a TRB on stream 4's
   ring. The cancel's Set TR Dequeue sets stream 1 (`5473` / `5563`); c1 reads it back equal; c2 places streams 2-4,
   with stream 4 at its own position.
4. **The second cancel.** Its Stopped event names a TRB at the position just set for stream 1. The Set TR Dequeue sets
   stream 2; c1 is equal. c2 then reads **stream 4's context holding stream 1's position** (`5473` / `5563`), off
   stream 4's ring: `HCD_DEQ_V_UNPLACED`. The device is given up and cycled: `cfg.deq.giveup=..25`, the cancelled
   pipe's stream 2.
5. The counters per start: `StreamDeqChecked` 8 (2 cancels x 4 reads), `Unplaced` 1, `GiveUps` 1. There is no
   `StreamDeqMismatch` and no `StreamDeqResent`: c1 read back equal both times, and c2 never resends by design.
6. **After the cycle.** `pdo.ioctl=00220007` (IOCTL_INTERNAL_USB_RESET_PORT) and `00223E67`
   (IOCTL_XHCI98_CLOSE_STREAMS), refused `C000000E`, are xhciuas's teardown calls reaching the departed PDO: harmless.
   The eight `xfer.unmatched=00020300` are the Realtek RTL8157 network adapter's bulk-in (slot 2), unrelated.

**Speccy's commands, read in the emulator (legs SA, SB below):** vendor CDBs DFh and 24h (512 bytes in) at every start,
plus 85h at the first. Only ATA PASS-THROUGH (A1h, 85h) is answered by the driver after its first refusal, so DFh and 24h
reach the drive at every start: two refusals, two cancels.

**HWiNFO (`034959`, capture 4).**
1. The drive answered nothing for about 13 s: a READ on stream 4, then three status-only commands.
2. The recovery cancelled DCI 5 stream 4, then status (DCI 9) stream 1. That Stopped event named stream 3; Set TR
   Dequeue stream 1 = `34C2`.
3. Then status stream 2 was cancelled. c1 read the endpoint Running (`readback=..23`), stopped it again, and c2 found
   **stream 3 holding `34C2`**, stream 1's position, while stream 3 still held a status TD. The give-up was
   `00050925`: DCI 9, the status endpoint. That is the difference from Speccy's `0515` / `0525` (DCI 5, data-in).

**HWMonitor after HWiNFO (`035038`, capture 5): the single-cancel form.**
1. At +765 ms the A1h on stream 3 is refused. The Stopped event names stream 4 (`6390`); Set TR Dequeue stream 3 =
   `5F33`; c1 and c2 find nothing.
2. At +828 ms stream 3's next READ completes at TRB `5F40`.
3. At +843 ms stream 4's READ of 8192 bytes is rung, and the event that comes is **a second Success naming `5F40`**, a
   TRB of stream 3's completed TD.
4. Stream 4's own TD at `6390` never completes. At 59 s: "timed out ... the drive answered but its data never arrived",
   then a device reset.

The same shape in the first boot's HWMonitor time-out session (`010559`): TRB `5710` on stream 1 completes at +46 ms and
again at +62 ms, after stream 2's doorbell (`xfer.unmatched=00010501`, TRB `5710`); then stream 2's READ times out. The
capture lacks the initiating cancel.

**The Babble session (`023320`).** Cancel stream 1, the Stopped event names stream 2, Set TR Dequeue stream 1 = `5472`.
At stream 2's next doorbell, Babble Detected names TRB `5470`, stream 1's set position.

**The MSI boot** (`040507`, `040540`, `040558`):
- one give-up and cycle per Speccy start;
- HWMonitor's refusal followed by two time-outs and three give-ups on the status endpoint in one recovery;
- the interrupt mode makes no difference.

### Reading

In every capture, the position the cancel's Set TR Dequeue writes for stream X later appears as another stream's:
- **the replay:** a second completion of X's last TD after another stream's doorbell, while that stream's own TD never
  runs, so its command times out;
- **Babble** at X's position;
- **the position read in another stream's context** at the next cancel, so the device is given up and cycled.

The working reading is that this controller holds a cached state for the stream it last ran, and a Set TR Dequeue for a
different stream also loads its pointer there. xHCI 4.6.10 updates only the named stream's context. The driver side was
checked (context indexing, the command's Stream ID and SCT, the tag-to-stream mapping) and explains none of the foreign
values.

The trace's stream column comes from which ring holds the address. A duplicated event is consistent with a second DMA
into a completed request's buffer (the client's own memory, `XhciDmaStaging` 0 in these reports), but does not prove it.

- **3.5.0.0's give-up.** It follows record 17 4.12.8's own rule (an unplaced position gives the device up). Its cost is a
  PnP removal, and so the lost files.
- **The single-cancel form** is not caught by 4.12.8: it shows as a time-out and a device reset.
- **Phase 49's QC4-QC9** never reached c2's give-up: QEMU's resync (4.12.4) sets every stream at every stop.

### Legs (emulator; XP x64; the published `3.5.0.0`; usb-uas `x-ata-passthrough-refuse`)

| Leg | Emulator | Program | What it shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| SA | 49.39 build (`cf4e9880...`) | Speccy 1.32 from L:, 3 starts, a copy-compare loop and an open file on L: | Speccy sends DFh, 24h (512 bytes in) and 85h at its first start; DFh and 24h again at each later start (not answered by the driver); 85h answered by the driver after its first refusal. `StreamDeqChecked` 48, no give-up, no cycle (QEMU's controller has no such fault); 16/16 copies PASS, the open file kept, Speccy open at every start |
| SB | the same, plus the stale-stream fault | Speccy from C: | the same commands; the stale-stream fault's time-outs (2) and device resets (2), no cycle; 16/16 copies PASS, the open file kept |

**The model.** usb4-emu `qemu-xhci x-stream-setdeq-current`, an uncommitted test build on a usb4-emu worktree
(branch `w50-hwm`, from `w49-smart`). A Set TR Dequeue for a stream other than the endpoint's current one loads its pointer into the current
stream's cached state. Three builds:

| Build | `qemu-system-x86_64.exe` | The current stream | With it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `emu50` | `0bcf3284...` | set when a TD is fetched | nothing happens: a refused command's own stream is current |
| `emu50b` | `6b150797...` | set at a successful completion | masked by the driver's QEMU resync (4.12.4), which re-reads every context at each stop |
| `emu50c` | `2a3a3dfd...` | as `emu50b`, plus `x-stream-setdeq-keep`: the cache outlives a stop unwritten | the BEFORE legs below |

**The BEFORE legs** (`emu50c`, the published `3.5.0.0`, refusal on, a copy-compare loop, a file held open on L: and a
reader of 32 reference files):

| Leg | Program | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| BA | HWMonitor 1.62 from L:, 5 starts | **The time-out and replay forms.** At start 1 HWMonitor hung and could not be ended (`taskkill /f` left it) with L: at 100 % activity. Timeouts and aborts climbed to 9 and 9 by start 2. Events inside no queued TD on DCI 5, streams 1, 10, 12 and 13 (the replay signature). The guest then ended without a shutdown at 18:51 (the cause was not read). On the next boot of the same leg: timeouts 40, aborts 40, the copy loop stalled after its sixth round, and the final read of the loop's file failed (fc errorlevel 2). No cycle (QEMU's resync keeps c2 quiet), and the reference files never differed |
| BB | Speccy 1.32 from L:, 3 starts | the same family. Speccy could not be ended at its first start; timeouts 7, aborts 6, one device reset; events inside no queued TD on DCI 5 and DCI 7; no cycle; the open file was kept and the copy file compared equal |

The model reproduces the time-out and replay forms and the hung program on `3.5.0.0`. It does not reproduce the
give-up and cycle: by design, the write-back is hidden from the driver's QEMU resync, and on QEMU only that resync
would see it.

### The state on 2026-11-16 (kept from the roadmap row)

Moved here when Phase 50's rows were shortened (2026-11-16). The fault was reported from one computer in fourteen
reports, and the same fault has been seen in the field under Windows 7 x64 as well as XP x64. The design as the
row stated it on 2026-11-15 (record 17 section 4.12.10, on branch `w50-uasfix`): on that controller, for a UAS
driver that declares it recovers, no stream position command is sent, a withheld endpoint is held until it is
rebuilt, and xhciuas recovers the drive by rebuilding the endpoints or by a reset that Windows does not see as a
removal; a UAS driver that does not declare it - Microsoft's on Windows 8 and later, an older xhciuas - keeps
`3.5.0.0`'s behaviour on that controller (owner, 2026-11-15); the field captures are host test vectors. Built on
that branch (`9ea4a3c38`, `573cfeb40`, `bfcb0a747`), not merged, its guest legs running. A setting with the values
0, 1 and 2, in the family of the quirk values, is to be added (owner, 2026-11-16): 0 off, 1 the listed controllers
(today `8086:1E31` alone), the default, 2 every controller. Confirmed only when the reporter runs a build.

## MEBOOTDROP.1 (Phase 50's 50.22) 98 SE and ME: a child stopped when a containment drops it during the start (2026-11-15)

Development host A, branch `w50-meboot` from `3.5.1.0` at `a5c3d2950`. The design is record 17 section 4.13.10 (new),
reviewed and revised before any code; the code reviewed again before its commit `be9121788`; the reading below is
in the record at `6a0281001`, reviewed the same way. Merged as `2876eeb17` (`be9121788`, `6a0281001`). The
planned entry MEBOOTDROP.1 became Phase 50's task 50.22.

**What the hang is.** Read again from Phase 49's traces (`E:\xhci98-scratch\w49\legsa\ME-H1-boothang.log`, the
control `E:\xhci98-vm\p49\legsa\a2m\debugcon-T.log`): the tablet's PDO START, its class driver's first request (a
GET_DESCRIPTOR) held and then failed DEV_NOT_RESPONDING at the containment, STOP, the relations without the PDO, and no
REMOVE. The STOP is the one ME sends after a failed START (task 43.49), not a start-up rebalance as 49.16 placed it, and
the REMOVE that never reached this driver is the one ME's `hidusb.sys` holds after a failed START and a STOP (43.49's
reading). In the uncontained control the same STOP came and the child stayed listed, and ME finished starting.

**The change.** On 98 SE and ME alone, a PDO a containment's drop takes off the bus is marked; every relations answer
carries it, with its gone hub or composite parents, while PnP holds it stopped, so ME is not asked to remove it. Its
next START ends the carry, is answered by the departed-PDO rule of record 13 section 10.5.2 (the ghost, success from
the copies, so `hidusb.sys` reaches its started state first; a hub or composite parent refused), and asks for the
relations again; its REMOVE ends it too. The roadmap entry said "refuse its next start": a refusal would leave
`hidusb.sys` in the failed state again, so the ghost rule answers it instead. The serial-id check counts a carried PDO.
Nothing is marked on Windows 2000 and later, so no relations answer, START or REMOVE changes there.

**Builds.** Gated `all` x86 of the base `a5c3d2950` for the before legs (`E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\meboot\gated-base-x86.log`,
"BUILD + GATES PASSED (release qemu)"; a first run of it was void, a source edit having landed in the tree while it
compiled, and was run again on a clean tree). Gated `all` x86 of the change (`gated-new-x86.log`, passed; host tests
passed, `test_enum` 750 checks) and gated `release` amd64 (`gated-new-amd64.log`, "BUILD + GATES PASSED (release)").
Binaries, before: qemu flavour `5456968b...`, release `ad234ed0...`; after: qemu flavour `ca838923...`, release
`aefa6049...` (x86 `xhci98.sys`).

**Method.** QEMU under TCG, one vCPU, the q35 ME and 98 SE bases, the release package installed by its INSTALL.BAT,
the qemu flavour copied over `xhci98.sys`, `XhciDmaStaging` 1 machine-wide and `XhciQemuStageFault` 0x0001000C (the
hold with the containment armed, at the first transfer) or 8 (the log alone). Each start is a fresh overlay of one
prepared image (ME before: `mb`; ME after: `mn`, armed `mnh`; 98 SE after: `sn`, armed `snh`), so every run is a cold
start of the same disk. Up to three guests at once; the host was shared with other guests, nothing here
timing-bound. Logs and shots under `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\meboot\<leg>\`.

| Leg | System, build | At power-on | What the device PDO saw | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mr1, mr2, mr4, mr5 | ME, before | tablet | START, the request failed at the containment, STOP, relations, no REMOVE | **stopped at the start 4 of 4** (SeaBIOS "Booting from Hard Disk..." or the ME logo at 7 min) |
| mr3 | ME, before | Bulk-Only stick | START, the failed request, STOP, then REMOVE | desktop (a new-hardware restart prompt): the omission alone does not hang ME |
| n1m, n4m, n5m, n6m, n7m | ME, after | tablet | START, the failed request, STOP, `pdo.carry` serial 1, then only capabilities and ids at each relations query | **desktop 5 of 5**; Device Manager: "USB Human Interface Device", Code 10 |
| n3m | ME, after | `usb-hub`, tablet at its port 1 | the tablet's STOP; `pdo.carry` for the hub PDO (root hub's answer) and the tablet (the hub FDO's answer) | desktop (restart prompt for the new hub) |
| n2m | ME, after | stick | START, the failed request, STOP, carried | desktop; the stick stays listed with its failed start (before: removed) |
| s1s | 98 SE, after | tablet | START, the failed request, relations, REMOVE; no STOP, no carry | desktop, as 49.16 read 98 SE |
| s3s | 98 SE, after | hub and tablet | the new hub's install wizard held the tablet's START past the leg | not read |

**The carried PDO afterwards (ME, after).** n6m: Device Manager's Refresh brought the relations (still carried), the
capabilities and the ids, and no START. n7m: the tablet's Properties read Code 10 ("This device is either not present,
not working properly, or does not have all the drivers installed."); the controller disabled (QUERY_STOP and STOP of
the controller and the root hub; nothing to the stopped tablet) and enabled (the controller started again, the
ledger at the start showing 278000h kept from the containment, the tablet carried again, no START to it, not enumerated
again: its port waits on the carried PDO), then Shut Down finished. So the ghost START and the removal after it, and a
REMOVE of the carried devnode, are not read: ME sent neither.

**Controls (after).**

| Leg | System | Order | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| c1m, c1s | ME, 98 SE | tablet at power-on, the log alone (no hold) | desktop, no carry |
| c2m | ME | stick hot-plugged at the desktop, then `device_del` | started; relations, REMOVE; Shut Down finished |
| c2s | 98 SE | tablet hot-plugged, then `device_del` | started; relations, REMOVE; Shut Down finished |
| c4m | ME | Device Manager, the tablet removed, then Refresh | QUERY_REMOVE, two reads cancelled, an ABORT_PIPE completed, REMOVE; Refresh: START, the requests of a start, reads; Shut Down finished |
| c4s | 98 SE | the same | the same order; found again through its wizard and started |
| c5m | ME | the hold armed, no device at power-on, the stick plugged at the desktop | START, the failed request, STOP, carried; Shut Down finished (49.16 read STOP, relations, REMOVE here) |
| c5s | 98 SE | the same with the tablet | relations, REMOVE, no STOP, no carry; Shut Down finished |
| c3q | ME | standby and wake with the tablet | suspended (QEMU "suspended"), woke, the resume kept the tablet (`resume keep, restored`), its reads completed after the wake |
| c3r | 98 SE | the same | the same; Shut Down after the wake did not finish in 4 minutes (below) |

The standby legs ran on images made for 50.6's legs (`bme\mei-51.qcow2`, ME on an i440FX machine, and
`b98\q98dock-51.qcow2`, 98 SE on q35 with the disk on PIIX; read-only backings of overlays here), with that branch's
package and this build's qemu flavour copied over `xhci98.sys`. On those images the installed driver suspended and woke
too before the copy. The images made for these legs refused the standby before any power request reached the driver
(c3m and c3s; ME's `mb` image under the before build too, c3b; ME's `mn` image on an i440FX machine, c3p): the
helper's call returned at once. 98 SE's Shut Down after the wake on `q98dock-51` did not finish: the q35 base notes
(`E:\xhci98-vm\q35-bases\STATE.md`) record that 98 SE's Shut Down hangs once `xhcicm` is installed, which that image
has; not attributed to this change, and not read on the before build.

**NT.** Not run. Every new branch reads the mark, which is set only where `IoIsWdmVersionAvailable(1, 0x10)` is false;
a controller that never marked a PDO answers no carry at its first test (`CarryArmed`), the START asks for relations only
when it cleared a mark, and the REMOVE writes 0 over 0.

**Rates.** Before: ME with the tablet stopped at the start 4 of 4. After: ME with the tablet reached the desktop 5 of 5
(and 1 of 1 behind a hub).

**Not read.** The carried PDO's next START (the ghost, its STOP and REMOVE, the deletion), and a REMOVE of a carried
devnode (the controller disabled with the device carried sent it none); 98 SE behind a hub; a composite device; NT;
real hardware.

## TBSTBYWB9X.1 (Phase 50's 50.24) 98 SE standby: a dock's or switched enclosure's own switch put back (2026-11-15)

The owner's word of 2026-11-15: build the former 50.12's reviewed design (record 21 section 6.1.6, `49348eeee`) as a
self-contained unit; whether it goes into `3.5.1.0` is decided afterwards. Branch `w50-s9x` after merging `3.5.1.0`
(`58c64886f`, no conflicts; `gen-cm-snap.py` no change). Merged as `653d752fd` (the branch's tip `d1a973711`; every
commit named below is in its history). The planned entry TBSTBYWB9X.1 became Phase 50's task 50.24.

**Standing: every reading below is the emulator's.** No real computer was available for a standby - no bench
machine of this project can enter Stand by - so nothing here has been read on a real dock, enclosure or host
router. The owner decided on 2026-11-15, on these readings alone, to take TBSTBYWB9X.1 into `3.5.1.0`; a bench
reading is owed whenever a machine that can enter Stand by is available.

**The design re-read against the merged code.** No behaviour change needed. 50.10's hunks in `cm_reenum.c`,
`cm_power.c` and `cm_nhi.c` are the NT filter route's; the one shared point is `CmReenumResumed`, where the
resume's identity mask is handed to the worker. One refinement of item 5 b's wording: the eject paths' binding is an
activity sequence inside `cm_ejectos.c` (every devnode-changing call advances it at its start and end and waits
while a write-back pass is under way), in place of a count advanced by each eject path through the worker.

**What this says.**
- On 98 SE a dock or switched enclosure whose router is the one recorded at the suspend is written back whole - the
  generic dock, the switched enclosure and both real-dock models (up to 10 nodes) - with nothing removed: no query,
  no removal, and none of 49.31's fatal 0E screens, which appear only on the removal path (c1, f8c). A held file no
  longer costs the drive: the drive stays under its letter (t3, t4, o2, f3), where section 6.1.5 alone left a refused
  removal and no drive until a restart (50.6's k-legs); the held file's own data written before the sleep is lost on
  98 SE across a standby whatever the unit (i2: no switch, nothing of this change's), so this is no guarantee for
  open files.
- A unit gone or swapped while asleep is never written (`go` 0x11 from the core's identity comparison) and is
  handled as before (t6, t7).
- The doubt path: the obligation is taken and its removal made by section 6.1.5's recovery; on a refusal the slow
  retry is armed by the obligation (t9, f9). After an accepted removal the undo is what lets the drive come back:
  read on the enclosure (f8c, f8e) and on the dock (f8d, f8f).
- ME (out of scope: no table) and the chain (no table) are as before (m1, m2u, c1, c2); ME hibernation PASS with this
  package (h1u, h2u).

**Not read.**
- The bench: every leg is the emulator's. Real docks and enclosures behind a real host router on 98 SE (the TS3 Plus
  and HP G2 are the emulator's models, without drives), a dock's own xHCI or network function in use across the
  standby, and 98 SE hibernation (no S4 offered to 98 SE on these vehicles; owed to a machine whose firmware does).
- Who numbers the dock's chain-port bridge (f8b): no configuration-space trace in the emulator. In some resumes the
  pass read it already as its copy (f1c; s1 had one such node too), in others at reset (t1): something on Windows' side
  restores that bridge at the resume, racing the pass; with the forced doubt it wrote through the routing the pass
  had opened.
- The doubt path's natural causes (only the qemu flavour's forced stop drives it); the release flavour on the doubt
  path (no forced stop there).
- t6: the drive's return after the plug by the program's checks (the late check fell at the plug).

### TBSTBYWB9X.1: two faults fixed before the merge (2026-11-15, after the owner's decision to merge)

The owner decided to take TBSTBYWB9X.1 into `3.5.1.0` on the emulator's readings alone: no real computer was
available for a standby (no bench machine of this project can enter Stand by). Read again for the merge,
`2b3ef8ad8` showed two faults, fixed below; the branch brought to `3.5.1.0` first (`71b55ad6b`, merge of
`2876eeb17`, no conflicts; the snapshot generator no change).

**Commit `2e2b23aee`.**
- A standing obligation always reaches its removal: under the doubt, section 6.1.5's verdict names the unit's
  upstream port from the unit's own record alone (`CmPortsUnitVerdict`), whatever the note, the place or the
  verdict hold now - an upstream port that stopped answering while its devnode stands, or a note a later suspend
  refreshed, left the obligation holding the member's re-enumeration with no removal ever asked. The minute retry
  asks by the record when the member itself does not read or reads reset (`CmPortsSlowPlace`, `slow` low byte
  F2h when the record names nothing), at the member's secondary bus kept with the place list (`UnitSec`, which the
  undo reads too; a later suspend's header does not replace it), and the removal names the child devnode at that
  recorded bus (`CmPortsUnitNameBus`). Host vectors in `test_unit_rules` (`test_cm_ports` 843 checks): a doubt
  whose upstream port reads all ones is lost and its removal step is REMOVE; the retry's place by the record for
  an unreadable or reset member; a BUS_02 child named when the member reads bus 03; a refreshed note.
- `SuspUuid` joins `gen-cm-snap.py`'s hashed names (`cm_snapf.c` regenerated, width 0, `CM_QS_FD_HASH`);
  `test_cm_snap` now fails any listed field ending in `Uuid` that is not a hash (it failed on the old table, 1 of 93).
- Record 21 section 6.1.6: the heading and item 15 say every reading is the emulator's and no real computer was
  available for a standby; items 6 and 11 and "Where" carry the two fixes.
- Reviewed and revised: the retry had still been gated on the member's own live read, the recorded bus could be
  replaced by a later suspend's header, the removal named the child at the bus read now, and the note could be
  replaced by a later suspend; each corrected as described above.

**Builds** (`2e2b23aee`): gated x86 `all` "BUILD + GATES PASSED (release qemu)" (`gated-x86-u5.log`), gated amd64
`release` "BUILD + GATES PASSED (release)" (`gated-amd64-u5.log`). `xhcicm.sys` x86 qemu `10997972...`, release
`4fdb6f68...` (`xfer98u5`).

**Legs.** The qemu flavour's test value stops a pass; it cannot make the upstream port stop answering while its
devnode stands, nor make the member unreadable: point (1) rests on the host vectors. The doubt path and the whole
path were run again on this build as a regression:

| f8h | Q, the dock, forced doubt [`2e2b23aee`] | removed, every node undone, numbered (`00002801`), E: back, compared at all three checks |

| f1g | Q, the dock [`2e2b23aee`] | written whole (4 nodes), nothing removed, checks PASS |

### TBSTBYWB9X.1: the undo proves each node before it writes (2026-11-15)

Every reading here is the emulator's, as above: no real computer was available for a standby. Branch brought to
`3.5.1.0` first (`288f1711f`, merge of `8498526f5`: roadmap and run-sheet changes only).

**Commit `d1a973711`.** The undo addressed a removed unit's nodes by the saved bus numbers and checked only vendor
and device before clearing command enables and bridge bus numbers; after the buses were given out again, a
same-model device at a reused bus could have been reset. Now every node is proven before anything is written
(`CmPortsUnitUndoPlan`, `CmPortsUnitPathRouted`): from the member down, the member reads secondary `UnitSec`, each
bridge of the path, at its proven place, reads the secondary bus its copy recorded inside the intersection of every
bus range above it, the node's own bus lies in that intersection, and the node reads as its copy beyond vendor and
device (class and revision, header layout, a function's subsystem); the path and the node's id are read again just
before each write. A node not proven is left untouched and logged (`resume-unit.undo` low byte 4) and does not keep
the obligation (the removal was made and the member has no child; the unit is forgotten and the numbering meets it
as it finds it); a refused read, a reset not taking or a suspend keeps it. A chain proven in part is undone in its
proven part: those nodes are shown to be this unit's, and resetting them only cuts the route to the rest, which no
devnode uses. Host vectors `test_undo_plan` (`test_cm_ports` 859 checks): a proven chain undone whole; a same-model
unit at a reused bus number (the member renumbered) never written; the member's range narrowed with the unit's
bridges' stale numbers and an identical NVMe at the bus now another member's - never written; partly proven; a reset
bridge's child; an id match with another class; nothing answering; a refused read; another connection. Reviewed and
revised (the bus ranges of the bridges above, at first not carried down the path, now carried). Record 21 section
6.1.6 item 10 and "Where" updated.

**Builds** (`d1a973711`): gated x86 `all` "BUILD + GATES PASSED (release qemu)" (`gated-x86-u6.log`), gated amd64
`release` "BUILD + GATES PASSED (release)" (`gated-amd64-u6.log`). `xhcicm.sys` x86 qemu `96199310...`, release
`8f454601...` (`xfer98u6`).

**Legs** (emulator, `d1a973711`):

| Leg | Vehicle, what | Result |
|---|---|---|
| f8j | Q, the dock, forced doubt | removed; the undo's plan: the NVMe at 03:00.0 **not proven** (`resume-unit.undo=00030004`: its downstream port, never written by the stopped pass, reads reset, so bus 3 is not routed), the chain port, the downstream port and the upstream port proven and reset (`...01`); numbered (`00002801`), E: back, compared at all three checks |
| f8k | Q, the enclosure, forced doubt | the same (the NVMe not proven, the two bridges reset), E: back, compared at all three checks; 49.31's fatal 0E once after the arrival (answered) |
| f1j | Q, the dock, the whole path | written whole (4 nodes), nothing removed, checks PASS |

The case this commit closes - a same-model device at a reused bus number - cannot be made in the emulator (its bus
numbers are not given out again under a standing devnode); it rests on the host vectors. The host vectors cover the
undo's plan, not its writes or the clean-up after them, which rest on the code's reading; and the re-check before
each write repeats the routing and the vendor/device id, not the plan's whole identity check.

## 50.17 (Setup's storage row): does Setup's update leave a mixed storage stack? (2026-11-16)

No branch change (reading and legs only). Development host A, the q35 w98se base
(`E:\xhci98-vm\q35-bases\w98se`, an ACPI install) as fresh overlays, the pinned emulator, one
vCPU and 512 MB a guest, `qemu-xhci` behind its root port and an `ich9-usb-ehci1` at `00:05.0`.
The sticks are QEMU's `usb-storage` (High Speed) over overlays of the q35 FAT test disk (volume
"ORICO"), hot-plugged by QMP on EHCI port 1 or the xHCI root port 3; the "reader" is a
`usb-bot` with two LUNs on EHCI port 2. Kit, scripts, logs and screenshots:
`E:\xhci98-vm\p50\i35b\` (`pids.txt` has every start and stop). The storage packages ran only
inside these guests and their copies were deleted at the end.

The idea tested: that Setup's "Storage drivers for Win 98 SE" row, on an update from 3.4.0.0
to 3.5.0.0, replaces some of NUSB's mass-storage files with the download's English NUSB 3.3
copies (Windows Millennium's `USBSTOR.SYS` 4.90.3000.1) while the devices' driver keys still
load `wdmstub.sys,USBSTOR.SYS`, so that the update leaves a mixed storage stack.

### What the code says (3.4.0.0, 3.4.3.0 = `4b15fe696`, 3.5.0.0 = `7ae5896fb`, branch 3.5.1.0)

- The row is not new in 3.4.1.0. It came with 3.2.0.0 (`01bdcfa58`), and 3.4.0.0, 3.4.1.0,
  3.4.2.0, 3.4.3.0 and 3.5.0.0 all have it. Between 3.4.3.0 and 3.5.0.0 no line of the row's
  code changed: the lines that mention "stor" in that diff are Stor98's find report
  (`inst_storfind_*`) and the restore code. Between 3.4.0.0 and 3.4.3.0 the texts
  changed, the device ids are read through `dev_ids()`, the baseline got a bounds check and
  the progress display names the device step (`stor_job`); what is detected, defaulted and
  copied did not change.
  The branch adds nothing to it.
- How Setup reads what is installed (`xhciinst/inst_eng.c` `stor_read_states` 29606-29651,
  `stor_inf_states` 29521-29603; `inst_core.c` 11188-11357):
  - The five binaries (`USBSTOR.SYS`, `USBNTMAP.SYS`, `USBAUTH.SYS`, `USBU2A.SYS` in
    `SYSTEM32\DRIVERS`, `USBMPHLP.PDR` in `SYSTEM\IOSUBSYS`) are read by their SHA-256 against
    the download's.
  - The two INFs are every `*.INF` in `INF` and `INF\OTHER` named `USBSTOR.INF` /
    `USBNTMAP.INF`, or a device INF whose text names `USBSTOR.SYS` / `USBMPHLP.PDR`.
  - Each file's state is absent, this installer's own (recorded under
    `HKLM\Software\xhci98\Storage\Files`), the download's bytes, or other bytes.
  - `HKLM\...\Uninstall\USB20U` (NUSB's uninstall entry) is read; a key that cannot be read
    counts as present.
  - `WDMSTUB.SYS`, `NTMPDriver` and the devices' driver keys play no part in the detection.
- The row's default (`inst_stor_default` 11336, `inst_stor_half_default` 11521):
  - With `USB20U` present it is unticked, whatever an earlier run recorded.
  - Without it, an earlier run's recorded choice decides; with no recorded choice it is
    unticked as soon as any of the seven is found that is not this installer's own. The one
    exception: a lone `USBSTOR.INF` with a valid package and this installer's route admitted
    (a half-made install it can repair) is ticked, recorded choice or not. Neither package
    looks like that (below).
  - The window (`xhciwiz.c` 1716, from `storInclude`) and the console's `/yes` and `/defaults`
    (`stor_question` 29845) take that default.
- What a ticked run (or `/storage`) does:
  - `stor_run_begin_body` (30412) records `Storage\Choice` and goes on only when the case
    admits the copy (`inst_stor_route` 11329: nothing found, or only the download's own bytes,
    or only this installer's).
  - All seven present with any other bytes (case "complete"), or some present with other
    bytes (case "other"), copies nothing. The plan says "nothing copied: existing files kept"
    or "a file found does not match this download, so storage is not installed".
  - Even on the route only absent binaries are copied: a `.TMP` beside the target, then
    `MoveFileA`, which never replaces a file (30078-30143). An INF is placed in `INF` only
    when no file of its name is there (`inst_stor_inf_set` 11439).
  - The package's copy of the seven, the `DevicePath` entry for it, the `SilentClasses`
    entries and the device installs all need that copy to have been made (`storCopyOk`).
  - The device installs (`stor_stage` 30891) take only devices with no driver, or with a
    driver key but Code 28 and no service (`stor_bound` 29987); a device bound to a storage
    driver is not installed again and its driver key is not rewritten.
  - An update runs the same code as a first install; there is no update-only storage path.
- What NUSB33D (the Czech "3.3c") looks like to it (measured in these guests): `USBSTOR.SYS`
  `9DEF2A07...` other; `USBNTMAP.SYS`, `USBAUTH.SYS`, `USBU2A.SYS`, `USBMPHLP.PDR` the
  download's bytes; `USBSTOR.INF` `AFB87B45...` and `USBNTMAP.INF` `C99C075D...` other;
  `USB20U` present; so case "complete", default unticked, and a ticked run copies nothing. The
  installed `USBSTOR.INF` with one Realtek line added (23,925 bytes, `F7C2D666...`) is other
  bytes in the same way.
- What the other storage package the issue's sender has, `USBSTACK.EXE` (with NUSB 3.5 CZ;
  `USBSTOR.SYS` 5.00.2195.6773, 21,584 bytes), looks like to it: `USBSTOR.SYS` `5759B3A9...`
  and both INFs other, the other four the download's bytes, no `USB20U` entry, so again case
  "complete", default unticked, nothing copied when ticked.

So no Setup from 3.2.0.0 to 3.5.0.0, in the window or the console, ticked or not, can replace
a storage file or INF of either package, or change a storage device's driver key.

### Legs

The NUSB33D guest (`cfg\n340.qcow2`) was built like this:

- a fresh overlay;
- NUSB33D's `_NUSB.INF` (its own install; its Czech `USER.EXE` comes with it, so the dialogs
  read Ano/Ne);
- the EHCI wizard (`USB2.INF`);
- 3.4.0.0 by `INSTALL.BAT /console /yes`;
- the stick (serial `I35BOT0001`) and the two-LUN reader installed on EHCI by Windows'
  wizard from `USBSTOR.INF`;
- the stick on the xHCI port (`E:`).

### The combination matrix (asked for after the four legs)

The other storage package is `USBSTACK.EXE` (with the NUSB 3.5 CZ download; `USBSTOR.SYS`
5.00.2195.6773, 21,584 bytes, `5759B3A9...`). It was installed through its `MSBSTACK.INF`
(`DefaultInstall`), as its own `USBSTACK.BAT` does for its "M" choice. That INF:

- copies a whole USB stack: `USBD.SYS` 20,752, `USBHUB.SYS` 40,560, `USBPORT.SYS` 139,120,
  `USBEHCI.SYS`, `USBHUB20.SYS`, `UHCD.SYS`, `OPENHCI.SYS`, `USBSTOR.SYS`, `WDMSTUB.SYS`,
  `USBUI.DLL` 74,240 and more;
- overwrites `USB.INF`, `USB2.INF`, `USBSTOR.INF` (24,417, `F6F962CE...`) and `USBNTMAP.INF`
  (1,186, `3D8323AF...`);
- writes `SilentInstall=1` on `Class\USB`, so its devices install with no wizard;
- adds no Add/Remove entry (no `USB20U`).

Its `USBSTOR.INF` loads the driver the same way, with `NTMPDriver=WDMSTUB.SYS,USBSTOR.SYS`.

How each cell ran:

- Each cell is one overlay.
- The stick known before the update (`I35BOT0001`) was installed and used under 3.4.0.0 in
  every cell.
- After the last restart, in the first session after a cold start, came the plugs:
  - a NEW stick (never seen) on EHCI, then its wizard or silent install;
  - its drive letter (`DRV.BAT`: `if exist X:\NUL`, `vol`, the USB Tree's report);
  - then another NEW stick on the xHCI port, read the same way.
- The VGA text buffer was read after each plug (a blue screen is text mode).
- Then the inventory (`INV.BAT`):
  - sizes, and `fc /b` against each package's files;
  - the registry: `Enum\USB`, `Enum\USBSTOR`, `Services\Class`, `Software\xhci98` and `USB20U`;
  - a 3.5.0.0 `/list` run, for Setup's own reading.

| Cell | Storage stack and order | xHCI98 path | Files in use after (USBSTOR.SYS / INFs / USBD / USBHUB / USBPORT) | Setup's reading | New stick EHCI | New stick xHCI |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | 3.3c, then USBSTACK, before xHCI98 | 3.4.0.0 console; known stick; window update to 3.5.0.0, defaults | all USBSTACK's: 21,584 / 24,417, 1,186 / 20,752 / 40,560 / 139,120 | USB20U 1, case complete, unticked | `E:` (silent install) | `E:` |
| X2 | USBSTACK, then 3.3c, before xHCI98 | the same | 3.3c's `USBSTOR.SYS` 21,552 and INFs; USBSTACK's `USBD` 20,752, `USBHUB` 40,560, `USBPORT` 139,120 (a mixed core) | the same | `E:` | `E:` |
| X3 | USBSTACK alone | the same | all USBSTACK's | USB20U 0, case complete, unticked ("Already installed. Left as-is.") | `E:` | `E:` |
| X4 | 3.4.0.0 first, then 3.3c (and the EHCI wizard) | known stick; window update | 3.3c's; `USBD` 18,912 | USB20U 1, unticked | `E:` | `E:` |
| X5 | the NUSB33D guest; 3.3c installed again after the update | window update, then NUSB33D's `_NUSB.INF` again (it asked for no restart), cold start | 3.3c's | USB20U 1, unticked | `E:` | `E:` |
| X6 | 3.3c, removed by its Add/Remove entry, then USBSTACK | 3.4.0.0 console; known stick; window update | all USBSTACK's | USB20U 0, unticked | `E:` | `E:` |
| X7 | the NUSB33D guest | 3.4.0.0 uninstalled by its console (`/uninstall /yes`), then a fresh 3.5.0.0 by the window | 3.3c's | USB20U 1, no recorded choice, unticked | `E:` | `E:` |
| X8 | the NUSB33D guest | window 3.4.0.0 -> 3.4.3.0, cold start, window 3.4.3.0 -> 3.5.0.0 | 3.3c's | USB20U 1, unticked (both runs) | `E:` | `E:` |

L1 to L4 and X1 to X8 make twelve runs. None showed a blue screen, a fault or a stick without
a drive letter.

- Under every stack, each stick's devnode has `NTMPDriver=wdmstub.sys,USBSTOR.SYS` and
  `InfPath=USBSTOR.INF`, and its disk unit has `PortDriver=USBMPHLP.PDR` and
  `InfPath=USBNTMAP.INF`.
- Setup never wrote a storage file, a storage INF or a storage device's driver key in any of
  them. In every log the "storage:" lines read the files and record only `Choice`.
- Inventories: `logs\inv-X1.txt` to `inv-X8.txt`, `inv-L4.txt`; cell logs
  `logs\cell-<cell>.txt`; screenshots `shots\<vm>-<cell>-*.png`.

Side findings:

- NUSB33D's own Add/Remove entry (`_USB2UN.INF`, X6) removes only its USB 2.0 part:
  `USB2.INF`, `USBEHCI.SYS`, `USBHUB20.SYS`, `USBPORT.SYS` and `USB20U`. Its storage files and
  INFs stay (`logs\inv-X6u.txt`).
- The 3.4.0.0 console uninstall (X7) touches no storage file. It deletes
  `Software\xhci98\Storage`, and the fresh 3.5.0.0 after it still leaves the row unticked,
  because of `USB20U`.
- The issue's USB Tree report lists `usbd.sys` 18,944 (Q281533's) and `usbui.dll` 147,456
  (98 SE's own). `USBSTACK.EXE` would have replaced both (with 20,752 and 74,240), so it is
  most likely not installed on that machine now.
- "Windows is shutting down" hung three times; QMP ended each after the wait (`logs\a-hang-001714.txt`,
  `c-hang-021217.txt`, `b-hang-022739.txt`). The hangs came in L1's guest after the stick
  legs, right after L4's console update (before its restart), and at the end of X6. This is
  task 50.19's hang, with no blue screen any of the times.
- Automation notes: an Explorer window left open for a removed stick reopens at the next
  start, hangs, and holds up Setup's restart until it is ended; a second MS-DOS box cannot
  write COM1 while the first holds it. One run of X8 had two scripts typing into it; it was
  discarded and X8 run again on a fresh overlay.

Pruned, with the reason:

- 3.4.0.0 -> 3.5.0.0 by Device Manager's Update Driver (INF only): no Setup run, so the
  storage code does not run. xhci98's INFs name no storage file (`src\xhci98.inf`,
  `src\uas\xhciuas.inf`: only `NTMPDriver=xhci98.sys` / `xhciuas.sys` and the UAS upper
  filter), and `usbd.sys` is copied with flag 16 (never over a file there).
- 3.5.0.0 back to 3.4.3.0: there was no fault to make stay or go.
- Q281533 before or after the stack, the memory patch, the tray running or not, and the reader
  present from power-on: run in "50.17" (the `up`, `fx` and `nn` rows) with NUSB33D, all
  PASS. The tray ran in every cell here.
- Known against never-seen stick: both were in every cell (the known stick before the update,
  new sticks after it).
- USBSTACK with Q281533 afterwards: the issue's report shows USBSTACK's core files absent.

A cell takes 25 to 45 minutes: about 40 for a cell that installs its storage stack on a fresh
disk, about 25 for one that starts from the saved NUSB33D disk. Three ran at a time. The
twelve took about three hours on development host A, the scripting included.

### Conclusion

The hypothesis is closed: Setup's storage row cannot have mixed the storage stack on that
machine.

- Its code never replaces a present file and never changes an INF of that name or the
  driver key of a device bound to a storage driver.
- With NUSB installed its default is unticked, in every release since 3.2.0.0, 3.4.0.0
  included.
- Twelve runs over both storage packages, in the listed combinations, showed no change by
  Setup and no fault.

For each Setup run, the issue sender's `C:\XHCIINST.LOG` will show:

- the `storage:` lines naming `USBSTOR.SYS` with "recorded no: state 3" (`9DEF2A07...` if it
  is 3.3c's, `5759B3A9...` if USBSTACK's);
- the other four binaries at "state 2", and both INFs at "state 3";
- `USB20U 1, choice n/n, source 0, case 1` (`USB20U 0` with USBSTACK alone) and
  `pack 1, default 0`, with `include 0` when the row was left unticked (if it was ticked:
  `include 1` or the window's `chosen 1`, the console's "/storage: installed without asking."
  or `storage: asked, include 1`, and then "Ticked: nothing copied: existing files kept.");
- no "Copied USBSTOR.SYS ..." line and no `storage record: Files\...` line.

A log without those lines would mean the hypothesis needs looking at again.

## 50.17 (old device entries): the reporter's answer of 2026-11-19, the code, and legs with old entries (2026-11-19)

Branch `w50-i35c`, from `3.5.1.0` at `779c6a5d2`; one commit, `caa30863f` (the issue record's section 8 and the
issues index row: the answer recorded, reviewed and revised). Development host A, the q35 w98se base
(`E:\xhci98-vm\q35-bases\w98se`, an ACPI install) as fresh overlays, the pinned emulator
`bin\asm4242-20261110-docks`, one vCPU and 512 MB a guest, `qemu-xhci` (`p2=4,p3=4`) behind its root port. Kit,
scripts, logs, exports and screenshots: `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\i35c\` (`pids.txt` has every start and stop).

### The answer

Recorded as facts in the issue record, section 8. In short: on the reporter's machine, with old entries under
`HKLM\Enum\USB` and `HKLM\Enum\USBSTOR` present, the fault came with `3.5.0.0`'s `xhci98.sys` and with the
driver's files deleted (0028:FF0FD32B), and not with `3.4.3.0`'s (swapped in by hand, installed by Setup, and its
files deleted and put back); polling (`XhciInterruptMode` 2) did not prevent it; with the old entries removed,
`3.5.0.0` gave no fault. Not stated: which entries, which port, which `usbstor.sys` in each test.

### What the code says (3.4.3.0 `4b15fe696` against 3.5.0.0 `7ae5896fb`, `git diff v3.4.3.0 v3.5.0.0 -- src`)

What decides a device's identity as 98 SE's Configuration Manager sees it, and so which `HKLM\Enum\USB\<id>\<instance>`
entry a plugged stick lands on or revives, item by item:

| What | Changed? | Could it change the Enum entry used, or what USBSTOR finds in it? |
|---|---|---|
| Hardware and compatible ids (`hcd_pdo.c`, BusQueryHardwareIDs / CompatibleIDs; `xhci_func.c`) | No: no hunk in either | No |
| Instance id: the serial when usable, else the place (`hcd_pdo.c` header, `XhciFuncInstanceId`, `XhciHubInstanceKey`, `hcdSerialTakenLocked`) | No: no hunk in the id code, `xhci_func.c` / `.h` unchanged | No |
| Task 49.34's "a serial counts only with no twin of it present" (`HcdSerialHold`, `HcdSerialUnique`, `KeepSerialId`) | New | No. Its callers decide whether a device the bus keeps across a disruption reopens: the resume keep (`hcd_enum.c` `hcdRkeepFlags`, `hcdRkeepRestore`), a link recovery's keep (`hcd_cfg.c` `hcdCfgRestore` with `linkKeep`, into `hcdCfgReplayResume`) and the Bulk-Only keep (`hcd_bot.c`); with a twin present the device is dropped or cycled instead of kept. `KeepSerialId` is filled at the PDO's creation and revival only for that check. The instance id still comes from `SerialId` through the unchanged code |
| The Bulk-Only keep (`hcd_bot.c`, new) | New | No. Its keep and restore act only at a system resume and only with `XhciResumeKeepBot` on; at a plug it observes the class driver's Bulk-Only traffic (`HcdBotAdmitLocked`, `HcdBotXferEnd`: the command block, the bytes returned, the medium state) to keep the keep's inputs, and sends or answers nothing differently |
| UniqueID in the capabilities | No (TRUE with a serial, as usbhub) | No |
| The composite parent (`HcdDevicePdoRepresentFunctions`) | One line: `KeepSerialId` copied with the other ids | No |
| Order and timing of a PDO's first requests (`hcd_enum.c`, `xhci_enum.c`) | Only the resume-keep decision | No |
| What the PDO answers: QUERY_INTERFACE, IOCTLs, URBs (`hcd_pdo.c`, `hcd_urb.c`) | The standard USB and PnP answers as before, with notes and counters added (`pdo.qi`, `pdo.ioctl`, `usbdx.*`); one private request of the project's own, the failure record `xhciuas.sys` sends (`hcdTelemetryIoctl`), also takes a second record version (`XHCI98_FAIL_VERSION2`) | No |
| Bus information, device text, string descriptors | No hunk | No |
| Registry and PnP calls of `xhci98.sys` (`IoOpenDeviceRegistryKey`, `IoGetDeviceProperty`, `IoInvalidateDeviceRelations`, `PoRequestPowerIrp`, VxD / CONFIGMG calls) | The same sites; the new ones are on xHCI98's own controller (`hcd_msgnt.c`, `hcd_inj.c`, mode 4) | No: none reaches a devnode of another controller |
| `hcd_pnp.c`, `hcd_power.c` | Mode 4's query-stop and resume handling, the controller's own | No |
| The 98-me INF | Values only: the MSI test values, `XhciStreamDequeueRepair`, `XhciEventRingTrbs` 1024 to 256 for a fresh install | No device id or devnode changed |

So nothing in `3.5.0.0` changes what Configuration Manager sees of a device on xHCI98's bus, and nothing in either
version reaches a devnode, a driver key or an Enum entry of a device on another controller. For a flash disk on the
Intel EHCI controller, as section 2 of the issue record has it, `xhci98.sys`'s code has no path to its devnode. What
does differ between the two files is their size (366,051 and 445,099 bytes) and their memory use (3.5.0.0 adds the
stream trace rings and their capture, and a fresh install's event ring is 256 TRBs where 3.4.3.0's default is 1024),
which can change where later images and allocations land; whether the fault's other address (issue record,
section 8) comes from such a move is not known, nor which file gave it.
That is a difference in layout, not a path, and nothing here shows it matters.

### The guests: old entries made the ways the reporter's history suggests

No earlier leg had old entries from other stacks: they installed NUSB33D, then xHCI98, then plugged. Two chains of
saved disks (`cfg\`), each step a cold start; the sticks are QEMU's `usb-storage` over overlays of the q35 FAT
test disk, the "reader" a `usb-bot` with two LUNs (the composite card reader's stand-in; QEMU has no
storage-and-smart-card composite). Serial numbers: `I35S1` (the stick, s1), QEMU's default when none is given (s2:
`1-<controller path>-<port>`, so a different serial, and a different entry, at each port and controller, the way a
device whose identity follows its port leaves one entry per port), an empty string (s3), `I35R1` (the reader, r1).
Before the first plug of every cell (and again after a cell's preparation where it says so), `HKLM\Enum\USB`, `HKLM\Enum\USBSTOR`, `Class\USB` and the live devnode list were exported
(`logs\ex\<cell>-*.reg`).

- **Chain A** (`exa.sh`: an `ich9-usb-ehci1` at `00:05.7` with three `ich9-usb-uhci` companions at `00:05.0` to
  `05.2`, like the Intel boards of the reporter's history, and a standalone `piix3-usb-uhci` at `00:06.0`): 98 SE
  installs its own UHCI stack (`USB.INF`); NUSB33D; the stick under 98 SE's UHCI stack with NUSB33D's storage (s1
  at two ports, s2), all `E:`; the EHCI driver (`USB2.INF`); s1 at EHCI ports 1 and 2 (it revives its UHCI-era
  entry, `E:`), s2 at ports 1 and 2 (new entries, `E:`), s3 (no devnode at all: NUSB's hub drops an empty serial
  string), r1 (`E:`); saved as `cA0`. Then 3.4.0.0, the same devices on the xHCI port and s1 on EHCI; the update to
  3.4.3.0 with s1 on both (`cA343`); the update to 3.5.0.0 (`cA350`).
- **Chain B** (the earlier legs' machine: `ich9-usb-ehci1` at `00:05.0`, no companions): 3.4.0.0 with its storage
  row (`/storage`: the download's NUSB 3.3 set, Windows ME's `USBSTOR.SYS` 4.90.3000.1); s1, s2, s3 and r1 on the
  xHCI port, each `E:`; NUSB33D over it (2000 SP4's `USBSTOR.SYS` and `WDMSTUB.SYS`); the EHCI driver; s1, s2
  (ports 1, 2), s3, r1 on EHCI; the update to 3.4.3.0 with s1 on both (`cB343`); the update to 3.5.0.0 (`cB350`).

The EHCI's first wizard was cancelled in both chains (to run the UHCI era, and in chain B because no USB 2.0
driver was there yet); 98 SE then leaves it at Problem 28 and never asks again. Its `Enum\PCI` key was deleted with
a `[-key]` line in a `.reg` file (98 SE's regedit takes it) and the next cold start offered the wizard.

### What the old entries did before any test (chain B)

The download's storage set writes its devices' driver keys with `NTMPDriver = USBSTOR.SYS`; NUSB33D's with
`NTMPDriver = wdmstub.sys,USBSTOR.SYS`. NUSB33D replaced the file with 2000 SP4's but left the old driver keys.
The stick then revived its old entry (`Enum\USB\VID_46F4&PID_0001\I35S1`, driver key `USB\0002`) on EHCI and on
the xHCI port alike, and:

- as the first storage device of a session it stayed at Problem 2, no letter, no blue screen (16:09 on EHCI under
  3.4.0.0, 16:47 on the xHCI port and 16:54 on EHCI under 3.4.3.0);
- the reader's old entry of the same form started (`E:`) at 16:33, after two sticks with NUSB33D's own driver keys
  had loaded in that session.

That the difference is whether `wdmstub.sys` was already loaded is an inference from the order; nothing of
`wdmstub.sys` or `USBSTOR.SYS` was read.

### The test cells

Each cell: a fresh overlay of a saved disk, a cold start, the exports (`logs\ex\<cell>-*.reg`: `Enum\USB`,
`Enum\USBSTOR`, `Class\USB`, the live devnode list), then the steps in order; a device plugged stays plugged unless a
step removes it. After each plug: up to 120 s for the Add New Hardware wizard (answered if it shows), the drive
letters (`if exist X:\NUL`, E: to J:), the live devnode list and the USB Tree's report (`DRV.BAT`), and the VGA
text buffer read for a blue screen at every poll. Cells, scripts and the runner: `scripts\tests.txt`, `ptest.sh`,
`runtests.sh`; every cell's log `logs\cell-<cell>.txt`. Steps are written `<device> <bus><port>`: e = the Intel EHCI
(on chain A behind it its UHCI companions), x = the xHCI port.

The letter check (`if exist X:\NUL` in a DOS box) saw only `E:` in a session with several disks, in the plain
NUSB-era cells (TA) as in the others, while Explorer opened a window for each disk's own letter (`E:`, `F:`, `G:`:
`shots\b-TE2-letters-EFG.png`) and every disk's devnode had started (Problem 0, the `SCSI\` disk devnode under each
`USBSTOR\` child): the check under-reports. "Started" below is read from the devnode list.

| TA1, TA2 | cA350, cA343 | s1 e1 started (its UHCI-era entry revived); r1 e2 started; s2 e3 new (wizard), started | none |
| TA3, TA4 | cA350, cA343 | r1 e2 started; s1 e1 started | none |
| TA5, TA6 | cA350, cA343 | s1 x3 started; r1 e2 started; s3 e1 (no devnode: NUSB's hub drops the empty serial) | none |
| TB1, TB2 | cB350, cB343 | s1 e1: old entry keyed `USBSTOR.SYS` alone, Problem 2; r1 e2 the same; s2 e3 new (wizard, NUSB33D's key), started | none |
| TB3, TB4 | cB350, cB343 | s2 e1 started (NUSB33D's key); s1 x3: the same old entry, now started, its old `USBSTOR\` child revived; r1 e2 started | none |
| TC1, TC2 | cA350, cA343; NUSB33A's setup run and its `USBSTOR.SYS` (Windows ME's, 21,040 bytes) copied over 2000's, cold start | s1 e1 started (its key `wdmstub.sys,USBSTOR.SYS` now loading the ME file); r1 e2 started; s2 e3 new (wizard), started | none |
| TC3 | cA350, as TC1 | s1 x3 started; r1 e2 started | none |

### What asks for power at these plugs (TG1, TG2)

`bp2.py` (copied from `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\i35\scripts`) on QEMU's gdb stub: a breakpoint at NTKERN's
`PoRequestPowerIrp` (`C026E9BE` on this base, as in "50.17 (continued)"), each call's caller, device object, minor
code, power state, completion routine and context logged, and the device object's header read (data only:
`logs\TG1-power.trace`). Through all seven plugs and unplugs, including the old entries failing and then starting:
one request, a `SET_POWER` D0 whose context is not a device object, at 20:42:32, the first plug of the session (s1,
its old entry; the hub's request, as in 50.17); none at the later plugs, the new stick's included. None from USBSTOR. At the shutdown that ended the cell: one D3 request per USBSTOR device (three, one driver
object), each callback run at once with its own device object, then the hubs' and other drivers' own, so the breakpoint was in place and saw them.

TG2 (the same steps on cB343, 3.4.3.0) had no request at any plug, and at its shutdown the same three USBSTOR D3
requests with their callbacks on intact device objects (`logs\TG2-power.trace`).

So in these states nothing at a plug sends a storage device a power request, the condition the fault's routine needs
(issue record, section 3).

### What this shows

- **Not reproduced.** No cell gave a blue screen: 25 cells over five saved states (`cA343`, `cA350`, `cB343`,
  `cB350`, a fresh base), besides the plugs while the chains were built. That covers the reporter's own sequence

  the file swaps (TE1 to TE3).

  session, and then starts; and a stick revives its old `USBSTOR\` child, from whichever stack made it. Removing an

- **The version question stays open.** Between `3.4.3.0` and `3.5.0.0` the code changes nothing a device on another

/SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART /LOG`, whole-registry and file-list diffs before and after; `logs\ex\prepg-cA-*.reg`),
exit 0, no restart asked. It installed `libusb0.sys` in `SYSTEM32\DRIVERS`, `libusb0.dll` in `SYSTEM32`, its program
folder (headers, libraries, its source, `install-filter.exe`, `testlibusb.exe`, `testlibusb-win.exe`), Start menu
links and an uninstall key; then ran `install-filter.exe -i`, which set `UpperFilters` = `libusb0.sys` on seven class
keys, `USB` among them, as the reporter's export has it on `USB`; then opened its test program (closed by hand with
Alt+F4). Saved as `cAG`.

**Each run** (`pcell.sh`): a fresh overlay of the cell's disk; the reader stand-in on the command line, so present
from power-on (cells E and EG: not attached at power-on; EG hot-plugs it after the stick); a cold start, the wait for
the taskbar; the boot log (`logs\ex\<run>-bootlog.reg`); the `Enum\USB`, `Enum\USBSTOR`, `Class\USB` and devnode
exports (`logs\ex\<run>-*.reg`); the loaded-image list; the stick stand-in plugged at EHCI port 1; the VGA text buffer
read for a blue screen every 10 s for 120 s (on a blue screen: its text, a shot, QEMU's register dump, the image list,
then a key); the image list again, the devnode list and the USB Tree's report (`DRV.BAT`); power-off. In the traced
runs (GT) only the pre-plug image list was taken (the later ones are skipped while the debugging stub is held). Logs
`logs\cell-<run>.txt`, `logs\<run>-img-*.txt`, summaries by `scratch\tools\runsum.py`.

**The loaded-image list** (`scripts\imglist.py`, data only): the guest paused, its mapped ranges at or above
`C0000000` saved with QEMU's `memsave`, the guest resumed; then VXDLDR's list of dynamically loaded devices walked as
the Windows 98 DDK's `vxdldr.h` documents it (`struct DeviceInfo`: next, load count, DDB, id, module name, signature,
object count, `struct ObjectInfo` table), from the module-name strings. WDM images loaded by NTKERN are in that list
with their objects (98 SE loads each section as its own object); a module's name is the spelling of the `NTMPDriver`
entry that loaded it. The saved ranges are searched only for those name strings, pointers to them and the nodes'
signature value; only the `DeviceInfo` and `ObjectInfo` structures and the name strings are interpreted, and no code
is examined or disassembled.

### The traced runs (data only)

`scripts\bp2.py` (from "50.17 (old device entries)") on QEMU's gdb stub (`-gdb`, ports 47171 to 47175), armed after
the pre-plug image list: a breakpoint at NTKERN's `PoRequestPowerIrp` (`C026E9BE` on this base), each call's
caller, device object, minor code, state, completion routine and context logged; with `I35_CBS=FF0E0940`, also a
breakpoint at the start of `USBSTOR.SYS`'s first object in `cAG` and `cBG`, where section 3's routine begins, its
return address and stack words logged and the context's device-extension field (`+0x28`) and that extension's
`+0x6C` read as data. Logs `logs\GT<n>-power.trace`.

- GT1 (G): no `PoRequestPowerIrp` call from arming (11:59:08) to the fault (11:59:27); the trace ended when the
  guest was stopped.
- GT2 (G2): none at the plug. At the shutdown: `HIT 1 caller FF0E2771 ... DeviceObject C18FFC68 Minor 02 PowerState
  4 Completion FF0E0940 Context C1900AE8` (USBSTOR, its fourth object), then `CALLBACK FF0E0940 (return C026E853)`
  with that context, then `HIT 3 caller FF06B9BE` (inside `libusb0`'s first object) for the same device object with
  no completion; the same for the second USBSTOR device; then other drivers' requests.
- GT3, GT4 (G): no `PoRequestPowerIrp` call; `CALLBACK FF0E0940 (return C0293BDD)` 1 s after the plug, GT4's stack
  words `C0293BDD C1C8ACE8 E42B99C4 E42B99FC 00000000 00000000 ...`, `[ext 0588003A ext+6C NOT READABLE]`; the
  blue screen at the first look, 11 s (GT3) and 13 s (GT4) after the plug.
- GT5 (G2): no call of either kind at the plug.

`C0293BDD` lies among NTKERN's addresses seen here (`C026E9BE`, `C026E853`) in the system area; the DDB chain read
by `scripts\ddbscan.py` (VMM's `struct VxD_Desc_Block`, data) does not place pageable code, so which component holds
it was not read.

### What the guest lacks against the reporter's machine

The composite reader (a two-LUN `usb-bot` stood in; QEMU has no composite device with a mass-storage function, and
the sibling project's simulator over `usb-redir` would need one written, so it was not built); the board's two Intel
EHCI controllers behind their rate-matching hubs and the VL805 (the guest: one EHCI with no hub, QEMU's xHCI); the
earlier boards' controllers, the other devices' `Enum\USB` and `Class\USB` entries and the reporter's
`Enum\USBSTOR`; the Czech 98 SE, its memory size and patch, section 2's `usbd.sys`; the version of `libusb0.sys` the
reporter has (the export names the filter, not its version).

### What this shows

- **Reproduced.** Section 1's blue screen, `USBSTOR(01) + 0000000B`, in every counted run that had both the reporter's
  class filter (`libusb0.sys` on `Class\USB`) and the reader's driver key spelling the stub `WDMSTUB.SYS` (G, CG, G
  under `3.4.3.0`, EG: 12 of 12), and in none that lacked either (A, B, C, D, E, F, G2, DG: 0 of 23); the traced
  runs agree (GT1, GT3, GT4 faulted; GT2, GT5 did not). Phase 2 below shows that the filter is not needed: with the
  reader plugged after the stick the fault comes without any filter (EP, NXa, NX), and the filter acted only through
  where the images were loaded.
- **The entry's other values do not matter here**: the working entry with only `Driver` changed faults (CG); the
  faulting entry with the key's stub name in lower case does not (DG).
- **The order of plugging is section 6's**: with the reader present from the start the fault comes at the stick's
  plug; with the reader absent, the stick works and the reader's plug faults (EG).
- **`3.4.3.0`'s `xhci98.sys` does not hide it here** (3 of 3), unlike on the reporter's machine (section 8).
- **No second image, no `PoRequestPowerIrp`**: in every image list taken, at most one stub and one `USBSTOR` image
  (none before the plug in E and EG, one of each after the stick); in the traced runs the faulting routine is
  entered at the plug with a context of 0 from `C0293BDD`, with no `PoRequestPowerIrp` call before it; phase 2 below
  reads what that call is: a second `DriverEntry` of the stub, for a second driver object.

### Phase 2: the root cause (owner, 2026-11-20, from 12:45)

Same rig, folders and ports; at most four guests. Data only: driver and device objects by the Windows 2000 DDK's
`DRIVER_OBJECT` (Type 4, Size 0xA8) and `DEVICE_OBJECT` layouts, IRPs by `IRP` / `IO_STACK_LOCATION`, the loader's
object table as before; no code of a closed image interpreted or disassembled. `scripts\drvscan.py` saves the mapped
ranges at or above `C0000000` (QMP `memsave`; with `--held`, while the debugging stub holds the guest), finds driver
objects by their Type/Size words and checks them field by field (name, `DriverInit`, `DriverExtension->AddDevice`,
`DriverUnload`, `MajorFunction`, each mapped to every image object it lies in), walks each driver's device objects and
their `AttachedDevice` chains, searches the saved ranges for words equal to USBSTOR's first object's address and keeps
only the hits outside every image's objects (the heap and the stacks), and dumps given addresses as IRPs where their
Type says so. `bp2.py` runs it at the breakpoint on USBSTOR's first routine (`I35_DRVSCAN`); `pcell.sh` runs it before
and after the plug (`DRVSCAN=1`).

| Run | Disk | What | Result |
|---|---|---|---|

The own filter (`scratch\tfilt\`, `tfilt.c`; built by `build.cmd` with the main tree's Windows 2000 DDK, free, x86;
TEST ONLY, not tracked, not packaged): attaches above each device of the class, passes every IRP down unchanged (power
with `PoStartNextPowerIrp`, `IoSkipCurrentIrpStackLocation`, `PoCallDriver`; `IRP_MN_REMOVE_DEVICE` passed down, then
detach and delete); `tfiltl.sys` (`-DTFILT_LOG`) also writes one line per IRP, and per completion (but for
`IRP_MN_REMOVE_DEVICE`, passed down without a completion routine), to QEMU's port `E9` (the guest's `debugcon-a.log`).
Placed by `TFP.BAT` (the file into `SYSTEM32\DRIVERS`, `TF.REG` / `TFL.REG` setting `Class\USB` `UpperFilters`), by
`ptfprep.sh`.

The NX guest (`cfg\workNX`, then `cNX` = `workNX` with `CA.REG` by `pprep.sh`): an empty overlay of the base on a
machine with no xHCI controller and the EHCI at 00:05.7 with three UHCI companions; 98 SE's own USB stack installed
for the companions by its wizards, NUSB33D, the EHCI's wizards, then the two stand-ins installed by their wizards, the
logged boot made the default (`pwnx.sh`, continued by `pwnx2.sh`, which answers each Add New Hardware wizard in turn,
`logs\cell-NX0b.txt`). Its `Class\USB` export holds no xHCI98 key (`logs\ex\cNX-prepclass.reg`).

`USB\0043`'s spelling and the image lists: USBSTOR's first object begins at the stub's 7th object, the overlap of
the image addresses, in G, G2, CG, DG, G under 3.4.3.0 and EG (with the filter) and in E and EP (without); of
these G2, DG and E did not fault (the results above), the overlap alone not being the second entry. In A, C, F
(reader at power-on, no filter) and TA (the own filter) the addresses do not overlap.

libusb-win32 0.1.12.2's source: a bare clone of the project's public repository
(`dl\github\libusb-win32.git`), commit `00eb39681301bb69d8ecb6b11176114018ec5678` (2009-07-07, "version 0.1.12.2";
`libusb/Makefile` `VERSION_MAJOR 0`, `MINOR 1`, `MICRO 12`, `NANO 2`), archived as text into `dl\src-0.1.12.2\`.
`libusb/src/driver/power.c` 35-98 (`dispatch_power`: set-power passed down with a completion routine, others skipped
down), 132-135 (after a system set-power completes, `power_set_device_state` for the matching device state), 189 and
202 (`PoRequestPowerIrp` on the device's PDO); `pnp.c` 97-101 (`PoSetPowerState` at `IRP_MN_START_DEVICE`);
`libusb_driver.c` 108, 147 (create and attach); `libusb/src/registry.c` 71-86 (the six default 9x class keys: usb,
