Void in phase 2: `ptf-cAT` at 12:43 (its waiter matched an old log line; started while guest c still ran the `cCG`
rebuild: the launch failed on the busy port, and the `cCG` saved at 12:44 was the wrong disk, by its size; both
discarded and redone); `ptf-cBT` at 12:59 (`cfg\cB` had been deleted in the 12:45 clean-up; the guest never
started; redone from a rebuilt `cB`); the first NX build, 13:34 to 14:08 (one EHCI and no UHCI companions: with no
xHCI98 the package's EHCI root hub stayed at Problem 2 and no stand-in enumerated; `void\cell-NX0-1334.txt`), and
the second's first form, 14:09 to 14:47 (its wizard step answered one wizard per cold start; continued by `pwnx2.sh`
on the same running guest, `logs\cell-NX0.txt` then `cell-NX0b.txt`).

### Void runs and refusals

- 10:02:41 to 10:03:40: the first four preparations (`cA`, `cB`, `cC`, `cD`) ended by `quit`: a dialog of an Internet
  Explorer window held the shutdown; their disks were discarded. The `cA343` preparation that followed on guest a
  was voided too: its runner was stopped by hand, and a `quit` sent at 10:08:38 met the guest in its own ACPI
  power-off (`pids.txt`); its disk was discarded. Power-off now presses Enter after 30 s and every 20 s, up to six times
  (`acpi-enterN` in the logs), and waits up to 360 s.
- 10:03: A2 and A3, first attempts: the boot outlasted the script's fixed 105 s wait with four guests up; the DOS box
  did not open. Their runners were stopped by hand and the guests by `quit` over their own QMP ports (10:08:42 and
  10:08:46, `pids.txt`). The boot now waits for the taskbar.
- The download of libusb-win32 by the worker: the first request (the release's file) and a second (the project's file
  feed) each returned HTTP 403; the next attempt was refused by the permission system, and nothing more was tried.
  The owner supplied the file.
- 13:30: entering the owner's status line, a pointer at the end of the status paragraph and the issues index row
  was refused by the permission system; the edit stopped, nothing was written, and the texts went to the
  coordinator (`edit\status7.py`, not run).
- The first orchestration that included the in-guest install was refused by the permission system; on the owner's
  answer the install ran once as a step of its own. A fifth guest was refused; the leg stayed at four.

## 50.20 (continued) The fix: no stream Set TR Dequeue for a declaring UAS client on a flagged controller, the setting, and the emulator legs (2026-11-16)

The fix of design record 17 section 4.12.10, built and read in the emulator. Field reports from one computer (an
Intel 7 Series xHCI `8086:1E31`, a UAS drive, `3.5.0.0`, XP x64 and later 7 x64 as well) showed a cancelled stream
transfer leaving the controller using one stream's position for another: a read completed twice and the next one
timed out, Babble, or 4.12.8's stream check giving the drive up and cycling it (a removal to Windows, open files
lost, and after three cycles the port held). The readings behind the design are in the section above.

### What was built

Branch `w50-uasfix`, on `3.5.1.0`'s `1035414a5`:

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `9ea4a3c38` | the bus: no stream Set TR Dequeue on a contract endpoint of a flagged controller; the debt that holds such an endpoint; the Error exit; RESET_PIPE as the client's endpoint recycle; the pure decisions with their vectors (`test_stream`, `test_uas`, `test_sdeq` - the field's thirteen captures as data); the qemu flavour's faults 33, 34 and 35; five counter words at 320 |
| `573cfeb40` | `xhciuas.sys`: the declaration at the streams open, the barrier, the proof (endpoint recycle or device reset), the command phase after a device reset (TEST UNIT READY per LUN) |
| `bfcb0a747` | record 17 section 4.12.10 and its references |
| `e4083ac36` | the owner's decision of 2026-11-15: the controller flag as a setting, `XhciStreamDequeueAvoid` (0 off everywhere, 1 the listed controllers - `8086:1E31` - the default, 2 every controller), in the form of the quirk values; counter word 325 |
| `9c21739ba` | a RESET_PIPE recycle Configure the controller refuses holds the endpoint for the client's device reset (found by leg XF4 below) |
| `e258676ac` | record 17: that hold's safety argument said apart for QEMU |

Gated builds (x86 all, amd64 all, the tools) passed on each code commit's tree; the
logs are kept with the scratch files.

### How the legs ran

- **Guest:** XP x64 SP2 (the field's system), a fresh overlay of the shared q35 base for every leg, 2 vCPUs.
  7 x64 SP1 for its two legs. Each leg: a setup boot, then a cold start per phase - the install, the drive made
  L:, the programs or the scenario - with a report (XHCITR's, as the Quick save takes it) after each step.
- **Package:** this tree's installer takes release-flavour drivers only (its build-marker check), and an unsigned
  64-bit package is refused on XP x64 too ("carries the Thunderbolt driver without its catalog"). So each leg
  installs the release amd64 package of the tree under test, made by `make-package.ps1`, after signing it inside
  the guest with a certificate made there (MakeCert, Root and TrustedPublisher; a catalog per INF made with WDK
  7.1's MakeCat and signed with SignTool), and then puts the qemu flavour's `xhci98.sys` and `xhciuas.sys` over
  the installed files and every copy a later device install could take them from, as Phase 49's swap kits did.
  The first report of every start shows the qemu driver loaded (`qemu.inj.latched`, `qemu.inj.streamflag`).
- **Emulator:** usb4-emu test builds (uncommitted, worktree `w50-hwm`): `emu50e` (`qemu-system-x86_64.exe`
  `5a4b09db...`) with `qemu-xhci x-stream-setdeq-current`, `x-stream-setdeq-keep`, `x-stream-dcs` and `usb-uas
  x-clear-halt`, `x-reset-ua`; `emu50f` (`435ce60c...`) adds `qemu-xhci x-stream-ep-error=N`: the first Stop
  Endpoint on a streams endpoint N s or more after the controller's start leaves that endpoint in Error, and a
  Set TR Dequeue is then taken in Error (QEMU never enters Error otherwise). The model logs every load
  (`xhci98-model: setdeq-current: loaded #N ...`) on QEMU's own log.
- **The drive:** `usb-uas` with a 128 MB `scsi-hd` (FAT16, L:), `x-ata-passthrough-refuse` on, on a SuperSpeed
  port.
- **The phase T:** three rounds of HWMonitor 1.62, Speccy 1.32 and HWiNFO64 6.43 started from L: (HWiNFO **build
  4380**; the field ran build **4385**; its start window answered Run, its settings left at their defaults, the
  drive scan and SMART reading on - its ATA PASS-THROUGH reads show in the drive's failure ring), each checked at
  6 s and 40 s and then closed; a report after each start. Meanwhile a 16 MiB copy-compare loop to L: and back
  every 20 s, a writer holding `L:\OPEN.TXT` open and appending a line every 2 s, and a reader comparing 32
  reference files of 1 MiB on L: with their originals. At the end the open file's size, the loop file and every
  reference file are compared again, and the event logs read.
- **Injection legs** run a scenario in place of the program rounds (fault writes to the machine-wide key; the
  rendezvous held about 4 s after it is reached).

AFTER is fault 33 argument 1 (on `bfcb0a747`'s binaries the fault sets the flag itself; from `e4083ac36` it
counts the controller as listed and `XhciStreamDequeueAvoid`, at its default 1, flags it); BEFORE is argument 2
(the QEMU resync off, the controller not listed, so unflagged and 4.12.8's give-up form can show). Both legs of a
pair run the same emulator switches; only the fault differs.

| W7A2 | `9c21739ba`, **7 x64 SP1, AFTER** (fault 33 arg 1), two rounds (the first try stopped at setup: the Run box does not elevate on 7) | L: present throughout, open file kept (5392 bytes), copies 25/25 PASS, 64 reference rounds clean, every program alive at every check; `StreamDeqUntrusted` 1, contract opens 3, debts 2 raised and released; time-outs 0, port resets 0, "Set TR Dequeues 0"; **0 model loads** | **pass** |
| XLG | `9c21739ba`, unflagged (no fault 33), the model off, faults 1D, 1E and 1F (4.12.8's legs) | 1D once: the stale dequeue sent (`qemu.inj.staledeq=0001070B`), the read-back found it different and set it again, then equal (`cfg.deq.readback` 07B1, 07B0; `StreamDeqMismatch` 1, `StreamDeqResent` 1), no cycle - as 49.39's QC legs; 1D three times (the give-up and cycle) is XGV above. 1E and 1F were armed but no stream Set TR Dequeue followed in that boot (the later refusals took no TD off), so neither fired; drive kept, 11/11 PASS, references clean | 1D unchanged; 1E and 1F not reached |
| XST5 | `9c21739ba`, STOP2: rendezvous point 2 (RESET_PIPE held between the clear and the recycle), Speccy run from C: and ended while held, then the disable, then the release | Speccy ended, the disable started while the recycle was held: "ok DI_NEEDREBOOT" again, the drive stayed started (Code 0). xhciuas answers a query-remove with success, so the veto comes from above it (a program that has opened the disk leaves it in use); the recycle then completed and the drive went on | not read: a stop with the obligation outstanding cannot be made in this harness (owed) |

**The failed recovery's drain.** Where a recovery could not complete - xhciuas's Dead path after a stalled bus
(XRV) and the controller reset of a recycle Configure with no completion (XF4, XF4N0) - the requests queued at
the drive were failed, not left waiting: the copy loop logged a failed round and the reader unreadable files at
that moment, the programs and the loops went on, and after the drive was found again every copy and every
reference compared equal. No leg hung in such a recovery.

### What the emulator's model can and cannot show

- It shows the driver against **one model** of the fault: a Set TR Dequeue for another stream loaded into the
  endpoint's current stream's cached state, kept across a stop (`-keep`). With it, the published behaviour (the
  unflagged control legs) gives the field's forms - the time-outs and replays (`xfer.unmatched`), the give-up and
  cycle with the open file lost, "Delayed Write Failed", a monitoring program ending by itself - and the fix's
  path gives none of them, with no load at all.
- A load is the only way the model corrupts anything, so "no load" shows that the modelled mechanism is avoided.
  It says nothing about a mechanism the model does not have.
- QEMU itself departs from a real controller: it fetches TDs early, restarts a Stopped endpoint on its own device
  wakeup (record 17 4.12.4), and its `usb-uas` asserts on a second data packet for one stream (the model's
  misplaced position). Two artefacts of the model, not of the driver, were seen in the unflagged legs: QEMU's
  `usb-uas` aborting (`dev-uas.c:979: usb_uas_handle_data: assertion failed: (uas->data3[p->stream] == NULL)`,
  XB2 and XD2), and the guest stopping after a cycle (XB1, XC1: both vCPUs idle, the clock interrupt still
  counted, no COM1 or xHCI interrupt, no answer to keys). The same cycle through `3.5.0.0`'s own fault-1D
  give-up, with the model off (XGV), did not stop the guest.
- A rendezvous held longer than xhciuas's 5 s proof budget makes it ask for a device reset by design; in XRV,
  with the hold still on, that recovery failed too and the drive ended in the Dead path. The later legs hold
  about 4 s after the point is reached.
- A Windows disable is vetoed by any handle on the drive (an open file, a program running from it, a program
  holding the disk for SMART), so the disable legs stop the loops first and end the program before the disable.
- The refused recycle's held endpoint on QEMU: see record 17 (not shown there; the fault-34 legs read the model's
  loads and any event on the held endpoint before the device reset).

### What is not read

- **The field controller.** Only the reporter's Intel 7 Series controller can show that, given no stream Set TR
  Dequeue and fresh contexts from the Drop and Add or the device reset, it no longer misplaces a stream, and
  whether its hidden state is discarded with the old context.
- A DMA into a completed client buffer on real hardware (`XhciDmaStaging` 0, the field's setting): no emulator
  leg can see it; the reporter's copy-compare and reference reads are the check.
- **98 SE and 2000: not run.** `xhciuas.sys` opens streams on any SuperSpeed UAS drive whatever the system
  (`uas_fdo.c`: the streams open follows the drive's SuperSpeed configuration alone), and a UAS drive has run at
  SuperSpeed on 98 SE before (`runs/run-49.md`), so the contract path is there. What these legs use is not: the
  trigger - a request the drive refuses with its data-in posted - comes from the monitoring programs, run here in
  their XP x64 and 7 x64 builds, and the leg kit is written for XP and later (`reg`, `tasklist`, `diskpart`,
  scheduled tasks). One leg each is owed, with a trigger of its own (a program there that sends a vendor or
  pass-through request the drive refuses).
- A second drive's command disturbing the first's endpoint on the real controller (record 17, "Mixed clients"):
  the model is per endpoint, so the two-drive leg cannot show it.
- Two endpoints gated in one recovery (the partial recycle of fault 34): the emulator's drive gates the data-in
  endpoint alone at a refusal; the host vectors hold that case.
- Faults 1E and 1F (4.12.8's restarts) in this tree: armed, but no stream Set TR Dequeue followed in the boot
  (XLG); 1D's resend and give-up paths are read (XLG, XGV).
- The drive found again after a PnP removal while owed: QEMU's hot-plugged `usb-uas` came back at 12 Mb/s and was
  not enumerated (XPN); the removal itself is read.
- Speccy on 7 x64 in the BEFORE leg (refused by Windows from the drive there).
- **A stop with the obligation outstanding** (the drive disabled while its recovery is under way, then started
  again): Windows vetoes the disable whenever a program has opened the disk, and every trigger here is such a
  program (XST to XST5); owed. A disable and enable with nothing owed (XEE3) and a removal while owed (XPN) are
  read.

### For the reporter: the test build and what to send

A draft for the owner to rephrase (the test build is the release flavour of the tree, signed as the owner signs
test builds):

1. Copy every file you would lose to another disk first.
2. Install the test build over `3.5.0.0` (Setup, Install/update) and restart Windows (on 7 x64 in test-signing
   mode, as for `3.5.0.0`). If `XhciForceBulkOnly` was set to 1 as the way round the fault, set it back to 0, then
   unplug the drive and plug it in again.
3. In the xHCI98 USB Tree, View > Settings: `XhciStreamDequeueAvoid` is 1 (the default).
4. With the drive plugged in and a file on it open (the browser running from it, for example), start HWMonitor,
   Speccy and HWiNFO (its SMART reading on, as used) three times each, one after another; on XP x64 and on 7 x64
   where both are used.
5. Say whether the drive disappeared or Windows showed "Delayed Write Failed", whether any program stopped
   responding or ended by itself, and whether a large file copied to the drive and back compares equal
   (`fc /b`).
6. Take a Quick save in the USB Tree after the last start and send the folder. If the drive still disappears,
   `XhciStreamDequeueAvoid` 0 brings back the `3.5.0.0` behaviour, and `XhciForceBulkOnly` 1 stays the way round
   it.

What the Quick save is read for, in order:

- the "Linux quirks" block's last row: `XhciStreamDequeueAvoid` "read 1 (as read): mode 1, the listed
  controllers; id listed; policy on", and `StreamDeqUntrusted` 1;
- `StreamContractOpens` 3 and the `usbdx.contract` notes (the UAS driver took the recovery on all three
  endpoints);
- `StreamDebts` with `cfg.debt.raise` and `cfg.debt.release` in pairs, at most one RESET_PIPE per refused
  request, `cfg.recycle.refused` absent or followed by a device reset;
- `StreamDeqWithheld` 0 (anything else is a defect of the design), `StreamDeqGiveUps` and `StreamDeqChecked` 0, no
  `cfg.deq.giveup` or `cfg.deq.cycle`, no port on hold, `CyclesRefused` 0, "QEMU stream-context quirk" absent, and
  in the stream trace no Set TR Dequeue Pointer command naming a stream but an Error exit's (`cfg.deq.errorexit`);
- the drive's record: time-outs 0, no "the drive answered but its data never arrived", the failure ring holding
  the programs' refusals (sense 5/20/00) and, around a device reset, BUS_RESET endings only; port resets only where
  a refusal met other commands in flight or a RESET_PIPE failed (a refused Configure, a failed clear, an
  endpoint in Error);
- no Babble on a streams endpoint, and no `xfer.unmatched` whose TRB lies in a completed TD of the same stream.

Only this reading can show that the Intel 7 Series controller itself, given no stream Set TR Dequeue and fresh
contexts, no longer misplaces a stream.

### Cleanup

All of these legs' emulators were stopped by their own process id (every start and stop is in the leg folder's
`pids.txt`; no guest is running). Deleted: every overlay (system disk and drive images), every leg's transfer
folder and both kits - which held the third-party programs, HWMonitor 1.62, Speccy 1.32 and HWiNFO64 6.43 build
4380 - and the programs' originals in the scratch and VM folders; none of them was run on the host or tracked.
Kept: each leg's serial logs (with every report), the driver's debug-port trace, QEMU's own log, the screenshots,
the command lines and the leg logs; the leg scripts and the kit's batch files; the emulator builds `emu50e` and
`emu50f` (their sources are uncommitted changes in the usb4-emu worktree `w50-hwm`, as a patch with the
scratch files).

## 50.20 (continued, 2) 98 SE and 2000 against the emulator's model of the fault, and a stop with a recovery outstanding (2026-11-19 and 20)

Guest legs only; no code changed. What "50.20 (continued)" left for an emulator: the 98 SE and 2000 legs, and a
stop with a recovery outstanding. The reporter's reading of a build stays the one reading of the field controller.

### The build under test, the guests and the emulator

- **The build.** The gated x86 build of `779c6a5d2` (branch `3.5.1.0`; no file under `src\` other than Stor98's
  differs from the tip `9747cd96f`), left by the 50.35 and 50.36 legs in their worktree: its records
  `out\gated-x86-qemu.txt` (`xhci98.sys` `783EF699...`, `xhciuas.sys` `ECDABE5D...`) and `gated-x86-release.txt`
  (`87F5EDCE...`, `3046918B...`), `dirty=0`; the files used were checked against them by hash. The `qemu` flavour is
  the one under test (fault 33 makes the emulator's controller count as listed; fault 35 is the rendezvous).
- **How it was installed.** No package of that build existed and this tree's installer takes release-flavour drivers
  only, so each guest has the published `3.5.0.0` installed by its Setup (`INSTALL /console /yes /nopause`; 98 SE
  with `/storage` for NUSB 3.3's seven storage files from the `3.5.0.0` download, both without Stor98), the UAS drive
  installed once by Windows' New Hardware wizard (`xhciuas.inf`), and then the tip's `qemu` `xhci98.sys` and
  `xhciuas.sys` put over the installed files and every copy a later install could take them from (98 SE through
  `WININIT.INI` at the next start; 2000 by copying, as the XP x64 legs' swap). The INF the tip adds three values to
  (`XhciCancelStatus`, `XhciUnplugComplete`, `XhciStreamDequeueAvoid`, each written at 1) is `3.5.0.0`'s here, so the
  first two are absent and read as their default 1; `XhciStreamDequeueAvoid` is written for each leg (below). The
  first report of every run on the tip's files (all but the `3.5.0.0` runs below, and the starts that stalled before
  any report) shows them installed (`xhci98.sys` 542539 bytes, `xhciuas.sys` 47712) and the `qemu` flavour running:
  `qemu.inj.latched` with the start's fault 33 value, or `FFFFFFFF` at value 2, which has none, and at values 1 and 0
  `qemu.inj.streamflag`.
- **Guests.** The q35 bases of 98 SE and 2000 SP4, one processor, TCG. One prepared image each (the install, the
  drive, the swap; a read-only layer), one layer per value of `XhciStreamDequeueAvoid` on it (read-only), and a fresh
  overlay of the layer for every run; 98 SE cold starts only.
- **Emulator.** usb4-emu test build `emu25c` (`qemu-system-x86_64.exe` `aaf9768b...`; "50.25" above): the model of
  "50.20 (continued)" - `qemu-xhci x-stream-setdeq-current`, `x-stream-setdeq-keep`, `x-stream-dcs` - with `usb-uas
  x-clear-halt` and `x-ata-passthrough-refuse`, plus 50.25's `usb-uas x-refuse-rw-every=N` and its fix of
  `usb-uas`'s cancel of a live request. QEMU's own trace events `usb_xhci_ep_set_dequeue`, `usb_xhci_ep_stop` and
  `usb_xhci_ep_reset` went to its log, so every Set TR Dequeue Pointer the driver sent is counted from the
  emulator's side, with its stream ID.
- **The drive.** `usb-uas` with a 128 MB FAT16 `scsi-hd` holding 16 reference files of 1 MiB, attached on
  `xh.0` port 4 by its QOM `attached` property 30 s after the guest said it was ready (a fresh overlay per run).
- **The trigger.** The monitoring programs of the XP x64 legs have no 98 SE or 2000 build, so the refusal came from
  two places: once per run the field's kind - ATA PASS-THROUGH (16) IDENTIFY with its data-in posted, refused 5/20/00
  by `x-ata-passthrough-refuse` (98 SE: `ASPI9X.EXE` through Windows 98's ASPI; 2000: `ATATEST.EXE` on E:; both from
  `test\atatest`, built for the leg); and throughout, `x-refuse-rw-every=64`: every 64th READ or WRITE refused at once
  with UNIT ATTENTION 6/29/00 and its data packet left pending, so the host cancels a TD on a stream, as at a
  monitoring program's refusal, and the class driver retries the command.
- **The values** (machine-wide `Services\USB`, read at each start), as the XP x64 legs had them:

| Layer | `XhciStreamDequeueAvoid` | Fault 33 (`XhciQemuInject` at the start) | So |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1 (the default) | `01210001`: the controller counted as listed, as `8086:1E31` is (XA1, XS1) | flagged; the contract |
| 0 | 0 | `01210003`: counted as listed, QEMU's resync off (XS0) | unflagged: `3.5.0.0`'s check and cycle, so the model can bite |
| 2 | 2 | none: QEMU's controller is not listed (XS2) | flagged by the value alone |

- **A run.** A cold start; a report (`XHCITR /report`, as the Quick save takes it) once the drive is there; the ATA
  trigger; a report; then 98 SE: ten rounds, each a 16 MiB copy to the drive compared there, copied back and compared
  again, then the 16 reference files compared with their originals; 2000: at once, 30 such copy-compare rounds, a
  reader of the reference files round after round, and a writer holding `E:\OPEN.TXT` open and appending a line every
  2 s, compared at the end with its own copy; then the last report. **The 98 SE clock**: in leg 1 the guest's
  `GetTickCount` was read at the start, when the drive came and at every round, against host time (COM1 lines
  stamped on the host as they arrived; the table's column): no leg-1 98 SE start was in the slow state; all ran at
  host rate except r98v1-6 to -8, whose clock ran at 0.40 to 0.89 of host rate over their first rounds, when the host
  was at its busiest, and at host rate after (the table's footnote); r98v2-3 stalled before its first reading. The
  leg-2 98 SE scripts read the clock less: there the reading is how long one fixed wait at the start took in host
  time - L2a-98e's 70 s wait took 78 s (host rate over that interval only; its later clock reads were saved to files
  and sent to COM1 together, so their arrival times say nothing), L2a-98d's 209 s (the slow state, about 0.33: void).

  DCI 7 for a READ, DCI 8 for a WRITE) and every debt was released, almost all by xhciuas's RESET_PIPE recycle
  (`cfg.debt.release` `...0001`), on 2000 one to three a run by a device reset's replay (`...0101`, a refusal while
  other commands ran; port resets 1 to 3); no give-up, no cycle, no hold, no time-out; the drive kept (E: present to
  the end, no Unsafe Removal box, no Delayed Write Failed); every copy-compare and reference compare equal, the open
  file kept and equal. **No Set TR Dequeue Pointer naming a stream**, by QEMU's own trace and by the driver's: the
  only three commands of each run name stream 0 - one per endpoint at the streams open, before the contract is
  acknowledged (each after a Stop Endpoint on DCI 5, 7 and 8); **no model load**; `StreamDeqWithheld` 0.
- **Value 0, the control**: no contract (no `usbdx.contract`, `qemu.inj.streamflag` 1: resync off, unflagged); each
  cancel sent its stream Set TR Dequeue (QEMU: naming a stream), the model loaded it into the current stream's cached
  state, and 4.12.8's c2 found the misplaced position: on 2000 the drive given up and cycled (`StreamDeqGiveUps`,
  `StreamDeqUnplaced`, `cfg.deq.cycle`; Windows' "Unsafe Removal of Device" for xHCI98 USB Attached SCSI Storage and
  "Delayed Write Failed ... T.BIN. The data has been lost"; after the cycles the port on hold, every later copy
  failed, the open file lost), on 98 SE the debug port's "hcd: cycling port, location=00000004". In five of the six
  control runs the guest then stopped (2000: keys not taken, COM1 and the xHCI interrupt no longer counted, the
  processor halted; 98 SE: the clock stopped, the xHCI interrupt no longer counted, the processor in the VMM or a DOS
  box; r98v0-1 stopped after the model's second load with no cycle seen, EIP `c000a881`), as XB1 and XC1 did on XP
  x64 after a cycle with the model on; those runs were ended by hand once the evidence was taken (`hang-info.txt` in
  each run's folder). The control shows the model biting; the stops after it are on `3.5.0.0`'s path with the model
  on, as on XP x64 ("50.20 (continued)", "What the emulator's model can and cannot show"), and say nothing of the
  contract path.
- **The 98 SE stall at value 1 (r98v1-2): not placed.** In round 1 of r98v1-2, during the reference reads, the
  guest stopped at 19:47:04: the taskbar clock frozen, the processor busy in the VMM (five samples, ring 0, no HLT,

  completed when the guest stopped**: its Stop Endpoint is the last thing in QEMU's trace, and nothing of the driver

  stall; (4) the tip at value 1 with the model off (r98v1n-1): as
  r98v1-1; (5) three more value-1 runs with the model on (r98v1-6 to -8): each as r98v1-1 - 147 refusals, 149
  recoveries completed, every compare equal. After r98v1-2, nine runs at values 1 and 2 on 98 SE (eight with the
  model on) ran to their end with no stall. Left open: a 98 SE stall with a contract recovery unfinished, once in

### Leg 2: a stop with a recovery outstanding

**What it is meant to show, and the expectations, written before the first leg-2 run** (scratch
`leg2-expected.md`, 2026-11-19 19:25, kept unchanged): the stop is asked while xhciuas's recovery is under way - its
obligation set and its RESET_PIPE held between the device's clear and the recycle by rendezvous point 2 - and:

- E1: the trigger's refusal - an ATA PASS-THROUGH ended CHECK CONDITION 5/20/00 with its data-in posted -
  `cfg.debt.raise` for slot 1 DCI 7, and `qemu.inj.rv.reached` with point 2;
- E2: the stop asked while held does not finish while held;
- E3: after the release either the recycle completes first (`cfg.debt.release` for DCI 7) and the stop then runs as
  an ordinary stop, or the stop's teardown retires the endpoint object with its debt, which ends with it (no
  release note); either way no stream Set TR Dequeue, no model load, `StreamDeqWithheld` 0, no controller reset, no
  cycle;
- E4: the stop completes and nothing is left pending (the eject reports the drive stopped, the trigger program ends,
  the guest stays responsive, no request of the drive outstanding in the bus);
- E5: no fault;
- E6: after a replug the drive enumerates at SuperSpeed, its streams open with the contract again
  (`StreamContractOpens` +3), the trigger is refused again and recovered by a recycle, and the drive answers: on 2000
  `PTCANCEL`'s 8 READ(10)s all complete with SCSI status 0, on 98 SE `ASPI9X`'s INQUIRY completes;
- 2b, in addition: at the stop's drop, the endpoint the emulator left in Error takes the Error exit - one Set TR
  Dequeue per stream on that endpoint only, `cfg.deq.errorexit` per stream, `StreamErrorExits` counting them, then
  the Drop.

**How the stop was made.** The XP x64 legs could not make it: Windows refuses a removal while a program has the disk
open, and every trigger there was such a program. Here: the drive has no file system (a blank 64 MB disk), so no
volume is mounted; the stop is the USB Tree's own `XHCITR /eject id=<the drive's USB instance id>` (query-remove,
then remove); and two traps found on the way decided the order. (1) The eject first reads the tree through the
driver, which a held controller thread answers only after the hold: started inside the hold (L2a-2kb), its
confirmation appeared only once the hold had run out its 60 s (`qemu.inj.rv.released=00020258`). So the eject is
started first and its confirmation left on screen. (2) A trigger program that keeps the disk open is the XP x64
legs' veto again: with `ATATEST` (its next ATA request waits behind the recovery), Windows answered "xHCI98 USB
Attached SCSI Storage is in use (a program has a file or folder open on it)" (L2a-2ke). So the trigger is
`PTCANCEL`'s single pass-through READ(10) with `usb-uas x-refuse-rw-every=2`, run until one READ comes back refused
(CHECK CONDITION, `scsi=02`): the program has then ended and closed the disk. The confirmation is answered from
inside the guest (a VBScript's `SendKeys`, 1 s after the refusal), because the host's keys were arriving 15 to 20 s
late under the host's load (L2a-2kc). The release (fault 23 arg 0) comes 30 s (2a) or 55 s (2b) after the trigger.
A Device Manager-style disable (`DC.EXE disable`, SetupAPI) asked during the hold never reached the drive: no
query-remove at its PDO, the device still running afterwards (L2a-2kd); not used.

| Run | System | What was read | Against the expectations |
|---|---|---|---|
| L2a-2kf | 2000 | Notes in order: `cfg.debt.raise=01070102` (the refused READ's data-in TD taken off) -> `qemu.inj.rv.reached=00020001` -> `pnp.pdo=00040104` (IRP_MN_QUERY_REMOVE_DEVICE at the drive's PDO, while held) -> `qemu.inj.rv.released=0002012E` (30.2 s, the release) -> `cfg.debt.release=01070001` (the recycle, after the release) -> `pnp.pdo=00040204` (IRP_MN_REMOVE_DEVICE); debug port: minor 1, then the held RESET_PIPE's "thread URB done, function/status=1E000000", then minor 2. The USB Tree: "Windows has stopped QEMU QEMU HARDDISK UAS Device. You can now unplug the device."; `DC list`: problem 24 (stopped, waiting to be unplugged). No stream Set TR Dequeue (QEMU's trace: every one names stream 0), no model load, no time-out, no controller reset, no cycle. Replug (QOM `attached` false, then true about 30 s later): SuperSpeed, `StreamContractOpens` 6, `PTCANCEL`'s 8 READs all completed (4 with data, 4 refused by `x-refuse-rw-every=2`, each recovered by a recycle) | E1 changed: the trigger is a READ refused 6/29/00, not the ATA refusal (the ATA trigger program kept the disk open, L2a-2ke); its debt on DCI 7 and the point reached as expected. **98 SE: the stop asked inside the hold was refused by Windows 98, because the trigger's next request was waiting
behind the recovery; a stop with the recovery owed and nothing waiting above it was not made.** On the reference drive
(FAT16 E:, no file open on it), with rendezvous point 2 armed, the eject's confirmation on screen with the focus
(the window that started it waits on it), the trigger `ASPI9X` (its ATA PASS-THROUGH (16) refused) and the release
55 s later in windows of their own, the confirmation answered inside the hold (L2a-98e: the trigger at about
22:15:25, OK at 22:15:46, the hold's release window still open): "Windows refused: E: is in use. A program may have
a file open on it, or a DOS box may be using it." `ASPI9X`'s next request (A3) waits behind the recovery, so the
drive is busy when the query-remove comes, and 98 SE's own storage stack vetoes it, as XP x64 and 2000 veto a stop
while a program has the disk open. Notes: `cfg.debt.raise=01070102` -> `rv.reached=00020001` -> no `pnp.pdo` (the
query-remove never reached the drive's PDO) -> `rv.released=00020207` (51.9 s) -> `cfg.debt.release=01070001` (the
recycle); `ASPI9X`: "A3 ATA12 SMART READ DATA: no answer in 10 s, abort sent; waiting", then "ended status=04"
after the release. After the replug: contract opens again, `ASPI9X` answered (its A1 refused again and recovered by
a recycle), the 16 reference files compared equal; no stream Set TR Dequeue, no model load, no fault. Against the
expectations: E1 as expected (the ATA refusal, DCI 7, point 2); the stop refused, so E2 to E4 are not read on
98 SE; E5 and E6 as expected for this run. Earlier tries, none of them a reading of the stop:
L2a-98 (the blank drive; a fatal exception 0E "at 0028:C1CC95B6 in VXD APIX(03) + 00000326" while the trigger ran,
which the host's Enter meant for the confirmation dismissed instead; the eject, confirmed after the release, was
refused "in use"; the guest did not then shut down and was ended); L2a-98b (the confirmation without the focus, so
the Enter went to the DOS window and the eject was confirmed after the release: "Windows has stopped QEMU QEMU
HARDDISK (E:)"); L2a-98c (the 98 SE start stall, before the drive); L2a-98d (the guest's millisecond clock in the
slow state, the 70 s wait taking 209 s: void for a timed leg). Two side checks of the APIX fault: the eject alone on
the blank drive (X98raw) and `ASPI9X` held 50 s by the rendezvous on the reference drive with no eject (X98h50:
"A3 ... no answer in 10 s, abort sent; waiting", then "ended status=04" after the release; X98h05, held 5 s: every
request answered): no fault in either, so the fault is seen once and its cause is not read.

### What these legs show, and what they do not

- **98 SE and 2000 on the contract path.** On both systems `xhciuas.sys` declared the recovery at the streams open,
  the bus acknowledged it on all three endpoints, and with the controller counted as listed (value 1) or every
  controller flagged (value 2) the driver sent no Set TR Dequeue Pointer naming a stream - by the emulator's own
  trace, over 6 runs of 2000 and 11 model-on runs of 98 SE (and one with the model off), with 51 to 147
  refusals of the emulator's each - so the model never loaded anything. In every run that ran to its end every
  refusal ended in an endpoint recycle (on 2000 a few in a device reset, a refusal while other commands ran), the
  drive was kept and every compare equal; r98v1-2 stalled with its last recovery unfinished (above). The control
  (value 0) shows the same model biting on both systems, as on XP x64.
- **A stop with a recovery outstanding.** On 2000 it was made: a stop asked while the recycle was held waited for it,
  the recycle completed first, then the stop ran to its end; with the status endpoint left in Error at the stop, the
  stop's abort held it without a command and the debt ended with the device's record; nothing left pending, no fault,
  the drive working after a replug. On 98 SE the one reading is a refusal: with the trigger program's next request
  waiting behind the recovery, Windows 98 refused the stop ("E: is in use"); the recovery then completed and the
  drive worked. With nothing above the drive waiting on it (S98a, below), the 98 SE stop waited for the recovery
  and then completed, as on 2000.
- **What they do not show.** Only the field controller can show that the Intel 7 Series controller, given no stream
  Set TR Dequeue and fresh contexts, no longer misplaces a stream ("50.20 (continued)"). The Error exit (a DROP of an
  endpoint in Error) is still read on XP x64 alone (XEE3): no stop here dropped an endpoint in Error. The trigger on
  98 SE and 2000 is the emulator's refusal of reads and writes and one ATA PASS-THROUGH per start, not a monitoring
  program; no 98 SE or 2000 build of the field's programs was run. Timing: the clock coverage is as in "A run"
  above; one 98 SE start (L2a-98d) was in the slow state and is void.
- **98 SE stalls.** Eight 98 SE starts stalled with the processor in the VMM or a DOS box: on the tip's files
  r98v1-2 (round 1, value 1, its last recovery unfinished), r98v2-3 and L2a-98c (at the start, no drive), r98v0-1
  (control, after the model's second load, no cycle seen), r98v0-2 and r98v0-3 (control, after the cycle); on
  `3.5.0.0`'s with the model on, r98vR-4 and r98vR-5 (round 1). r98vR-6 was not a stall but an abort of QEMU's
  `usb-uas`. r98v1-2, r98v2-3, L2a-98c and r98vR-5 at or near the addresses of 49.36's bare 98 SE stalls; see "The
  98 SE stall at value 1 (r98v1-2): not placed" above, and "The r98v1-2 stall, placed by count" below (one more
  mid-run stall, s2v03r, and three start wedges).

### The r98v1-2 stall, placed by count (the owner's decision of 2026-11-19: the row waits for this reading)

**Method, fixed before the first run** (`E:\xhci98-vm\p50\sdq\STATE.md`, 23:35).
- **The guest.** The 98 SE image prepared again as above (the first one was deleted at the cleanup): the published
  `3.5.0.0` with NUSB 3.3's storage files, the drive's driver installed by its wizard, the tip's `qemu` `xhci98.sys`
  and `xhciuas.sys` put in by `WININIT.INI`, and the value layer folded into the image: `XhciStreamDequeueAvoid` 1,
  fault 33 arg 1, and `XhciQemuStageFault` 8, the `qemu` flavour's per-request log: every URB that reaches a device
  PDO is written to the debug console as it arrives and as it is completed, with its IRP, so an unfinished request
  is visible as an "in" with no "out". A fresh overlay per run, cold starts only.
- **More trace.** QEMU's trace events, time-stamped (`-msg timestamp=on`): the xHCI interrupt line
  (`usb_xhci_irq_intx`), every event queued (`usb_xhci_queue_event`), every runtime-register write (IMAN and ERDP:
  the driver's acknowledgement of an interrupt and of the events it consumed), the doorbells (`usb_xhci_ep_kick`),
  the commands (slot enable, disable, address, configure, evaluate, reset; endpoint enable, disable, stop, reset,
  Set TR Dequeue) and port resets.
- **V runs** (value 1, the model on): as r98v1-1 - the drive with `x-ata-passthrough-refuse` and
  `x-refuse-rw-every=64`, ASPI9X's ATA refusal, ten copy-compare and reference rounds, reports.
- **C runs** (the control): the same image, the same steps and load, with no drive and the model off: the rounds
  copy to `C:\SDQ\W` and compare there (the guest's own disk), ASPI9X finds no device.
- **Interleaved** V and C on three slots; the stop rule: 20 V and 20 C runs that are not void, or two captured
  mid-run V stalls first (C then to the same count). Why 20: at the rate seen before (1 stall in 11 V runs) 20 runs
  catch it again with 85 % probability; 20 C runs give the bare rate of a mid-run stall on this host tonight at the
  same exposure.
- **A stall** (COM1 silent for 300 s before the end): the harness takes, before anything else, two screens about 130
  s apart (does the taskbar clock move; 72 s for a start wedge), 20 register samples, the PIC and interrupt counts
  twice, the stack words at the sampled ESP, the debug console's and QEMU's log tails, and the image ranges
  (`imgrange.py`: from the counter block the `qemu` flavour prints, the controller's `DEVICE_OBJECT` and its
  `DRIVER_OBJECT`, whose `DriverUnload` bytes are found once in this build's own file, so the base is exact; and the
  same through the drive's PDO for `xhciuas.sys`). Measured live in two runs: `xhci98.sys` at FF03EAC0-FF0B7DFF,
  `xhciuas.sys` at FF0B8220-FF0C2A7F, the same in both. A start that never reaches the batch (mewedge's 9x logon
  wedge on this host, run-50 "50.34 follow-up") is void, recorded and run again.

**The count** (2026-11-19 23:57 to 2026-11-20 04:52, three slots; evidence `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\sdq\s2v*`, `s2c*`).

| | V: value 1, the model on, the drive | C: no drive, the model off |
|---|---|---|
| starts | 22 | 21 |
| void: a start that never reached the batch | 2 (s2v03, s2v09) | 1 (s2c16) |
| counted | 20 | 20 |
| ran to their end | 19 | 20 |
| stalled in mid-run | **1 (s2v03r)** | **0** |
| compares equal (runs that ended) | 20 of 20 each, 160 reference compares each, none unequal | the same |
| emulator refusals (runs that ended) | 147 or 148 each | - |
| recycles completed (debug port) | the refusals + 2 (the two ATA refusals) in every run | - |
| stream Set TR Dequeue; model loads | 0; 0 (3 Set TR Dequeues per run, none naming a stream) | 0; 0 |

- **The start wedges** (void): all three alike - the batch's DOS window open and blank with the hourglass, nothing
  on COM1, the taskbar clock frozen across the two screens 72 s apart while the timer interrupt went on being
  counted (about 200 a second), every register sample in the VMM (`c00036a3` to `c0003712`, `c000a4d8` to
  `c000a882`; s2c16 mostly `c005335e`, one of 49.36's addresses), none in either driver. The drive is plugged only
  after the batch's first line, so none of them had one; two V and one C - not a V-only matter.
- **s2v03r, the stall.** Round 1, during the reference compares (the window "SDQ - FC"; the last COM1 line "===R 01
  BACK SAME" at 04:19:43) - the same phase as r98v1-2.
  - *The recovery and its step.* The emulator's 49th refusal (a READ, tag 9, stream 9, sense 6/29/00) came at
    04:20:13.837, 0.6 s after the 48th's recycle had ended (its Stop Endpoint at 13.201, the endpoint recycled at
    13.215). For it the emulator queued the command pipe's completion and the status pipe's (the sense); the driver
    took the interrupt and acknowledged both (IMAN, then ERDP past them), and its per-request log shows the command
    and status requests completed. The data-in request on DCI 7, stream 9 never completed. After it: **no Stop
    Endpoint** (the 48th's was the last), no command, no doorbell - nothing more reached the controller after
    04:20:13.838, and the emulator owed nothing (no event queued after the driver's last acknowledgement; the
    controller's interrupt line, IRQ 10, shared with the SATA and SMBus functions, counted no further during the
    capture). xhciuas cancels the data transfer in its stream recovery and waits for it; xhci98's cancel routine
    only marks the transfer and wakes the controller thread, which sends the Stop Endpoint (`src\hcd_io.c`,
    `hcdCancel`) - and the thread never did. xhciuas went on by its own clock (`src\uas\uas_xport.c`): its stream
    recovery's wait (at most 5 s) ended in a device reset, which waits up to 5 s more for every transfer to come
    back (`uasWaitAllFree`, 500 sleeps of 10 ms); none came back, so no RESET_PORT was sent, the drive was marked
    dead and a cycle asked of the bus - the debug console's last line, "hcd: uas resume state, op/value=04000000"
    (the CYCLE op; xhci98 answered it and woke the thread), and the thread did nothing with that either (no port
    reset in QEMU's trace). So at least 5 s after the refusal the guest was still running xhciuas's worker on timed
    sleeps, while xhci98's controller thread had done nothing since the 48th recycle.
  - *The guest.* The taskbar clock reads 4:20 AM in all three screens (the harness's periodic one at 04:23:20, the
    capture's at 04:25:30 and 04:27:42): frozen, within the minute of the refusal. The timer interrupt went on being
    counted (116246, 118653, 142657 over 132 s); 20 register samples all in the VMM (`c0003621` to `c0003712`,
    `c000a4d8` to `c000abd9`, `c00514a1`, `c00535a5`, `c00535f4`) but one at `00000204`; none in `xhci98.sys`
    (FF03EAC0-FF0B7DFF, measured in this run) or `xhciuas.sys`.
- **Reading.** The stall's first visible failure is the driver's: xhci98's controller thread did not act on a cancel
  that came 0.6 s after it had finished the previous recycle, nor on the cycle asked 5 to 10 s later, while the rest
  of the guest still ran; the freeze of the whole guest followed within the minute, which fits Windows 98's file
  system waiting on the reference read that never completed. r98v1-2 is consistent with the same picture one step
  later (its Stop Endpoint was sent, its recycle never completed). Why the thread did not run its pass - a lost
  wake, a wait it never left, or the VMM not scheduling it - is not in these files: the register samples were all
  elsewhere, and the thread's own state was not read before the guest was ended. The VMM addresses are shared with
  the start wedges and with 49.36's bare stalls, so they mark where a waiting 98 SE guest idles, not a cause. By
  count alone the control does not separate (1 of 20 against 0 of 20); over this and the first count, 2 of 31
  model-on runs at values 1 and 2 stalled, both in round 1 with a recovery unfinished, and none of this count's 20
  controls stalled in mid-run.
- **Not settled, and what would settle it:** the thread's state at the stall - its wait object and whether its wake
  was signalled - read live from the guest's memory (the `qemu` flavour prints the address of its counter block,
  inside the controller's device extension) when the next one is caught.
- **Slips.** The harness's log followers (one Python poller per run, reading COM1's file every 0.2 s) were never
  told to stop - its stop-file name was a pattern that matched nothing - so up to about 36 of them ran beside the
  guests until their own 4-hour limit or until stopped by process id at 04:12; fixed then, and every run that ended
  after that stopped its own. Host load was higher than it needed to be during the count, which the clock column
  above covers.

### Leg 2 on 98 SE: the stop with a recovery outstanding and nothing waiting on the drive (S98a, 2026-11-20)

The case left owed above. The drive has no file system (the blank disk), so no volume holds it, and the trigger is
`ASPI1.EXE`: ASPI9X's source with its A3 and A4 requests left out (scratch only, `tools\atatest\aspi1.c`; it prints
under ASPI9X's own name), which sends one ATA PASS-THROUGH (16), takes its refusal and ends - nothing above the
drive waits on it. The image is the stall-placement image (value 1, fault 33 arg 1), the model on, kit10: rendezvous
point 2 armed, the eject started in this window with `start /w` so that its confirmation has the focus, the trigger
and a 55 s release in windows of their own 30 s later, the host's Enter 33 s after the eject marker.
- **Read.** ASPI1's A1 ended CHECK CONDITION 5/20/00 and the program ended ("done"; at 00:24:22 its window is gone
  from the taskbar while the release window is still there, `S98a\h-ok.png`). The confirmation was answered at
  00:24:04. Notes in order: `cfg.debt.raise=01070102` -> `qemu.inj.rv.reached=00020001` -> `pnp.pdo=00040104`
  (IRP_MN_QUERY_REMOVE_DEVICE at the drive's PDO, while held) -> `qemu.inj.rv.released=00020258` (the point's own 60
  s bound: the release window's 55 s, a background DOS window's wait, ran longer) -> `cfg.debt.release=01070001`
  (the recycle, after it) -> `pnp.pdo=00040204` (IRP_MN_REMOVE_DEVICE). The USB Tree: "Windows has stopped QEMU QEMU
  HARDDISK. You can now unplug the device." (`h-res.png`). No stream Set TR Dequeue (QEMU's trace), no model load,
  no fault. After the replug (QOM `attached` false, then true): `StreamContractOpens` 6, ASPI9X answered (INQUIRY
  good; A1, A3 and A4 refused 5/20/00, a new start's first refusal and xhciuas's own answers after it).
- **Against the expectations:** E1 (the ATA refusal, DCI 7, point 2), E2 (the query-remove came while held; the
  removal finished only after the recovery), E3 (its first form), E4, E5 and E6 as expected. So on 98 SE, as on
  2000, a stop asked while the recovery is held waits for the recovery and then completes.

### Side findings (not this task's to fix)

- **A fatal exception in APIX on 98 SE, once.** L2a-98 (leg 2, the blank drive): "A fatal exception 0E has occurred
  at 0028:C1CC95B6 in VXD APIX(03) + 00000326. The current application will be terminated." while `ASPI9X` ran with
  its drive's recovery held by the rendezvous and the USB Tree's eject confirmation open; the guest did not shut
  down afterwards. Not reproduced by the eject alone (X98raw) or by `ASPI9X` held 50 s with no eject (X98h50, on
  the reference drive). Seen once; the cause is not read. Evidence: `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\sdq\L2a-98\h-box.png`.
- **The USB Tree's eject waits on the driver before it asks.** `XHCITR /eject` reads the tree through the
  controller's door first, so while the controller thread is held (a rendezvous here; a stalled command in life) its
  confirmation does not appear until the thread answers (L2a-2kb: 60 s). Another reading, from elsewhere in this
  phase and not checked here: the installed `3.5.0.0` tray's hold watch uses the snapshot pass-through every
  10 s and keeps the door gate while it waits for the controller thread - the likely reason the confirmation came
  only after the hold.

## 50.38 98 SE: the stall in 50.20's legs, read live (2026-11-20)

Guest legs and a source reading only; no code changed, nothing built. What "The r98v1-2 stall, placed by count" left:
why the stall's recovery did not finish - in `s2v03r` xHCI98's controller thread sent no Stop Endpoint for a cancelled
stream transfer - read from the guest's memory while it is stalled.

### The thread's wake and wait, from the source (the build under test, `779c6a5d2`)

- **The wait.** The controller thread (`src\hcd_ctl.c`, `hcdThread`) waits on its work event with a 100 ms time-out
  (`HCD_POLL_MS`), then runs one pass: `hcdPoll` (the `qemu` flavour's fault poll, the health poll, the counters, the
  recovery and containment steps), then, under the power gate, `HcdEnumService`, then the log flush. The work event is
  a synchronization event; `HcdThreadWake` sets it and only that wait consumes it. So a missed wake alone cannot keep
  the thread idle: with or without it, the wait ends after 100 ms and a pass starts, provided the thread is scheduled
  and its previous pass has returned (this bounds the idle wait, not a pass's length).
- **The cancel's work.** The cancel routine (`src\hcd_io.c`, `hcdCancel`) marks the transfer, its pipe's
  `CancelPending` and the controller's `CancelWork` under the controller lock, then wakes the thread. The pass's
  `HcdCfgCancelService` (`src\hcd_cfg.c`) takes and clears `CancelWork` under the same lock and walks every pipe and
  stream with a mark; it runs in `HcdEnumService` whenever the controller is powered and not halted
  (`ControllerFailed` or `ScratchTainted`). So a marked cancel is acted on at the next pass that gets that far.
- **So a thread that ignores a cancel for seconds** either does not get through its pass (blocked inside it), or
  passes with the cancel service gated off (unpowered, halted). The second leaves traces this harness reads (a failed
  or tainted controller starts a recovery, which the debug port and QEMU's trace show; a power change runs through the
  power gate), and none was seen in `s2v03r`.
- **Where a pass can block** (unbounded waits and calls into other code, from the source): the power gate
  (`HcdPowerGateEnter`: a wait with no time-out, its bound counting only Windows 98's odd early returns), held by
  other parties too - the door's snapshot (`hcd_door.c`, `hcdDoorSnapshot`, the USB Tree's and the tray's reads), the
  power paths, the `qemu` flavour's hardware faults; the waits for a pipe's cancelled records to be freed (`hcd_io.c`,
  `hcdWaitCancelledOne` with no budget, through `HcdIoPipeWaitCancelled` from the endpoint work of `hcd_cfg.c` -
  `hcdCfgAbortPaused`, so the aborts and the RESET_PIPE recycle's `hcdCfgReset` when it resets the host side with
  transfers still busy, `hcdCfgRecoverDequeue`, `HcdCfgResumeSettle`: 1 ms sleeps and a completion pass until every
  cancelled record is free) and for a pipe's records before it is freed (`hcdWaitPipeOne`, at a pipe's or the streams'
  close); pool and IRP allocations made by the pass; the `qemu` flavour's once-a-second registry read (`hcd_inj.c`,
  `HcdInjPoll` -> `HcdCtlQemuReadDword`: `RtlQueryRegistryValues` on the machine-wide key, and on 98 and ME
  `IoOpenDeviceRegistryKey` on the driver key when the value is not machine-wide - here it is); and every IRP the
  thread completes itself: `HcdIoDeferred` from the thread, `hcdCfgComplete` (every URB the thread serves: RESET_PIPE
  among them) and the streams requests complete at PASSIVE_LEVEL, so the client's completion routine, and on Windows
  98 whatever the storage stack above starts from it, runs on the controller thread. `hcdCfgComplete` prints "thread
  URB done" and the per-URB log's "out" line before it calls `IoCompleteRequest`, so neither line says the completion
  returned.

### The live reading: how

- **The guest and the run.** The 98 SE image prepared a third time as in "The r98v1-2 stall, placed by count" (the
  published `3.5.0.0`, the drive's driver by its wizard, the `qemu` `xhci98.sys` `783EF699...` and `xhciuas.sys`
  `ECDABE5D...` of `779c6a5d2` put in by `WININIT.INI`; the images were the same build as the counts before,
  `XhciStreamDequeueAvoid` 1, fault 33 arg 1, `XhciQemuStageFault` 8); the same V run (the model on,
  `x-ata-passthrough-refuse`, `x-refuse-rw-every=64`, ten copy-compare and reference rounds); QEMU's trace as there,
  plus the runtime-register reads, among them the MFINDEX read the health poll makes on every pass of the controller
  thread - so the trace shows whether the thread is still passing.
- **At a stall** (COM1 silent for 300 s), before the capture: the controller's record read from guest memory twice, 20
  s apart, as data (from the counter block whose address the `qemu` flavour prints; the field offsets from this
  build's own compiler listing, checked against the address printed): the pass counters (`CheckCallbacks`,
  `HealthPolls`), the flags that gate the pass, the work event, the power and door gates and the command event (an
  `NTKERN` event: its kind, the waiting thread, signalled or not), every pipe and stream with a mark, a pause or a
  debt; a 512 MB save of guest memory; the controller thread's stack found in it by `hcdThread`'s return addresses and
  its frame chain walked (each return address placed in a function by matching this build's compiler listings against
  its own `xhci98.sys`); the same for `xhciuas.sys`'s recovery worker; then the capture as before. Rehearsed on a
  healthy guest first: the thread's stack found once, at `hcdThread+2c` (its idle wait), `CheckCallbacks` about 10 a
  second.
- **The stop rule** (written before the first run, `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\sdq\STATE.md`, 2026-11-20 06:5x): V runs only,
  until a captured mid-run stall whose reading names where the thread is; an inconclusive first capture continues to a
  second; else 45 counted runs. Start wedges void, recorded and run again. The first capture (s4v15) showed the thread
  idle and the recovery stopped elsewhere (below): read as settling its own kind but not `s2v03r`'s, so the count went
  on to a second capture, which came at s4v23.

### The count

host's restart at 08:51 and are void. s4v01 to s4v03 started inside the host's slow window of 05:50 to 07:16 (new
processes started late: their drive came 66 to 76 s after the batch's first line instead of 30 s); their results are
as every other run's and they are counted.

| ran to their end | 19 |

- **s4v15** (round 1, the reference compares; the last COM1 line "===R 01 BACK SAME" at 08:17:40). The emulator's 32nd
  refusal (a READ, tag 9, sense 6/29/00) at 08:18:04.371, 0.9 s after the 31st's recycle (the endpoint recycled at
  03.521). This time the controller thread did its part: the Stop Endpoint on DCI 7 at 04.376, its events

    stack's frame chain ends at `hcdThread+2c`, the idle wait. No gate held (the power and door gates signalled), no
    flag, `CancelWork` 0. DCI 7: paused, with its 50.20 debt (`DeqDebt` 1: held for the client's recycle, record 17
    section 4.12.10), its 16 streams paused, nothing held or open.
  - *xhciuas's recovery worker: inside the allocation of the RESET_PIPE's IRP.* Its frame chain (return addresses as
    data): `uasRecoveryWorker+e1` -> `uasStreamRecover+8b` -> `uasResetPipe+43` -> `UasSyncUrb+15` ->
    `uasInternalIoctl+1a`, the return from `IoAllocateIrp`. By the source, `uasResetPipe` allocates its URB
    (`UasAlloc`) before that call, and no RESET_PIPE was logged by the bus driver, which logs every URB as it arrives.
    Below that frame, the stack holds words that fit the calls it is in (as data; which of them are live return
    addresses is not read): addresses just past the entry points xhciuas's import slots hold for `IoAllocateIrp` and
    `ExAllocatePoolWithTag`, the pool tag `Irp ` and the IRP's size `94h`, then addresses in the VMM's range
    (`c000cad2`, `c001519a`, `c001532f`, `c0013ea4`, `c00160e0`) beside a size `1000h` (a page). Consistent with an
    allocation that did not return inside the kernel; no RESET_PIPE reached the bus driver up to the end of the run.
- **s4v23** (round 1, the reference compares; "===R 01 BACK SAME" at 09:18:11): the same, word for word. The 34th
  refusal at 09:18:39.166, 1.2 s after the 33rd's recycle (37.940); the Stop Endpoint at 39.170, acknowledged; the
  data-in request cancelled; no RESET_PIPE (35 recycles completed). The clock stopped at 9:18 (the capture's screen at
  about 09:26); the timer interrupt counted on (114071 to 140484), the xHCI interrupt flat at 2521. The controller
  thread alive and idle (+194 and +195 in 20 s; MFINDEX reads every 100 ms to 09:26:23), at `hcdThread+2c`, no gate
  held, DCI 7 paused with its debt. The recovery worker at the same frame chain, inside `IoAllocateIrp`, the same `Irp
  `, `94h`, `1000h` and the same VMM addresses below it.

### Reading

- **Two kinds of the stall.** In both, a stream recovery of xhciuas's had begun: the refused READ's data transfer
  cancelled by xhciuas, which holds the drive's other requests until the recovery ends (`uas_xport.c`: the pump closed
  while `Recovering`). The read Windows 98 is waiting for is among what does not complete, and the whole guest stops
  within the minute (the taskbar clock, every program). They differ in how far the recovery got.
  - **Kind B** (read live in s4v15 and s4v23; r98v1-2 of the first count is compatible with it - its Stop Endpoint
    sent, its recycle never completed - but was not read live): the cancel was done (Stop Endpoint, the request
    completed as cancelled), the endpoint left paused with its debt waiting, as designed, for the client's RESET_PIPE;
    xhciuas's recovery worker never sent it: it was inside `IoAllocateIrp` for that request, and stayed there to the
    end of the run while the drive's read was held by that same recovery. What the kernel was doing there is not read
    (its code is closed). xHCI98's controller thread was alive and idle, waiting for that request.
  - **Kind A** (s2v03r, once in the count before, read from files only): the cancel was asked but never done: no Stop
    Endpoint, the data-in request never completed; the endpoint's state then was not read. The bus driver's controller
    thread did not act on the cancel, nor on xhciuas's later cycle request, while xhciuas's own worker went on by its
    clock, its later requests' allocations succeeding (its cycle request reached the bus driver 5 to 10 s after the
    refusal). Not caught live in this count.
- **Kind A, the candidates from the source** (none proven; each is read at the next kind-A capture by the frame chain
  of the controller thread and the gates' events, which this harness now takes):
  1. *A lost wake*: excluded as a cause by itself by the wait's form (above): the 100 ms time-out starts a pass
     without any wake, so a thread idle for seconds needs one of the others.
  2. *The pass gated off* (unpowered, `ControllerFailed`, `ScratchTainted`): against - no recovery, no containment, no
     power change in the debug console or QEMU's trace.
  3. *The thread inside a completion it ran*: the thread completes some requests itself at PASSIVE_LEVEL (the
     cancelled transfers, the recycles' RESET_PIPEs), and on Windows 98 what runs above may start the next request in
     the same call. For: the controller thread's stack holds leftover return addresses (stale words below its live
     frame, so of earlier calls, at an unknown time) of xhciuas's completion (`uasXferDone`) and its pump (`uasPump`)
     in s4v15 and s4v23, and in s4v15 also of a request entering xhciuas from above (`uasPdoScsiInside` ->
     `UasEngineSubmit`), so such calls have run on it; an allocation made there would meet kind B's wait; and in
     s2v03r the thread's last visible work was the 48th recycle's RESET_PIPE, whose "thread URB done" and "out" lines
     come before its `IoCompleteRequest`, so the files do not show that completion returning; the requests after it
     may have started inside it. Against: nothing in the files places the thread there either.
  4. *A wait for cancelled records inside the thread's endpoint work* (`hcdWaitCancelledOne` with no budget, above):
     for - it waits until every cancelled record of the pipe is freed, with nothing else bounding it; against - the
     48th recycle (which enters that wait only when transfers were still busy, not known here) finished its commands
     and printed its end, so it was not left in it, and no later RESET_PIPE or abort reached the thread; a recycle or
     abort of a pipe whose cancelled record cannot be freed was not seen.
  5. *The power gate held by another party that is itself blocked*: for - the thread's wait on it has no time-out;
     against - of the holders, the door's snapshot does only register reads and copies to a buffered request's system
     buffer under it, and no power change was under way.
  6. *An allocation or registry read of the thread's own pass*: the pass's own pool and IRP allocations (any flavour),
     and the `qemu` flavour's once-a-second registry read from the thread (the release flavour has no periodic
     registry read). For: they run on the thread at PASSIVE_LEVEL, and kind B shows an allocation can fail to return
     at this phase. Against: no capture. Only the registry read is the test flavour's alone: if it were the cause,
     kind A would not reach a release build.
  7. *The thread not scheduled*: against - in both kind-B captures the controller thread kept passing every 100 ms
     with the whole guest stopped, so the freeze itself does not stop it.
- **What this means for the targets.** Windows 98 and ME share `NTKERN`'s allocator, so ME is open to kind B as 98 SE
  is (not run). For Windows 2000 and later the documented contract is that nonpaged pool and `IoAllocateIrp` may be
  called up to DISPATCH_LEVEL and may fail (xhciuas then takes the device reset); what was measured is that none of
  50.20's 2000 runs stalled.

### Not settled, and what would settle it

- Kind A's cause: a live capture of it (this harness, unchanged).
- Kind B's allocation: what it waits on inside the kernel (closed code; not read). A change that takes the allocation
  off the recovery's path would show by count whether the stall goes with it: at the rate of these counts (kind B read
  live in 2 and compatible in 1 - r98v1-2 - of 52 model-on runs at values 1 and 2: 11 in the first legs, 20 in the
  first count, 21 here), 50 runs with none would happen by chance about once in twenty, if the rate holds.

### Harness

- The COM1 follower (`tail.py`) now also ends when its emulator's process has ended, whatever ended it, and the run
  script checks it went (each run since 09:11: "follower ended by itself"); none was left after any run.
- Evidence: `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\sdq\s4v15`, `s4v23` (`thrstate-1.txt`, `thrstate-2.txt`, `stackscan.txt`,
  `retscan-uas.txt` - s4v23's taken by the run script, s4v15's made afterwards from its memory save, the run having
  predated that step -, `stall-capture.txt`, the screens, the debug console and QEMU's log; `thr.bin`, the memory
  save, kept until the row is decided).

## 50.38 (continued): the recovery's requests on memory made at the start, built and counted (2026-11-20)

The owner's choice of 2026-11-20 for 50.38 (the 98 SE stall of 50.20's legs read live as xhciuas's recovery worker
inside the allocation of its RESET_PIPE's IRP, "50.38" above): built apart from the release branch, its entry into a
release the owner's decision once these legs are read. Design record 17 section 4.12.11; branch `w50-uasf1`:
`5fa312e17` (the design), `17066cbe6` (the code: `src\uas\uas.h`, `uas_fdo.c`, `uas_xport.c`, and the test bits' line
in `build-and-test.md`), on `cfdc5fd1c`. `git merge-tree` of `17066cbe6` against the release line's `7129d517a`:
clean.

### The build

One gated build of `17066cbe6`, x86 `all` then amd64 `all` (`XHCI98_SELFTEST_SKIP_OK=1`), every record `dirty=0`; the
import gates of both xhciuas flavours passed with no new pair (48 pairs).

| `xhciuas.sys` | `ECB4C24B...` | `1A5A7FCF...` | `0FCFF3BF...` | `9E6621F7...` |
| `xhci98.sys` | `07014458...` | `A52BB890...` | `6A283569...` | `AFC6D837...` |

### What shows a request went on the set

The bus's per-URB log (`XhciQemuStageFault` 8) prints each URB's IRP. xhciuas's FDO record was read over QMP as data
(runtime) in `s5v01`, LA and LD (from the bus PDO the log names: `DEVICE_OBJECT.AttachedDevice`, its
`DeviceExtension`, the fields at this build's offsets from its own compiler listing of `FIELD_OFFSET`, `Kind` `UasF`
checked): there the logged RESET_PIPE IRP is the FDO's `RecoveryIrp`. Elsewhere only the log's one IRP per FDO is
read. A repeated IRP address in the log alone shows nothing: today's allocation and free gave one address for 32 of
`s4v23`'s 35 RESET_PIPEs.

Void, not counted: `s5v01` to `s5v04` (a harness fault of this worker: the run script was rewritten while three runs
executed it - they ran to their end with no stall, but without their watchdog -, and `s5v04`'s start found its port
taken); the start wedge `s5v27` (the 98 SE start wedge of 49.36, run again); `s5v41` (its QEMU ended by itself mid-run
with the guest working; run again as `s5v41r`).

**The count ended at `s5v47` by its rule: 41 counted runs.** The rule, written before the first run, ends the count at
a stall read as the recovery worker inside an allocation or waiting on a request to the bus it never got back. In
`s5v47` the worker waited on its RESET_PIPE, which it never got back; the reading below places the cause in the bus's
controller thread, stuck in the `qemu` flavour's registry read, but that makes no exception to the rule. The chains
were not stopped (this worker first read `s5v47` as the other kind), so 9 runs ran after it - `s5v48` to `s5v54`,
`s5v27r` and `s5v41r`, of which `s5v48` was already running when `s5v47` stalled and `s5v49` and `s5v50` started
during its capture -, reported here apart, outside the count.

- **No allocation stall observed** (runtime: the frame chains read from memory at each stall), neither in the 41
  counted runs nor in the 9 after them, and in no run did a recovery request fail to reach the bus: every ended run
  made its 149 RESET_PIPEs (the recycles of the 147 refusals and of the two ATA PASS-THROUGH refusals), all on one
  IRP, the FDO's `RecoveryIrp` (read over QMP in `s5v01`: `C1CC4500`, the IRP of every RESET_PIPE of that run). The
  count before had it read live in 2 of 52 runs and a third compatible with it from its files (`r98v1-2`, not read
  live). Taking 3 in 52 as the rate, a fixed rate a run, 41 runs with none happen by chance 0.0875 of the time, about
  once in 11 ((49/52)^41), and 50 with the runs after the count 0.0512, about once in 20 ((49/52)^50). That bounds a
  chance reading; it does not show the stall gone.
- **The stalls: 4 in the 41 counted runs** (`s5v07`, `s5v20`, `s5v21`, `s5v47`) **and 1 after them** (`s5v41r`). Four
  read live (runtime: the controller record and the frame chains from guest memory as data). In all four xHCI98's
  controller thread was inside the `qemu` flavour's once-a-second registry read and did not return - its frame chain
  `hcdThread+3a` -> `hcdPoll+14` -> `HcdInjPoll+124` -> `HcdCtlQemuReadDword` -> `hcdReadDword+24` -> `hcdQueryDword`,
  its pass counters flat over 20 s. In `s5v07`, `s5v20` and `s5v41r` it stopped before the refusal's Stop Endpoint:
  the refused READ's data-in transfer, cancelled by xhciuas, never completed (its IRP pending, Cancel set), and no
  xhciuas frame was on any stack. In `s5v47` it stopped one step later: the cancel was done (`C0000120`), and
  xhciuas's recovery worker had sent its RESET_PIPE on the recovery IRP - the bus logged its arrival (`urb: in ...
  C1CC7460 ... 0000001E`, the IRP of every RESET_PIPE of that run) - and waited for it (`uasStreamRecover+8b` ->
  `uasResetPipe+35` -> `UasRecoveryUrb` -> `UasRecoveryIoctl+87` -> `UasWaitEvent`), the IRP pending in the bus for
  the thread that did not return; in the count before, the RESET_PIPE never reached the bus and the thread was idle.
  These four are the pattern of `s2v03r` (the thread not acting on a cancel), and in them the cause is read: candidate
  6 of "50.38", the registry read of the thread's own pass, which only the `qemu` flavour makes. `s2v03r` itself was
  read from files only and its cause stays unplaced. `s5v21` is unplaced: the same picture from files (refusal #34
  with no Stop Endpoint after it; the cycle the recovery then asked reached the bus and was not acted on), the
  thread's MFINDEX reads going on to the end; its QEMU ended by itself three minutes into the stall, before the
  reading (no message, no host event).
- **The rate.** Stalls of either kind: before this change 4 in 52 (3 + 1); with it 4 in the 41 counted runs, 5 in the
  50 with the runs after (four placed in the `qemu` flavour's registry read, one unplaced). No allocation stall was
  seen, and the guest stalls about as often as before. A reading, not a proof: on 98 SE, while the drive's read is
  held by a recovery, a kernel service the recovery or the bus thread calls can fail to return - an allocation (the
  kind before), a registry read (these); what the kernel waits on there is not read. The release flavour makes no
  periodic registry read on the controller thread, so this count does not say whether a release build still stalls on
  98 SE; a count that answers it needs the `qemu` flavour's read moved off the thread first (option F3 of "50.38").

### Not settled

- Whether a release build of this change still stalls on 98 SE: of this count's stalls the four placed are in the
  `qemu` flavour's own registry read, which the release flavour does not make (the fifth unplaced); a count that
  answers it moves that read off the controller thread first (option F3 of "50.38", test flavour only).
- What the 98 SE kernel waits on when an allocation or a registry read does not return while a UAS read is held
  (closed code; not read).
- A stop or removal while the command phase's command itself is in the device: no rendezvous holds it there; the
  rundown argument of record 17 section 4.12.11 covers it.
- Coverage the design's plan names and these legs did not take: on 98 SE a second device reset of one FDO, the command
  phase run again on the same storage (LA's second fault fired but no second recycle was refused; LA and LD read one
  reset each - on XP x64 one FDO took two (XQAu3) and three (XF4u3)); on 2000 the device reset (fault 34), the cycle
  (bit 2), the CYCLE_PORT fallback (bits 2 and 3) and the abandoned command (bit 5) - 2000 ran the recycle (`r2kf1`,
  with one device reset the recovery chose itself) and the stop during a held RESET_PIPE (L2kS) only; on XP x64 the
  cycle by RESUME_STATE itself (bit 2 alone: XQCu3 took bits 2 and 3, so its RESUME_STATE was refused and the fallback
  cycled); the stop during a recovery on XP x64. Owed.

## 50.38 (kind A): the qemu flavour's trigger read moved off the controller thread (worker qpoll, 2026-11-20)

**Why** (this file's "50.38", and its count continued by worker uasf1). In 50.38's count on 98 SE the controller
thread of the `qemu` flavour was read live twice (`s5v07`, `s5v20`) inside that flavour's once-a-second read of
`XhciQemuInject` (`hcdThread` -> `hcdPoll` -> `HcdInjPoll` -> `HcdCtlQemuReadDword` -> `hcdReadDword` ->
`hcdQueryDword`, the machine-wide key's `RtlQueryRegistryValues`), never returning, the pass counters flat and a
cancelled data-in transfer waiting for its Stop Endpoint: the stall's "kind A". What the read waits for inside the
kernel was not read. The read exists only in the `qemu` flavour. Owner, 2026-11-20: move it off the controller
thread before the cut.

**The change** (`aa86bdafd`, documents `a9c4ec6a6`; design record 17 section 5, "The trigger reader", revision 40).
In the `qemu` flavour alone a thread of its own, the trigger reader (`hcd_inj.c`), makes the read with the same keys
(2000 to 10 the machine-wide key alone; 98 SE and ME both), on a 1 s deadline from the previous read's start (100 ms
while a rendezvous holds), and queues each new value eight deep under `InjLock`; the controller thread takes the
queued readings in order at each pass, through `XhciInjTake` and `hcdInjFire` as before, from the first admission 10
tolerance ticks after the start's latch; a held rendezvous (fault 23) searches the queue for its release. The reader
is made after the controller thread and joined after it: on 2000 to 10 on its thread object (the reference retried
until had, record 15 section 4.5.21); on 98 SE and ME on its exit event, set by the call chained into
`PsTerminateSystemThread` (`HcdThreadEnd9x`, record 15 section 4.5.22), so nothing of the image runs after its
signal. A read in progress at the stop is waited for without a bound, as the stop waited for the controller thread
inside the same read before: a read that never returns still holds the stop; it no longer holds the controller
thread's passes. The sampling contract changed with it (record 17): a value is taken once the reader has read it, in
the order read, but for a reading dropped when the queue of eight overflows (counted and noted) and the readings a
rendezvous passes over before its release; a value replaced before a read is not seen; a value deleted after it was
read is still taken. Every change is inside `XHCI_FLAVOUR_QEMU`.

**The builds.** One gated build of `a9c4ec6a6`, x86 then amd64 (`scripts\build-driver.cmd all`, then `all -amd64`,
after the tools' own builds; the self-test store's skip allowed), records `out\gated-*.txt` with `dirty=0`. The
release images were compared with the gated release images of `c5954cbdd` from the main checkout (`src` is the same
at `c5954cbdd` and at this branch's base `be50285c0`), section by section, with what the build stamps masked (the
COFF time stamp, the checksum, each debug directory entry's time stamp and data size, the CodeView record - the
PDB's signature and path; this worktree's path is 9 characters shorter - and the MISC record's three reserved bytes;
on amd64 the linker places the CodeView record inside `.rdata`, so what follows it there was compared realigned, and
`.pdata`'s unwind addresses with the shift taken out); and every source of `src\sources` was preprocessed (`/EP`)
with the release build's own compile line taken from that build's log, at `be50285c0` and at the tip, and compared
with blank lines dropped. As a control of the method the same was done with the `qemu` flavour's line.

**Where.** Development host A, QEMU, TCG, headless, the q35 machine, one processor and 512 MB a guest, at most four
guests at a time until 18:23, six from then (the recount) on ports 59900-59919; other work's guests and builds ran
throughout, so no time here is a timing of the driver alone. Each leg is a fresh overlay of a prepared image and a
cold start.

**The images.** `l98q`: worker uasf1's `l98f` (worker sdq's 98 SE `p98` with a UAS drive's stack and uasf1's `qemu`
`xhciuas.sys`, F1) with this branch's `qemu` `xhci98.sys` staged by `WININIT.INI` in one start and read installed in
the next (`dir`); `p2kq`: uasf1's 2000 image `p2k` with this branch's `qemu` `xhci98.sys` copied over the installed
file and every copy of it on C: (`fc /b`); `mbq`: worker cancelst's ME image `mb` (`3.5.0.0`) with it copied by
`SWAP.BAT` (`fc /b`: no differences). Each read-only after its preparation.

**The builds' readings.** Gated build of `a9c4ec6a6`: x86 and amd64 passed (`BUILD + GATES PASSED (release qemu)`
for each; `out\gated-*.txt`: `commit=a9c4ec6a6`, `dirty=0`). `xhci98.sys`: x86 `release` `096EC700...`, `qemu`
`4A235EAC...` (574,743 bytes); amd64 `release` `9BD30708...`, `qemu` `E130787D...`. The x86 `release` image against
`c5954cbdd`'s: every byte identical but for the COFF time stamp, the checksum, the three debug directory entries'
time stamps and data sizes, the CodeView record (the PDB's signature and path, 9 characters shorter, at the end of
the file) and the three reserved bytes of the MISC debug record; the FPO and MISC records' data compared equal. The
amd64 `release` image: `.text`, `.data`, `INIT`, `.rsrc` and `.reloc` identical; `.rdata` identical before the PDB
path's record with the stamps masked and after it once realigned (the shorter record moves what follows by 8 bytes);
`.pdata`'s 1120 entries identical but for their unwind addresses, each moved by those 8 bytes. The preprocessed
`release` sources: 78 of 78 identical on x86 and on amd64; the control, the `qemu` flavour's preprocessed sources:
32 of 78 differ on each (the files that include `hcd.h`, with `hcd_inj.c` and `hcd_ctl.c`).

**A value written at run time, still taken.** Three writes of `XhciQemuInject` (fault `01`, one lost interrupt,
sequences `11`, `12`, `13`, 8 s apart) to the machine-wide key by `regedit /s`, each marked on COM1 when `regedit`
returned; the delay is from that marker to the driver's `qemu inject: fired` debug-console line, both stamped with
host time as they arrived (to 0.1 s).

| Leg | System, image | Taken | Delays (s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `f2k1` | 2000, `p2kq`, this branch's `qemu` | 3 of 3 | 0.2, 1.1, 0.8 |
| `f98a` | 98 SE, `l98q`, this branch's `qemu` | 3 of 3 | 1.2, 1.6, 0.9 |

Both with the reader and with the old read the delays were within a read period and a pass or so, with the host
loaded throughout; these are observations, not a bound (a slow read or a long controller step delays a command under
either), and a step that depends on a command having been taken waits for its fired line. The rendezvous (fault 23)
was not run.

**The removal and the reload on 98 SE and ME (50.37's leg shape).** Each start: the controller removed by `DEVCYCLE
remove DEV_000D` (98 SE: from the layer's StartUp batch; ME: from the Run box by keys), the guest read alive 60 s
later (clock lines on COM1, `===ALIVE 60`), shut down, cold-started again. A start after a removal finds the
controller as new hardware: on 98 SE the Add New Hardware wizard was answered with Enter at its default buttons
(six), on ME Windows installed it again by itself; that start's load is the reload. The batch writes
`XhciQemuThreadExitSleep` 10000 at each removal, so from the second start on every thread end of this driver sleeps
10 s outside the image between its signal and its end. Read in the debug console at each removal: the controller
thread's 9x end (`thread end 9x` word 0 `00000101`) and the trigger reader's (`00000401`), each with its sleep, and
`qemu inject: trigger reader has exited`.
