recycle debts. The count's 50th run was started at 19:37 and the slots then took no new run; the last ended at
19:50. Before: with neither change 4 stalls in 52 model-on runs (worker sdq2, three of the recovery worker's kind,
one of the bus thread's); with F1 alone 4 in 41 counted runs and 5 with the 9 after them (worker uasf1, four placed
in the `qemu` flavour's registry read on the controller thread, one unplaced). As an illustration only: if runs were
independent and stalled at a fixed rate equal to those fractions (estimates from small counts, uasf1's including the
9 runs after its rule ended its count), none in 50 would come about 0.5 % of the time at 5 in 50 ((45/50)^50) and
about 1.8 % at 4 in 52 ((48/52)^50); neither assumption is established, and the result does not show either stall
gone. So, in this rig: a `qemu` test build with both changes - the UAS driver's recovery on memory made at the start
(F1) and the trigger read off the controller thread (this change) - did not stall on 98 SE in 50 runs. The release
flavour has neither the read nor the `qemu` flavour's per-URB log, so this is a reading of the test build in the
emulated rig, not of a release build.

reference retries of the reader's thread object (`XhciQemuThreadRefReader`); a creation of the reader that fails;

part.

another leg ran it (`f2k1`: the edit came after its readings, which were taken inside the part already read; the
lines after them failed to parse); the ME guest did not act on QEMU's power button, so its starts were shut down by
the Start menu. Other work's guests and builds ran on development host A throughout.

## 50.25 Windows 8's UAS driver on this bus: the emulator made to run it, its drive given a disk, and the stream recovery's design (2026-11-16)

Branch `w50-uasother`, from `3.5.1.0` at `875156613`. Record 13 section 6.13.12 holds the short-read change's reasoning; the stream
recovery is a design not yet in the tree (planned as record 17 section 4.12.11); this section holds what was read.

### The vehicle: why QEMU's UAS drive failed Windows' own UAS driver, and the change

49.45 and earlier runs read QEMU's `usb-uas` at Code 10 under `uaspstor` on every stack. Read from the device's side
(QEMU's own log and its trace events; no binary read), two causes:

- `uaspstor` sends CLEAR_FEATURE(ENDPOINT_HALT) to the status, data-in and data-out endpoints at its start, and
  QEMU's `usb-uas` STALLs it (49.45's QEMU log already held the three: "unhandled control request (req 0x201, val
  0x0, idx 0x82)", `0x83`, `0x4`). The fork's `usb-uas x-clear-halt` (50.20) answers it.
- With that alone (leg E1, 8 x64, Windows' own stack) still Code 10: `uaspstor` read string 0 and the serial number
  and the slot was disabled, with no SELECT_CONFIGURATION. `usb-uas` offers UAS at alternate setting 0 with no
  Bulk-Only setting; real UAS bridges offer Bulk-Only at 0 and UAS at 1.

usb4-emu test builds (uncommitted changes in the `w50-hwm` worktree's `src\qemu`, as 50.20's; diffs with the
scratch files): `emu25a` (`qemu-system-x86_64.exe` `b6f2c82c...`) adds `usb-uas x-bot-alt0` (Bulk-Only at alternate
setting 0, UAS at 1; descriptors only); `emu25b` (`ea1150be...`) adds `usb-uas x-refuse-rw-every=N` (every Nth
READ or WRITE refused at once with CHECK CONDITION, UNIT ATTENTION 6/29/00, its posted data packet left pending, as
`x-ata-passthrough-refuse` leaves an ATA PASS-THROUGH's; the class driver retries it): the refusal trigger with no
third-party program in the guest; `emu25c` (`aaf9768b...`) fixes `usb-uas`'s cancel of a live request's data
packet, which left the request marked asynchronous so that the next packet for it was completed from its setup
state and QEMU aborted (`hw/usb/core.c:574 usb_packet_check_state`), seen twice in leg L1 when `qemu-xhci`'s Stop
Endpoint cancelled every stream's packet in flight (QEMU's own stop, record 13 section 14).

| Leg | Guest, stack, device | Result |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | 8 x64 (q35 base), Windows' own USB 3 stack, `x-clear-halt` | `UASPStor` Code 10; no select |
| E2 | the same, `x-clear-halt` and `x-bot-alt0` | `UASPStor` started, the drive D:, I/O on streams; with `x-refuse-rw-every=40` and a copy-compare loop, 14 refusals, each costing one Stop Endpoint on the data-out endpoint and a Set TR Dequeue for the cancelled stream and, at 12 of the 14, one other (no RESET_PIPE, no clear, no port reset); 12/12 copies compared equal |
| G3 | 7 x64, the installed image of 49.45 (Windows 8's USB 3 stack and `uaspstor` 6.2.9200.16384 carried back by a third party, loaded under that party's signature in test-signing mode), both switches, refusals every 40 | `UASPStor` started with streams; at its start three Configure Endpoint commands each dropping and adding one stream endpoint (DCI 7, 8, 5) beside the clears; 82 refusals: 82 Stop Endpoint, 110 stream Set TR Dequeue, no Reset Endpoint on a data endpoint, no port reset; two copy-compare loops 8/8 and 4/4 |

### Under `xhci98.sys` before the fix: started, no disk

The tree at `875156613` (gated build, both architectures BUILD + GATES PASSED; the release amd64 package signed
in each guest with a certificate made there, the qemu flavour's `xhci98.sys` put over the installed one), fault 33
argument 3 and the model on:

| Leg | Guest | Result |

| G1 | 8 x64, Setup `/usb /takeover` | V1 interface answered at `0x602`, `STATIC_STREAMS` answered, three URB `0x35` opens of 15 streams granted (`82`, `83`, `04`); `UASPStor` Code 0 and no disk (diskpart lists none). Every status read 1024 bytes with flags `01` (IN, no `USBD_SHORT_TRANSFER_OK`), the sense IU 16 bytes, completed `80000900`: `xfer.short.err=01050201`, `uas.urb.len=04000010`, `uas.urb.st=80000900`, `XferShortRefused` 7; 90 commands, no RESET_PIPE or RESET_PORT |
| G2 | 7 x64 image (carried back), `xhci98.inf` forced on the controller, its `uaspstor` left on the drive | the same: started, three opens, no disk, `XferShortRefused` 7 |

This is the field report of 49.45 ("started with four pipes, no disk"), reproduced.

### The fix (`4ea4a96a8`) and its legs

Record 13 section 6.13.12: on a PDO whose `GUID_USBD_INTERFACE_V1` was answered at `0x602`, a bulk or interrupt
IN that ends short completes as a success, as Microsoft documents for xHCI ("On xHCI host controllers,
USBD_SHORT_TRANSFER_OK ignored for bulk and interrupt endpoints.", "USB Bandwidth Allocation"); every other PDO
and transfer unchanged. The gated build of the tree with it (its logs kept with the scratch files): x86 and amd64 BUILD + GATES
PASSED, `test_usbdx` 342 checks, 0 failures; amd64 `xhci98.sys` qemu `6309A865...`, release `CF99A11E...`; x86
release `E12BB844...`. Legs on those binaries (kit as above, `emu25b`, `emu25c` from L1's third run on), a
SuperSpeed `usb-storage` stick on port 3 beside the UAS drive on port 4; copy-compare loops (a file copied to the
drive and back, compared both ways; on 8 x64 and 7 x64 the UAS drive's volume dismounted after the loop and the
file compared again from the device):

| Leg | Guest, client | Result |
|---|---|---|
| L1 | 8 x64, Setup `/usb /takeover`, `UASPStor` on the UAS drive (both switches, refusals every 40), `USBSTOR` on the stick | the UAS disk present (F:); after QEMU's two aborts above (emulator, fixed in `emu25c`): UAS loop 12/12, stick loop 6/6, the dismounted re-read equal; 15 refusals, 15 cancels; `XferShortRefused` 0, every `uas.urb.st` 0; `usbdx.v1` answered, three opens |
| L2 | 7 x64 image (carried back), `xhci98.inf` forced, its `UASPStor` on the drive (both switches, refusals every 40) | the disk present (E:); loops 8/8 and 6/6, the dismounted re-read equal; 58 refusals, 55 cancels; `XferShortRefused` 0 |
| L3 | 7 x64 (q35 base), Setup `/usb`, `xhciuas` on the UAS drive (`x-clear-halt` only), `USBSTOR` on the stick | unchanged: no `usbdx.*` and no `xfer.short.err` note, `XferShortRefused` 0; loops 8/8 and 6/6 |
| L4 | XP x64 SP2 (q35 base), Setup `/usb` (Windows' unsigned-driver and new-hardware prompts answered by the harness), `xhciuas` and `USBSTOR` | unchanged as L3; loops 8/8 and 6/6 |

### The stream recovery: what was read for its design

At each Stop Endpoint on a data endpoint, counted from QEMU's trace (another command alive: its command IU received
and its status IU not yet sent; the refused command itself not counted):

| Leg | Stack | Stops | No other command alive | Only the cancelled stream set | Both |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E2 | Windows 8's own | 14 | 8 | 2 | - |
| G3 | carried back to 7 | 82 | 82 | 54 | - |
| L1 | `xhci98.sys`, `4ea4a96a8` | 17 | 8 | 11 | 7 (41 %) |

`uaspstor` was never seen to send RESET_PIPE, CLEAR_FEATURE or a port reset after a refusal; it cancels the data
request only, and reused a cancelled tag only after that cancel completed.

### Not read

- The stream recovery itself: not built. For a UAS client that does not declare (the bus recycling the endpoint
  itself in place of a stream Set TR Dequeue) it was designed six times and no design was accepted: every version
  that could be argued needed the bus's own per-tag account of the drive's UAS traffic, a quarantine of cancelled
  records until hardware retirement, and changes in the cancel, drain, wait, teardown and publication paths that
  every client runs through; and the case it could take - one refused command with no other task alive and no
  other request on its endpoint - met 7 of the 17 stops (41 %) in the one session read under `xhci98.sys`. The
  owner's decision (2026-11-16): the Intel 7 Series stream fault is not catered for under Windows' own UAS driver;
  50.25 ends with the short-read change and a limitation in the user documents, and `3.5.1.0` does not wait for a
  recovery.
- A real UAS drive under `uaspstor` on this bus; the Intel 7 Series controller.
- 8.1 x64 and 7 x86 (the carried-back x86 driver); 98 SE and 2000 for the short-read change (no client there
  queries the V1 interface, record 13 section 6.13.4).
- The fault model (`x-stream-setdeq-current`) with the fix: G1 and G2 had it on, but no command completed there.

### Cleanup

Every guest of these legs was stopped by its own process id (`E:\xhci98-vm\p50\uasother\pids.txt`); the overlays,
logs and screenshots are kept for the stream recovery's legs. The carried-back files were used only inside the
guests and are not tracked.

## 50.26 The status a cancelled URB carries: `XhciCancelStatus` (2026-11-16 to 2026-11-17)

Branch `w50-cancelst` from `3.5.1.0` at `b5f311b54`: eleven commits, `13683b8f3` (design record 13 section 6.15,
draft) to `bf635c320` (the `legal-provenance.md` section 4 row), then the changes made before the merge (the last
part of this section). The legs below ran on the gated builds of `2087fcbe1` (x86 release and qemu, amd64 release,
and the amd64 qemu flavour built after them; `dirty=0`); `bf635c320` differs from it by one documentation line.
Development host A, QEMU TCG, headless, the q35 bases in `E:\xhci98-vm\q35-bases\` (the stock-stack readings on 98
SE and ME on `-M pc`), fresh overlays. The evidence is under `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\cancelst\`; each folder has a
`STATE.md` and a `pids.txt` with every start and stop.

What it is. Up to `3.5.0.0`, `xhci98.sys` completed a cancelled URB with the USBD status `0x00010000` on every
system, the value of the Windows 98 and 2000 driver kit headers. Later headers and later USB stacks use
`0xC0010000`. The IRP's own status is not this item's subject and is not changed by it. `XhciCancelStatus` chooses
which of the two a cancelled URB, and each unanswered packet of a cancelled isochronous URB, carries:

- `0`: `0x00010000` everywhere;
- `1`, the default (owner, 2026-11-16): what each system's own stack gives - `0x00010000` on 98 SE and ME,
  `0xC0010000` on 2000 and later;
- `2`: `0xC0010000` everywhere.

Any other value is read as `1`. The driver takes both values as cancelled inside at every setting. The value is
read when the controller starts. Both INFs write `1` into the controller's key with the no-overwrite flag
(`0x00010003`), so a value already there is kept. The installer and the USB Tree list it with the other settings.
The snapshot's log carries `urb.cancel.value` (the value read; `FFFFFFFF` when absent) and `urb.cancel.out` (the
word chosen). Below, L is `0x00010000` and E `0xC0010000`.

### Each system's own stack (the table behind mode 1)

A probe driver (a sibling project's, test-only, used unchanged, never packaged), bound to QEMU's `usb-mtp` at Full
Speed and hot-plugged on each controller, in guests with no `xhci98.sys`: a pending bulk IN read and a pending
interrupt IN read, each ended by `IoCancelIrp` and by `URB_FUNCTION_ABORT_PIPE`, logging the IRP status and the URB
status. Twice per controller on 2000 to 10 and on the UHCI stacks of 98 SE and ME, the same both times; once on
their OHCI stacks. x86 guests only. Kits: `m9x\` (98 SE, ME) and `mnt\` (2000 to 10).

| System | Stack | Cancelled URB |
|---|---|---|
| 98 SE, ME (stock) | `UHCD`, `OPENHCI` 4.10.2222, 4.90.3000 | L (UHCI and OHCI, both requests, both ways) |
| 98 SE with the added USB 2.0 stack (an earlier probe run the same day) | EHCI | E |
| 2000 SP4 | `uhcd.sys` 5.0.2195.6655 (UHCI, not through usbport) | L |
| 2000 SP4 | usbport and `usbehci` | E |
| XP SP3, Vista SP2, 7 SP1, 8.1, 10 22H2 | usbport (UHCI, EHCI); `USBXHCI` on 8.1 and 10 | E |

A transfer ended by `IoCancelIrp` completed `0xC0000120` (`STATUS_CANCELLED`) on every stack. A transfer ended by
`ABORT_PIPE` did too on OHCI, usbport and `USBXHCI`, but not on the old UHCI stacks (98 SE, ME, 2000's `uhcd`):
there the transfer's IRP completed `0x00000000` with its URB at L. The abort request's own IRP completed
`0x00000000` everywhere. Not measured: a pending control request (the emulated device answers at once),
isochronous requests, and the x64 stacks. The record is `legal-provenance.md` section 4's row (`bf635c320`) and
record 13 section 6.15.6.

### The legs: does any class driver behave differently by the value?

Each system ran the qemu flavour at absent, `1` and `0` (and `2` where shown), each value taken up after the
change by a cold start, a restart or a disable and enable of the controller (the value read back from the snapshot
each time), and the class drivers' behaviour was compared value against value. The driver's words
were read from the snapshot on every system, and on 2000 and later also from the per-request log
(`XhciQemuStageFault=8`); on 98 SE and ME the per-request log was not used. The release flavour was installed at
its default on 98 SE, 2000, XP, XP x64, 8.1 and 10 (fresh), and on 7 as an update over `3.5.0.0`; not on ME or
Vista.

- **98 SE and ME** (`legs-9x\`):
  - Words: on 98 SE the INF-written `1`, absent and an explicit `1` -> L; `0` -> L; `2` -> E. On ME `1` and absent
    -> L; `0` -> L (the first change to `0` did not take: the next start read `FFFFFFFF`; set again, then read
    `0`); `2` -> E. The probe gave the same (IRP `0xC0000120`).
  - At the default, `0` and `2`, the same at every value: HID unplug and replug; a 50 MB copy-compare; an unplug
    during a read (the blue "open files" screen, then General failure / Abort, and the stick mounts again); on ME
    an audio device unplugged while playing survived and played again (valid trials: 3 at `1`, 1 at absent, 1 at
    `0`, 1 at `2`; one absent trial not counted, the play never started).
  - A hub with a tablet and a stick behind it, unplugged whole: passed at the default on both (ME's Unsafe
    Removal dialog for the stick, as on `3.5.0.0`); not run at `0` or `2`.
  - At the default the new build behaves as `3.5.0.0` on both systems. A black ME desktop seen once, on a start

### The update through Setup (`legs-setup\`)

On a fresh overlay, `3.5.0.0` was installed from its released zip by its own Setup (`INSTALL.BAT /console /yes
/nopause`) and the devices checked; then Setup's window (`SETUP.EXE`) of the gated build's package was run over it
and the guest restarted as Setup asked. That package was laid out by family as a release is, with the Setup and
tools of the same gated run; it is not a `make-release` upload set. Legs: the value never set, `0` in the
controller's key before the update (98 SE and 7), and `0` machine-wide (`Services\USB`) before the update (7).

**These legs read Setup's same-version repair, not its update.** The branch is not version-bumped: its package is
`3.5.0.0` like the installed one, so Setup took its "same version, other bytes" path ("Replace files (same
version)"):

- on 98 SE that path replaces `xhci98.sys` and `xhciuas.sys` through `WININIT.INI` and does not install the device
  again, so the INF's `1` was not written, and the driver used its default;
- on 7 it reinstalls the device with the new INF, so the `AddReg` ran;
- on 7 the same `DriverVer` also made Setup skip `xhciuas` (the driver store holds another build with the same
  version; exit code 4). No UAS device was used in these legs.

The update path, which the `3.5.1.0` cut's newer version takes and which installs the devices again, was not run;
it is to be read at the cut.

| Leg | Registry after the update and restart | Words | Devices |
|---|---|---|---|
| 98 SE, never set | none anywhere | `FFFFFFFF` -> L | tablet and USB keyboard work; stick copy-compare the same; unplug during a read as above; mounts again; copy-compare the same; no USB devnode with a problem |
| 98 SE, `0` in the key | the key's `0` kept | `0` -> L | as above |
| 7 x86, never set | the key `1` (written by the update) | `1` -> E | tablet, keyboard, disable and enable, replug; stick copy-compare, unplug during a copy (it failed 63 s after the unplug), replug, Safely Remove; no problem device of ours |
| 7 x86, `0` in the key | the key's `0` kept | `0` -> L | as above |
| 7 x86, `0` machine-wide | `Services\USB` `0` kept, the key `1` written | `0` -> L (the machine-wide value wins) | as above |

The Settings dialog showed each value before the update: "Current: 1 (default)", or "Current: 0", on 7; "Current:

### Seen at `0` and at `1`, not part of 50.26: the wait after an unplug (now 50.28)

On 8.1, in timed in-flight unplug repetitions (`legs-nt10\w81\run-0u/1u/1v/0v/0v2/1w-e.log`):

- `usbstor`: in the four timed repetitions (two at `0`, two at `1`) the bulk URB pending at the unplug was
  cancelled 20.3 to 20.4 s after it and the device removed at 21.3 to 21.4 s; three more at `0`, not timed that
  way, failed about 21 s after the unplug.
- `uaspstor`: in some repetitions the copy failed about 20 s after the unplug with event 129 (a reset) logged - at
  `0` once (of 8 repetitions) and at `1` four times (of 7); in the three of those timed against the requests the
  cancels came about 16.5 s after the unplug, 1.4 to 1.7 s after the reset's logged second (the guest's clock, at
  1 s resolution, against the host's), and the removal at about 21.5 s. The other repetitions failed within about 4 s.
- On 7 and Vista, the copy failing about 62 s after an unplug that cancelled a transfer in flight (above), at `0`
  and at `1`; not timed against the requests.

The logs show the timing only. That the wait is the class driver's own time-out, reached because `xhci98.sys`
holds a departed device's pending transfers until their client cancels them (design record 13 section 10.5), is an
inference from that timing, not something these logs show; and the readings cover only the systems and values
above (not `2`, and no build before 50.26 was timed the same way). The change that follows from it is a separate
item, roadmap 50.28.

### Before the merge: only the fields a completion wrote are encoded (2026-11-17)

Read again for the merge, `bf635c320` encoded more than its rule said. `HcdUrbOut` ran the encoder at every URB
completion of a device PDO, and the encoder rewrote any L it found. L is a client's value too: a client that
reuses the URB of a cancelled transfer hands it in with L still in its header and packets. So a completion that
never wrote those fields - the composite parent's answer to a request it does not support, the packets of an
isochronous request refused as malformed - turned the client's own L into E at `1` and `2`. The run sheet above
was corrected in the same reading (each system's qualifications restored from its report, the wait after an
unplug stated as an inference and left to 50.28, the old UHCI stacks' aborted transfer completing
`STATUS_SUCCESS`).

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `4b82a5312` | `HcdUrbOut` and `XhciPipeUrbCancelOut` take `ours`: `HCD_URB_OUT`, at the six completion sites that write the fields themselves (the done list, the deferred refusals, a held request's release, the thread's completion), passes 1; `HcdCompleteIrp`, which completes what the dispatch refuses or answers at once and writes no packet, passes 0 and leaves the URB as it came (the qemu flavour's log line still written). `test_pipe`, new cases: with the setting choosing E, a refused request whose client left L in its header and every packet - an isochronous request the composite parent does not support (header not written), one refused as malformed (header written `0x80000300`, packets not) and a bulk one - keeps every byte; the same isochronous image completed by a path that wrote it has its header and four packets encoded; the mixed-packet and bound cases as before |
| `0e30dec83` | record 13 section 6.15: 6.15.3 says why only the fields a completion wrote are encoded and why in this form, 6.15.4's dispatch row, 6.15.5's acknowledged ambiguity removed, 6.15.7's host tests; two readings qualified (the IRP was `STATUS_CANCELLED` in the probe's 98 SE readings but not on every stack; the 98 SE and ME OHCI readings were taken once); `tuning.md`: a transfer still waiting when its device was unplugged keeps its device-gone packets at every value |

### The shutdown fault compared with `3.5.0.0` (2026-11-17)

The fault seen at one shutdown of the guest pass above was run again, beside release `3.5.0.0`, with a corrected
harness. Development host A, QEMU TCG, headless, one processor a guest, two guests at a time (other guests were
running on the host). The evidence is under `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\s98shut\`: `STATE.md`, `results.txt`, `pids.txt`
with every start and stop, and one folder per start (`sess.log`, `serial.log`, `debugcon.log`, `plug.log`,
`cmdline.txt`), its screenshots in `shots\`.

- **A**: the gated x86 build of `6bc996b13`, the `3.5.1.0` tip ("BUILD + GATES PASSED (release qemu)", `dirty=0`),
  its qemu flavour staged by `make-package.ps1`: `xhci98.sys` `0197880420E14BB6...`, `xhciuas.sys`
  `269F07FB6B2460A8...`, the gated record's. The guest pass's package (`0e30dec83`) was not reused: 50.27's source
  changes were merged into `3.5.1.0` after that gate.
- **B**: `releases\3.5.0.0\98-me\xhci98.sys` (`b3ea6650d0df7f64...`) and `xhciuas.sys` (`50254935a448b471...`),
  the release flavour, so B's driver writes nothing to port `0E9h`; `XHCITR.EXE` from the same release.
- **The guest**: fresh overlays of the faulting start's own chain (the legs' 98 SE guest: `3.5.0.0` by its Setup,
  the legs build by Device Manager, the probe driver). One start per build placed its two files through
  `WININIT.INI` and wrote `XhciCancelStatus` `1` in `Services\USB`, as the guest pass did; every start below is a
  fresh overlay of that state (so the first start after the update, as the faulting start was), with a fresh
  overlay of the stick.
- **The session**, the faulting start's: `XHCITR /report` and an `fc /b` of the installed files against the kit's
  in an MS-DOS window; `usb-mtp` and the probe's four cancels; tablet and USB keyboard plugged, a line typed
  through the USB keyboard, the pointer moved; the stick plugged (98 SE opened an Explorer window on it by itself
  at every arrival) and a 50 MB copy-compare; then Start, Shut Down, "Shut down", OK. The harness checked the
  screen at the interaction boundaries (the desktop after the start, the Run dialog before a command is typed into
  it, the taskbar after a window closes, the first window active before it is typed into, the Start menu, the Shut
  Down dialog) and waited for each step's COM1 marker before the next step; the keys of a command typed into an
  open Run dialog or MS-DOS window were not checked one by one. A start was counted only when its COM1 markers all
  arrived, once each and in order; a start that failed a check was stopped with no further key and is not counted.
  The end of a shutdown is QEMU's `SHUTDOWN` event with reason `guest-shutdown` (the guest powered off), or the
  screen at 300 s.
- **Disturbed**: the first MS-DOS window (`XHCITR`, `fc`) is left open, holding COM1, through the probe (whose COM1
  lines then do not arrive, as in the faulting start's probe logs), the HID plug, a second window's write to COM1
  (`KB.BAT`: "Write fault error writing device COM1", answered F; two prompts every time) and the stick's arrival;
  it is then closed and the copy runs as in the clean session. **Stick absent**: the same with no stick and no
  copy. **Controller disabled**: A's files, the controller disabled in Device Manager ("Disable in this hardware
  profile"; the controller and its root hub then shown disabled) in the image these starts are made from; the
  disturbed session without the probe, the USB keyboard or the copy (nothing drives them), the devices plugged at
  the same points; `xhci98.sys` wrote nothing to port `0E9h` in those starts.

| Configuration | Starts counted | Completed (power-off) | Fault | Hung |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A, clean | 10 | 10 | 0 | 0 |
| B, clean | 10 | 10 | 0 | 0 |
| A, disturbed | 15 | 13 | 2 (`AD4`, `RAD11`) | 0 |
| B, disturbed | 21 | 20 | 1 (`RBD07`) | 0 |
| A, disturbed, stick absent | 10 | 9 | 1 (`RAN07`) | 0 |
| B, disturbed, stick absent | 10 | 8 | 2 (`RBN02`, `RBN09`) | 0 |
| Controller disabled (A's files), disturbed | 18 | 18 | 0 | 0 |

Every fault was the guest pass's screen: "A fatal exception 0E has occurred at 0028:C029983B in VXD VWIN32(05) +
00002363. The current application will be terminated.", shown at 45 s and still shown at 300 s, when the guest was
stopped by QMP. On A's three faulting starts the driver's port-`0E9h` log has no line from the shutdown and no
controller power-dispatch entry (no `hcd: power minor` line), as far as that trace is complete: it ends with the
stick's PnP capability queries (`AD4`, `RAD11`) or with HID transfer counters (`RAN07`, no stick). Every completed
shutdown with A's controller enabled (32 starts) logged `hcd: power minor`, `quiesce: halted` and
`SuspendController: halted`; the controller-disabled starts, with A's files, have empty driver logs. Every
completed shutdown powered off within 3 s of the OK (for A01, A02, B01 and B02, before the harness recorded the
event's reason, QEMU exited within 3 s).

What these counts show, and no more:

- The fault is reproduced with the released `3.5.0.0`.
- Every counted fault followed the disturbed session; the clean session faulted in 0 of 20 starts.
- The stick is not needed for this reproducer (faults in 3 of 20 starts with the stick absent).
- With the controller disabled, 0 of 18; with it enabled, 6 of 56 disturbed starts. That is suggestive, not
  established: the disabled control also ran without the probe, the USB keyboard and the copy.
- A is the qemu flavour and B the release flavour, so the two builds' rates are not comparable.

Also seen, on both builds and with the controller disabled:

- A start whose desktop background was never painted (the Windows 98 logo on blue behind the icons and the
  taskbar, still at 900 s): 3 starts of A, 4 of B, 4 with the controller disabled, and the image's first start;
  the Start menu, Shut Down and the power-off worked on each. They ran no session and are not counted above. One
  more (`AD1`, A) was stopped by the harness at 300 s.
- A key that did not arrive: the first Win+R after the desktop, or Ctrl+Esc, opened nothing in 20 s in 3 starts
  of A, 5 of B and 4 with the controller disabled; the harness checked the screen and sent it again. Two starts of
  A (`A03`, `RAD05`), from before the harness repeated a key, were stopped there and are not counted.
- Not counted either: `RAN01` and `RAX01`, stopped by checks of the variant script that were then corrected.

Not run: the release flavour of A; a qemu flavour of `3.5.0.0`; B with the controller disabled (no `xhci98.sys`
runs then under either build); the guest pass's `rundll32 user.exe,ExitWindows` (the Start menu was used
throughout); real hardware. Guest memory and code were not read. Every guest of this comparison is stopped
(`pids.txt`); the overlays and the kit's copies of the probe files are throwaway.

### The shutdown fault narrowed by its conditions (2026-11-17 to 2026-11-18)

The comparison above left the fault unexplained, with xHCI98 not ruled in or out. The same reproducer was run
again with each part of its session a switch, on machines with and without an xHCI controller, until the
conditions it needs were found. Diagnosis only: nothing in `src\` changed. Development host A, QEMU TCG
(the emulator build of the comparison above), headless, one processor and 512 MB a guest, at most four guests at
a time (other work's guests were running on the host). The evidence is under `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\s98diag\`:
`results.txt` (one line a start), `pids.txt` (every start and stop), `queue.txt`, the harness in `tools\`
(`sess3.sh`, `slot-v3.sh`, `v.sh`, `cfg\*.env`, `counts3.py`), and one folder a start (`sess.log`,
`serial.log`, `debugcon.log`, `plug.log`, `cmdline.txt`, the fault screen's text in `faulttext.txt`); its
screenshots in `shots\`.

**Builds** (`91131cd4d`, the `3.5.1.0` tip, `dirty=0`; Git Bash with Windows' own directories first on `PATH`,
`XHCI98_SELFTEST_SKIP_OK=1`): gated x86 `all`, "BUILD + GATES PASSED (release qemu)"; gated amd64 `release`,
"BUILD + GATES PASSED (release)" (`xhci98.sys` `EF22244E...`; built, not run: no x64 guest belongs to this item).
The guests ran the x86 images from the build's output directories, each hash equal to the gated record's:
release `xhci98.sys` `7996AFAD...` and `xhciuas.sys` `7D5B399C...`; qemu `xhci98.sys` `272EA667...` and
`xhciuas.sys` `EBC957DD...`; `XHCITR.EXE` `34F73854...`.

**The guests**: fresh overlays of the comparison's chain (the legs' 98 SE guest), each image made the way the
comparison made its own: one start placed the two files through `WININIT.INI` and wrote `XhciCancelStatus` `1`,
so every counted start is the first start after that update.

- `prepR`: the tip's release files. `prepQ`: the tip's qemu files (the trace on port `0E9h`).
- `prepB`: `releases\3.5.0.0\98-me`'s two files; used only for machines with no xHCI controller, where no
  `xhci98.sys` loads.
- `prepU`: no xHCI controller; a PIIX3 UHCI controller (`piix3-usb-uhci`) added, which 98 SE installed with its
  own driver ("Intel 82371SB PCI to USB Universal Host Controller"), then the tablet and keyboard plugged on it
  and installed by 98 SE's wizards ("USB Human Interface Device"), then the update start. The xHCI98 package
  stays installed in this image (and in `prepB`'s); with no xHCI controller its `xhci98.sys` and `xhciuas.sys`
  cannot load. Read in one start of it (`CHK1`, a `dir /s` and two `regedit /e` exports to COM1): `XHCIPFW.VXD`
  and `S98VSD.VXD` are only in `C:\XHCI98\` and the legs' kit folder, `Services\VxD` has no key for either,
  and no `stor98.mpd` is installed; the Run key starts the xHCI98 USB Tree's tray (`XHCITR.EXE /tray`) at
  every start, so the tray ran in every configuration below but `U-notray`.
- `prepUT`: `prepU` after that start, with `XHCITR.EXE` renamed away at the next start through `WININIT.INI`
  (the Run key then names a missing file; no message was seen) and the update re-armed: no tray.
- An EHCI controller with three UHCI companions (`ich9-usb-ehci1`, `ich9-usb-uhci1` to `3`) was tried first
  (`prepE`): 98 SE installed its UHCI driver on the three companions and none on the EHCI, but no tablet or
  keyboard on companion ports 1, 3 or 5 (12 Mb/s) was ever enumerated. Abandoned; nothing was counted on it.

**The session** is the comparison's "disturbed, stick absent" one, with its parts as switches:

- Always: an MS-DOS window (window 1) with `XHCITR /report` and an `fc /b` of the installed files, each
  ending in its COM1 marker; then Start, Shut Down, "Shut down", OK.
- **Hold**: window 1 stays open, holding COM1, while a second window (`command /c KB.BAT`) writes to COM1 and
  meets "Write fault error writing device COM1", answered F at each prompt (two every time); window 1 is then
  activated and closed. Without the hold, window 1 is closed before anything else and the second window's line
  reaches COM1.
- **MTP**: `usb-mtp` plugged and the probe's four cancels, then unplugged.
- **Tablet**, **USB keyboard**: plugged (the keyboard after the tablet), each by its own switch. With the USB
  keyboard plugged QEMU sends every key to it; without it, to the PS/2 keyboard.
- **The pointer**: two moves, then a click on window 1's title bar to activate it, by the tablet where it is
  plugged; in the `-ms` configurations the same through the PS/2 mouse (relative moves); otherwise no pointer
  input at all and window 1 is activated by Alt+Tab.
- **The end**: QEMU's `SHUTDOWN` event with reason `guest-shutdown` is a completed shutdown; otherwise at 150 s
  the screen is read (a text-mode fault screen from video memory, else a screenshot), then from `Q10` on the USB
  keyboard is unplugged and one key sent to the PS/2 keyboard, and 120 s more watched.

The harness checked the screen and the COM1 markers as the comparison's did. A start was counted only when its
COM1 markers all arrived in order and its shutdown was asked for; a start that failed a check was stopped and
replaced. Changed during the runs, each for the starts begun after it (the start named is the first it served):
a desktop never painted no longer skips the session (it is run on that desktop and the start counted, every
counted start); the fault screen's key goes to the PS/2 keyboard (`Q10`); after the USB keyboard's plug the
Run dialog is opened by a tablet click on Start and R, not Win+R (`H05`; `H01` and `H04` had the Win key held
after Win+R, so the typed command ran Windows shortcuts); a Start menu that does not open to Ctrl+Esc is
clicked with the tablet (`Q08`), and from `G13` on a start whose Start menu opens neither way is shut down by
the ACPI power button and counted ("power button" in the table) instead of being replaced; the PS/2 click aims
at half the distance (`S03`, `Y03`: the guest moved the pointer two pixels a count).

"Hung": still running 150 s after the OK with no fault screen: `R18` on its desktop with the clock stopped (an
hourglass after the key); `P17`, `H23`, `U04` and `V14` after the ACPI power button, their Start menu having
opened neither to Ctrl+Esc nor to a tablet click. `R18`'s result line in `results.txt` says `FAULTSCREEN`: the
harness classed the screen by its share of blue, and the never-painted desktop is blue; its screen text and
screenshots show the desktop, so it is counted hung. `N08` (`NOX`) is counted completed by the definition
above: QEMU's `SHUTDOWN` event came with reason `guest-shutdown`, and the process had not exited 10 s later.
"Not counted": stopped by a check and replaced (`R06`, `Q07`, `G03`, `G12` and `H22`, a Start menu that would
not open, before the power button was used; `H01`, `H04` and twelve `X-kbd` starts, the second window not
closed after its F answers, the ones looked at (`H01`, `H04`, `K06`) with the Win key held after Win+R; `H20`,
a lost key; `S01`, `S02`, `Y01`, `Y02`, the PS/2 click before its aim was halved; `S12`, no marker from the
first window; `V06`, no second window for the write, and `V19`, no Run dialog, after lost keys; `P06`, below).
A desktop never painted was seen in 24 counted starts, in eleven of the configurations, and is counted in
place.

So every count above is of shutdowns that followed a completed scripted session, not of starts attempted: 28
starts were stopped by a check and replaced by starts of their own numbers (the last column; `X-kbd` counted
20 of 32), and the rule for a Start menu that would not open changed during the runs (five such starts
replaced before `G13`, four counted as hung after it). The rows are not comparable with one another, and
neither are the two USB drivers' rows.

**What the fault names.** All ten: "A fatal exception 0E has occurred at 0028:C029983B in VXD VWIN32(05) +
00002363. The current application will be terminated.", read from video memory, already on screen 45 s after
the OK - the same text, address and offset as the comparison's faults with `3.5.0.0` and with the tip's qemu
build, and now `U02`'s, `V03`'s, `V17`'s and `V20`'s with no xHCI controller in the machine. After one key
(`Q10`, `H06`, `H09`, `P08`, `U02`, `V03`, `V17`, `V20`) the screen went back to "Windows is shutting down" and
stayed there for the 120 s watched; `R07`'s and `R08`'s key went to the USB keyboard and the fault screen
stayed.

**The trace** (the qemu flavour, `Q-full` and `Q-hid`). In each of the 39 completed shutdowns the driver's
port-`0E9h` log has, before its first `hcd: power minor` line, the HID clients' interrupt reads being
cancelled: stopped-endpoint lines for both HID devices' interrupt endpoints and `transfers cancelled` lines,
three in 38 of them and two in `Q19` (values `00000005` and `00000007`). The one faulting traced start here
(`Q10`) has neither: its log ends with HID transfer counters, with no shutdown cancellation and no controller
power request, as in the comparison's three faulting starts; in `G03` and `G12` (no Start menu) the log ends
the same way. From that one faulting trace it is inferred, not shown, that the fault came before Windows
closed the HID devices' reads and before the controller's driver was asked anything for the shutdown; the
trace does not exclude earlier activity of the driver as a cause.

**The conditions the failures shared**, as far as these counts go (neither is shown to be necessary in
general, and no USB HID device is shown to be enough):

- A USB tablet was present at every fault and hang. A fault or a hang came in 11 of 140 counted starts with the
  hold and a tablet or USB keyboard plugged (`R-full`, `Q-full`, `Q-hid`, `X-hid`, `X-tab`, `X-kbd`, `U-hid`;
  15 of 160 with `U-notray`), and in 0 of 120 with the hold and no USB HID device (`X-mtp`, `X-bare`, `X-ms`,
  `NOX`, `NOX-ms`), 40 of those with the same pointer moves and click through the PS/2 mouse. With the
  tablet and no USB keyboard: `P08` and `P17`. With the USB keyboard and no tablet (`X-kbd`): none in 20, a row
  that also had no pointer input at all, so the tablet and the keyboard are not cleanly compared.
- The COM1 contention was present at every fault and hang: 0 of 20 with the tablet, the USB keyboard, the MTP
  probe and the same windows but nothing contending for COM1 (`R-nohold`).

**What the controls establish:** the fault can occur with no xHCI controller in the machine, with the tablet
and keyboard served by Windows' own UHCI driver rather than this driver (`U02`; and the hang `U04`), and with
the xHCI98 USB Tree's tray never started (`U-notray`, its icon absent from the taskbar: `V03`, `V17` and
`V20` faulted and `V14` hung). Those controls kept the installed package and ran `XHCITR /report` in the
session, so they do not show independence from the package as a whole. Also not needed for it: the MTP probe
and its cancels (`X-hid`, `X-tab`); the stick (here and in the comparison). The helper `xhcihlpr.sys` is never
installed on 98 SE. The `XhciShutdownReset` and `XhciIntelShutdownToEhci` values (`tuning.md`, the
shutdown-related ones) were not varied: both act after the controller's power request, which no faulting
traced start reached. The fault screen names where the exception surfaced, `VWIN32`; that is not shown to be
its cause.

**Also seen**, beside the counts:

- A Start menu that did not open to Ctrl+Esc, the desktop otherwise drawn (nine starts, every one with a
  tablet or USB keyboard plugged, `U04` among them under Windows' own UHCI driver). Seven of them also resisted
  a tablet click on the Start button; `R06` and `Q07` came before that fallback and had no click tried. The
  ACPI power button then did not shut the guest down in 150 s (`P17`, `H23`, `U04`, `V14`).
- Keys lost or held through the USB keyboard on xHCI98: Win+R's Win key held (`H01`, `H04`, `K06` and, by the
  same check, the other eleven `X-kbd` starts not counted), a lost R (`H20`). Not compared under the UHCI
  driver, where the Run dialog after the keyboard's plug was opened by the tablet click.
- `P06`: "A fatal exception 0E has occurred at 016F:BFF87164." on the screen 300 s after the start, before the
  session (nothing plugged yet); seen once.

**Reading.** The fault was reproduced after COM1 contention with a USB tablet present, including with no xHCI
controller and the tray never started. This does not attribute it to Windows 98 SE or clear the package as a
whole; it shows that this driver serving the HID devices is not required for it. No code path of this driver
is implicated by these readings and no driver change is proposed. The counts are small and conditional on a
completed session (above): 0 of 120 and 0 of 20 bound the other conditions only roughly, and no rate here is
compared between configurations or drivers. What is not established: what the guest's own components do at
that offset, which this project does not read.

**Open items** from this reading, unattributed and not closed by it:

- A Start menu that does not open with a USB HID device plugged, and the four starts that then did not shut
  down by the ACPI power button (`P17`, `H23`, `U04`, `V14`); seen under this driver and under Windows' own
  UHCI driver; cause not read.
- Keys lost or held through the USB keyboard under this driver (the Win key held after Win+R, a lost key);
  cause unresolved; not yet compared under Windows' own USB driver.

Not run: real hardware; a guest never given the xHCI98 package; the tablet alone under the UHCI driver; the
shutdown-related values. Every guest of this item is stopped (`pids.txt`, which has a second stop line for two
of its starts, `prepE` and `N37`); the overlays and the kit's copies of the probe files are throwaway.

## 50.27 The updated interrupt function taken into `xhci98.sys` and `xhcicm.sys`, and the thread starts' join (2026-11-16 to 2026-11-17)

Branch `w50-msiun`, from `3.5.1.0` at `42483176a`, worktree `E:\xhci98-wt\w50-msiun`. Every reading below is from
QEMU guests on development host A, in two passes on the tip's builds: the first on 2026-11-16 (fresh overlays in
`E:\xhci98-vm\p50\msiun\`, every start and stop in its `pids.txt`, QMP ports 47710 to 47719), the second on
2026-11-17 (`E:\xhci98-vm\p50\msiun-legs\`, its own `pids.txt`, QMP ports 47740 to 47751, headless; other guests
were running on the host at the same time, so no reading here is a timing). The owner restarted the host between
the second pass's last legs and the 8.1 leg (50.27.8); nothing was running then that a result below depends on.

### 50.27.1 What was found before the change

- **The vendored header** was the previous copy exactly (the same bytes, CRLF); nothing of this tree's own was in it,
  so nothing had to be carried over. The new copy differs from it by the end call `MsgIrqUninitialize` (with its
  pure decision, the event kind 129, the call number 12 and a count of quarantines) and by comments that mark the
  library's attach mode reserved; no other line.
- **`xhci98.sys`** has its own unload routine (`hcdUnload`). The library is started once per image at the first
  mode-4 start that can resolve (`hcdMsgNtLibrary`), and right after it the image is kept for the boot
  (`HcdDmaKeepImage`, `DriverUnload` cleared), which design record 15 section 4.5.3 gave as the answer to the
  mapping having no release. So no unload ever followed a library start, and there was no page left behind per
  load: one page per boot, with the image.
- **`xhcicm.sys`** is resident from `DriverEntry` on 2000 and later: the link-state registration (`CmNvlinkInit`,
  task 45.31) clears `DriverUnload` at the first load of each boot and gives it back only if that registration
  fails. The message path also makes it resident before its first claim. So `cmUnload` runs on NT only after a
  failed link-state registration, and there was no page left behind per load there either.
- So "left one page mapped at each unload", as the roadmap row was first written, holds for neither driver as it
  runs.

### 50.27.2 The decision and the change

The design (record 15 section 4.5.21, revision 16; record 21 section 4.5.19) was reviewed before the code. It first
proposed dropping `xhci98.sys`'s keep at the library's start so that the end call would release the page at the
unload. The owner chose the conservative form (2026-11-16): **the call is defensive only**, and nothing of either
driver's behaviour changes. A further reason recorded against the alternative: a start whose
`ObReferenceObjectByHandle` of the new controller thread failed waited only for `ThreadExited`, which the thread
sets before its call into `PsTerminateSystemThread` (`hcd_ctl.c`), so an image free to unload after a library start
would have exposed that window (50.27.3 closes it).

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| bf7c8a4b5 | the design note, first form (records 15 and 21) |
| 8b1050ad5 | the note revised to the owner's decision |
| 8fe241db9 | the vendored interrupt header taken again (read 2026-11-16; CRLF SHA-256 `f2b6b8f9d855cb887cca73a6483a054bc9eef3f0c0bfd0692bbf7263a74ac54b`, LF `74f1afce5a7b51c8b74d3cfbb4d0613c772d03a1687f52020367804bc251467b`); `hcdUnload` ends with `HcdMsgNtEnd` and `cmUnload` with `CmRirqNtEnd`, each calling `MsgIrqUninitialize` and writing its status on the qemu flavour's port-`0xE9` channel (`msg4.uninit`, `cm.irq.msg.uninit`, the latter through the new `CmLogImageNote` of `cm_log.c`); `IN_USE` recorded, never retried; both seams refuse a header without the call; `legal-provenance.md` section 2a and `source-files.md` |
| c7b9584fa | the notes: the call defensive only, in both drivers; the thread-start residual; the full list of claim-release statuses |
| 8f4febf8e .. 494a85e91 | the thread starts' join (50.27.3) |

Which unloads reach the call: in `xhci98.sys`, every unload of an image that never started the library (98 SE, ME,
Vista and later, any `XhciInterruptMode` but 4, a mode-4 image whose starts were all refused before the library was
called), where it returns `OK` having done nothing; no unload of a started copy reaches it. In `xhcicm.sys`, only an
unload after a failed link-state registration (abnormal); there it ends a copy started with no claim, or does
nothing. No new import; no new registry value an INF writes; no user-visible string.

No host test was added: the change has no pure decision of its own (the library's decision is the header's, with
its own host tests); a pure helper for the dropped alternative was written and withdrawn with it.

### 50.27.3 The thread starts' join (folded in by the owner, 2026-11-16)

On 2000 and later a start whose `ObReferenceObjectByHandle` of a new system thread failed used to end with only the
thread's exit event waited for, which the thread sets before its call into `PsTerminateSystemThread`, so an unload
in that window could run under it. The creator now keeps the handle and retries the reference every 10 ms until it
holds the thread object (fail-closed: no limit, the first failure logged at once, the failures counted), so every
stop joins on the object: the controller thread and the idle callback thread of `xhci98.sys`, the
connection-manager thread of `xhcicm.sys`, the adapter worker of `xhcinet.sys`. The completion workers and the
finer-timer thread already did, retrying at their join; the 98 SE and ME path is unchanged; `xhcinet6.sys` has no
system thread. Design record 15 section 4.5.21, "The thread starts' join"; records 21 section 4.5.19 and 35
section 18.

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| 8f4febf8e | the design, before the code |
| bd5049aa7 | the design revised after its review: fail-closed stated, the first failure logged, the system-process restriction, the network driver |
| 710017a27 | the code (`HcdThreadReference`, `cmThrReference`, `netRefThread`) |
| 717d08ca3 | one qemu forcing value per thread (`XhciQemuThreadRefCtl`, `...Cb`, `...Cm`, `...Net`: that many reference attempts refused before one is let through) |
| 494a85e91 | the qemu-only late start failure (`XhciQemuStartFailLate`) |

The forcing values are read by the qemu flavour only and written by no INF; the release flavour passes zero.

How the guests were given the build: the installer refuses a qemu-flavour driver in a package folder ("A driver
from another build is in the folder"), so every guest installed this branch's x86 release package
(`make-package.ps1 -Flavor release`, laid out by family, with this tree's installer and USB Tree; in the second pass
staged from the tip's gated outputs, every image equal to the gated record) and then had the qemu-flavour images of
the build under test copied over the installed ones (`Q.BAT`) before its next start - on 98 SE and ME after the
first restart that followed the install, then a Shut Down and a cold start - and before anything was read the guest
compared the installed files with the qemu images byte for byte (`H.BAT` / `HP.BAT`, `fc /b`).

### 50.27.10 What these legs do not show, and what was not run

What the legs show: the end call reached and returning `OK` on every unload of an `xhci98.sys` copy that never
started the library (XP and 2000), mode 4 and the connection manager's ring interrupt behaving and residing as
before the change, each forced reference failure retried until the thread object was held and then run and torn
down cleanly (the controller's, the idle callback's and the connection manager's threads on XP or 2000, the network
driver's on XP and on 2000), the 98 SE and ME start, disable and enable unchanged, and then (the forcing values set after that) a start and
a shutdown unchanged with them present,
the network driver's start, stop, disable, enable and unload with traffic on XP and 2000, and `xhcinet6.sys`'s on
8.1 against XP (no thread there; a no-regression reading). They do **not** show:

- **The actual unmapping.** No unload that reached the call had a mapping to release: every one returned `OK`
  having done nothing, and an `xhci98.sys` copy that started the library never unloads (by design, 50.27.1).
- **The abnormal connection-manager unload** - the library started, no claim followed, then `cmUnload` - which is
  the case `xhcicm.sys`'s call exists for. It needs a failed link-state registration on NT; no injection was added
  for it, and it was not run.
- **The abandoned idle-callback context joined by the unload.** No client in these guests keeps its idle callback
  running at a teardown, and the qemu flavour has no injection that holds one (`XhciQemuSuspHoldDx` leaves a pended
  Dx IRP unclaimed, record 15 section 7.2.12's leg T3, which is not a callback in progress); a deterministic reading
  needs an injection in the callback path, a driver change. Not run.
- **The window the join closes.** The forcing values refuse a fixed number of attempts and then let one through, so
  the legs show the retry and the join on the held object; they do not reproduce an unload running during a
  thread's exit, nor a reference that never succeeds (the start then waits without limit, by design).
- **Standby**: not shown (50.27.9); standby after a forced failure in the same boot was not run (`xps3b`, an
  overlay of `xpa`'s disk, had booted and hibernation was off when the host restart stopped it; not taken up again,
  since the resume it needs cannot be read here); standby on 2000 not tried (36.28 and 49.16: it never suspended
  with the Cirrus adapter, and has no logon without one).

Not run, besides:

- `xhcinet.sys` on 98 SE and ME (its 9x start is unchanged) and on Vista and 7 (the same NT path as XP's).
- Device Manager remove and refresh of the controller on 98 SE and ME (disable and enable were read).
- The comparison build `42483176a` on 98 SE and ME: nothing above differed from what the 9x path is written to do.
- Free system PTEs on 2000 (no reader on that guest).
- Any amd64 image in a guest (built and gated only), and any real hardware.

`E:\xhci98-vm\p50\msiun-legs\pids.txt`). NUSB 3.3's files were used only in the 98 SE kit and guest; they were deleted from the kit after
the legs. The overlays, logs and screendumps are kept.

## 50.28 A departed device's pending transfers on Windows 2000 and later: `XhciUnplugComplete` (2026-11-16 to 2026-11-17)

Branch `w50-gone`, from `w50-cancelst` at `bf635c320` (50.26 before its merge), worktree `E:\xhci98-wt\w50-gone`:
the design note `a73230791`, revised `f7bfb93fd`, the code and host vectors `87dfe2c02`, the setting's contract
`11ac55097`, the note as built `f5175df0f`; then the merge of `3.5.1.0` and the changes made before this branch's
merge (50.28.9). Design record 13 section 10.5.3. Every reading below is from QEMU guests on development host A
(q35, `qemu-xhci`, TCG, headless), the `qemu` flavour unless said. The evidence is under
`E:\xhci98-vm\p50\gone\` (the first pass: the storage legs before and after, and HID, hub and audio after) and
`E:\xhci98-vm\p50\gone-legs\` (the second pass: the legs the first did not reach); each has a `STATE.md` and a
`pids.txt` with every start and stop.

What it is. Up to this change `xhci98.sys` held a departed device's pending transfers on every system until their
client cancelled or aborted them or Windows closed the device's PDO (record 13 section 10.5), a rule made for 98
SE, whose HID driver asked again without end when its transfers were failed early (27-V.1). A storage driver that
sends nothing more after the unplug then waited out its own time-out before the removal went on (50.26's legs,
"Seen at `0` and at `1`"). Now, on Windows 2000 and later, once the device's PDO is unlisted and the relations
request issued, a held transfer is completed `DEVICE_GONE` (`USBD_STATUS_DEVICE_GONE`, `0xC0007000`, the IRP
`STATUS_DEVICE_NOT_CONNECTED`, `0xC000009D`), and one the drain reaches after it is not held; 98 SE and ME keep
holding; a contained controller's holds stay. `XhciUnplugComplete`: `1`, the default, that rule; `0`, held on
every Windows, as before. Read at the controller's start; the snapshot's log carries `urb.gone.value` (the value
read, `FFFFFFFF` when absent) and `urb.gone.policy` (`00000001` at once, `00000000` held).

### 50.28.1 How the readings were taken

- **Times** are host-measured: `dcwatch.py` samples the guest's debugcon file every 0.1 s from just before the
  unplug and `dctime.py` gives each line the time its bytes first appeared. "SR" is the PDO's SURPRISE_REMOVAL
  (`PnP minor=00000017`), measured from the unplug. A completion time is the first non-success URB completion of
  the per-request log (`XhciQemuStageFault` 8) before the SR. The XP and 2000 overlays of the first pass had no
  per-request log, so their rows have SR times only.
- **The storage leg**: a `usb-storage` stick under `usbstor` (or the `usb-uas` drive where the row says),
  unplugged by QMP `device_del` while a 50 MB copy to it runs - on 8.1 and 10 when the drive's block statistics
  show I/O moving, on Vista and 7 once the per-request log shows the bulk traffic, on XP and 2000 once the
  write-through copy has passed 4 MB. "Fast" is a copy that failed within about a second; "slow" one that ran to
  the client's time-out.
- **Per request** (second pass, `urbcheck.py`): every `urb: in` paired with its `urb: out` by IRP address over a
  debugcon segment. "Double" is an `out` with no `in` since the last `out` of the same IRP (bug check 0x44 would
  follow); "pending" an `in` with no `out` by the segment's end.
- **The sweep's line** in the build the legs ran, `hcd: departed PDO reported, serial/gone/cancelled=SSSSGGCC`, was
  written only for a PDO whose sweep claimed something, with the `DEVICE_GONE` and `CANCELED` counts; it did not
  count the holds left to a closing, which record 13 section 10.5.3 point 11 asked for (added before the merge,
  50.28.9). Where a closing released holds, the evidence is the per-request log and the closing's own line
  (`hcd: held URBs released, count`).
- **Builds in the guests.** First pass: before, the `qemu` x86 package of 50.26's gated build at `2087fcbe1` (the
  hold on every system); after, the `qemu` x86 `xhci98.sys` of a gated run of `f5175df0f`'s sources recorded
  `dirty=1` (`1E465964...`), copied over the installed file (on 10, whose loaded image cannot be overwritten,
  renamed first) and Windows restarted. Second pass: the gated `qemu` builds of `f5175df0f` (`dirty=0`): x86
  `155FDF64...`, amd64 `BA2B7ABF...`; and the comparison build, the gated `qemu` x86 build of `2087fcbe1`
  (`1B63520A...`; `2087fcbe1..bf635c320` changes nothing under `src\` or `scripts\`). Each second-pass guest
  compared its installed `xhci98.sys` with the build's after the restart that loaded it (`fc /b`, or the kit's
  `T5 /cmp` on 2000 and XP: identical).
- `XhciCancelStatus` was as 50.26's legs left it in the first pass (`1` on Vista and 10, `0` on 7 and 8.1; it does
  not change a `DEVICE_GONE` completion) and deleted (its default) in the second.

logged before it. A completion's status does not say whether it was the transfer pending at the unplug, completed
by the drain, or a request submitted after the unplug and refused. At `0` slow and fast repeats came by chance, as
before. A "fast, not captured" repeat is one whose copy failed within a second but whose watch began after the

### 50.28.4 The non-empty sweep, containment and resume (second pass)

An unplug reports its PDO before the drain, so the sweep it runs finds nothing held; these legs make the drain
come first. `XhciQemuInject` fault 5 (a real Run/Stop clear: the health poll reads HCH, the recovery's invalidation
drains every device through `hcdDropAll` before each PDO is reported), written while a tablet and a keyboard
(interrupt reads always pending), a copy loop to a stick and `usb-audio` playing were active, as each row says.

| System | Label | Fault, stage | Activity at the fault | Sweep lines (serial: gone) | URB in / out, double | SR / REMOVE | After |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7 SP1 | S1 | HCH, 8 | HID; copy ended; no audio | 2 (2:2, 1:2) | 194 / 194, 0 | 3 / 3 | devices back |
| 7 SP1 | S2 | HCH, 8 | HID; audio (229 iso in 8 s) | 3 (2 each) | 358 / 360, 0 | 5 / 5 | devices back |
| 7 SP1 | S3 | HCH, 8 | HID; audio; copy transferring | 3 (1, 2, 2) | 4994 / 4996, 0 | 5 / 5 | HID works; the copy in flight failed |
| 7 SP1 | G2 | HCH, `0x38` (both delays) | HID; copy loop; audio not playing | 1 (1:1); `qemu.sweep.gap` x4, `qemu.abort.gap` x7 | 1246 / 1246, 0 | 5 / 5 | HID works |
| 2000 SP4 | S1 | HCH, 8 | HID; audio (825 iso in 8 s); copy ended | 3 (2, 2, 3) | 378 / 380, 0 | 5 / 5 | HID works; the stick's new devnode Code 31 (50.28.8) |
| 2000 SP4 | S3 | HCH, 8 | HID; audio; write-through copy in flight | 4 (1, 2, 2, 3) | 63450 / 63453, 0 | 5 / **4** | HID works; the copy loop resumed |
| 2000 SP4 | G1 | HCH, `0x38` | HID; audio; copy in flight | 1 (13:1); `qemu.sweep.gap` x4, `qemu.abort.gap` x2 | 1174 / 1178, 0 | 5 / **4** | HID works |

The out counts above the in counts are completions of IRPs that went in before the segment began. In G1 and G2
the SURPRISE_REMOVALs landed inside the sweep's 3 s delay and their closings completed the holds first (`C0000120`
after `held URBs released`, counts 2, 2, 4 on 2000), leaving the claim one IRP. On 2000, `usbaudio.sys`'s
resubmissions were refused `C000009D` until its SR (87 to 159 isochronous refusals per run), and on 7 in G2 21
SELECT_INTERFACE requests on the audio PDO were refused inside the delay, bounded by its SR.

- **Containment** (fault 6, `USBSTS` all-ones, then cleared and the controller restarted; HID, copy and audio
  active; D1 on 7 and on 2000), and the same with the copying stick unplugged 1.2 s before it (U1, on 7 and 2000;
  on 2000 only the containment fired, its HCH overwritten before the thread read it): the controller contained
  (`containment RELEASED`), no sweep line, and every held request completed `C0000120` at its PDO's closing, none
  `DEVICE_GONE` after the containment; in U1 the stick's bulk read completed `C000009D` at once first (an ordinary
  departure, reported before the containment). No double, no IRP left pending; SR / REMOVE 5 / 5 on 7, 5 / 4 on
  2000. **Not reached**: a departure whose teardown Stop Endpoint failed before a containment, record 13's exact
  case. No built injection fails a teardown Stop Endpoint (fault 26 answers Context State Error, taken as stopped).
- **Comparison build on 2000**, the same fault with copy, audio and HID (C1, C2, `1B63520A...`): SR / REMOVE 5 /
  **4** in both, no double, no sweep (it has none). So the REMOVE not seen in S3, G1, D1 and U1 is older than this
  change; the devices came back at the same locations and worked, and which PDO did not get its REMOVE was not
  read.
- **A resume's re-initialization** (2000, `XhciResumeKeep` 0, tablet, keyboard, stick and audio; hibernate, cold
  start on the same overlay): SR / REMOVE 5 / 5, no sweep line (nothing was held at the report), 11 `C000009D`,
  3579 in / 3575 out (4 pending: the new HID reads), no double; tablet, keys, the stick's read-compare and audio
  pass afterwards. The resume path reported and swept with nothing to claim.

One cold boot per row, each after a boot that copied the row's driver in (`fc /b`: no differences);

(the first ME boots, on a newer overlay, met the Add New Hardware wizard for the audio location; their audio rows

  completed `C0000120`/`00010000` at the REMOVEs, 0.2 to 1.4 s after their port changes where those were timed; no
  sweep line, no double, no `DEVICE_GONE` on a HID PDO, no resubmission; the replugged keyboard opened the Run

### 50.28.7 Two readings followed up

- **Windows 10, one URB refused at the dispatch** (`C000000D` / `80000200`) after the HID replug: the first pass's
  log (`legs-nt10\w10\debugcon-a1.log`) names function `0x32`, `CONTROL_TRANSFER_EX`, sent to the device newly
  enumerated after the replug, refused by `hcdSubmitUrb`'s default case as an unsupported function; the comparison
  build's logs carry the same refusal. It is not a departure's completion. Which driver sent it was not read.
  `hcd_urb.c`'s comment there, which said no target sends one, is corrected (50.28.9).
- **2000 at `0`, a copy unfinished 190 s after the unplug** (the first pass's third repeat): repeated three times on
  the tip at `0` (each result awaited up to 240 s): the copies failed 11 to 12 s after the unplug, the held bulk
  read completed `C0000120`/`C0010000` and the SR came at 9.4, 9.7 and 10.2 s (`usbstor`'s own time-out, the old
  rule); the comparison build three times: the same, SR at 8.7, 9.4 and 10.1 s. The 190 s case did not recur in
  six; it stays unresolved, and whether the build before this change does it too is not settled by them.

- No double completion in any segment checked, and no REMOVE that held up a re-enumeration.
- 2000: one REMOVE of five not seen after a halt recovery with a copy in flight, on the tip and on the comparison
  build alike (50.28.4).
- 2000: the stick's new devnode at Code 31 once, after the first halt with the stick idle (tip S1), cleared by a
  replug; not seen in the tip's S3, G1 or the resume, nor in the comparison's C1 and C2. No cause read.
- ME: the screen black for the rest of one boot after a stick leg (tip, default), the driver still logging the
  tablet's reads and the shutdown completing. 50.26's legs met a black ME desktop once too; seen once here in five
  ME boots with a stick leg. Not attributed.

`3.5.1.0` at `c74e462e0` (roadmap rows only) merged first (`32b8e1f35`). Then two changes, each compiled only under

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `f373c85ca` | the per-request log's event line, `urb: event seq/irp/event/serial`, in the log's own sequence and written under the cancel spin lock where each step is decided: `01` an abort's horizon recorded (the IRP is the ABORT_PIPE), `02` the abort's seeded delay ended (its release next), `03` a report's relations request issued (its seeded delay next), `04` the claim marked the PDO, `05` the forced drain of bit 21; `10` held by the drain, `11` held (another hold), `12` not held because the PDO is marked (its caller completes it `DEVICE_GONE`), `13` completed `CANCELED` at the hold, `14` declined (its caller completes it); `20` claimed `DEVICE_GONE`, `21` claimed `CANCELED`, `22` left by the claim; `30` released by an abort, `31` by a closing, `32` cancelled by its client (`hcdParkedCancel`), `33` by an unproven stop, `34` by a 9x select. `XhciQemuStageFault` bit 6: the abort delay (bit 4) 6 s instead of 0.5 s; bit 7: the report's delay (bit 5) 75 s instead of 3 s, longer than a storage client's own time-out; bit 20: an invalidation's drop does not drain every device first, so each device is drained at its record's free, after its report and claim; bit 21 (with 20): each device is drained between its relations request and its claim instead. HCRST has taken every slot by then, so neither drain is earlier than the hardware's release |
| `0295dca74` | bit 22: a report records an every-pipe abort horizon on each PDO it reports, after its relations request and before its delay, as an ABORT_PIPE whose handle cannot be placed records one (`HcdIoAbortMark`), and once the claim has run releases what that horizon covers (`HcdIoParkedRelease`), as that abort's release would; event `06` marks it. For a system whose clients send no abort between a hold and the closing (below) |

### 50.28.12 What these legs do not show, and what was not run

They show, in the emulator, at the default: on 2000 and later a drive unplugged during a copy failing at once with
its SR within about a second, where the build before held it to the client's time-out in some repeats on each
system it ran on (2000, XP, Vista, 7, 8.1 and 10 under `usbstor`; XP x64 was not run before); HID, hub and audio
clients ending and coming back at a replug;
the sweep claiming held requests after a halt recovery with no double completion and every PDO's REMOVE that came
completing; a contained controller's holds staying held; 98 SE and ME unchanged against the comparison build; and, by
the per-request log's event lines (50.28.10), which path completed each held request in the orderings the design
names - a claim after an abort's horizon (on 7 with bit 22's forced horizon), a client's own cancel inside a seeded
delay, a closing inside one, and the drain on either side of the claim - each request completed once; and
(50.28.11) a drive under `xhciuas.sys` and a stick behind a hub failing at once on every system from 2000 to 10 and
coming back at the replug, and on ME at `0` a request in flight at the unplug held until its client cancelled it,
completed once.
They do **not** show:

- **That the slow case cannot happen at the default.** None of 42 repeats was slow; the earlier build's slow
  repeats came by chance at each unplug.
- **Which request a `C000009D` was**: the transfer pending at the unplug, completed by the drain, or a request
  submitted after it and refused. The status is the same. In the first pass, on 2000 and XP no completion was
  logged at all (those overlays had no per-request log); in 50.28.10's legs the event lines name the path for each
  held request on every system they ran on.
- **A count of holds left to a closing above 0**: the count line was written in 50.28.10's legs with its gone and
  cancelled counts, and no claim there found a closing PDO still holding (`left` 0 in each).
- **A client's own ABORT_PIPE before a claim on an NT 6 system**: on 7 no client sent one to a PDO between its
  drain's hold and its closing; the claim after a horizon was read there with bit 22's forced horizon, and with a
  client's own abort (`usbaudio.sys`) on 2000 only. Accepted as a reduction (owner, 2026-11-17, 50.28.11).
- **A drain on a second processor racing the claim**: bits 20 and 21 move the drain to either side of the claim on
  the controller thread; a drain on another processor landing there by itself was not caught. The mark and the hold
  are both taken under the cancel spin lock (record 13 section 10.5.3 point 6), which the host vectors do not run.
- **The controller's stop**: its drop (`hcdDropAll`, which drains every device and reports each PDO as the
  invalidation does) is not reached on NT in the emulator, where Windows removes the children before it disables a
  controller (record 13 section 10.5.3 point 14); the invalidation's drop stands in for it. Accepted as a reduction
  (owner, 2026-11-17, 50.28.11).
- **A failed teardown Stop Endpoint before a containment** (50.28.4): no injection reaches it. Accepted as a
  reduction (owner, 2026-11-17, 50.28.11).
- **Why** 8.1's and 10's PnP held the SR behind an outstanding request; what Vista's to 10's `hidclass.sys` and
  NT's `usbaudio.sys` do beyond the outcomes above; other makers' drivers.
- **The 2000 case at `0`** left unfinished at 190 s (50.28.7).
- **Why** Windows' UAS driver on 8.1 had its SURPRISE_REMOVAL about 5 s after the unplug when its stream requests had
  completed at 0.3 s (50.28.10).
- **Why** a `usb-uas` drive put back by `device_add` after an unplug did not work on Vista (its requests cancelled
  one after another by `xhciuas.sys`, no volume), on both emulators, when the same drive taken off and put back by
  its `attached` property came back every time (50.28.11).
- **ME after a held request**: the REMOVE came only once ME's "Disk Write Error" box was answered, and in two of five
  trials the keys sent ended at a black screen with no REMOVE and a shutdown that never ended (50.28.11, as 50.28.8's
  ME anomaly). Whether the build before this change does the same with a request held at the unplug was not run; on
  ME the rule is unchanged (the hold), and the black screen is not attributed.

Branch `w50-trkey` from `3.5.1.0` at `c74e462e0`: `f934ffe7d` (design record 25 section 25, committed before
the code), `b4a3d6e1c` (the code, the host suite, `xhcitr\README.TXT`, `snapshot-reader.md`,
`source-files.md`), `0aca6ce27` (section 25's quoted texts as built). The gated builds ran once, at the end, on
`0aca6ce27` (below). The legs ran this tree's `XHCITR.EXE` and `XHCITR64.EXE` built from `b4a3d6e1c` (SHA-256
`8c492a17...89146e` and `ce63f4de...6fb5d6`; `0aca6ce27` changes two documents only) beside the released
`3.5.0.0` package, whose drivers this item does not change. Development host A, QEMU TCG, headless, the q35 bases
in `E:\xhci98-vm\q35-bases\`, fresh overlays; the evidence (serial logs with every report and device report,
screendumps, the kit and its scripts) is under `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\trkey\`, with a `STATE.md` and a `pids.txt`
holding every start and stop.

What it is. Save Report (and `/report`) lists under each USB device's node every value of the device's driver key
and of the driver keys of the devnodes below it, read only, whatever driver each has; the device report
(`/snapshot`'s `.DEV` or `.D<k>`) has a section "USB devices' driver keys" with the same entries. Every value is
listed with its name, type and size, and with its data unless withheld (section 25 item 3). Before this item the
report read four values of that key (`DriverVersion`, `InfPath`, `MatchingDeviceId`, `ProviderName`) and never
reached a devnode below the device, and the device report listed only the devnodes `xhci98.sys` and `xhciuas.sys`
drive (section 25 item 1). Save Report's own snapshot run and an all-controllers run's later controllers pass
`/nokeys`, so a report carries each key once. The first version (`b4a3d6e1c`, the host suite and legs just below)
took only a device's immediate `&MI_` children in the report and every `USB\` devnode in the device report; it was
reviewed and revised ("Revised", below): both outputs now take one walk.

### The withheld names as whole words (the owner's decision, 2026-11-17)

Superseded the same day by the owner's rule in the next section; this section is left as it was read.

Commit on `w50-trkey`: `3047d5a43` (`tr_reg.c`, `test_trreg.c`, design record 25 section 25 item 3 and section 13,
`xhcitr\README.TXT`, `snapshot-reader.md`). The owner decided that the test which withholds a value's data by its
name matches every term as whole words, so that diagnostic values such as `HotKey`, `KeyIndex` and `TokenCount` keep
their data. The rule as it now is: a name's words are its runs of letters, split at every character that is not a
letter and where a small letter is followed by a capital; a value's data is withheld when the name's last word or
words, case ignored, spell one of the terms (`PASSWORD`, `PASSWD`, `PASSPHRASE`, `PWD`, `SECRET`, `CREDENTIAL`,
`PSK`, `TOKEN`, `LICENSE`, `SSID`, `PIN`, and the compounds `PASSKEY`, `WEPKEY`, `WPAKEY`, `WPAPSK`, `PRODUCTKEY`,
`NETWORKKEY`, `LICENSEKEY`, `DEFAULTKEY`, `PRESHAREDKEY`, `PINCODE`), with an `S` or none and only characters that
are not letters after it, or when `KEY` is the name's one word (`Key`, `Key0`, `KEY_1`, `Keys`). No rule that treats
`Key` as one word among the rest shows `HotKey` and withholds `WepKey1`, since both are a qualifier and `Key`; so the
secret-bearing uses of `Key` are named as compounds. What it now lets through that the earlier rule withheld: a term
not at the name's end (`PasswordHash`, `PskValue`, `SsidList`), a name in capitals alone that runs words together
(`USERPASSWORD`), and a name ending in `Key` that is neither `Key` alone nor a compound (`EncryptionKey`, `TrkKey1`).
Section 25 item 3 has the table of 78 names and their outcomes, the suite's table with the empty name beside them.

Host suite: `test_trreg` 254 checks, 0 failures (`3047d5a43`, run on its own, and again in the gated build below):
the table, each name with its outcome, and the guard-page bounds for the new rule (short names, among them `aKey`,
`HotKey`, `Keys` and `Pins`; 16383-character names ending in `Key` after a word and as the one word, in `Pin`, in
`Password` and `Passwords`, beginning with `Key`, and a term cut by the name's end). Against `tr_reg.c` of `7ca39a282`
(a scratch copy, not tracked) the same suite has 25 failures, each a name whose outcome the decision changed (19
table rows, `password_hash` to `*SSIdleTimeoutScreenOff`, and six bounds: `aKey`, `HotKey`, `KeyX`, `Keys`, `Pins`
and the long name ending in `Key`); none faulted at the guard page.

**The guest legs above were run with the earlier rule.** Of their observed lines the new rule changes one name:
`TrkKey1`, written on the NT legs (the first version's XP and 10 x64 legs, and the 2000 leg), was shown
withheld there (`"TrkKey1" = REG_SZ, 4 bytes: withheld (its name suggests a key or password)`) and would now be
shown with its data (`"TrkKey1" = REG_SZ "abc"`), since `Key` is not the name's one word
and `TrkKey` is no compound. `TrkPassword` stays withheld on every leg. Every other value name the legs listed
(Windows' own, the test values, the sibling driver's `Uac2*` values, the hubs' and the audio keys' values) keeps
its outcome: none was withheld before, and none is now.

### The owner's rule for the withheld names (2026-11-17)

Commit on `w50-trkey`: `05c4bd2db` (`tr_reg.c`, `tr_reg.h`, `test_trreg.c`, design record 25 section 25 item 3 and
section 13, `xhcitr\README.TXT`, `snapshot-reader.md`). The whole-word rule of the section above was reviewed and
revised: it showed every name ending in `Key` but a few compounds, and `PasswordHash`, `PskValue`, `SsidList` and
`USERPASSWORD`; and its `KEY` test spelled the word across other characters, so `K_e_y` and `K1E2Y` were withheld
although neither has the word `Key`. The owner then decided the rule (2026-11-17), recorded in section 25 item 3 in
place of the earlier wording:

- The terms are `KEY`, `PASSWORD`, `PASSWD`, `PASSPHRASE`, `PWD`, `SECRET`, `CREDENTIAL`, `PSK`, `TOKEN`, `LICENSE`,
  `SSID`, `PIN` and `PINCODE`. A name's data is withheld when, case ignored, a term's letters stand side by side
  beginning at the start of a word (words split as before: at each character that is not a letter, and where a
  small letter is followed by a capital), or anywhere in a word with no small letter, and after them come only, in
  order and each if there: an `S`; characters that are not letters; one of the words `HASH`, `HEX`, `VALUE`,
  `MATERIAL` or `LIST`, with an `S` or none.
- The harmless names `HotKey` and `ShortcutKey` (whole, case ignored, with an `S` or none) are shown: a draft list
  for the owner, `HotKey` being the owner's own example of a hot key setting and `ShortcutKey` the same setting's
  other name.
- So every name whose last word is `Key` or `Keys` is withheld but those two (`EncryptionKey`, `PrivateKey`,
  `CdKey`, `SharedKey`, `AuthKey`, `ApiKey`, `SessionKey`, `TrkKey1`), as are `PasswordHash`, `WpaPassphraseHex`,
  `PskValue`, `KeyMaterial`, `SsidList`, `Key1Value` and `USERPASSWORD`; `HotKey`, `KeyIndex`, `TokenCount`,
  `Monkey`, `Keyboard` and `*SSIdleTimeout` are shown; `K_e_y` and `K1E2Y` hold no term and are shown. What it
  lets through: a term followed by a word not of a secret's form (`PasswordString`), a term inside a word with small
  letters (`WPAPsk`, `userpassword`), a term spelled across other characters (`Pin Code`), and a secret under any
  innocent name or in a blob. What it withholds that is no secret: a capitals-only name ending in a term's letters
  (`MONKEY`, `TURKEY`), `KeyValue`, and every other name ending in `Key`. Section 25 item 3 has the table of 105
  names and their outcomes.

### Three spellings added to the owner's rule (2026-11-17)

Commit on `w50-trkey`: `9fce09f90` (`tr_reg.c`, `test_trreg.c`, design record 25 section 25 item 3,

### Findings, and what they are

- On `32ec266b6` the snapshot (`/dump`, x86 and amd64) did not print the reset-reason ring or the reason
  counters after the terminal line: "reset reasons 0 bytes at +0: not a shape this build reads" on 98 SE, 2000
  and XP x64, while the status request and the Tree showed the records. Fixed in `65a41906d` (the snapshot
  header's composer); retaken on 2000 and XP x64 above: the lines are printed.
- Code `24` outcomes 1 and 2: no `qemu.inj.noop.retired` note appeared in the ring; the engine gave the command
  up at the time-out (debugcon: "command: timed out, aborting TRB=01CDB0E0", then "hcd: controller reset
  requested, calls=00000002", then "event: command completion, code=00000019"). Outcome 5 showed no
  `cmd.abort.stuck` note. Each of 0 to 6 ended in `cmd.givenup` and one recovery (reason 2). This is today's
  wait, not a fault of the layer: the thread's command wait gives up at the same 5 s the watchdog fires and
  requests the reset, whose invalidation drops the layer's events and marker; the outcomes are step 3's to
  show (design record 17 section 4.15.9, "What step 2 alone shows of the outcomes", `754e1c96d`).
- Code `26`: the stick's `device_del` after the latch gave no `qemu.inj.disarm` note (the disarm was noted
  when the disconnect came on a running controller); after `T5 /restart` nothing was withheld. A latched
  controller's thread inspects no port, and every start clears the injection state (`HcdInjStart`); the
  design now says so (`754e1c96d`).

- Code `24` to `2B`'s lifecycle corrections were not read on their own in a guest: no guest action produced an
