- Code `26` behind a hub: only its refusal was read (`0x81`); nothing else is claimed for a hub's port.

- L1: a full reading after code 05 #3 (only XHRQ, so the four requests fitted the ten-minute window); a fifth

### The fatal-attribution fix, revision 23 and the merge with `3.5.1.0` (2026-11-17)

`w50-devfault-s12` continued from `407ec3258` (the engine's rewrite correction `c4d28ce81` still not in it):

- `54dedaf37`: a fatal Transfer Event names a device only when the engine matched it to a TD queued on that
  device's pipe. Both engines set `Fatal` before they resolve the pointer, so an Event Lost or Undefined Error
  inside no TD of an open pipe was staged with that pipe's device as the one involved. The engines now carry
  `Matched` out (set once the pointer resolves onto a queued TD); the three wrappers stage through
  `XhciTolWhyStageXfer`, which keeps the reset and `XFER_FATAL` with the code and names the place only when
  matched. The reset decision is the engine's `Fatal`, as before.
- `9eb5c0c58`: design record 17 revision 23 (documents only): the settlement state of a left command and its one
  admission exception, a left Enable Slot's debt kept across a successful Restore State, the returned slot's
  checks before its Disable Slot, and the narrower statement of the recovery entries' audit.
- `d71ccc252`: `3.5.1.0` merged (a merge commit). Design record 25: both sides had added a revision 37 and a
  section 25; the release branch's (task 50.29) keep their numbers, this branch's become revisions 38 to 40 and
  section 26, with every reference to it renumbered. This run sheet: the release's 50.28 and 50.29 sections
  first, then this branch's.

Host suites (`test\run-host-tests.cmd`, on `54dedaf37` before the merge): every suite passed; the new vectors
read `test_xfer` 4787 checks, `test_iso` 1540, `test_tol` 3786 and `test_snap` 580, 0 failures. The vectors:
EP0 and an interrupt pipe (`test_xfer`) and an isochronous pipe (`test_iso`), each with Event Lost and Undefined
Error - matched (`Fatal` 1, `Matched` 1), past the queued TD, a zero pointer, an address on no ring, and an open
pipe with nothing queued (`Fatal` 1, `Matched` 0, `Unattributed` 1); a refused code and a matched success; the
staging helper for the three paths (`test_tol`); and the reasons' block as the snapshot carries it, a matched
record's slot, root port, route and VID:PID at the reader's words and an unmatched record's all zero, the
reason and code kept (`test_snap`). No guest injection makes a fatal Transfer Event (code `1C` makes a Host
Controller Event), so the attribution was read on the host only.
After review, `test_iso` gained its own nonzero address on no ring (`Fatal` 1, `Matched` 0, `Unattributed` 1,
nothing retired), which the first vectors lacked for the isochronous engine: every host suite passed again,

(the string is not changed here): "recovery window  1 of 3 begun inside the window (at least ten minutes, about
22 by the clock); 0 refused".

#### Not run, or not reachable in this offer, and why

- The matched and unmatched attribution of a fatal Transfer Event: host vectors only. No forcing value makes a
  fatal Transfer Event (code `1C` makes a Host Controller Event); one that delivered an Event Lost on a pipe
  inside and outside a queued TD would.
- Code `28`: not reached (above). It needs a STALL on a device's EP0 that the thread recovers, or a RESET_PIPE
  whose Reset Endpoint the layer does not answer itself; no QEMU device tried stalls one.
- An unsuccessful submission of a withheld command (the count left unspent): not reachable by a guest action.
  A marked command's submission fails only when the controller is stopped or halted during it, or when the
  engine stays busy with another command for the busy wait's whole deadline; nothing a guest does arranges
  that. The host vectors (`test_inj`) are its record.
- The layer's addresses dropped across a Restore State or a resume: no guest slept (98 SE vetoed standby, the XP
  x86 guest has no sleep state, the 2000 guest's display driver vetoed it before). QEMU reports every Restore
  State failed, so a resume there is a reinitialization in any case; the HCRST of each recovery is the lifecycle
  the legs show, consistent with the clearing without demonstrating it.
- D3 (the request answered while the controller is powered down): needs a guest that sleeps; none did.
- The not-started answer (flag 1 clear): the door is absent until the start completes, on 2000 and 7.
- Outcomes 0 to 6 beyond what the earlier legs read: each ends in the thread's give-up and one recovery before
  step 3 (design record 17 section 4.15.9); No Op retirement, ordinary-completion precedence, a stuck abort and
  the divergence latch are not reachable in this offer.
- 98 SE: code 05 once, not four times (the window was spent while the wizard had the keys).

### The command engine's rewrite correction (branch `w50-abortfix`), code 24 outcome 3 on the emulator (2026-11-18)

Branch `w50-abortfix` at `cacf7759b` (`w50-devfault-s12` `64188a465` and the command engine's correction: a Command
Ring Stopped event that names the TRB the same abort's Command Aborted event just ended rewrites it as a No Op
Command), gated x86 build (qemu flavour): `xhci98.sys` sha256 `59949cbe...fa46`, `XHCITR.EXE` `a093acdb...f587`.
The comparison: the `w50-devfault-s12` (`d71ccc252`) qemu x86 `xhci98.sys` `f54d24ed...d209` (read with the same
`XHCITR.EXE`). Development host A, QEMU 11.1.0 TCG, headless, one guest. Evidence under
`E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\devfault4\legs-af\ev\AF\`; every start and stop in `legs-af\pids.txt`.

An ordinary completion keeps its precedence in the sense of the specified race between a completion and CA: a
command's own completion that arrives before the Command Aborted ends it, a Command Aborted after it matches nothing
and keeps nothing, and the stop does not take that TRB for the rewrite. That is not a tolerance of duplicate events:
a completion arriving after the Command Aborted that ended the same command is counted unmatched and does not
reverse the loss, and one arriving at that address after the rewrite is taken as the rewritten No Op's, since the
engine matches a completion by its address alone (design record 17 section 4.15.9, "What it does not change").

Gated builds of `cacf7759b` (clean tree): x86 `all` and amd64 `all -amd64` each "BUILD + GATES PASSED (release
qemu)", exit 0 (13:04 and 12:19), every gated record `commit=cacf7759b...`, `dirty=0`; `xhci98.sys` x86 release
`142F0559...7A0B`, x86 qemu `59949CBE...FA46`, amd64 release `B0BA76BF...56A7`, amd64 qemu `E475D889...0676`. The
host vectors are `test_ring`'s `test_stop_abandoned` (which command a Command Ring Stopped abandons: the
outstanding one first, the same abort's aborted TRB when the stop names it, nothing when it names the next TRB or
no abort is kept); the gated builds ran the host suites.

#### The comparison: the s12 file, outcome 3

The s12 file copied, cold start ("FC: no differences encountered", 542,394 bytes; "recovery window 0 of 3").

| Step | What was read | The line | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `24`, outcome 3, count 1 (`0x01240331`) | note ring | `qemu.inj.hang=24030103`, `cmd.timeout.trb=0B010000`, `qemu.inj.outcome=00000302`, `cmd.givenup=0B010000`, `ctrl.failed.why=0203010B`, `ctrl.recovered=00000001`, then `enum.port.slot=03010001` | the same notes as the abortfix file |
| | debugcon | "command: abort not written, CRCR=7F201001", "command: timed out, aborting TRB=7F2010E0", "event: command completion, code=00000019", "event: command completion, code=00000018", "hcd: controller reset requested, calls=00000001" | no "stopped on the abandoned command, rewritten as No Op Command" line: the position adopted with no rewrite |
| | `/dump`; the stick | "recovery window 1 of 3", "reset requested: CMD_NO_VERDICT at root port 3 route 00000 slot 1 [0000:0000], extra 11"; "FC: no differences encountered" | |

What changes: only the rewrite line. At outcome 3, with either file, the thread's wait gives up (`cmd.givenup`),
the reset follows and the stick comes back on the rebuilt ring, so the rewritten No Op at the withheld TRB is never
rung before the reset. That is what the loss outcomes read here (3, 1 and 2) end in; outcome 4, whose command
QEMU completes, ended otherwise (Findings). What the rewrite prevents - the aborted command running at the next
doorbell on the same ring - is not reached by any forcing value before step 3, as expected (design record 17
section 4.15.9, "What step 2 alone shows of the outcomes", which gives the reading behind it).

#### Findings

- Outcome 4 did not end in the give-up and the reset: the Address Device's own completion was matched
  ("command: completion matched outstanding TRB=7F2010E0"), then the Command Ring Stopped, then "hcd: address
  device, ok=00000001"; no `cmd.givenup`, no recovery ("recovery window 0 of 3"). Design record 17 section
  4.15.9 ("What step 2 alone shows of the outcomes") says every outcome ends in `cmd.givenup` and one recovery
  with step 2's build. Read once, on the abortfix file only (not on the s12 file). The record's sentence was wrong,
  not the engine or the layer: it is corrected (2026-11-18) to say what each outcome can end in - outcome 4 either
  passes, as here, or, when the wait's deadline is found passed first, gives up and recovers, the two 5 s
  deadlines having no fixed order.
- "command: abort not written" and "command: timed out, aborting" printed at the first abort of each start
  (outcome 3, and outcome 4 after the restart), not at outcomes 1 and 2 later in the same start; the
  `cmd.timeout.trb` and `cmd.givenup` notes were there each time.
- The outcome notes read `00000302`, `00000102`, `00000201`, `00000400` for outcomes 3, 1, 2, 4.

#### Not run, and why

- The next command's execution on the same ring after a rewrite, a wrap and the outstanding-No-Op divergence: not
  reached by the forcing values before step 3, since at each of the loss outcomes read here the thread gave up and
  the reset rebuilt the ring before another doorbell (why that holds for every forced abandonment: design record
  17 section 4.15.9, "What step 2 alone shows of the outcomes").
- An invalidation or a rebuild between the Command Aborted and the Command Ring Stopped: not deliberately
  exercised. The layer delivers the two events on separate drain passes, so the thread's give-up and the
  recovery's invalidation can fall between them as well as after both; no leg arranged either order (at outcome 3
  here the debugcon shows both events, then the rewrite, before "hcd: controller reset requested").
- Outcome 4, and outcomes 1 and 2, on the s12 file: not asked; only outcome 3 compared.

### The command engine's rewrite correction: the engine driven on the host, the guest's reach, and the gated builds of `7916b9e3b` (2026-11-18)

Branch `w50-abortfix` at `7916b9e3b`: `3.5.1.0` merged in (`089c5ab1a`, the tree unchanged), the host suite `test_cmd`
(`d55c31e08`), the documentation corrections above (`7916b9e3b`), then this section. No production source changed
since `cacf7759b`. Development host A.

#### The engine driven on the host: `test_cmd`

`test_ring`'s `test_stop_abandoned` pins the selector alone. `test_cmd` compiles `src\xhci_cmd.c` and
`src\xhci_init.c` into its own file by `#include`, unchanged, and answers their outward calls itself: the registers
of `xhci_pci.c` (CRCR answers CRR while the command ring runs, a CA write is counted, a pointer write is latched
only while CRR is 0), the command doorbell, which a modelled controller answers by executing the command ring from
its own dequeue and cycle state (following the Link TRB and its toggle) and posting one Command Completion Event
per command it runs, the timer service (the kept callback is the watchdog's rung 1, which writes the real CA), the
reset request and the slot layer (counted). Events reach `XhciCommandEvent` through a drain that holds the
controller lock, as the HCD's does. The model is this project's reading of 4.6.1 to 4.6.1.2, not a controller.
714 checks, 0 failures, in the host runner and in both gated builds.

| Scenario | Driven through | Read |
|---|---|---|
| An ordinary completion before the Command Aborted or the stop | submit, rung 1, the command executed, then the stop at the next TRB; again with a late Command Aborted and a stop naming the completed TRB | matched with its own code, the slot layer not told lost, aborting until the stop, no rewrite; the late Aborted unmatched and nothing kept; the stop on the completed TRB read as a position the ring cannot hold (divergence 4), not taken for the rewrite (3) |
| Aborted, then Stopped at the same TRB | submit (the doorbell fetches nothing), rung 1, the Aborted, the stop | the kept address and its generation; no submit admitted between; rewritten once as a No Op Command (type 23), cycle bit kept, parameters cleared, the position adopted, no reset |
| Aborted, then Stopped at the next TRB; the same with an earlier rewrite unanswered | as above, the stop one TRB on | adopted, nothing rewritten, the kept address consumed; with the marker set, no second-abandonment divergence |
| A Command Aborted with no abort of the engine's outstanding | the Aborted while the command is pending | nothing kept; the stop naming it adopts with no rewrite |
| Stopped without Aborted | the stop at the command, and at the next TRB | rewritten through the outstanding path; adopted and lost |
| Stopped before a late Aborted | the stop, then the Aborted | unmatched, nothing kept, the engine stays idle, the marker stands |
| An ordinary completion after the Aborted | before the stop; and after the rewrite | before: unmatched, the slot layer not told success, the stop still rewrites; after: taken as the rewritten No Op's (the marker cleared), and the No Op's own completion then unmatched - the engine matches by address alone, which is not a tolerance of duplicate events |
| The kept address's lifetime | the invalidation (`XhciControllerBeginQuiesce`); a new start (`XhciCommandInit` and `xhciProgramCommandRing`) with no stop between; `xhciRestoreState` over a modelled halted controller | cleared at each; after the start, a new command at the same address and in the same generation (the start resets both) completes, and a stop naming it is divergence 4, never the old abort's rewrite |
| The generation | the generation moved by the test between the Aborted and the stop (no live path does this: a submit is refused while aborting, and an invalidation and a start clear the address) | another generation's address not taken |
| Taken once | the stop that rewrites, adopts or diverges | consumed each time; a second stop is divergence 1 |
| The second abandonment | a rewrite left unfetched, the next command aborted at its own TRB | the reset asked for, staged as the engine's divergence with reason 2 and counted (`CmdDiverged`), the engine left aborting and refusing submits, the second TRB untouched |
| A refused rewrite | the earlier No Op's completion with a code no command carries, whose retirement flushes the ring and reclaims the aborted TRB, then the stop naming it | reason 3, the reset, left aborting, the TRB untouched |
| The restart after a rewrite (in every rewriting scenario above) | the next command submitted on the same ring | no CRCR write (no rebuild); the controller executes the No Op at the stopped TRB once and never the command it replaced; the No Op's completion retired by its marker, not unmatched; the next command executed, its own completion matched and reported to the slot layer; nothing left outstanding; and the ring stays in service for the command after |
| The wrap | the aborted command at the last usable TRB before the Link; the stop naming the Link; a rewrite on the second lap (cycle 0) | rewritten at the last TRB with the Link's type, cycle and toggle kept, the controller crossing the Link and the next command running at index 0 on the new lap; the Link address read as index 0, adopted, nothing rewritten, the Link untouched; cycle 0 kept and fetched |

Each scenario was checked against a deliberate break, in a scratch copy of the tree (none committed): the suite
failed under every one.

| Break | Checks failed |
|---|---|
| The stop never takes the aborted TRB (the correction undone) | 42 (the rewrite, the restart, the wrap, the divergences) |
| The selector ignores where the stop names | 3 (the next TRB with a rewrite unanswered: a divergence) |
| The invalidation does not clear the kept address | 1 |
| The start's and recovery's rebuild does not clear it | 2 (the field, and the new start's stop read as the old abort's rewrite: divergence 3 for 4) |
| The restore's rebuild does not clear it | 1 |
| No generation comparison | 2 |
| Not consumed at the stop | 5 |
| Kept when no abort of the engine's is outstanding | 3 |
| The generation not recorded with it | 43 |
| Rewritten as the transfer ring's No Op (type 8) | 11 |
| The rewritten No Op not recognised by its marker | 13 |
| No second-abandonment divergence | 12 |
| A refused rewrite adopts instead of resetting | 1 (the reason) |
| The Link address not read as index 0 | 7 |
| The rewrite not keeping the cycle bit | 9 (the second lap) |
| An Aborted matching nothing still keeps its address | 2 |
| A completed command's address kept for the stop | 3 |

Observed by the same suite, outside the specified sequence and unchanged: a second Command Ring Stopped naming the
second abandoned TRB, arriving after divergence 2 has asked for the reset and before the reset lands, finds no abort
kept and nothing outstanding and adopts the position, leaving the engine idle with that TRB unrewritten - the same
whether the TRB was ended by a Command Aborted (the correction's path) or was still outstanding at the first stop
(the path before it). The reset already requested is what ends it.

#### The guest's reach before step 3

The restart the correction is for - the rewritten No Op executed, then the next command on the same ring - is not
reached in a guest by any forcing value before step 3, and no forcing value was added to reach it. Read from the
code (`hcd_enum.c`, `hcd_svc.c`, `xhci_cmd.c`, `xhci_init.c`, `hcd_ctl.c`): every command the forcing values withhold
is a thread command (`hcdCommand`, where the layer's mark is taken), and the thread's wait ends at the command's
loss (`XhciSlotCommandLost`, from a Command Aborted naming it, a stop ending it while outstanding, or an
invalidation) or at its 5 s deadline with `cmd.givenup` and `HcdSvcRequestResetWhy`, which marks the controller
failed under the controller lock before the thread goes on; `XhciCommandSubmit` refuses a failed controller; the
recovery runs on the same thread, invalidates the engine and rebuilds the command ring (`xhciProgramCommandRing`)
before `XHCI_EXT_FLAG_INITIALIZED` goes up again. So no doorbell reaches the ring a rewrite was made on. The one
command abandoned with no waiter is the start's and the recovery's asynchronous No Op self-test, which the layer
cannot withhold (its hook is in `hcdCommand`) and whose rewrite would be a No Op over a No Op. Once step 3's
settlement lets the wait outlast the abort, the restart becomes a guest leg; until then it rests on `test_cmd`.

#### The legs on the tip's binary: code 24 on 7 x86, 98 SE and XP

Branch `w50-abortfix` at `7916b9e3b` (gated x86 build, qemu flavour, dirty 0): `xhci98.sys` sha256
`dd9eb983d9f4e0e6b22dd3e2d9857bdd7dd5e6e0d62f0f9455c7a16403676e49` (542,538 bytes), `XHCITR.EXE`
`7d6c17a82044345e24c0affdf47a85212177e8ab7f881a817748e76a08c9fe07`. Functionally the driver of the earlier legs'
`cacf7759b`; the commits since are a host test suite and documents. Development host A, QEMU 11.1.0 (7 x86) and the
snapshot QEMU (98 SE, XP), TCG, headless. Evidence under `E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\abortfix2\legs\ev\` (`W7`, `W98`,
`XP`); every start and stop in `legs\pids.txt`.

Each step: `XhciQemuInject` set (on 7 and XP a REG_DWORD in HKLM `...\Services\USB` by `reg add`; on 98 SE a .REG
file by `regedit /s`; the sequence byte changed each time), then the stick (`usb-storage`, QEMU `xh.0` port 3 = the
driver's root port 3) unplugged and plugged by QMP (`device_del`, `drive_add` where needed, `device_add`); the
debugcon read from a byte mark taken before the step, `XHCITR /dump`'s note ring read as the records added since
the previous dump, and on 7 and XP a file written to the stick, read back and compared (`fc /b`).

How the debugcon prints, which bears on what can be read: the lines "command: stopped on the abandoned command,
rewritten as No Op Command, TRB=...", "command: abort not written, CRCR=...", "command: timed out, aborting TRB=..."
and "command: completion matched outstanding TRB=..." are printed only when the value differs from the last one
printed at that line, and at most 32 times per driver load (`XHCI_DBG_VALUE_CHANGED`, `src\xhci_dbg.h`). A later
abort at the same TRB address in the same load prints none of them; the `/dump` text carries no count of the
rewrite.

### Findings

- **F1.** The first replug after a root port's hold releases the hold (`qemu.inj.disarm`, `tol.loc.rearm=<port>04`)
  but the device is not enumerated: the port stays Failed for 70 s or more, and a second replug enumerates it. Read
  6 times (2000 twice, 98 SE, ME, XP, 7); at a hub's port one replug was enough. Section 4.15.9's leg 1 expects one.
- **F2.** A device hot-plugged behind a hub whose EP0 is withheld from its first enumeration (`25`, port byte bit
  7) ends as departed - three attempts, each `enum.xfer.gone=00000603`, then "hub port given up, disabled" - with no
  `dev.fail.alone`, no spread and no hold; the same fault at a root port, or after a published device's cycle at a
  hub port, holds the place with reason 4. Read on 2000 and 98 SE, once each. Section 4.15.5 asks for the
  `UNANSWERED` cause and the hold. The hub port's words, captured afterwards on 2000 (a single reading of each case,
  "F2's hub port status and change words" at the end of this step's legs): the reset that enables the fresh
  device's port leaves the C_PORT_ENABLE QEMU's hub raises with it, which the path check reads as a departure; read
  as an emulator artefact, and nothing is proposed in the driver.
- **F3.** A test-hook gap, not a driver behaviour: bit 7 of the argument of `24` and `25` is not acted on
  (`xhci_inj.h` still reserves it), so the late path's Stop Endpoint runs and section 4.15.9's leg 7 - a scratch
  taint, a failed Disable Slot, an interrupted or failed settlement - cannot be forced.
- **F4.** A root hub started while a debt stands has every root port's Enable Slot refused ("Failed, cause no
  slot"); when the debt then clears with no reset, nothing looks at those ports again, and no device is listed
  until a further root hub disable and enable. Read once on 2000 and once on XP; when the debt ended in an HCRST
  instead, the recovery enumerated everything.
- Recorded, not a finding: the hub whose port was being enumerated had its interrupt endpoint taken from Running
  to Disabled by its Disable Slot with no Stop Endpoint first (5 of 5); every other hub got a Stop. QEMU's trace
  cannot show whether a TD was on that ring.

Every leg that depends on F1, F2, F3 or F4 stopped at the finding; the others ran on. The three parts follow.

#### Findings

1. **A root port held with reason 4 is released by the first replug but the device is not enumerated until a second
   replug.** After `device_del`, about 6 s, `device_add` at the held root port: `qemu.inj.disarm` and `tol.loc.rearm=<port>04`,
   two port status changes, and nothing more for 70 s or longer (2000: the `/dump` port table "7  Failed  ?"); a second
   `device_del`/`device_add` enumerates at once. Read four times: 2000 (mouse, port 7; usb-audio, port 7), 98 SE (mouse,
   port 6), ME (mouse, port 6). At a hub's port (ME, after `24` behind the hub) one replug released and enumerated.
   Design record 17 section 4.15.9 leg 1 expects the device to enumerate after the one `device_del`/`device_add`.
2. **A device plugged behind a hub whose EP0 transfers are withheld from its first enumeration is read as departed, not
   held.** `25` with the port byte's bit 7, persistent, then a fresh plug at the hub's port: each attempt
   `qemu.inj.hang=25080600 enum.xfer.gone=00000603`, three attempts, "enumeration failed, port/cause=01010004", "hub port
   given up, disabled"; no `dev.fail.alone`, no `tol.spread`, no `tol.loc.hold` (2000 and 98 SE, one reading each). The same
   withholding at a root port (98 SE R5) gives cause 8, two attempts and the hold; at the hub port after a published device's
   cycle (2000 H) it gives `dev.fail.alone`, cause 8, two attempts and the hold. Section 4.15.5 asks for cause `UNANSWERED`
   and the hold for a present device with no PDO. (The hub port's words for both cases were captured afterwards: "F2's
   hub port status and change words" below.)
3. **Argument bit 7 of `24` and `25` is not acted on in this build.** `xhci_inj.h` still reads "For 0x24 and 0x25, bit 7 is
   reserved for the recovery command that follows (not acted on before step 3)"; with `0x1F258891` the late path's Stop
   Endpoint ran (QEMU trace "usb_xhci_ep_stop slotid 5, epid 1") and the device was cycled with no reset. Design record 17
   section 4.15.9 leg 7 (the stop hangs, Disable Slot hangs) and item 5's scratch taint and failed Disable Slot quarantine
   therefore cannot be driven. A test-hook gap, not a driver behaviour.

Readings recorded only (not findings):
- One physical device can add up to three "failed alone" records: the cycle's and one per aborted Address Device or pre-PDO
  attempt (2000 R: `dev.fail.alone` three times, "failed alone 3 device(s) this start"; the count in the note runs on
  across places: root port 7 `tol.spread=00070001` to `00070003`, then hub place 0x101 `tol.spread=01010004`).
- The new `/dump`'s root port table names the new cause as "?" ("7  Failed  ?").
- The Tree showed the held hub port 8.2 (2000 H) as "[Port 2, USB 1.1] (empty)", "Connection: no device connected", while
  `/dump` read "hub 0 port 2 ... NOW HELD, the device stopped answering" and the device was still attached; a held root port
  showed "(on hold)". Single reading.
- 98 SE: with the `usb-audio` device installed and attached, `XHCITR /dump` did not return and the desktop went black with
  an hourglass (EIP c000a882); stopped by QMP. The 50.26 legs recorded the same class of stop with `3.5.0.0`.
- ME: the first overlay of the ME image stopped at boot with "Error: 0E : 0177 : BFF62170" on the `3.5.0.0` driver; a
  fresh overlay booted normally. Single reading, before the new file was copied.
- `T5 /dis` of a `usb-kbd` answered "ok 0" on 2000 (keyboards were not disabled), and a `T5 /restart` with the FS keyboard
  attached failed its disable ("ok 0"); with it removed the restart worked.

#### Not run, or not reachable, and why

- Item 3: the stream families (UAS recycle, streams close, resend), the function unconfigure (`usb-audio` presents one
  function), the selective-suspend rewind (`XhciSelectiveSuspend` 0) and the resume keep's replay (no standby: the 2000
  image's display driver vetoes it, 98 SE vetoes it): not reached. `28` and `29` were reached through EP0's STALL recovery
  and an ABORT_PIPE's cancel, not through a RESET_PIPE.
- Item 5: the scratch taint and the failed Disable Slot's quarantine (Finding 3); `InputHeldSlot` (needs an aborted
  re-address under RESET_PORT, which `2B` stops before).
- Item 8: the release flavour's code 24/25 fault (no injection in that flavour); a fresh install with no earlier driver key
  (the 1 was written by an update over a deleted value).
- Item 2 on 2000: the device moved to another port (read on 98 SE only); a SuperSpeed device at a USB 3 root port.
- Items 4, 6 and 7: the third part's.

#### Slips

- 2000 H: two copy loops ran at once and the log kept only 11:19:43 onwards (17 of 17 identical), after the fault; the
  copies during the hub fault are not evidence. 98 SE H98: the two copies' markers were matched from the earlier leg (the
  wait looked at the whole serial log); those two are not evidence (fixed: the waits read only new output).
- 2000 O: the first outcome-3 value was written with nine digits and read back as `FFFFFFFF`, which fired as `FF` (CLEAR);
  rewritten as `0x21240731`.
- 2000 U: the controller key was set to 7 by a mistyped command before the first (refused) `/force` and put back to 0 before
  the successful one.
- 98 SE: one `ISO.BAT` write timed out and wrote nothing (redone on the next boot); one boot read "absent" where machine-wide
  deleted plus controller 0 was meant (the controller 0 came on the next boot).
- No permission refusals.

### 50.30 step 3 (device isolation): the guest legs on XP, XP x64, Vista, 7, 7 x64, 8.1, 8.1 x64, 10 and 10 x64 (2026-11-18)

Branch `w50-devfault-s3` at `73f6cf55b`, the gated builds named above (x86 `all`, amd64 `all -amd64`,
`dirty=0`; `bin\HASHES.txt`). Development host A, QEMU TCG, headless, at most three of these guests at once beside
the other parts' guests (up to eight QEMUs on the host), so no timing below is a performance reading. Emulation only:
every reading is of QEMU's `qemu-xhci` (1B36:000D) and its emulated devices; the controller's abort behaviour is the
injection layer's (design record 17 section 4.15.9), never QEMU's. The q35 machine of `q35-bases\launch-q35.ps1` with
its pinned QEMU build (`q35-bases\bin\asm4242-20261110-docks`), except leg U2 on 7, which ran on a second QEMU test
build, `p50\uasother\emu25c` (`aaf9768b...`), whose `usb-uas` device takes `x-clear-halt=on`. Evidence: `E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\devfault9\w2\ev\<guest>-<leg>\`; every
start and stop with its pid in `w2\pids.txt` (30 START, 30 STOP: four of the stops are not QMP stops and say so - QEMU's
own exit at a QMP command, and three hibernation power-offs, 7 once and 10 x64 twice).

#### Item 1: the final qemu driver installed, `tol.isolate`, the recovery-status request

Settings on every guest: `XhciDeviceIsolation` absent in both keys, `XhciTolerance` 1 (`tol.value=00000001`), the
controller key's `XhciSelectiveSuspend` 0 (XP from boot e: 1, for leg P); `XhciQemuStageFault` 8 (left by an earlier
task) deleted before the legs; 8.1 x86 keeps a machine-wide `XhciCancelStatus` 0 and 10 x86 a machine-wide 1 (left by

Not reached, and why:
- Stream open (`hcdCfgStreamsOpen`): `xhciuas` opens its streams right after the select configuration, so `27` (the
  next Configure Endpoint, armed at the thread's once-a-second read) takes the select's command first (XP's enable
  above) and the device is removed before its streams open.
- Stream recycle on a contract endpoint (RESET_PIPE of a UAS stream endpoint): needs code `21` read at the
  controller's start and a refused command with its data-in posted (50.20's legs used the emulator's
  `x-ata-passthrough-refuse` and third-party programs sending ATA PASS-THROUGH); these guests have no such program.
- The read-back's resend (`hcdCfgDeqReadBack`, `29`): `29` takes the next Set TR Dequeue of the device, which is the
  cancel's own, before any resend.
- Function unconfigure with a command: the function's driver unconfigures it only after its stream stops (alternate 0,
  no endpoint); during a stream the disable first sends ABORT_PIPE and RESET_PIPE, whose recycle meets `27` first.
- Resume replay: shown on 10 x64 only (above); XP offers no hibernation, 7 did not resume, and standby is offered by
  none of XP, 7, 10 x64 (display driver) or the earlier legs' 98 SE and 2000, so no standby-resume replay was read.

In none of the legs above a `ctrl.failed` note or a recovery (XHRQ "recov 0").

#### Findings

1. **F1 confirmed on XP and on 7, one reading each:** after a root port held with reason 4,
   `device_del`, 6 s, `device_add` gives `qemu.inj.disarm=00000005 tol.loc.rearm=00000504` and nothing more (90 s on
   XP, 76 s on 7); a second replug enumerates at once. At a hub's port one replug was enough (XP and 7).
2. Nothing on these systems contradicted the design; F2 and F3 were not re-investigated (`25` with the
   port byte's bit 7 was used only on a published device's cycle, which ends held as designed).

Readings recorded only:
- `XHRQ.EXE` opens `\\.\HCD9` on XP and on XP x64 (under WOW64); on Vista, 7, 7 x64, 8.1 x64 and 10 x64 it opens no
  `\\.\HCDn` (its output only "XHRQ done"); `XHRQ.PS1` reads `\\.\XHCI98HC0` on 7, 8.1, 10 and their x64 forms. Vista
  has no PowerShell, so the request's words were not read there.
- QEMU's stock `usb-uas` refuses CLEAR_FEATURE(ENDPOINT_HALT) at the streams close ("not taken ... outcome=...0001",
  three endpoints), so a disable of the UAS drive closes no stream with a command on the stock emulator.
- On 10 and 8.1 the loaded `xhci98.sys` cannot be overwritten ("The process cannot access the file because it is being
  used by another process"); it was renamed first.

#### Slips

- Two kits were rebuilt while their guests (XP a, 7 a) ran, so their transfer drives lost files; both guests were
  restarted before any leg (the copies already made were checked identical after the restart).
- XP I3: `T5 /dis 46F4&PID_0002&MI_00` unquoted - cmd split it at `&`, so `46F4` matched the stick too: the stick's
  disable answered "needreboot 1" (it stayed started; the copy loop went on SAME) and the composite was disabled; both
  enabled again, the function enabled by its own name.
- XP c: a QMP `input-send-event` naming `device: tab1` made QEMU exit ("Property 'qemu-fixed-text-console.device' not
  found"); the release matrix was redone on boot d (the event sent without a device).
- The XP and 7 legs R, H and C first wrote their files into the same `ev\<leg>` folders; the 7 files overwrote XP's
  dumps and reports, which were fetched again from the XP guest's own `C:\W2\LOG` copies (`ev\xp-*`); the XHRQ
  outputs are in each guest's `vms\<guest>\agent.log`.
- On XP several `/dump`s waited minutes behind a snapshot window the closer did not reach (Found New Hardware and
  Files Needed windows open); the reader was changed to start XHCITR, wait for its text file and close it.
- 10 x86: the swap moved `xhciuas.sys` away before the copy, so it was missing for one boot; copied back (SAME) at the
  next; no UAS leg ran there.
- No permission refusals.

Multiprocessor HAL; `NP=2` read in the guest). Evidence: `E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\devfault9\w3\ev\<leg>\` (`steps.txt`,

Guests: 2000 = an overlay of devfault3's `k2\p2k` (the SMP base + the test agent + `3.5.0.0`), the new file copied
over the installed one by the agent and taken up by a cold start; XP = an overlay of `p50\gone-ev\nt5\xpa` (XP SP3 x86
with an earlier qemu build of xhci98 and the test agent), the new file copied by `PREP.BAT` and taken up by a cold start.
Both: `XhciDeviceIsolation` absent, `tol.isolate=0000FF03`, XHRQ "iso FFFFFFFF/1/1", `/dump` "isolation value none (the
default 1), mode 1, listed yes, applies yes". Triggers: `XhciQemuInject` in the machine-wide key (`T5 /setdw`); devices
plugged and unplugged by QMP; routes by the agent (`T5 /dis`/`/en` of `USB\XHCI98_ROOT_HUB` or of the controller's
`PCI\VEN_1B36&DEV_000D` devnode), by `rundll32 powrprof.dll,SetSuspendState` (XP hibernation) and by QMP
`system_powerdown`. The timed legs (`tools\leg_rh.py`, `leg_e6c.py`, `leg_pw.py`, `leg_sd.py`) arm the fault, plug the
target, watch the debugcon for the target's `hcd: enable slot` (Address Device's `24`) or `hcd: address device, ok=1`
(Evaluate Context's `2A`) line, and raise the route at once.

How a left command is made here: `24` (or `2A`) with the port byte `0x88` (any device behind a hub at root port 8) and a
fresh plug at a hub port, so the withheld command is the thread's own enumeration command (pre-PDO), and the route
arrives inside the 5 s (outcome 1: the layer's clean abort at the watchdog) or 10 s (outcome 5: no stop event, rung 2's
`cmd.abort.stuck` and the engine's reset) the command stays outstanding. `cmd.left` reads TRB type 31:24, slot 23:16,
endpoint 15:8 and the route bits 7:0 (`HCD_LEAVE_*`: 08 the root hub's removal, 10 a device power IRP).

QEMU's `usb-hub` is a full-speed hub with no speed property (`-device usb-hub,help`: attached, msos-desc, pcap,
port-power, port, ports, serial), so no full/low-speed device behind a high-speed hub (no TT: the debugcon's
"behind hub, TT slot/port/MTT=00000000" for every device here) can be built in this emulator.

| two debts one after another | 2000 boot b: E6B, E6D, E7A in one controller start, each settled (two by the settlement, one by the HCRST) before the next; E7E, E7G, E7H, E7J and E7M after later controller starts in the same guest boot (E7B's restart, the disables and enables of E7C and E7D, and the restarts after E7K and E7L); XP: X6A, X7G, X7A in one controller start, in that order | each `cmd.left` followed by its own `cmd.left.settling`/`settled` or `cmd.left.hcrst` before the next `cmd.left` | shown |

Not driven in item 7, and why:
- Mode 4's query-stop (refused or cancelled), and an interrupted settlement after it: Windows sends `IRP_MN_QUERY_STOP_DEVICE`
  only for a resource rebalance; nothing reachable from user mode here asks for one (the controller's PCI resources
  cannot be changed in Device Manager under ACPI, and XP has no PCI Express native hot plug for a new device to force
  one). Not driven. A harness gap, not a hardware requirement: the driver's query-stop path exists, and a controlled
  rebalance or a kernel test arrangement could drive it; whether to build one or defer it is open.
- A settlement command interrupted by a route, and an ordinary settlement failure (followed by a power interruption
  and the resume): both need a Stop Endpoint or Disable Slot of the settlement withheld or failed; no injection code
  withholds either (`24`/`25` bit 7 is not acted on in this build, F3), and QEMU completes both. Not driven; a
  test-hook gap, owed in emulation once the hook exists.
- A successful Restore State with owed records, and the restore guard: QEMU's xHCI declares no FSC (the driver's
  "save: declined"), so every resume here is a reinitialization (HCRST), and an HCRST resume does not reach the
  guard. Owed on a controller that declares the save capability; this emulator's controller does not.
- The shutdown route on XP: the blind XP guest ignored the power button (XSD). On 2000 (E7S) it was reached through
  the shutdown's device power IRP; the shutdown worker's own bit (`HCD_LEAVE_SHUT`) is not separable from it here,
  and the direct transition (`HCD_LEAVE_DIRECT`) and the controller's removal bit (`HCD_LEAVE_REMOVE`, raised after the
  stop body's) were not reached on their own.
- 98 SE: see "Not run".

#### Item 4: another device's debt refusals

Partly. Shown (2000, one reading each): a mandatory reset requested by a caller while a debt stands is deferred, not
discarded, and delivered once as the debt clears. E7M: a hub's Configure Endpoint left by the root hub's removal; the
hub's bring-up keeps the reset (record 17 section 4.15.0 item 2) and requests it at once, under the debt:
`ctrl.reset.left=010B000C` (CMD_KEPT, slot 11, extra 12; `/dump` "ResetLeftSuppressed 1  thread reset requests a left
command deferred"); the settlement then runs (`cmd.left.settling=0C0B0200`, its Disable Slots in tier order) and clears
(`cmd.left.settled=00000000`), and the deferred reset is requested after it: `cmd.left.owed.reset=010B010C`,
`ctrl.failed.here=00000001`, `ctrl.failed.why=01080B0C` (once), one recovery (`ctrl.recovered=00000001`, XHRQ "recov 1
calls 1"). E7J: the same deferral (`ctrl.reset.left=010B000C`) when the engine's own reset came first: one recovery,
the HCRST dropping the deferred request (no `cmd.left.owed.reset`).

Not driven: the same for **another** device. The debts behind this reading, reconciled: 16 legs ended a wait, 12 of
them with the debt read in the note ring - 2000 E6B, E6D, E7A, E7E, E7G, E7H, E7J, E7M (eight, each with its own
`cmd.left`) and XP X6A, X7A, X7G, XP4 (four) - and four inferred from the order alone, with no ring read (the ring
goes with the controller, or with the guest at its power-off): the controller-disable legs E7C, E7D and X7C, and the
shutdown leg E7S, which supplies lifecycle ordering, not a captured `cmd.left`. In the 12 rings read no
`cmd.left.admit` note appeared, because no command naming another live device's slot was ever issued while a debt
stood; for the four inferred legs nothing about admission was read. The admission refusals that
were read are the detach's Disable Slots (each `cmd.left.owed`, the design's
"quarantined as owed", no mark) and the enumeration's Enable Slots after a root-hub start inside the debt (E7E, E7G,
X7G: `enum.port.fail=0P020000`, cause 2), and in XP4 the retry's Enable Slots under the power route (`code/slot=00010000`);
Enable Slot marks nothing by design (`XhciTolAdmitMarks`).

Why the sequence was not built with these legs' routes: a debt is taken only when a route's bit ends a wait,
and every route reachable here removes or powers down every other device of the controller before or as its bit is
raised - the root hub's removal and the controller's disable reach the driver only after the PnP manager has removed
every child (E6A, E6C: a child with a class driver even delays the removal past the withheld command), the power
transition only after every child's own power IRP, the shutdown likewise - and the debt lasts only until the engine
ends the left command (at most 5 s with outcomes 0 to 3, 10 s with outcome 5, then the engine's reset), so no class
driver of another device of this controller is left to send a RESET_PIPE, and no device to selectively suspend, while
it stands. The one route that leaves the other devices running (mode 4's refused query-stop) was not driven (above).
A RESET_PIPE, a selective-suspend Stop and the other mandatory-reset callers under another device's debt, that
device's marking (`cmd.left.admit`), its failing alone at the clearing (`XhciTolMarkedFails`) and its caller's duplicate
request therefore stay owed in emulation, through an integration harness that keeps the other devices and opens the
refusal window on purpose (the settlement runs before ordinary service, so the harness must hold the window open);
this is a harness gap, not a hardware requirement. (The deferral and delivery mechanism they share with E7M is shown
above.)

#### Findings

F4. **A root hub started while a debt stands enumerates nothing, and nothing enumerates its devices after the debt
is settled without a reset.** 2000 (E7G) and XP (X7G), one reading each: the root hub's removal leaves the Address
Device (`cmd.left=0B0A0008` / `0B0B0008`); its start follows at once (`T5 /en`, 1.1 s and 0.8 s); every root port's
Enable Slot is refused under the debt (`enum.port.slot=0P000000`, `enum.port.fail=0P020000`, then `...0101`), so each
port ends "Failed, cause no slot, retries used 1"; the settlement then completes with no reset (`cmd.left.settling`,
`cmd.left.settled=00000000`), and 20 s or more later the port table still reads "Failed no slot" at every port with a
device (2000: 1, 6, 7, 8; XP: 3, 5, 6, 8) and no hub or device is listed. Only a further disable and enable of the root
hub brought them back. When the debt ended in a recovery instead (E7E, outcome 5), the HCRST's re-enumeration did bring
every port back. Item 6 asks that every device enumerate again once the root hub is re-enabled; section 4.15.3 closes
admission to the enumeration while the debt stands but names no second look at the ports it refused once the debt
clears. The same refusal at a hub port under the power route (XP4: "hub port given up, disabled, hub/port=00000102")
was overtaken there by the resume's reinitialization. Only the legs that start a root hub inside a debt depend on it.

#### Readings recorded (not findings)

- No left can be made by the root hub's removal (or the controller's disable) while a device with a class driver is
  below the root hub: the class driver's REMOVE sends ABORT_PIPE, which the controller thread serves only after the
  enumeration's withheld attempts have ended (E6A, E6C). Every item 6 and 7 debt here was therefore read with the
  class drivers' devnodes disabled (their slots, configured endpoints and the hubs still the bus's).
- Every settlement here that took a record behind the target's hub issued no command for the left device but its
  Disable Slot (Address Device and Evaluate Context left before any endpoint was configured), so the settlement's Stop
  Endpoints read are the hubs' interrupt endpoints only.
- In 4 of 7 Address Device detach debts the first withheld attempt ended (`cmd.aborted`) before the route arrived and the second
  attempt was the left one; the PnP manager took 1 to 6 s from `T5 /dis` to the root hub's REMOVE.
- The note ring goes with the controller at its removal, so a controller-disable leg is read from the debugcon only.
- XP after a resume from hibernation: the test agent ran the hibernation command line again after each of two resumes
  (the guest hibernated three times in all, each time ending QEMU by itself); a fourth start with
  `powercfg /hibernate off` as its first command stopped it. The ring was read on that start.

#### Not run, or not reachable, and why

- Item 4: another device's part not driven (above). Item 6: the TT case (QEMU's hub is full speed only); a left with a class driver below the
  root hub (above). Item 7: query-stop, the interrupted and the failed settlement, successful Restore State, shutdown
  (above).
- 98 SE: not run. The routes exist there (the root hub's removal from Device Manager), but 98 SE has no scripted
  disable or removal: Device Manager is driven by keystrokes, and the removal must reach the driver inside the 5 to
  10 s the command stays outstanding, with no class driver below the root hub (98 SE cannot disable a devnode from a
  script either, so its mice, tablet and stick would have to be unplugged instead). Not attempted in the time.
- Items 1 to 3, 5, 8 and 9: the other parts'.

#### Slips

- 2000 E7B: `24` persistent with outcome 5 stayed armed across the recoveries it caused, so each recovery's
  re-enumeration of hub B (slot 6, behind root port 8) met it again: two more ENGINE_ABORT_STUCK recoveries and the
  latch ("controller LATCHED FAILED: the recovery window refused a fourth"). Cleared with `FF` and `T5 /restart`
  ("recovery window 0 of 3"). Not a driver reading.
- 2000 E7I: `27` persistent (outcome 1) for a plugged hub's Configure Endpoint: the command was aborted before the
  route reached the driver, and a hub keeps the reset (`ctrl.failed.why=01080B0C`, CMD_KEPT, extra 12), so two
  recoveries followed (the second at hub B's Configure Endpoint in the recovery's re-enumeration). No left; cleared with `FF`.
- 2000 E7K and E7L: `27` count 1 outcome 1 for a plugged hub with the route at the hub's configuration descriptor
  (E7K) or started 0.3 s before the plug (E7L): both times the abort came before the root hub's REMOVE, so no left and
  the hub's CMD_KEPT recovery, one each (`ctrl.failed.why=01080B0C`). E7M (2.5 s lead) placed it. Each time the
  controller was restarted (`T5 /restart`) before the next, so the window stayed below the latch.
- 2000 E7C: the first run's target was still plugged from the previous leg (QMP "Duplicate device ID"), so nothing
  fired; rerun.
- Two host shell commands of mine started an interactive Python by mistake (a stray `python -`); both were stopped
  at once, nothing reached a guest.
- No permission refusals.

### 50.30 step 3 (device isolation): F2's hub port status and change words, on 2000 SP4 (two processors) (2026-11-18)

Finding F2 asked what made the driver read a fresh device behind a hub, its EP0 withheld from the first enumeration,
as departed rather than held. This reading captures the hub port's status and change words for that case and for
the published device's cycle that does end held, side by side. **Emulation only**: QEMU's `usb-hub` model and its
own trace events; no driver behaviour was changed, and a single reading of each case.

Images: the same final qemu x86 `xhci98.sys` (`b12e77c6...92d4`, `bin\HASHES.txt` of the step-3 legs, its copy on
the transfer drive hashed again the same, `E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\devfault10\x2k-hashes.txt`), copied into a fresh
overlay of the same 2000 SMP image (devfault3's `k2\p2k`) and taken up by a cold start: "cmp: identical, 555666
bytes", `NP=2`; `XhciDeviceIsolation` absent, `tol.isolate=0000FF03`, XHRQ "iso FFFFFFFF/1/1". Development host
A, QEMU TCG, headless, one guest; the same pinned QEMU build as the step-3 legs. Two starts and two stops, each
logged with its pid and each stop led through QMP (`E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\devfault10\pids.txt`). Evidence:
`E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\devfault10\ev\F2A\` and `ev\F2B\` (`dbg.txt` the debugcon since the leg began, `qemu.txt`
QEMU's `usb_hub_*`, `usb_xhci_slot_*`, `usb_xhci_ep_*` and `usb_xhci_port_*` trace events turned on over HMP for the
leg, `notes-*`, `dump-*`). Topology: a `usb-hub` at QEMU port 4 (root port 8, QEMU's hub address 3), a mouse at 4.1;
the target a `usb-mouse` at 4.2 (hub port 2). In QEMU's words a port status of `0x101` is connected and powered,
`0x103` also enabled; a change of `0x10` is C_PORT_RESET, `0x2` C_PORT_ENABLE, `0x12` both.

| Leg | Setup | The hub port's words (QEMU trace, hub port 2) | The driver | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F2A, fresh plug | `25` port byte `0x88` persistent (`0x4125881F`), then the mouse plugged at 4.2 | at the attach "status 0x101, changed 0x1"; C_PORT_CONNECTION cleared; five reads "status 0x101, changed 0x0" (connected, not enabled); "set_port_feature ... reset"; then "status 0x103, changed 0x12"; "clear_port_feature ... change-reset" only; Enable Slot, Address Device; after the withheld EP0 transfer the path read "status 0x103, changed 0x2". The same at each of the three attempts; at the give-up "clear_port_feature ... enable", then "status 0x101, changed 0x2" and "clear_port_feature ... change-enable" | `qemu.inj.hang=25080500 enum.xfer.gone=00000503` three times, "enumeration failed, port/cause=01010004", "hub port given up, disabled, hub/port=00000002"; no `dev.fail.alone`, no `tol.spread`, no `tol.loc.hold`; `/dump` no hold | as F2's first reading: departed |
| F2B, a published device's cycle | the 4.2 mouse plugged and enumerated with nothing armed, then `25` the same (`0x4325881F`) and `T5 /dis` + `/en` of its USB devnode | before each reset "status 0x103, changed 0x0" (the port still enabled); "set_port_feature ... reset"; "status 0x103, changed 0x10"; "clear_port_feature ... change-reset"; after the withheld transfer "status 0x103, changed 0x0". At the give-up "clear_port_feature ... enable", then "status 0x101, changed 0x0" | "select configuration failed, USBD status=80000800", "cycling port, location=00000101", `dev.fail.alone=08050204`, then two attempts each `enum.xfer.gone=00000503 dev.fail.alone=08050203`, `tol.spread=01010001` to `01010003`, "enumeration failed, port/cause=01010008", "location held, location/reason=00010104"; `/dump` "hub 0 port 2 charges 1 ... NOW HELD, the device stopped answering" | held, as designed |

After each, `FF` and one unplug and plug at 4.2: "hcd: device enumerated at location=00000101" (one replug at a hub
port, as in the earlier legs).

What the words show: the one difference between the two cases is the C_PORT_ENABLE the reset leaves. In F2A the
reset enabled a port that was disabled, and QEMU's hub raised C_PORT_ENABLE with C_PORT_RESET ("changed 0x12"); in
F2B the port was already enabled and the reset raised C_PORT_RESET alone ("changed 0x10"). The driver's hub port
reset (`HcdHubPortReset`, `src\hcd_hub.c`) clears C_PORT_RESET and no other change, so in F2A the enable change is
still set when the failed transfer's path check runs, and that check (`HcdHubPathPresent`, the same file) takes a
connect or enable change as a confirmed departure: it read "status 0x103, changed 0x2" - connected, enabled, the
enable change alone - and the failure was taken as the device's departure (cause 4) instead of an unanswered
device (cause 8, the hold). The enable change stayed set through all three attempts and the give-up's disable
("status 0x101, changed 0x2" after it in F2A, "changed 0x0" in F2B) until the driver cleared it then.

How it is read: an emulator artefact, not a driver fault. Design record 13's deferral path check
(`hcdSerialDeferGone`) records what a hub's C_PORT_ENABLE means - a hub raises it when an error disabled the port,
which PORT_ENABLE clear says already - and that QEMU's `usb-hub` raises it at port resets too, with the port
enabled; this capture narrows the second to a reset that enables a disabled port. On a hub that raises it only for
an error disable, the port also reads not enabled, which the same path check takes as a departure already, so on
such a hub a reset alone does not make the F2 sequence; here it needs the model's extra change. No change to the driver is proposed on this reading. Recorded only: the
two path checks differ - the deferral's leaves C_PORT_ENABLE alone out, `HcdHubPathPresent` takes it. Not read: the
same sequence on 98 SE (the driver code is the same shared code; the 98 SE rig has no scripted agent, so the leg was
not repeated there), and any real hub. (Record 17 revision 26 revises this disposition: the transition is the
emulator's, but an enable change is sticky on real hubs, and the two path checks are to share one predicate.)

The step-3 debt legs' arrangement (a hub tree under root ports 5 or 7 and 8, every class driver's devnode disabled,

| X7G (outcome 1, three tries) | XP | `cmd.left=0B090008`, the owed records, `cmd.left.settling=0B090200`, `cmd.left.settled=00000000`; the root hub's start (its enable took 12 s) came after the settlement each time, so no Enable Slot met the debt: no deferral, and every root port enumerated | the clean-settlement resumption **not reached** (timing) |

Not reached, and why: the resumption after a **clean** settlement (E7G's arrangement) needs the root hub's start
to come inside the debt, which lasts at most the 5 s of outcome 1; on this host, shared with other work, the
removal and the start took 12 to 83 s, so the settlement always came first (XP) or no debt formed (2000). The
host vectors hold the service's parts, not the service: the machine's cause 9 and its zero retries, the resumption's
conditions (`test_enum` `test_deferred`), the obligation's protocol as the functions the driver calls - taken and
replaced, dropped once, left standing while admission is closed, served as resume, drop or stale, ended by an
HCRST's generation (`test_defer_obligation`, added after these legs) - and both clearings opening admission to the
same decision (`test_tol` `test_left_defer_open`). They do not run `hcdDeferService` itself, the inspection that
follows a resumption, or the thread and lock around them: the clean-settlement resumption stays owed in a guest on
2000 and XP, until a quieter host or an arrangement that holds the debt open with the hubs live (the query-stop
hook of record 17 section 4.15.16 E) reads it. Real slot exhaustion is not buildable in this
emulator (`qemu-xhci` has no slot-count property, `-device qemu-xhci,help`); its unchanged cause and retry rest on
`test_deferred`. The hub-port refusal by the XP4 and E7S routes was not run; X7E shows the same handling (cause 9,
no retry, no give-up) for a hub's port under the root hub's route.

#### The 98 SE hub port's replug (the lost first replug of the F1 legs)

Ten rounds on the `5935d9ec7` image, the `usb_hub_*` trace on from before the first (a hub at QEMU port 4 with a
mouse at 4.1; each round `24` `0x88` persistent, a fresh mouse at 4.2 held, `FF`, `device_del`, 6 s,
`device_add`): **10 of 10 enumerated at the first replug** (`ev\H10-98\rounds.txt`, each round's debugcon and
trace kept).

On the `23ceaad05` image, after D1's hold, three 6 s replugs at the same hub port in a row were not enumerated (the
first and third with the trace on; before the first, the `FF` had not been taken - it was written with the same
sequence byte - which does not change that no attempt was made at all), and a replug with a 20 s gap was
enumerated at once. The trace of each lost
one (`k98\ev\...\qemu-e-lines1-100.txt`, `ev\D1R2-g98\qemu-r.txt`) stops at the same point: "usb_hub_detach",
the status report, one GET_STATUS "status 0x100, changed 0x1" and its C_PORT_CONNECTION cleared; "usb_hub_attach",
one GET_STATUS "status 0x101, changed 0x1" and its clear; then nothing. The 20 s replug's trace has one more
disconnected look between them ("status 0x100, changed 0x0"), then the attach, the hold's release
(`tol.loc.rearm=00010104`) and the enumeration. So the hold stands because the stable-disconnect evidence (a
disconnected look once the interval has passed, on the driver's tolerance clock) was not complete when the device
came back, and after the reconnect no further disconnected look can come. The hub port's due look is scheduled
from the controller thread's passes (`XhciTolLocDiscDue`); why the 6 s gap was enough in every round of the ten
and in the 2000 legs, and not in these readings on an idle 98 SE, is not established. No change is proposed here;
recorded for the design (a hub-port analogue of F1, timing-dependent).

### 50.30 step 3 (device isolation): the 98 SE hub port's replug after a hold, with the tolerance clock read (2026-11-19)

The observation recorded at `a41cfe163` ("The 98 SE hub port's replug"): on 98 SE, after a hold at a hub's port,
three replugs with a 6 s gap were not enumerated, a 22 s replug was, and ten of ten 6 s replugs had been on the
`5935d9ec7` image. By the decision of 2026-11-19 taken on the owner's behalf, the observation gets clock evidence
before any repair is designed; none is designed here. **Emulation only**: QEMU's `qemu-xhci` (1B36:000D), its
`usb-hub` and `usb-mouse`, the hold made by the injection layer. Development host A, QEMU TCG, headless, shared
with other work (14 to 16 QEMU processes on the host during the rounds, CPU load 42 to 97 %, read before each round
and each replug).

Image: the gated qemu x86 `xhci98.sys` of `23ceaad05` (`12418D56...35EC`, 556,674 bytes; the driver sources of
`a41cfe163` are those of `23ceaad05`, its two later commits touch only XHCITR and the run sheet), copied into a
fresh 98 SE overlay of the step-3 98 SE image and taken up by a cold start ("===SWAP NEW SAME===", then "===CMP NEW
SAME==="); that build's XHCITR (`613DE17D...3720`); XHRQ (`895D9E83...8381`). One guest start for the copy, one for
the rounds, both stopped through QMP.

How the clock was read:
- QEMU ran with `-msg timestamp=on`, so each `usb_hub_*` trace line carries the host's time (microseconds).
- A file-only script stamped every debugcon and serial line with the host time it first appeared (0.1 s polling).
- XHRQ's header word "clock" (the tolerance clock, `Tol.Clock`) was read through the DOS box before and after each
  round, with the host time of its line.
- XHCITR `/dump` prints the guest's own local time beside the tolerance clock.

Each round:
1. The topology: a hub at QEMU port 4 (root port 8), a mouse at 4.1.
2. The hold: `25` port byte `0x88` persistent outcome 1 (`0xSS25881F`) and a fresh mouse at 4.2. Two attempts,
   each noted `dev.fail.alone=08030203` and `enum.xfer.gone=00000303`, then one "enumeration failed,
   port/cause=01010008", "location held, location/reason=00010104" and "hub port given up, disabled": D1's hold.
   Eleven rounds gave 22 failed-alone entries and 11 holds (`FIN\dump-fin.txt`).
3. `FF` with a fresh sequence byte ("qemu inject: fired=SSFF0000" read each time).
4. `device_del` of the held mouse, the gap, `device_add`, then a wait of 60 s for "device enumerated at
   location=00000101".
5. If not enumerated, a second replug with a 30 s gap.
6. In the P rounds, the guest was stopped over QMP (`stop`, `cont`) for about 5.3 s inside the gap, 1 s after the
   detach, once the driver's disconnect look had been taken. Host time then passes that the guest does not run.
   "Guest stopped" below is approximate: the difference between the host time logged just before the stop command
   was sent and the time logged just after the cont command returned, so it includes both commands' own overhead
   (the QMP STOP and RESUME events were not kept). "Guest s to the attach" is the detach-to-attach time less that.

| Round | detach to attach, host s | guest stopped, s (approx.) | guest s to the attach (approx.) | the port's next disconnected read ("status 0x100, changed 0x0"), s after the detach | result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R01 | 6.15 | - | 6.15 | +2.40 | enumerated |
| R02 | 2.18 | - | 2.18 | none before the attach | **not enumerated**; the 30 s replug: read at +2.39, enumerated |
| R03 | 3.20 | - | 3.20 | +2.46 | enumerated |
| R04 | 6.21 | - | 6.21 | +2.48 | enumerated |
| R05 | 2.24 | - | 2.24 | none before the attach | **not enumerated**; the 30 s replug: read at +2.39, enumerated |
| R06 | 6.25 | - | 6.25 | +2.38 | enumerated |
| P1 | 7.61 | 5.29 | 2.32 | +7.61 (2.3 guest s), just before the attach | enumerated |
| P2 | 10.71 | 5.37 | 5.34 | +7.58 | enumerated |
| P3 | 7.65 | 5.32 | 2.33 | +7.55 (2.2 guest s) | enumerated |
| P4 | 6.62 | 5.31 | 1.32 | none before the attach | **not enumerated**; the 30 s replug: read at +2.40, enumerated |
| P5 | 6.81 | 5.42 | 1.39 | none before the attach | **not enumerated**; the 30 s replug: read at +2.42, enumerated |

**The tolerance clock in these rounds:**
- 9.62 to 9.99 ticks per host second over the 17 intervals between two XHRQ samples with the guest running
  throughout.
- 7.39 to 9.44 ticks per host second over the five intervals that contain a stop. With the stop taken out that is
  9.7 to 10.1 ticks per second of the guest running, and none while it was stopped.
- The final `/dump`: "tolerance clock 13930 ticks" at the guest's "local time 2026-11-19 08:21:34". That is about
  9.9 ticks per guest second since the controller's start. The guest's clock was then about 30 s behind the host's,
  27 s of which are the five stops.

**What the rounds show:**
- **The due look is taken on time.** In the eight uninterrupted disconnects long enough for it (R01, R03, R04, R06
  and the four 30 s replugs) the hub port was read disconnected once more ("status 0x100, changed 0x0") 2.38 to
  2.48 s after the disconnect look. That is 24 ticks (`XHCI_TOL_STABLE_DISC_TICKS`) at 9.9 ticks per second:
  `hcdTolService` raising the port's change bit at `XhciTolLocDiscDue`, and the hub service reading the port. In the
  three stopped-guest rounds that enumerated, the read came at +7.55 to +7.61 host s.
- The release needs that read, not only the elapsed ticks: `XhciTolLocObserveChange` sets the stable-disconnect
  evidence only on an unchanged, powered, fault-free disconnected observation once 24 ticks have passed, and the
  reconnect after it released the hold (`tol.loc.rearm=00010104`, one per round in the note ring). Enumeration
  followed within 0.2 to 0.3 s.
- **A reconnect before the due look leaves the hold.** The trace of each lost replug is the trace recorded at
  `a41cfe163`: one read at the disconnect ("status 0x100, changed 0x1" and its clear), one at the reconnect
  ("status 0x101, changed 0x1" and its clear), then nothing. Once the port is connected no disconnected read can
  come, so the hold stands until the next replug.
- **Host time the guest does not run does not count.** With the guest stopped for about 5.3 s, a 6.6 to 6.8 s host
  gap (about 1.3 to 1.4 s of guest time) was lost twice (P4, P5), like the 2.2 s gaps (R02, R05). In P1 and P3 the
  read came about 2.2 to 2.3 guest seconds after the disconnect and the replug was enumerated. In R01, R04 and R06
  a 6 s host gap was enough each time. This is a qualitative demonstration with a deliberately stopped guest: it
  shows stopped time excluded from the interval. It does not reproduce the condition of the earlier boot below (a
  slow tolerance tick while the guest's time of day kept pace), and no counter was sampled inside a stop.

**The earlier lost replugs, re-read from their own records** (`E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\devfault10\k98\ev\`):
These records hold no clock sample bracketing any lost replug, so what follows are averages before a snapshot, not
measurements of the gaps themselves. The host times of the snapshots are reconstructed: the steps files log when
the leg pressed Enter for `/dump`'s message box, and `k98\tools\l98.sh` presses it 45 s after it first sees the
"===DUMP" line, polling every 5 s, so the line was seen 45 to 50 s before that entry. XHCITR prints a record's age
as ticks divided by ten, truncated, so "47 s ago" is 470 to 479 ticks.
- **The `23ceaad05` boot where three 6 s replugs were lost** (98 SE boot e; QEMU's process created at 00:31:10,
  `k98\vms\g98\pids.txt`; the lost replugs at 00:39:10, 00:46:58 and 00:48:43, the 22 s replug at 00:50:25):
  - The D3 `/dump` printed "local time 2026-11-19 00:45:02" and "tolerance clock 2851 ticks". Its Enter was logged
    at 00:46:01, so the line was seen at about 00:45:11 to 00:45:16: the guest's clock was about 10 to 15 s behind
    the host's.
  - The controller's start in that boot was not read. Assuming it came within seconds of QEMU's start, as in the
    rounds above (the settle line at 07:58:11 against the process at 07:58:08), 2851 ticks took about 830 s:
    **about 3.4 ticks per second on average, a third of the nominal rate**.
  - The same `/dump`'s failed-alone ages are consistent with that. "About 47 s ago" and "52 s ago" (470 to 529
    ticks) belong to the failures after the 00:42:11 plug, about 2.5 minutes before the snapshot, and "125 s ago"
    and "130 s ago" (1250 to 1309 ticks) to D1's failures about 6.5 minutes before it: roughly 3 to 3.5 ticks per
    second. These are coarse, the failure times being taken from the steps files, not timed.
  - If that rate held at the replugs, 24 ticks took about 7 to 8 s: the 6 s replugs (detach to attach about 6 to
    7 s) would end before the due read, and the 22 s replug after it. That is what the traces of the lost replugs
    show (no second disconnected read) and what the 22 s trace shows (one). It is a consistent explanation, not a
    measurement: two of the three lost replugs came after the snapshot, and none is bracketed by a clock reading.
  - The guest's own time of day kept pace with the host. Why the tolerance tick (a 100 ms relative timer re-armed
    from its DPC, `hcdTolDpc`) averaged about 290 ms in that boot was not established. In the rounds above, on the
    same image, it ran at about 101 ms.
- **The `5935d9ec7` boot where A4's first replug was lost** (98 SE boot b, the replug at 22:12:19):
  - Its five `/dump` pairs of local time and tolerance clock (B, A1, A3, A2, A4) give 9.9 to 10.0 ticks per guest
    second.
  - Between A2's `/dump` (guest 22:09:12, about 22:09:16 to 22:09:21 by the host) and A4's (guest 22:12:12, about
    22:13:40 to 22:13:45 by the host), the guest's own clock fell about 84 s behind in about 264 s: it ran at about
    two thirds of host time, 6.8 ticks per host second on average. That average alone gives 24 ticks in 3.5 s,
    inside a 6 s gap.
  - More locally, A4's newest failed-alone age, "about 32 s ago" (320 to 329 ticks), belongs to a failure between
    the plug at 22:11:31 and the hold seen at 22:12:00, about 100 to 134 s before the snapshot: about 2.4 to 3.3
    ticks per host second in the minutes around the replug. That suggests the guest was slowed further then, but
    still does not measure the replug's own gap.
- **The ten rounds of 10 of 10** (`5935d9ec7`, boot c) took no clock reading.

**Reading.**
- No scheduling defect is shown. In every uninterrupted disconnect long enough for it, the driver's due read came
  24 ticks after the disconnect look, and no round showed it missing once due.
- A hold at a hub's port is released by a replug whose disconnect lasts long enough for that read: at least
  `XHCI_TOL_STABLE_DISC_TICKS` (24) of the tolerance clock, then one disconnected observation. That is about 2.4 s
  at the nominal rate.
- The 6 s replugs lost at `23ceaad05` are consistent with a tolerance clock averaging about 3.4 ticks per second in
  their boot. That explains them if the rate held at the replugs; no reading brackets them.
- This is not the root-port case repaired in `5935d9ec7`: there the second look was missing; here it is present and
  on time.
- Recorded for the design, with no change proposed: on an emulated 98 SE the tolerance tick averaged about 290 ms
  over a boot while the guest's time of day did not slow. If such a rate persists, every tolerance interval lasts
  about three times its nominal host time (the stable disconnect about 7 s). Whether a 98 SE machine on hardware
  shows a late tick was not read.

**Not run:** ME, 2000 and XP at the hub port (2000's 6 s replugs were enumerated in the earlier legs), and the
`release` flavour (no injection). Evidence: `E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\devfault11\a\ev\` (`<round>\steps.txt`,
`timeline.txt`, `dbg.txt`; `stamped-b.txt`, the stamped trace, debugcon and serial lines; `summary.md`; `FIN\`, the
final XHRQ and `/dump`). Starts and stops: two guest starts and two stops, both through QMP, and one stamping script
(file-only) started and stopped, each logged with its pid (`a\pids.txt`). No permission refusals.

**The permission refusal, and the owner's answer.** At 08:43 one shell command that would have started XH1's
resume and case 1's third reading (O3, with QEMU's trace) together was refused by the permission system before it
ran. Both steps were parked at once, with no second attempt. The owner's answer, through the coordinator: the two
steps may be run as two separate plain commands, each on its own, and a further refusal is again a hard stop. Each
was then run so, with no refusal: XH1's resume at 09:40 (the overlay had stayed hibernated), O3 at 09:43 on a new
start of the XP stream guest.

**What was not run, and why:**
- Case 9 (part E's query-stop): not prepared on these images, E being still in design.
- The Windows 7 resume controls (SH0, SHU) and the XP self-hibernation reading were not repeated: they explained the
  earlier rig, not the driver.

**Readings recorded, not findings:**
- XP: case 3's second reading (R2) was the drive's fourth failure in about six minutes, and its place was then held
  (`tol.loc.hold=00000101`; `/dump` "root port 1 charges 3: re-enumerations 3 of 3 ... NOW HELD, re-enumerations
  spent (powered)"). That is the re-enumeration budget as designed; the controller restart that latched case 2's
  flag started the place afresh.
- 2000: the first try of case 6 armed nothing, because the leg script wrote the word with a doubled "0x" prefix
  ("qemu inject: no such fault=00000000", `qemu.inj.unknown=00000000`). It is kept as `h2\ev\IH-try0`; IH and IH2
  are the readings.
- Vista: the kit's copy step found no `xhciuas.sys` in its kit, so the installed one was left as it was. Case 7 uses
  no UAS device.
- XP: the first try of XH2 armed nothing. The leg's driver was cut off by a time limit while its pre-hibernation
  `/dump` waited; that `/dump` never returns on blind XP after a resume (a known property of the rig). The guest's
  agent stayed busy until its own 400 s limit. XH2 was then run without that `/dump`, and its post-resume reading
  was taken with the rig's poll-and-close reader.

Starts and stops, each logged with its pid (`s2\pids.txt`, `r2\pids.txt`, `h2\pids.txt`, `f2\pids.txt`):

  4 / 4, 2000 2 / 2, Vista 2 / 2, Windows 7 for the simulator 2 / 2.

  the powerdown (the resumed Windows 7 and the resumed blind XP). All the others were QMP powerdowns.
- The simulator was started and ended five times, each by `taskkill /PID`.

#### What stays owed, and readings against the record

Not reached in these legs, each owed in emulation with its arrangement: E's system SET_POWER waiting for a queried
exercise and ending it by the cancel (XP's hibernation reached the controller's IRP 11 to 27 s after its request,
outside the 15 s hold; the wait-and-cancel answer itself was read on the query-remove, XE3A), and a stop or a
surprise removal with an exercise active (neither a rebalance nor a surprise removal is reachable on these guests;
their hand-off rests on its host vectors); C's leg 5 (no second route came inside the settlement's 5 s withheld
Disable Slot) and leg 6 (above: the point is released only by its bound, since the controller's own power IRPs
follow its children's, which wait for the held thread - this arrangement cannot show the recovery deferred across a
power transition on these guests); the XP4 and E7S routes' hub-port refusal (the withheld command's wait ends at its
watchdog or its verdict before the power route comes; the refusal itself - cause 9, no retry, no give-up - is read at
a hub's port under the exercise's debt in B1 and B2). Of B's legs, a fresh accepted connect at a
deferred port cancelling its obligation before the service, the root hub disabled while ports owe (both of
leg 5), and a hold that stands before the debt kept across the settlement (leg 6) were not run. The restore-clear
route and real slot exhaustion stay as recorded (QEMU declares no save capability; `qemu-xhci` has no slot-count
property).

Read against the record (recorded, no change made): in C2 and C3 the recovery's recorded reason is `CMD_KEPT`
(above; record 17 revision 34 names it in legs 2 and 3, the owner's decision of 2026-11-19); with `2D` bit 7 clear
a released query's own route bit leaves a command made during its interval (E2 with
bit 7 clear), as a real released query does - the record's "no debt" there is about the exercise's own withholding;
and the stick's Code 10 in B1 was the arrangement's: the persistent `24` held the thread in two 5 s waits ahead of
the stick's configuration.

### 50.30 step 3 (device isolation): the snapshot report's line widths, and a recovery request a resume served (2026-11-19)

Two findings of the step-3 session of `6bc886f64` that it noted and did not follow. Host work only: no guest was
started.

**The widths.** XHCITR's snapshot report - the dump's `.TXT`, the `.DEV` the same engine writes, and the console
lines of `/dump`, `/snapshot` and `/probe` - holds a line to 79 columns. A static sweep of `xhcitr\tr_snap.c` (every
format split at its newlines, each number counted at the most digits it can take, each `%s` at the longest text it
can be given) found about 165 line formats that pass 79 at those values, some 40 of them even as written: among
them the enumeration decode's look (140 columns), reset (95), speed (80) and slot (83) lines, the reset reasons'
`reset requested:` line (178 with every count at 10 digits), the event ring's choice (186 for the self-test's own
0.96 controller with 1024 asked for), the recovery window line (102 as written) and the tolerance terminals' words (up to 145). `57133633e` keeps each within 79 by
layout alone, the device of `652519be0` made general: a line is printed whole when it fits, as before; a wider one is
broken after its own clauses (the space after a `,`, `;` or `.` of its format, never inside a value), else at the
last space that fits, and wrapped under its first value. Hand-wrapped prose that passed 79 is joined and wrapped
between words. No word changes. Left as they are, for the owner: table rows (the PORTSC table's all-ones note, 83
columns at any value; the root ports table, 106 with the longest speed source; the selective-suspend table, a
96-column heading), verbatim data (the note ring, registry values, ids, paths), self-test output, and the USB Tree's
own texts (its details pane and Save Report's node text are not this engine's).

The snapshot self-test now decodes the look, reset, speed, slot and prwait records and the reset reasons block (the
latch's record, all 24 reasons counted at 4294967295, isolation unset in mode 255) at their widest; `snaptest.cmd`
checks the wrapped lines, follows each earlier check onto the lines its text now wraps to, and fails any line of the
decode logs past 79 columns but the rows of their tables.

**The recovery request.** After a resume reinitializes a failed controller, `RecoveryRequested` stays set while
`ControllerFailed` is cleared (`XhciInitController` clears only the latter). Read in the code, at release 3.5.0.0 and
on this branch alike: the word is set by the first latch of `HcdSvcRequestReset`, by `HcdControllerFail` and by
`hcdRecover` after a failed attempt; cleared by `hcdRecover` as a recovery begins and by `HcdMsg4LostLatch`; read only
by `hcdRecover`'s gate, together with `ControllerFailed`. Every way to `ControllerFailed` outside a recovery either
sets the request itself or shuts that gate (`Tol.Unreadable` for the containments, `Msg4Lost` for the lost message),
the recovery window is charged only past the gate, no suspend, stop or removal path reads the word, and a start
zeroes the extension. So the stale word can neither begin a recovery nobody asked for, skip one that is owed, nor
count one: harmless. The one other reader is 50.30's qemu-only point 3, which reads it alone: armed after such a
request, it would hold a thread pass that owes no recovery (no leg arms it so). A comment at `hcdRecover`'s gate
says so; there is no pure function to pin with a host vector, and no driver code changed.
