### 50.30 step 3 (device isolation): a run of failed recoveries across a resume, and three snapshot tables reshaped (2026-11-19)

Two items after the session of `e68a713d4`: a finding of its code reading, and the three report tables it left for
the owner, reshaped by the owner's decision of the same day (shape only, no word changed).

**The run of failed recoveries across a resume.** `RecoveryFailuresConsecutive` is raised by every charged refusal
(`XhciRecoverCharge`; `xhciRecoverOnce` at a refusal and when nothing was decoded) and was cleared only by a recovery
that succeeds; a start zeroes it with the extension. `hcdRecover` begins a recovery only while it is below 3 and
latches the FAILURES terminal at 3; `hcdResumeContained` refuses a resume only at a terminal. So with one or two
failures in a row and the next recovery owed - paced, deferred or not yet reached - a resume is admitted and, a
latched-failed controller never being saved, reinitializes: `XhciInitController` clears `ControllerFailed` and the
controller runs again, while the count, `RecoveryRequested`, the window's stamps and the failure stamp stay. A later,
unrelated fault then began its run with those c failures counted and got 3 - c recoveries (two or one) before the
controller latched stopped, at both `XhciTolerance` values. Read the same at release 3.5.0.0: older than this phase.
Design record 07 section 7 makes the count a bound on a run (a refusal raises it, a success clears it; a budget spent
on a controller another path already brought back is Finding T's expiry-date defect), so the run now ends at the
resume too: `hcdResume` sets the count to 0 when `XhciResumeController` has succeeded through a reinitialization
(`ResumeReinits` advanced across the call), under the controller lock, and notes `ctrl.run.resumed` with the count it
ended (`ac1c51110`: the pure `XhciTolResumeFailures` and its host vector `test_resume_run`; design record 17 revision
37, section 4.6). A restore, a resume that found nothing programmed, a failed resume and a terminal refusal keep the
count; the window keeps its stamps, so at `XhciTolerance` 1 a fault inside the same ten minutes still meets the
window. The change is in `src\hcd_power.c` (`hcdResume`) and `src\xhci_tol.c`; it runs in every flavour on every
resume, a guest that arms no injection included, and changes something only after a resume that reinitialized a
controller with a run of failures counted.

The guest leg did not reach its case, on XP SP3 x86 (blind, two processors, `XhciTolerance` 0, no USB device; the
qemu x86 image of `ac1c51110`). The fixture is task 49.35's: `1B` with `FF` holds every HCRST, `1C` starts the
recovery, and each attempt is refused and charged. RR1 armed rendezvous point 3 right after `1C`, to hold the next
owed recovery with a failure counted: refused (`qemu inject: refused=63230003`) - every injection but CLEAR and the
over-current release (`04`) is refused on a failed controller (`XhciInjNeedsLive`), so point 3 can be armed only
before the first failure and holds only the first, uncharged request; the three attempts failed and the controller
latched (XHRQ `term 2 recov 3`). RR2 asked for hibernation right after `1C`: the controller's suspend came after two
charged refusals (`ctrl.recover.refused` twice, then `power.suspend.first` and `save: declined - the controller is
latched failed`), the very state of the finding; but the CLEAR of the reset hold, attempted at the suspend's debugcon
line, never reached the guest (the agent did not answer as the system went down: no "written" record), so the
resume's own reinitialization was held at the reset and refused (`init.refused.step=00000009` after
`power.resume.first`, no `ctrl.run.resumed`), the resume failed, and the run went on from 2 to 3 and latched - the
case of a failed resume keeping the count, as designed. RR2's later fault (`1B` and `1C` after the resume) was
refused on the latched controller (`qemu inject: refused=641B00FF`, `refused=651C0004`; XHRQ still `term 2 recov 3`),
so no fresh run began. A resume that succeeds with a run counted needs the hold ended after the second failure and
before the resume's HCRST; neither arrangement tried gave that window. The fix rests on its host vector. Owed: a
resume that reinitializes a controller with one or two failures counted, then a later fault that gets three
recoveries (at `XhciTolerance` 1 outside the window of the earlier ones) - on a bench, a controller whose recovery
fails and whose resume then succeeds, or in a guest with an arrangement that ends the reset hold in that window.

### 50.30 (device-fault containment): the 98 SE tolerance clock at a third of its rate in one boot, read again (2026-11-19)

The question (owner, 2026-11-19): in devfault10's 98 SE boot e on the `23ceaad05` qemu image the tolerance clock
averaged about 3.4 ticks per host second over the first 14 minutes of the boot (nominal about 10); if that rate held
during the replugs, the 24-tick wait before the hub port's due look took 7 to 8 s, which would explain the lost 6 s
replugs (no clock reading brackets them); in eleven later rounds on a fresh boot it ran at 9.6 to 10.0. Why it ran
slow in that boot was not established (section "The 98 SE hub port's replug after a hold, with the tolerance clock
read", above). **Emulation only**: QEMU TCG on development host A, headless, one processor a guest, 98 SE fresh
overlays; the host shared with other work throughout (18 to 32 QEMU processes, CPU load 65 to 99 % at the readings,
logged before each one). No code change; no design record edited.

**Conclusion: (a), an emulator or host artifact - the reading the evidence supports, not a proof.** The tolerance
clock is a count of the guest's own millisecond clock (about 10 ticks per second of it, whatever the load, in every
full-rate boot read); boot e overlapped a period of the same night in which every 98 SE guest the keys worker
started (task 50.36) had that millisecond clock at 0.34 to 0.36 of host time, with or without this driver; and boot
e's tick ran at 0.34 of a full-rate boot's. So boot e's slow tick is most likely the guest's whole millisecond clock
at a third, not a late timer of the driver. What is not shown: no reading in a slow boot took both clocks (boot e
took no millisecond-clock reading, and no guest of mine entered the slow state), so a driver-side delay in that boot
is not excluded by measurement; nothing in 52 boots under every load the owner named slowed the tick at all, and the
same factor appeared without the driver. The slow state's host-side cause is not established. What stands behind
the reading: 52 boots of mine (51 boot folders) with 235 timed intervals of the tolerance clock against host time,
all at full rate (9.69 to 10.01 ticks per host second; 9.87 to 10.06 per second of the guest's `GetTickCount` in the
208 intervals with the probe); keys' 130 timed starts; boot e's own records; and, as a reading of the likely
mechanism only, QEMU's count of the guest's timer interrupts.

#### What drives the tolerance clock (source, worktree `b80630837`; `hcd_svc.c` unchanged since `23ceaad05`)

- One timer per controller, the same code on 98 SE and NT: `hcdTolDpc` (`hcd_svc.c`) first runs the lost-interrupt
  backstop's step (`HcdCtlBackstopTick`: under the controller lock it reads the event ring's state and, when an event
  has stood unserved for the backstop interval, queues the interrupt's own DPC once; it never drains inline), then
  under `TimerLock` adds one to `Hc.Tol.Clock` and arms the same `KTIMER` again, relative, for `XHCI_TOL_TICK_MS`
  (100 ms). So that step's work, and the time to take the controller lock, are on the tick's path; no thread and no
  wait are. The controller thread only reads the count (`HcdTolNow`).
- A tick is therefore the interval from one DPC to the next: the 100 ms relative due time as the system's clock
  interrupt quantizes it (record 17 section 4.0 and the comment above `hcdTolDpc`: it may expire up to one clock
  period early, so it can also be shorter), plus the DPC's queueing delay, plus the backstop step and the lock times
  before the re-arm. A late tick is lost, never made up: nothing reads elapsed time. Ticks cannot coalesce (a
  single-shot timer, re-armed only by its DPC). Record 17 section 4.0 accepts this on purpose: each tick is credited
  at 45 ms (so an interval can only run long), and "a delayed DPC stretches any of them further".
- On 98 SE `KeSetTimer` is a time-out of the VMM (`runs/run-44.md`, 44.29: VWIN32 places it on the asynchronous
  time-out list, which runs with the clock), so its expiry is measured on the VMM's millisecond time. The tick thus
  counts the guest's millisecond clock (the one `GetTickCount` and message times read), at about 101 ms a tick: 9.9
  ticks per second when that clock keeps time. On NT the same code gave 9.04 and 9.15 ticks per guest second in
  two earlier XP dump pairs (`devfault11\s2\ev\O1`, `R2`), about 109 ms a tick, which fits expiry on a 15.6 ms
  clock interrupt (an interpretation; the XP clock period was not read).
- In every reading below the tolerance clock ran at 9.87 to 10.06 ticks per second of `GetTickCount`, whatever the
  load: in full-rate boots the tick keeps a fixed ratio to the guest's millisecond clock.

#### Boot e's records, read again (`devfault10\k98\`)

- QEMU created 00:31:10 (`vms\g98\pids.txt`); one 98 SE guest, one processor, 512 MB, the `qemu` image `12418D56`,
  the `usb_hub_*` trace on (host side), no tablet, a hub and mice hot-plugged for the legs, one MS-DOS Prompt
  (`shots\g98-lost2.png`). The debug port carried 474 lines (22 KB) in 20 minutes: no per-request log, no heavy
  output. No copy to a stick in this boot.
- The `/dump` of 00:46 (line seen 00:45:11 to 00:45:16 by the host): "tolerance clock 2851 ticks", "local time
  2026-11-19 00:45:02"; XHRQ a few seconds before: "clock 2839"; the line watcher's looks 2852 (it runs from the same
  DPC). From a controller start about 5 s after QEMU's (as in every boot below; boot e's own start was not read),
  2851 ticks in about 840 s is **3.4 ticks per host second, 0.34 of the 9.9 of a full-rate 98 SE boot**, an average
  over the first 14 minutes; the boot ran to 00:51:14 with no later clock reading. The failed-alone ages agree: D1's

- Earlier 98 SE snapshots of this phase (file-only scan of every `/dump` and `/report` with a local time and a

#### The keys worker's clock readings of the same night (task 50.36, read only)

`E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\keys\first-final.txt`, `table-final.txt`, its `tools\firstwinr.py`: the clock keys measured
is the guest's message time (a journal hook's event time, the `GetTickCount` millisecond clock) against the host's
send times, per start. Of 130 timed starts, 24 ran at 0.34 to 0.36 and two at 0.41 and 0.43; the rest at 0.97 to
1.00. Every start from 00:47:32 to 01:36:41 (23) was at about a third; every start from 01:43:50 to 02:18 at full
rate; in the morning the three starts of 08:21:40 to 08:21:49 were low (E10 0.43, F10 0.41, E11 0.35), those four
to five minutes before and after at full rate. Nine of the 24 slow starts had no xHCI98 driver on the keyboard's
path (Windows' own UHCI driver on an image that never had the package, `uhc` arms, and the PS/2 keyboard on that
image, `ps2u`). The count of QEMU processes keys logged at each start does not separate the two states (slow at 15
to 23, full rate at 4 to 21). (`ev\keys-timeline.txt` here lists each start.)

**Boot e and keys' slow starts are very likely the same phenomenon:** boot e ran from 00:31 to 00:51 and overlapped
the window of slow keys starts (the earliest timed one at 00:47:32, in boot e's lifetime; none was timed before);
its tick ran at 0.34 of a full-rate boot, keys' millisecond clock at 0.34 to 0.36; and in full-rate boots the tick
keeps a fixed ratio to that clock (above). Keys' starts show the state with no xHCI98 driver at all, so the state
itself is one of the guest's clock, not of this driver's timer. The one difference in the accounts, "the guest's
time of day kept pace", is a different clock: `GetLocalTime` in boot e did not slow; keys measured the millisecond
clock, which did. Neither worker read both clocks in a slow boot, so whether the tick kept its ratio there, and
how 98 SE keeps its time of day apart from the millisecond clock in that state, were not read.

#### Readings (the method's step 3)

Rig: the method of "The 98 SE hub port's replug after a hold, with the tolerance clock read", above,
extended. Fresh overlays of three prepared disks (each an overlay of devfault9's step-3
98 SE image, `devfault9\w1\vms\p98`, with one image copied in at a first start, "===SWAP <img> SAME===", then shut
down): **Q23** = the `23ceaad05` qemu x86 `xhci98.sys` (`12418D56...35EC`, boot e's image); **R80** and **Q80** =
the gated build of `b80630837` (`dirty=0`), release `8E2E57CE...7F32` and qemu `82B2F324...EE73`; each start checked
with "===CMP <img> SAME===" (Q80 was prepared and not used). Every 30 s (60 s in L1) `CLK.BAT` in the one MS-DOS
Prompt wrote to COM1, in order: a probe of the guest's clocks (`TICK.EXE`, scratch-only, MSVC 6.0: `GetTickCount`,
`timeGetTime`, the performance counter, `GetLocalTime`), XHRQ's header ("clock N", the tolerance clock), the DOS
`time`, the probe again. A file-only script stamped each COM1 and debug-port line with the host time it arrived (0.1
s polling). Rates are between consecutive samples (about 30 s). Host load (free memory, CPU load, QEMU process
count) logged before each sample. Three guests at most, one processor each.

- **No condition slowed the tick.** Debug output (none in the release image; up to 1.9 KB a second on the qemu
  image), the per-request log, a moving tablet, a second busy DOS box, a busy storage copy, the release flavour, and
  host load up to 99 % with up to 32 QEMU processes, an hour of uptime, and 52 starts from 10:50 to 12:44 all left
  it at 9.7 to 10.0 ticks per host second (the lowest intervals are those in which `GetTickCount` itself ran 1 to 2 %
  behind host time).
- **The tick follows the guest's millisecond clock.** In every interval with the probe, 9.87 to 10.06 ticks per
  `GetTickCount` second; `timeGetTime` and the performance counter (1,193,180 Hz, the timer chip's) moved with
  `GetTickCount`; `GetLocalTime` and the DOS time agreed with it within 0.97 to 1.02 over single 30 s intervals
  (their own reading granularity) and within 0.3 % over L1's hour, in these full-rate boots.
- **The guest's timer interrupt** (QEMU's own `info irq`, i8259 line 0, read every 30 s over a second monitor
  socket, `ev\irqwatch.txt`): 384 readings from 11:29 to 12:49 on the three slots, giving 343 rates between
  adjacent readings 30 to 51 s apart: 322 of them at 193 to 210 a second, a 5 ms timer period, and the other 21
  above 210 (up to 379), each 30 to 50 s after a guest's start, before 98 SE set its period. None was low. A guest
  millisecond clock at 0.32 to 0.35 is what 64 to 70 deliveries a second would give, about one per 15.6 ms, the
  default period of the host's clock: the shape QEMU's timer callbacks would take if its main loop woke only that
  often. This is offered as the likeliest mechanism, not read: no guest of mine entered the slow state, and
  nothing on the host was read (no host probes, by the brief); neither the host's timer period nor QEMU's
  callbacks were measured. It would fit keys' observation that the state followed the time of the start (a
  host-wide state at the time), not the arm.
- With the stick copy running, keystrokes typed into the foreground prompt were lost (the Enter of four sample
  commands); a side observation of the emulated 98 SE under a compatibility-mode disk copy, not followed.

#### Reading

- (a), as the most likely reading: boot e's slow tick was the guest's whole millisecond clock running at about a
  third of host time, a state the same emulator and host gave that night to every guest the keys worker started
  then, with or without this driver. What marks it as the emulator's or the host's: it is two-valued (about a third
  or full rate), it followed the time of the start across every arm, it appeared with no xHCI98 driver at all, and
  no load inside the guest produced it here. Its likely shape (the guest's timer interrupt delivered at a coarse
  host wake-up) has no counterpart in a hardware timer chip; no hardware was measured.
- In no reading did load, debug output, the per-request log or the flavour move the tick from about 10 per second of
  the guest's millisecond clock.
- For the hub-port replug: at a full-rate clock the stable-disconnect wait is 24 ticks, about 2.4 s; in a slow-state
  boot it would be the same 24 ticks of a slowed guest clock, about 7 s of host time. A test that times replugs on
  98 SE in emulation should read the guest's clock (XHRQ's "clock" twice, or `GetTickCount`) before trusting a
  lost replug; in that section's rounds a full-rate boot lost none of three uninterrupted 6 s gaps.
- No design change is proposed. (Recorded for the owner: the tolerance clock, like the OS's own timers, counts the
  OS's millisecond clock; making it independent of that clock would mean crediting each DPC with elapsed time from
  another source. Record 13's import table lists, as evidenced on 98 SE, `KeQuerySystemTime` (which record 17
  section 4.0 set aside: it follows changes of the system time), `KeQueryInterruptTime`,
  `HAL!KeQueryPerformanceCounter` and the data export `KeTickCount`; whether any of them kept host time in the
  slow state was not read, and being importable does not make one independent of the slowed clock.)

**Not run:** ME, 2000 and XP; hardware. The slow state was not entered on demand (no artificial host load, by the
brief).

Evidence: `E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\slowtick\` - `ev\<boot>\` (`stamped.txt`: every COM1 and debug-port line with its
host time; `steps.txt`: phases, host load, starts and stops), `ev\survey.txt`, `ev\irqwatch.txt`,
`ev\keys-timeline.txt`, `ev\histrows.tsv` (earlier snapshots' local time and tolerance clock), `tools\` (the rig,
`ana2.py`, `phase.py`), `probe\tick.c`, `x98-hashes.txt`, `pids.txt` (every guest, stamper and mover start and stop,
by pid). Starts and stops: 55 guest starts (3 preparation, 52 measurement), each stopped through QMP
(system_powerdown; three of them, B01, B03 and C01, with a DOS box stuck on a COM1 write fault, needed a QMP quit
after it), plus one stray start by a quoting slip in the kit, quit at once; 56 stamping scripts (one of them, the
slip's, ended at once) and 4 tablet movers (file-only and QMP-only host scripts), each logged with its pid. Load
phases lost to the kit (a second DOS box cannot write COM1 once the first owns it; a mover holding the only QMP
socket) are not counted above. No permission refusals.

### 50.30 (device isolation): three readings before the merge - the first audio play on 2000, the 98 SE shutdown during a forced hang, and the sleep delay with a recovery owed (2026-11-19)

Three readings the owner asked for before the 50.30 branch merges, each against a control on the base the branch
started from. Guests only: nothing in `src\` changed and nothing was built. **Emulation only**: QEMU's `qemu-xhci`
(1B36:000D) and its emulated devices, development host A, QEMU TCG, headless, shared with other work (about fifteen
other QEMU processes and 80 to 90 % CPU load read at the start), so no time below is a performance figure: each time
that decides something is read against its own control on the same host in the same hours.

**Images.** Readings 1 to 3 ran the branch's gated build of `ea5eadc5a` (`E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\devfault14\binC6\HASHES.txt`,
`dirty=0`): release x86 `xhci98.sys` `89DE993F...3D3D` (474,062 bytes), qemu x86 `xhci98.sys` `D9BF7F04...D556F`
(561,635 bytes) and `xhciuas.sys` `C71B3439...02E6`; `XHCITR.EXE` `C225C430...6D1B` (`binW`, the same driver code).
Commit `ac1c51110` (a reinitializing resume zeroes the count of consecutive failed recoveries) came on the branch
while reading 3 was already being measured; its readings were kept on `ea5eadc5a` (no sleep of reading 3 with a fault armed resumes, and
nothing in that commit is on a suspend path), and the two resume cases at the end ran on its gated images
(`E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\devfault17\binR1\HASHES.txt`: qemu x86 `xhci98.sys` `5CABE514...6BD2`). **Control:** release
`3.5.0.0` as published (`releases\3.5.0.0`, identical to tag `v3.5.0.0`): `nt-x86` and `98-me` `xhci98.sys`
`B3EA6650...4E49` (445,099 bytes). No qemu-flavour build of a base without 50.30 exists on the host, so the control
has no injection layer: where a reading needs a fault forced, the control runs the same session without it, and
what `3.5.0.0` does there is read from its code (named where used).

#### Reading 1 - Windows 2000: the first audio play after the install

**What was asked.** In devfault13's release matrix on 2000 (`RM2K`) the first `T5 /play 3` after `usb-audio`'s
first attachment did not end within T5's watchdog ("watchdog: still running after 63000 ms, exiting"); three plays
on later attachments ended. Repeated here: the exact sequence on the 50.30 release image and on the control,
alternating, with what was outstanding at the watchdog and whether the device recovers without a replug.

(`-machine pc`, ACPI multiprocessor HAL), 512 MB, the T5 agent on COM1, the guest image of devfault13's rig (an
overlay of devfault3's `p2k`: 2000 with the published `3.5.0.0` installed by its `INSTALL.BAT`, a usb-tablet at QEMU
port 2 and a stick at port 1). One run: a **fresh overlay**; start 1, **the install**: `T5 /cmp` of the installed

and usbaudio's pipe aborts and resets - 42 `ABORT_PIPE` and 43 `RESET_PIPE` URBs, each answered at once

and none was left; the console carries no time, so where the 50 s before the open and the 13 s after it went is not
read from it.

**Reading 1: older - reproduced on `3.5.0.0` at the same rate, no 50.30 regression shown - and most likely the rig's
timing.** The first play on a device's first attachment met T5's 63 s watchdog on 50.30 and on `3.5.0.0` alike (2 of 6
each; and once in 3 qemu-flavour repeats). In every such run the play had begun while Windows 2000 was still bringing
the audio function up for the first time, and the time went in Windows' audio calls: the device list and the open took
48.6 to 59.7 s (once `waveOutGetNumDevs` had not returned at 63 s), and after the open no progress line came before
the watchdog (3.3 to 14.4 s). The driver requested no reset and began no recovery, its counters after the watchdog showed
only the standing reads outstanding, and Q18's console shows every request it saw answered; the device played on the
same attachment without a replug every time. With the play started only after the install had ended (W15, W16, WQ17)
the first play ended inside the watchdog on both builds, though W15's first play still took 33.5 s from start to close
(29.4 s from the open to the reset with no progress line), where W16's took 9.5 s. The explanation - the first use of
2000's audio path after its install is slow (the kernel streaming devices appear only then: `wdmaud`, `sysaudio`,
`kmixer` in R01's `/list` after the watchdog), and T5's 63 s bound is shorter than that when the play comes early - is
an inference from these timings, not a trace inside Windows; it fits devfault13's `RM2K`, which played at 82 s after
the plug, as these did.

#### Reading 2 - 98 SE: the shutdown during a forced hang

**What was asked.** In devfault13's lifecycle row the guest twice did not end within 4 to 5 minutes of the ACPI
power button while `24` (root port 6, persistent, outcome 5) kept the controller in recoveries, with the Add New
Hardware Wizard on screen; with nothing hot-plugged it ended at once. Settled here: whether the hang or the wizard
stops the shutdown, and whether the control behaves the same.

**Arrangement.** 98 SE, one processor, 512 MB, q35 with the controller behind a root port (`launch-q35.ps1 -Os
w98se`, `-msg timestamp=on`), each start a fresh overlay. Images: the 50.30 image `X` = devfault9's `p98` (98 SE and
`3.5.0.0` by its `INSTALL.BAT`, the 98 SE base of these legs) with the qemu x86 file of `ea5eadc5a` placed over the
installed one (`SWAP QEMU SAME`, then a clean shutdown); the control `C` = `p98` itself (`CMP OLD SAME` at every
start: the published `3.5.0.0` file). `XB` and `CB`: the same two with the hot-plugged devices' drivers installed
beforehand (one start each: the tablet at QEMU port 1, a stick with serial `DF16STK98` at 3 and a `usb-mouse` at 2
hot-plugged; the stick's Add New Hardware Wizard - the only one raised - answered by Enter; screenshots
`s98\ev\pXB\`, `pCB\`; a clean shutdown). Every start: the desktop and one MS-DOS Prompt; the guest clock read
twice 20 s apart (a probe printing `GetTickCount`; the ratio to host time); the driver file compared with the kit's.

- **A, as devfault13 ran it** (its `LS98B`): `INJ` `xx24065F` written first (in devfault13's order it came after
  the plugs; here the first start, `XA1`, typed it into the stick's wizard, which had taken the focus, so it was
  never written: the injection only arms `24` for an Address Device at root port 6, which the tablet (5) and the
  stick (7) do not meet, so writing it first changes nothing else); the tablet hot-plugged at QEMU port 1, 10 s,
  the stick at 3, 67 s, a `usb-mouse` hot-plugged at QEMU port 2 (root port 6), 30 s, the power button (QMP
  `system_powerdown`), up to 300 s. On the control the same session: the value is written and ignored (the
  release flavour has no injection layer), so A on the control is the wizard with no hang.
- **B**: A's session on `XB` / `CB`: no wizard (the stick's driver installed), the same forced hang on `X`.
- **C, nothing hot-plugged**: on `XB` / `CB` the tablet, the stick and the mouse at port 2 present from power-on;
  `INJ` `xx24065F`, 6 s, `INJ` `yy050000` (`05`: a real Run/Stop clear, so a recovery begins and its re-enumeration
  meets `24` at root port 6 - the forced hang with no device plugged), 30 s, the power button, up to 300 s.

**Results** (`s98\results.txt`; per start `s98\ev\<run>\`: `steps.txt`, screenshots at the power button and 20, 60,
150 and 300 s after it, the debug console before and after the power button; `tools\summ2.py` reads them):

| Arrangement | 50.30 (`X`, `XB`) | Control `3.5.0.0` (`C`, `CB`) |
|---|---|---|
| A: the stick's Add New Hardware Wizard up, the forced hang on 50.30 | **not ended in 300 s, 5 of 5** (`XA2` to `XA6`); each with `24` fired, "abort did not complete", "ring will not stop - requesting controller reset" before the power button and further reset requests after it; no power line ("power minor") reached the debug console after the button | **not ended in 300 s, 5 of 5** (`CA1` to `CA5`): the wizard and no hang (nothing injected; nothing on the debug console, the release flavour writes none) |
| A without the hang (`XA1`: the value typed into the wizard, never written) | not ended in 300 s (1 of 1) | - |
| B: no wizard, the forced hang on 50.30 | **ended, 5 of 5**: 13, 14, 14, 16 and 34 s; the hang running (`24` fired, stuck abort, reset requests) and after the button the recovery loop still going until "power minor, type, state=00020006" (S5) and `00020104` (D3) came | ended, 5 of 5: 3 to 4 s |
| C: nothing hot-plugged, the forced hang on 50.30 (`05` then `24`) | **ended, 5 of 5**: 14, 15, 33, 34 and 35 s; "controller halted itself", the recovery, then at root port 6 the stuck abort and reset requests, S5 and D3 at the end | ended, 5 of 5: 3 to 4 s |

Every start's guest clock ran at host rate (0.980 to 1.007 guest milliseconds per host millisecond over 20 s; no
start in the slow state, so none is void). Every A start's screenshots show the wizard for "USB Mass Storage Device"
in front through the 300 s, the MS-DOS Prompt idle behind it; no B or C start shows a wizard. The B and C times on
50.30 are longer than the control's because the shutdown waits for the recovery loop the injection keeps going
(each recovery, then the stuck Address Device at root port 6 for about 20 s, then the next), not for anything the
control has to do; they are the forced hang's cost, and every one ended.

**Reading 2: the rig's.** A shutdown by the power button did not end whenever the Add New Hardware Wizard was up -
on 50.30 with the forced hang (5 of 5), on 50.30 without it (1 of 1), and on the control `3.5.0.0` with no fault
of any kind (5 of 5) - and always ended without the wizard: on 50.30 with the forced hang running (10 of 10), on the
control in the same sessions with no fault (10 of 10). The forced hang does not stop 98 SE's shutdown; a wizard raised by a hot-plugged device that has no
driver yet does, under either driver. One further thing a run showed: a program still running in the MS-DOS Prompt
(an `fc` of two different files, at the first preparation of `XB`) also stopped the shutdown, with 98 SE's "You must
quit this program before you quit Windows" box (`s98\ev\pXB-void1\off-hang.png`); that image was not used.

#### Reading 3 - the sleep delay with a recovery owed (XP hibernation; 7 hibernation and standby)

**What was asked.** With a HID device served by Windows' class driver on the controller and a recovery owed, the
machine cannot finish going to sleep until the recovery has run (devfault14's XC6: while `ControllerFailed`
stands, `HcdEnumService` runs no `HcdCfgCancelService`, so a class driver's cancelled reads complete only at the
recovery's invalidation, and the power manager sends the controller its own IRPs only after its children's). Measured
here: from the sleep request to the machine off, with no HID device, a keyboard, and a keyboard and a mouse on the
controller; the same sleep with no recovery owed as the baseline; what bounds the delay; and whether `3.5.0.0`
delays a sleep the same way.

**Arrangement.** XP SP3 x86 (an overlay of `p50\gone-ev\nt5\xpa`, blind: `-vga none` and S3/S4 enabled, as the
earlier XP hibernation legs) and 7 SP1 x86 (an overlay of `p50\gone-ev\nt6\w7s`, `-rtc base=localtime`), one
processor each, prepared once (`r3\img\pXP`, `pW7`): the qemu x86 file of `ea5eadc5a` placed over the installed one
(XP `cmp: identical, 561635 bytes` at every start; 7 `===CMP NEW xhci98 SAME===`), `XhciQemuInject` and
`XhciQemuStageFault` deleted, hibernation on, and every device below enumerated once so its driver is installed.
`XhciDeviceIsolation` absent (the default `1`; XHRQ `iso FFFFFFFF/1/1`: the qemu flavour lists QEMU's controller, so
the new handling applies). No tablet. Hub A (`usb-hub`) at QEMU port 4 (root port 8) in every start. Devices from
power-on: **a** none other (no HID device on the controller), **b** a `usb-kbd` at QEMU port 1, **c** the keyboard and
a `usb-mouse` at QEMU port 2. The target `t2` (a `usb-mouse`) is hot-plugged at hub A's port 2 in every start; in the
arrangements below its Address Device is withheld, so it never gets a class driver. Every start a fresh overlay of the
prepared image. The debug console is stamped with host time by a tail on the host (`dbg-stamped.txt`, `dbg-rel.txt`:
seconds from the request).

- **P, a recovery owed and held** (devfault14's means, without its debt): `xx230003` (`23` point 3: the thread held
  at a requested recovery's entry, before the power gate, until a route's bit is raised or its bound), then
  `yy248851` (`24`, root port 8 behind a hub, count 1, outcome 5: no stop event at the abort, so the engine requests
  the reset itself, `ENGINE_ABORT_STUCK`), `t2` plugged: "command: timed out, aborting" 5 s after the plug, "abort
  did not complete" and "ring will not stop - requesting controller reset" 20 s after it, then "rendezvous reached,
  point/count=00030001" - and at that line the sleep is requested.
- **N, a recovery owed but not held** (no `23`): `yy248851` alone, the sleep requested at `t2`'s "enable slot" line
  (0.2 s after the plug), so the thread is inside its wait for the withheld Address Device when the sleep begins.
- **N0, the same at `XhciDeviceIsolation` 0** (a third prepared image with the value machine-wide, XHRQ `iso 0/1/0`):
  today's handling - the thread gives the command up at 5 s and requests the reset - which is also what the release
  flavour does at the default on every controller (its table is empty: `xhci_tol.c` `xhciIsolationTable[] = { 0 }`,
  so "listed no, applies no") and what `3.5.0.0` does.
- **B, the baseline**: no injection; `t2` enumerated; the sleep requested 25 s after the plug.

The request: XP `rundll32 powrprof.dll,SetSuspendState` with hibernation on, 7 `shutdown /h`, each started detached by
the guest agent; "off" is the QEMU process's end (the guest's own S4 power-off), timed on the host from the moment the
command was sent. 7's standby: the same prepared image with no display adapter (`-vga none`; see "Slips"),
`powercfg -h off` after the start, then `rundll32 powrprof.dll,SetSuspendState 0,1,0`; "off" is QMP `query-status`
reading `suspended`, polled every 0.2 s.

**Results** - seconds from the request to "off" (hibernation: the QEMU process ended; standby: QMP `query-status`
read `suspended`) (`r3\results.txt`; per start `r3\ev\<run>\` with `steps.txt`, `dbg-stamped.txt`, `dbg-rel.txt`;
`r3\ev-<run>.out`; `tools\summ3.py`):

| | a: no HID device | b: keyboard | c: keyboard and mouse |
|---|---|---|---|
| **XP, hibernation** | | | |
| B, no recovery owed | 8.2 | 8.5 | 8.1, 8.5, 8.1 |
| P, recovery owed and held | 8.6, 8.0, 9.3 | **72.4, 71.7, 71.7** | **72.1, 71.6, 72.2** |
| N, owed, not held (default) | | | **26.1, 26.5** |
| N0, the same at isolation 0 | | | 11.6, 11.5 |
| **7, hibernation** | | | |
| B | 34.4 | 30.6 | 37.1, 36.1, 15.8 |
| P | 33.1, 33.1, 10.3 | **81.1, 80.7, 81.4** | **73.6, 80.9, 81.8** |
| N (default) | | | **55.0, 55.7** |
| N0 (isolation 0) | | | 44.7, 39.1 |
| **7, standby** | | | |
| B | 14.8 | 27.2 | 22.1, 17.1 |
| P | 15.7, 9.4, 11.4 | **79.5, 79.8, 68.1** | **80.1, 78.6, 79.6** |
| N (default) | | | 41.6 |

7's own time to hibernate varied from 16 to 37 s with nothing owed, so on 7 the driver's share is read from the
stamped console rather than from the totals: the controller's system query and device D3 against the request.

- **What bounds it - the recovery, which alone ends the HID devices' wait.** Observed: with a HID device on the
  controller and the recovery held (P b, c), the controller's system query came at once (XP +1.7 to +2.0 s; 7 +4.9
  to +33.1 s, as in its baselines), and then nothing until the recovery: "slots invalidated, dropping every device"
  (the recovery's invalidation, which completes every transfer it was given), within 0.1 s in the host-stamped console the controller's set
  power ("power minor, type, state=00020005" on hibernation, `00020004` on standby) and its D3 (`00020104`), then off
  0.1 to 6.4 s later. That invalidation came 65.8 to 66.1 s after "rendezvous reached" on XP (6 of 6) and 68.0 to
  80.0 s on 7 (12 of 12): the release of point 3 at its bound (600 polls of 100 ms each with the key's read - 60 s
  nominal, longer in elapsed time under the guest's timer), inferred from the stamps; the release note itself was not
  read, since no start resumed. With no HID device (P a) the controller's D3 came as in the baseline (XP +2.3 to
  +2.4 s, 7 +4.7 to +29.0 s, standby +9.2 to +15.5 s), with no "slots invalidated" before it and "save: declined -
  the controller is latched failed" after it: the recovery had not run before the suspend - by devfault14's XC6R
  reading, the D3's route bit let the point go and the recovery met the power gate and deferred - and there was no
  delay. Inferred, as record 17 section 4.15.16 C has it ("which request each waits for is inferred, not traced"):
  that what the HID devices' power-down waits for is their cancelled reads, which a failed controller completes
  only at the recovery's invalidation; observed is that the delay comes only with a HID device and ends at that
  invalidation.
- **Without the held point the delay is the thread's command wait.** N (the sleep requested while the thread waited
  for the withheld Address Device): "timed out, aborting" at +4.9 to +5.0 s, "abort did not complete" and "ring will
  not stop - requesting controller reset" at +19.9 to +20.0 s, the recovery's invalidation within 0.1 s, then the
  controller's IRPs: on XP the D3 at +20.0 s (baseline +2.3 to +2.6 s), off at 26 s, **18 s longer than the
  baseline**; on 7 the invalidation at +20 s and the system query after it as 7's baseline puts it after its
  children - about 30 s later on hibernation (+50.2, +50.4 s), 21.1 s later on standby (+41.1 s). N0 (isolation 0,
  the 5 s give-up): the reset requested and the invalidation at +4.9 to +5.0 s, the D3 at once on XP (+4.9, +5.0 s),
  off at 11.5 s, **about 3 s longer than the baseline**.

**The worst case the design allows** (record 17 section 4.15.3 and the code at `ea5eadc5a`). A cancelled read is
completed by the controller thread's pass (`HcdCfgCancelService`, run only while the controller is not failed,
`hcdHalted`, `hcd_enum.c` 8386) or by an invalidation, so a sleep that meets a device which stopped answering waits
for the thread's current wait and then for the invalidation:
- the thread's wait for a command: `HCD_COMMAND_WAIT_MS` 5 s where the new handling does not apply (isolation 0, or
  the default on an unlisted controller); where it applies, phase 2 up to `HCD_COMMAND_VERDICT_MS` 16 s more, **21 s
  after the submit** (the abort ladder's worst case is 20 s, read here as +20.0 s); a thread EP0 transfer's wait
  `HCD_TRANSFER_WAIT_MS` 5 s, after which the late-transfer path (`hcdEp0Late`) may issue further work before any
  recovery is requested - a Stop Endpoint, the upstream hubs' GET_STATUS probes, the retirement's Set TR Dequeue
  Pointer - each with its own wait; the code bounds each wait, not that sequence as a whole, so for a device that
  stops answering a thread control transfer this reading gives no single figure;
- then the recovery (`hcdRecover`, `XhciRecoverController` at DISPATCH_LEVEL with `InitBelowPassive`, whose register
  waits end after their short stall phase there): an attempt that finds a reset still running returns before
  invalidating anything (`XHCI_RECOVER_RESET_BUSY`), is waited for up to `XHCI_TOL_RESET_SETTLE_MS` 1 s and run again,
  at most `HCD_RECOVER_CONTINUES` 3 times; an attempt that fails stays owed and the next is paced
  (`XHCI_TOL_RECOVER_GAP_MS` 500 ms), up to three failures in a row (`XHCI_RECOVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS`); a terminal
  controller (those three, or the window refusing a fourth) gets one invalidation from `hcdTerminalRelease`. So
  seconds beyond the wait in the ordinary case, and in the worst a run of failed attempts and their gaps before an
  invalidation ends the waits; not measured here (in every start that ran a recovery its first attempt reinitialized the controller: one
  "init complete" line and no refusal).
  The one case with no bound is older than 50.30: an invalidation without proof that the controller stopped (no
  HCH, Bus Master Enable not proven) pins the buffer and keeps every transfer (35-T.6).
- Point 3 (`23`, the qemu flavour only) adds its 60 s bound (66 to 80 s in elapsed time here); nothing like it is in
  the release flavour.

**Is this new with 50.30?** No; it is older, and 50.30 lengthens it only where its handling applies. The same guard
stands in `3.5.0.0` (`hcd_enum.c` 6432: `HcdCfgCancelService` inside `if (!hcdHalted(hc))`, `hcdHalted` =
`ControllerFailed || ScratchTainted`, unchanged), and `3.5.0.0`'s thread gives a command up at 5 s and requests the
reset (record 17 section 4.15.3, "Today") - N0's path, measured on 50.30's qemu image at isolation 0 (11.5 s on XP,
about 3 s over the baseline); the published `3.5.0.0` itself was not measured (it has no injection layer). 50.30's
new wait raises that to the 21 s bound (N, 26 s on XP) - but only where the handling applies, and the release
flavour's table is empty (`xhciIsolationTable[] = { 0 }`): at the default `1` it applies on no controller, so a
released 50.30 delays such a sleep as `3.5.0.0` does; only `XhciDeviceIsolation` `2` (every controller, at the
user's own risk) brings the 21 s.

### Owed after the three sessions

- The sleep legs where no guest's control resumes (2000 SMP, XP and 98 SE standby; 2000 and XP hibernation; ME
  standby on q35): (f) on those systems and its `XhciInterruptMode` 4 half, (f2) on 2000 and 98 SE, (f4) with a UAS
  drive, (g2), the standby halves of (k) and (l), and (i)'s missed pass by a standby; no verdict. (f) and (f2) were read
  by hibernation on 7 x64 (session 2).
- (j): the cancelled query-remove or query-stop while a try is held (an application's refusal comes before the driver's
  query, and a stopped controller has no device whose file system could refuse it; the cancel was read on a running
  controller, XP); a true surprise removal of the controller (2000 took QEMU's removal as an ejection; the q35 guests
  have no hot-pluggable slot for it). (s): the stop inside a committed burst and the burst's outcome note, on 2000 and
  98 SE: session 2's 2000 run disabled after a terminal-1 reading, which does not prove an attempt was still running,
  and the note is unreadable after the stop; on 98 SE the disable lands 10 to 20 s after its keys and a held-reset
  burst lasts moments.
- (c): the device added at once at another root port on 98 SE, XP and 7 x64 (there it was added again after the
  try), and at the other controller on 98 SE, XP and 7 x64 (the q35 guests here have no second USB controller); read
  on 2000.
- (a): the Tree's line and the tray clearing after the try, on each guest (the stopped state's lines and the red icon

### The request left standing by a reinitializing resume (7 x64): an open item of the merge, read

The merge of tasks 50.30 and 50.31 found that task 50.31's healthy pass reads `RecoveryRequested` alone, while a
resume's reinitialization serves an owed recovery without clearing that word (the comment at `hcd_ctl.c` about line
3310). Read on the 7 x64 guest above (`XhciFailedRetrySec` absent, `XhciQemuRetryScale` 3: the clean run 2000 ticks;
the tablet and the stick unplugged first): the controller restarted, `05` four times, the try recovered (level 1);
inside the clean run `23` point 3 armed and `05` written ("rendezvous reached"), then `shutdown /h`: the power route
bit let the point go (`qemu.inj.rv.route=00000010`, `qemu.inj.rv.released=0003002D`), the recovery met the suspended
controller and deferred, "save: declined - the controller is latched failed"; relaunched (the resume): reinitialized,
XHRQ `term 0 recov 4 calls 5` (the request counted, no recovery begun). Then 7.5 minutes healthy (clock 1292 to 5944):
XHRQ `retry 5/1/FFFFFFFF` at every read, the snapshot "level 1", "clean run owed, not timed", no `ctrl.retry.reset`
(`S7B`). Then `05` until the window's third: latched at level 1 (`ctrl.retry.latched=03010021`, 33 ticks, twice
level 0's 17 at this scale), where a clean run ended would have left level 0; after that try (the word cleared by the
two recoveries before it) the clean run ended on time (`ctrl.retry.reset=00000001`, level 0 by clock 10045) (`S7C`). A
first run at scale 10 (`S7`) read nothing: its clean run had ended before the failure. Shown: the backing off does
not end while the word stands. The repair is "50.31 (stale request)", below.

## 50.32 The USB Tree's restart of a controller: the 98 SE and ME remove and rescan, read in guests (2026-11-18)

**Emulation; each row is a single reading.** Task 50.32 offers the restart on 98 SE and ME only if a guest
reading shows that a remove and rescan works on both (owner, 2026-11-17); design record 25 section 27 item 3 is
what was asked, and its answer. Nothing of the product was built or changed for it.

**Where.** Development host A, QEMU 11.1.2 (the q35 bases' pinned emulator, `asm4242-20261110-docks`,
`4959a9ab...`), TCG, q35, `-display none`, one processor, 512 MB, `qemu-xhci` (`p2=4,p3=4`) behind a
`pcie-root-port` at 00:1c.0, started by the q35 bases' launcher. 98 SE: an overlay of the installed 98 SE image
task 50.30's step 3 legs made (the q35 98 SE base with `3.5.0.0` and NUSB 3.3's storage files). ME: an overlay of
the installed ME image task 50.26's legs made (the q35 ME base with `3.5.0.0`). The driver in both is `3.5.0.0`'s
`release` flavour: the restart is a configuration-manager sequence, and no driver change is part of it. Plugged
after the desktop: `usb-tablet` at port 1 and a `usb-storage` stick (an overlay of the shared FAT test disk) at
port 3, `E:` on both. The evidence, every start and stop with its pid (six of each, all stopped through each
guest's own QMP port), and the program's source are under `E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\treerst\`.

**The program.** A throwaway Win32 console program (never tracked, never packaged), built with the repository's
MSVC 6.0 (`/SUBSYSTEM:CONSOLE,4.0`), started from Run by keystrokes over QMP, its output sent to COM1 (a file on
the host). It loads `cfgmgr32.dll`, looks each routine up with `GetProcAddress`, and finds the controller
(`PCI\VEN_1B36&DEV_000D`) by a walk from the root devnode. "cycle": `CM_Query_Remove_SubTree(dn, 1)`
(`CM_QUERY_REMOVE_UI_NOT_OK`); if accepted, `CM_Remove_SubTree(dn, 1)`; the old handle's status and a
`CM_Locate_DevNodeA` of the id; 2 s; `CM_Reenumerate_DevNode(parent, 0)`; a poll every 500 ms of up to 60 s for
the controller and its subtree started; the subtree printed. "hold": `E:\HOLD.BIN` opened for writing with no
sharing, 4 KiB written every 2 s for 40 s, closed and reopened. A batch file copied a 1 MiB file to the stick and
compared it (`fc /b`).

**The routines.** On both, by `GetProcAddress`: `CM_Locate_DevNodeA`, `CM_Get_DevNode_Status`, `CM_Get_Child`,
`CM_Get_Sibling`, `CM_Get_Parent`, `CM_Get_Device_IDA`, `CM_Query_Remove_SubTree`, `CM_Remove_SubTree`,
`CM_Reenumerate_DevNode`, `CM_Setup_DevNode`, `CM_Disable_DevNode` and `CM_Enable_DevNode` found;
`CM_Query_And_Remove_SubTreeA` and `CM_Request_Device_EjectA` absent - as record 24's A.1 names say. 98 SE reports
4.10.2222, ME 4.90.3000.

**The subtree** on both, before and after every cycle, seven devnodes, each started with problem 0: the
controller `PCI\VEN_1B36&DEV_000D&SUBSYS_11001AF4&REV_01\00E000` (its parent the root port,
`PCI\VEN_1B36&DEV_000C&SUBSYS_00000000&REV_00\BUS_00&DEV_1C&FUNC_00`), the root hub
(`USB\XHCI98_ROOT_HUB\...`), the tablet and its HID devnode, the stick (`USB\VID_46F4&PID_0001\DF9W1STK1`), its
`USBSTOR\DISK...` devnode and the disk below it.

| # | System, start | What was open on `E:` | Query | Removal | Rescan | Controller found again | All seven started | After |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 98 SE, a | nothing | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.5 s after the rescan | 2.7 s | |
| 2 | 98 SE, a | nothing | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.6 s | 2.1 s | copy and compare: no differences; the tablet moved the pointer; no dialog on the screen |
| 3 | 98 SE, a | an MS-DOS Prompt whose current drive is `E:` | 0 (accepted) | 0 | 0 | 0.7 s | 3.2 s | `dir` in that prompt listed `E:` |
| 4 | 98 SE, a | that prompt in `copy con E:\HOLD.TXT`, "abc" typed | 0 (accepted) | 0, returned 4.1 s after the query | 0 | 0.6 s | 2.2 s | Ctrl+Z: "1 file(s) copied"; `type E:\HOLD.TXT`: "abc" |
| 5 | 98 SE, b | the program's "hold" writing `E:\HOLD.BIN` | `17h` (`CR_REMOVE_VETOED`) | not called | | | | nothing removed; all 20 of the program's writes succeeded, 81920 bytes on reopen |

After every accepted removal the old devnode handle's status read `CR_INVALID_DEVNODE` (`0x5`) and the id was not
found until the rescan; `CM_Reenumerate_DevNode` returned at once and the controller was absent at that moment,
so the return is not synchronous on either system. No Add New Hardware wizard came: the removal leaves the
instance key, which Device Manager's Remove deletes (section "50.30 to 50.32 steps 1 and 2", L1, where its Refresh
ran the wizard).

**What this shows, and what it does not.** On both systems, under emulation, a Win32 program's query-remove,
remove and rescan of the parent restarts the controller and brings its devices back, and a program's open file on
a drive of the controller refuses the query. On 98 SE a prompt's current drive and a file the prompt held open did
not refuse it (rows 3 and 4; the file was whole after, which is one reading of a buffered write and says nothing
of a write in flight). ME's prompt leg did not run: the prompt opened from Run showed no prompt and nothing typed
into it appeared; it was closed with its close box, which asked nothing, and the leg is not counted. Not read
here: a controller latched after repeated failures restarted this way (the qemu flavour's injection, record 25
section 27's T.27), a hub, a UAS drive, ME's own storage path beside a prompt, and real hardware.

**Starts.** ME's first start stopped at a blue screen before the desktop, before any step ("An error has
occurred... Error: 0E : 0177 : BFF7B018"); Enter left a black screen, and the guest was stopped. The second start
came up in Safe mode; it was stopped, that overlay deleted and a fresh one started (start c). A start fault of the
same form was met on an overlay of the same ME image in task 50.30's legs. After rows 1 to 4 and 7 and 8
both guests were shut down to give them a new transfer disk (the "hold" mode); 98 SE's shut down ended by itself,
ME's did not in 150 s and was ended by QMP quit, and its next start ran ScanDisk first. At the end 98 SE shut down
by itself and ME was ended by QMP quit after 120 s.

### 50.32 The drive letters and the devnodes that claim them (2026-11-18)

**Emulation; a single reading on each system.** Design record 25 section 27 item 7 (revision 43) places every local
drive letter by the one devnode that claims it in `CurrentDriveLetterAssignment`, and refuses where a letter has no
claimant; the item asked for this reading before code. Nothing of the product was built or changed for it.

**Where.** As the section above: development host A, the same emulator, q35, TCG, `-display none`; fresh overlays
of the same two installed images (98 SE with `3.5.0.0` and NUSB 3.3's storage files; ME with `3.5.0.0`), each with
a floppy controller added (`isa-fdc` with a blank 1.44 MB image), a CD-ROM (`ide-cd` with a small ISO; on the ICH9
AHCI controller, port 2 on 98 SE and port 0 on ME, where the launcher puts it), the transfer disk, and after the
desktop a `usb-tablet` at port 1 and the `usb-storage` stick at port 3. The first launch of each was refused by the
emulator before a process existed (the floppy controller's older `driveA` property); the second, with a `floppy`
device, started. Two starts and two stops, each by its pid through its own QMP port; ME's shut down did not end in
120 s and was ended by QMP quit.

**The program.** The same throwaway program, with a "letters" mode: the Windows and system directories
(`GetWindowsDirectoryA`, `GetSystemDirectoryA`); a walk of the whole devnode tree from the root (`CM_Get_Child`,
`CM_Get_Sibling`, `CM_Get_Device_IDA`, any answer but success or `CR_NO_SUCH_DEVNODE` counted as a failure); for
every devnode its `Class` and `CurrentDriveLetterAssignment` read from `HKLM\Enum\<id>`; then `GetLogicalDrives` and
`GetDriveTypeA` of each letter (with `SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS`), each letter's claimants and each claimant's chain of
parents to the root.

| | 98 SE (4.10.2222) | ME (4.90.3000) |
|---|---|---|
| Windows and system directories | `C:\WINDOWS`, `C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM` | the same |
| The whole-tree walk | 63 devnodes, no failure, depth 8: complete; every devnode has its `Enum` key | 67 devnodes, no failure, depth 8: complete; every devnode has its key |
| Letters (`GetLogicalDrives`) | A, C, D, E (mask `0000001D`) | A, C, D, E (mask `0000001D`) |
| A: (the floppy), type 2 (removable) | one claimant, `FLOP\GENERIC_NEC__FLOPPY_DISK_\ACPI&*PNP0700&000` (class `DiskDrive`), its chain `ACPI\*PNP0700\0`, `ROOT\*PNP0C08\0000`, `HTREE\ROOT\0`; no dialog or wizard was seen for the new controller | the same |
| C: (the system disk), type 3 (fixed) | **no claimant** (the AHCI disk) | **no claimant** (the disk on the `piix3-ide` primary channel) |
| D: (the transfer disk), type 3 | **no claimant** (AHCI) | one claimant, `ESDI\GENERIC_IDE__DISK_TYPE95_\MF&CHILD0001&PCI&VEN_8086&DEV_7010...` (class `DiskDrive`), its chain `MF\CHILD0001\...`, `PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_7010...\BUS_00&DEV_1E&FUNC_00`, `ACPI\*PNP0A08\00000000`, `ROOT\*PNP0C08\0000`, `HTREE\ROOT\0` |
| E: (the USB stick), type 3 | one claimant, the stick's `SCSI\QEMU____QEMU_HARDDISK___2\...` disk devnode, its chain through `USBSTOR\...`, `USB\VID_46F4&PID_0001\DF9W1STK1`, the root hub, the controller `PCI\VEN_1B36&DEV_000D...`, its root port and on to the root | the same |
| The CD-ROM | no letter | no letter |
| System Properties, Performance | "File System: Some drives are using MS-DOS compatibility", "Virtual Memory: MS-DOS compatibility mode", "Drive C is using MS-DOS compatibility mode file system.", "Drive D is using ..." | the same with drive C alone |

**What this shows.** On both systems, under emulation, every letter served by a protected-mode driver - the floppy,
ME's IDE disk on the secondary channel, the USB stick - is claimed by exactly one devnode whose chain reads, and the
stick's chain passes through the xHCI controller. Every letter served in MS-DOS compatibility mode - here the system
disk on both, and 98 SE's transfer disk - is claimed by no devnode, and Windows reports its paging in compatibility
mode on both. The CD-ROM on the AHCI controller got no letter on either. So item 7's rule as written refuses on both of
these images, whose system disk is served through the firmware; it does not tell which controller serves such a
disk. Not read here: a machine whose system disk runs in protected mode (98 SE or ME on an IDE disk with its own
driver), a CD-ROM with a letter, a compressed volume, a `SUBST` letter, a RAM drive, and real hardware.

## 50.32 stage 1: the USB Tree's restart of a controller on 2000 and later, read in guests (2026-11-18 and 19)

**Emulation; each row is a single reading.** Design record 25 section 27, stage 1: the controller's restart on 2000
and later as Windows' stop-and-restart request (`DIF_PROPERTYCHANGE`, `DICS_PROPCHANGE`), with the driver's lifetime
part (task 50.32's driver addition) telling the start. The rows are acceptance legs T.28 to T.32's NT readings as far
as the emulator gives them; the latched and contained cases, XP x64, Vista, 7 x86, 8 and 8.1 were not read here.

**Where.** Development host A, the q35 bases' pinned emulator (`asm4242-20261110-docks`), TCG, `-display none`, the
emulator's xHCI controller (`1B36:000D`, `p2=4,p3=4`) with a `usb-tablet` and a `usb-storage` stick (an overlay of the
shared FAT test disk) on it. XP SP3 x86 (q35, two processors, 1 GB), 7 SP1 x64 and 10 22H2 x86 (q35, two processors,
2 GB each): the controller behind a `pcie-root-port`, the stick at root port 3; it is `D:` on XP and 7 (the kit's
transfer disk `E:`) and `E:` on 10 (the kit `D:`). 2000 SP4 (the SMP image, `-machine pc`, two processors, 512 MB):
the controller straight on the `pc` machine's bus, no root port, the stick at root port 1. Each guest an overlay of
an installed image another Phase 50 leg had prepared. Every start and stop is logged with its pid under
`E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\treerst\legs\`, with the screenshots (`ev\`) and the kits.

**Starts.** The first start of 10 (pid 141236, 2026-11-19 01:32) ended with a reboot of the development host before
any reading was taken: it is void and gave no row. Rows B are its replacement, a fresh overlay (start b); rows C
reuse that overlay, shut down cleanly after rows B, in start c.

**What ran.** The driver: the gated `release` build of c7e39a8ff (`xhci98.sys` x86 SHA-256 `107B3758...`, amd64
`8A2E3E23...`), copied over the installed file (on 10 the loaded file was renamed first) and read after a restart of
Windows; on 7 x64 signed in the guest with a throwaway certificate. Older drivers: the released `3.5.0.0` (no
recovery-status request) on XP; on 7 x64 and 10 the earlier branch builds the prepared images held, with the request
but without the lifetime part: 7 x64 `5F47B91F...`, 10 `B12E77C6...` (stamped `3.5.0.0`, 555,666 bytes). The
tool: rows marked * `XHCITR.EXE` built from 556aad524; rows A from 6e965d7e4's sources (`XHCITR.EXE` `3BB1F218...`,
`XHCITR64.EXE` `6A8BC556...`); rows B the gated build of 6e965d7e4 (`5854406F...`); rows C the gated build of
59360cd4b, the stage 1 code as reviewed and revised (`97B7F4B8...`). `XHCITR /restart "id=<instance id>"` from a
batch file that records the exit code, unless the row says the window; Restart chosen in the confirmation. "A file
held open" is the kit's `HOLD.BAT`: `start "HELD" cmd /c "(pause) > <stick>:\HELD.TXT"`, a prompt holding the
file open for writing until a key reaches it. On XP it was released (a key sent to the window) before the next
row, and Windows restarted before the Run As row after it; on 10 the holder was ended (`taskkill`) before the
elevation rows.

the stick's directory listed; on 2000 the answer and the exit code alone.

**What this shows, and what it does not.** On XP, 2000, 7 x64 and 10 x86, under emulation, the stop-and-restart
request restarts the controller and the controller runs again, its stick readable where that was checked (above);

gives "cannot tell" (S4); a file held open on the stick makes Windows ask for a restart of the computer and mark the
controller (W1, W5, exit 3) and the next request reports the earlier mark (W6); elevation, the hand-over and Run As

build (rows C) refuses a device change between the question and the call (R9) in the run and in the window, which
asks again with the new list. A23's text names "Protect my computer", XP's box; 2000's dialog has none, and on 7 the
same text answers a restricted token with no prompt: its wording is the owner's. Not read: a latched or contained
controller, a refusal with the mark set (W5 after a refusal is a host vector only), the tray's items, R4 and A16,
XP x64, Vista, 7 x86, 8 and 8.1, and real hardware.

## 50.32 stage 2: the USB Tree's restart of a controller on 98 SE and ME, read in guests (2026-11-19)

**Emulation; each row is a single reading.** Design record 25 section 27 revision 48, stage 2: on 98 SE and ME the
restart is a query-remove, a removal and a rescan of the controller's parent, refused whenever a local drive letter is
unclaimed (R13, the owner's decision of 2026-11-19), while a placed letter or USB storage is on the controller (R18,
R12), and as item 7 says otherwise. The rows are some of acceptance leg T.27's readings; those not taken are listed at
the end, and their absence is not a limit of the emulator.

**Where.** Development host A, the q35 bases' pinned emulator (`asm4242-20261110-docks`), TCG, `-display none`, one
processor, 512 MB, the emulator's xHCI controller (`1B36:000D`, `p2=4,p3=4`) behind a `pcie-root-port`. On it, plugged
after the desktop: a `usb-tablet` (QEMU port 1), a `usb-kbd` (port 2) and, where a row says so, a `usb-storage` stick
(port 3, an overlay of the shared FAT test disk). 98 SE: a fresh overlay of the image another Phase 50 leg had
prepared (the q35 `w98se` base, `3.5.0.0` and NUSB 3.3's storage files); ME: a fresh overlay of the ME image another
leg had prepared (the q35 `me` base and `3.5.0.0`). Both with a floppy controller (`isa-fdc` and a blank 1.44 MB
image). Every start and stop is logged with its pid in `E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\treerst2\pids.txt`, with the screenshots
and readings in `ev\` beside it.

**The two disk arrangements, read first** (the throwaway program of "50.32 The drive letters and the devnodes that
claim them", its `letters` mode; `ev\*-letters.txt`):

| Arrangement | 98 SE | ME |
|---|---|---|
| system disk on `piix3-ide` without the launcher's geometry hints, the transfer disk on its secondary channel, the floppy controller | A:, C:, D: each claimed by one devnode (`FLOP\...`, `ESDI\...` twice), none through the xHCI controller; the walk complete (63 devnodes) | the same (63 devnodes), read on a start of another fresh overlay of the same image, whose shutdown ME then refused (a standby box) so that it was ended; the legs' overlay took no reading of its own, its rows passing the tool's own drive rule |
| the same without the floppy controller | A: listed (removable) with no claimant; Performance: "Drive A is using MS-DOS compatibility mode file system." | not read |
| 98 SE: the system disk on ICH9 AHCI (its image's own arrangement); ME: `piix3-ide` with the hints (its own); the floppy controller | A: claimed; C: and D: with no claimant (the firmware's disks) | A: and D: claimed; C: with no claimant |

98 SE asked once for the PIIX IDE controller's driver (Add New Hardware, `C:\WINDOWS\INF\MSHDC.INF`) and a
restart, taken as a cold start; ME asked nothing. On the first start with the devices, with the tablet and the
keyboard plugged, 98 SE's Add New Hardware asked for a "USB Human Interface Device"; the keys did not reach it while
the keyboard was plugged, so the keyboard was unplugged and the wizard answered by its default search of Windows'
driver database (its restart declined), and the keyboard plugged again asked nothing; later it asked for the stick
("USB Mass Storage Device", `C:\WINDOWS\INF\USBSTOR.INF`). ME asked for none of them.

**What ran.** The driver: the gated `release` build of 5ba611d5e (`xhci98.sys` x86 SHA-256 `5B0722FC...`), copied
over the installed file (`fc /b`: no differences) and read after a cold start. The tool: `XHCITR.EXE` of the same
gated build (`C76A8996...`), run from the transfer disk as `start /w XHCITR.EXE /restart "id=<instance id>"` from a
batch file that sent the exit code to COM1; Restart chosen in the confirmation. "Safely Remove" is
`XHCITR /eject "id=<the stick's instance id>"`, answered OK.

| Leg | Windows | Disks | On the controller | Answer (as shown) | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a keyboard and a mouse, every letter placed | 98 SE | piix, floppy | tablet, keyboard | the confirmation: "USB Human Interface Device, port 5 - mouse", "USB Human Interface Device, port 6 - keyboard", C7 (no C8: the PS/2 keyboard and mouse outside it); "Controller restarted": "Windows removed xHCI98 USB 3 Controller (Red Hat QEMU xHCI) and looked for it again. It has started again. It is running." | 0 |
| a stick with its letter | 98 SE | piix, floppy | tablet, keyboard, stick (E:) | no confirmation; R18 "Drive E: is on xHCI98 USB 3 Controller (Red Hat QEMU xHCI), so the controller is not restarted. Unplug the drive's device, and then restart the controller." | 1 |
| the stick stopped with Safely Remove | 98 SE | piix, floppy | tablet, keyboard, stick (no devnodes) | R12 "USB storage is connected to xHCI98 USB 3 Controller (Red Hat QEMU xHCI): USB device 46F4:0001, port 3. Unplug it, and then restart the controller." | 1 |
| the stick unplugged | 98 SE | piix, floppy | tablet, keyboard | the same confirmation; "Controller restarted": the same three lines | 0 |
| a letter unclaimed | 98 SE | AHCI, floppy | tablet, keyboard | no confirmation; R13 "The tool could not tell which controller drive C: is on, so it does not restart this controller. Restart Windows instead." | 1 |
| a keyboard and a mouse, every letter placed | ME | piix, floppy | tablet, keyboard | the confirmation as on 98 SE; "Controller restarted": the same three lines | 0 |
| a stick with its letter | ME | piix, floppy | tablet, keyboard, stick (E:) | R18 as on 98 SE | 1 |

| a letter unclaimed | ME | piix with the hints, floppy | tablet, keyboard | R13 naming C: as on 98 SE | 1 |
| a controller stopped after repeated failures | 98 SE | piix, floppy; the `qemu` flavour | tablet | latched by `XhciQemuInject` code `05` (HCH) four times in the controller's key: four "controller halted itself" in the trace; `/restart`: "Controller restart": "Restart it from Device Manager, or restart Windows." (the approved line); the window (this build, after the installed `3.5.0.0` tray was ended): Action > Restart Controller... shown disabled, the details "Status: Stopped after repeated fail[ures]" and the note "Restart it from Device Mana[ger]..." (cut by the pane), four records "reset requested: HEALTH" | 1 |

The stopped controller's row ran on the same 98 SE overlay after the rows above, with the gated `qemu` flavour of
5ba611d5e (`ABBA7501...`) copied in the same way and a cold start. The first window opened in that row was the
installed `3.5.0.0` tool's, which the running tray instance showed (no Restart item); it is not counted.

What was checked after a restart: the answer box closed by a key the keyboard on the controller sent, and the
tablet moved the pointer (98 SE: a line typed in the prompt as well); the stick's directory was listed before its
rows. Screenshots: `ev\s98-L1-*`, `s98-L2-*`, `s98-L3-*`, `s98-L4-*`, `sme2-L1-*`, `sme2-L2-*`, `sme2-L3-*`; exit
codes `ev\s98-e-exits.txt`, `sme2-b-exits.txt` and the serial logs; the latch's trace `ev\s98-h-debugcon.log`.

**What this shows, and what it does not.** On 98 SE and ME, under emulation, with every local letter claimed by one
devnode off the controller, the removal and rescan restart the controller with a keyboard and a mouse on it, the
confirmation says so (C7), and both work after; a stick with a letter on it refuses (R18), and so does the same stick
stopped with Safely Remove and still plugged in (R12); with the system disk in MS-DOS compatibility mode the restart
is refused before anything is asked (R13). Line 2's S1 came from the removal (the controller gone, then found
started); line 3's N3 needs the recovery-status request, which the `3.5.0.0` driver the images held does not serve,
so it also shows that the copied driver was the one loaded. A controller stopped after repeated failures is not
restarted there: the approved line answers, and the window's item is disabled. A floppy letter with no floppy
controller is unclaimed: such a 98 SE machine is refused (R13) whatever is plugged in. Not read: T.27's composite
audio device; R13 with nothing on the controller and with a stick on it; a veto (A10), A11, A12 and A19 to A22, R16,
R15 with a network drive, R13's form naming no letter and a settle that times out, all host vectors only; a hub on
the controller; the Performance tab of the arrangement whose letters are all placed (its letters were read with the
program alone); the window's right-click menu and the tray; ME's stopped controller; and real hardware.

### 50.32 stage 1 on 7 x86: a running and a stopped controller restarted (2026-11-19)

**Emulation; each row is a single reading.** Two of the stage 1 rows owed by the section above it: 7 SP1 x86, the
`qemu` flavour, a controller restarted while running and after it stopped after repeated failures (acceptance legs
T.30 and T.21 in part).

**Where and what ran.** Development host A, the q35 bases' pinned emulator, TCG, two processors, 2 GB; a fresh overlay
of the 7 x86 image another Phase 50 leg had prepared (its agent run by the logged-on administrator, elevated); the
emulator's xHCI controller behind a `pcie-root-port` with a `usb-tablet` and, at root port 3, a `usb-storage` stick
(D:). The gated `qemu` flavour of 5ba611d5e (`xhci98.sys` `ABBA7501...`) copied over the installed file and the
driver store's copy and read after a restart of Windows; `XHCITR.EXE` of the same gated build (`C76A8996...`) as
`XHCITR /restart "id=<instance id>"` from a batch file that records the exit code; Restart chosen in the
confirmation. The stop after repeated failures: `XhciQemuInject` code `05` (HCH) four times in `Services\USB`, each
answered in the trace by "controller halted itself" and a reset request (calls 1 to 4); after the fourth, "slots
invalidated, dropping every device" came at once, without the reset's work the trace shows after the first three,
and the devices were surprise-removed. Start and stop in `E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\treerst2\pids.txt`; screenshots
and the trace in `nt\ev\`.

| Leg | Answer (as shown) | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| a running controller | the confirmation: "USB Input Device, port 6 - mouse", "USB Mass Storage Device, port 3 (D:) - storage", C4 and C7; "Controller restarted": "Windows accepted the restart request for xHCI98 USB 3 Controller (Red Hat QEMU xHCI). It has started again. It is running." | 0 |
| the controller stopped after repeated failures | the confirmation: "Its devices were removed when it stopped." (C3, an empty list); "Controller restarted": the same three lines; the stick back (Windows' AutoPlay for ORICO (D:)) | 0 |

**What this shows, and what it does not.** On 7 x86, under emulation, the stop-and-restart request restarts a running
controller and one stopped after repeated failures, whose devices come back. Not read on 7 x86: a standard user's
elevation, the window and the tray's item for the stopped controller, a contained controller (R2), and the latch's
recovery-status answer before the restart (the confirmation's C3, which needs a complete walk finding nothing below
the root hub, is the reading taken).

**The tray, two controllers** (Vista x86, a second `qemu-xhci` behind a second root port, xhci98 on both; a
`usb-tablet` on an ICH9 UHCI controller, Windows' own driver, so that the pointer survives; the `qemu` flavour; the
tray `XHCITR.EXE /tray` started as the limited token; both controllers latched by `05` four times in `Services\USB`,
eight "qemu inject: fired" in the trace). Left-click on the tray icon, read by screendump:

| Tray | Menu (as shown) |
|---|---|
| F, the tray alone | "xHCI98 USB 3 Controller (Red Hat QEMU xHCI) stopped answering and 1 more...", "No device to stop" (grayed), "Open xHCI98 USB Tree": no restart item - the defect below |
| F, after "Open xHCI98 USB Tree" | the same with "Restart xHCI98 USB 3 Controller (Red Hat QEMU xHCI)..." twice; the second chosen: C3 with the shield, Allow; the answer as a balloon, "Controller restarted": the same three lines; the menu then with one restart item |

The two items read alike: both controllers carry the same Device Manager name, and the menu has nothing else to tell
them apart.

**Defects found, and fixed.** Each fix was reviewed, committed and built in a gated x86 build (below), and the row
that showed it read again on that build.
- *The tray alone offered no restart item* (above). The menu's item needs the controller's recovery status, which
  only the window's refresh read; the tray alone reads holds on a job that runs only with the hold notice on (off by
  default). 6dcd3e51f: the tray reads the recovery status where it already reads each controller's failed flag, on
  its own thread, never during a restart.
- *A device behind a hub folded into the hub's line* (98 SE, below). The list's hub test took only ids with
  `Class_09`; this driver's hubs carry the project-owned `USB\XHCI98_HUB` ids. bc6e2c329: the test takes those too
  (`tr_rst_is_hubnode`, with host vectors); read again on 8.1 x64 (the hub row above), 98 SE and ME.

**What this shows, and what it does not.** On XP x64, Vista x86, 8 x86 and 8.1 x86 and x64, under emulation, the
stop-and-restart request restarts a running controller; on XP x64 one stopped after repeated failures, offered on its
menu, and its devices come back. `XHCITR.EXE` on 64-bit Windows hands the run to `XHCITR64.EXE` and returns its exit
code, refuses with R4 and grays the item without it, and answers A16 when `XHCITR64.EXE` is gone by the time of the
elevated start. A contained controller is refused (R2) by the one-shot run and, from a window whose reading predates
the containment, by the checks made again before the call. Elevation answers alike on Vista, 7, 8 and 8.1: declined
A14, allowed the restart; a standard user on 7 is asked for an administrator's password and the restart follows. An
Explorer window on the stick made Vista ask for a restart of the computer and mark the controller (W1, W5, exit 3), as
a file held open did on XP and 10. The tray offers a restart item for each stopped controller and restarts the one
chosen (G). On XP x64 the guest's power-off did not end within 240 s with the controller left contained; the emulator
was ended. Not read: Vista x64 (its q35 base has no xHCI98 and no agent; owed), 8 x64, a contained controller from the
tray, and real hardware.

The stick's directory was listed after each restart and after A16; `XHCITR64.EXE` was moved back after A16.

**A restart Windows refuses in the session: what the tool does** (`xhcitr.c` `rst_call`, `tr_rst.c`
`tr_rst_answer` and `tr_rst_exit`; design record 25 section 27 items 2, 4 and 8). When the stop is refused,
`SetupDiCallClassInstaller(DIF_PROPERTYCHANGE)` still returns `TRUE`, so line 1 is A1 ("Windows accepted the restart
request for ..."), the request as Windows answered it. The settle then samples the driver's lifetime words every
500 ms for its full 30 s: none differs from the baseline, so line 2 is S3 ("The tool saw no new start of it."), an
observation of the samples, never a restart; line 3 is read fresh (N3 "It is running." for a controller that went on
running). Line 4 comes from what Windows set: the class installer's `DI_NEEDREBOOT`/`DI_NEEDRESTART` after the call
(W1 "Windows asks for the computer to be restarted.") and the devnode's `DN_NEED_RESTART` at the end (W5 "Windows has
marked <controller> to be finished at the next restart of the computer."), and W6 where the mark was already set
before the request. With W1, W5 or W6 the exit code is 3 and the title B2 ("Controller restart", the warning icon),
never B1. The answer is too long for the tray's balloon, so from the tray it is a message box as well. So the tool
never reports a restart that did not happen: S1 needs a new start identity with the driver's started flag, and a
refused stop draws no new start. The next step it gives is Windows' own: a restart of the computer. It does not say
that the refusal may come from a program using a drive of the controller, nor that closing it and asking again
restarts the controller without a restart of the computer (the row "the window closed" below); record 25 section 27
item 2 has the tool claim nothing about why Windows refused or asked for a restart.

**Vista x86, the refusal read four times.** The gated `qemu` flavour of 6dcd3e51f (`xhci98.sys` `90233D9A...`, SHA-1
`73A6019B...` read in the guest) copied over the installed file and the driver store's copy, read after a restart of
Windows, its trace on; `XHCITR.EXE` of the same gated build, run by the administrator (elevated). The stick plugged
after the desktop: a new instance, "Installing device driver software", then AutoPlay opened an Explorer window
"ORICO (D:)" on it.

| Leg | What was open on D: | Answer (as shown) | Exit | The trace |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| refused | AutoPlay's Explorer window | the confirmation as on Vista x64, no shield; after the settle, "Controller restart": "Windows accepted the restart request for xHCI98 USB 3 Controller (Red Hat QEMU xHCI)." "The tool saw no new start of it." "It is running." "Windows asks for the computer to be restarted." "Windows has marked xHCI98 USB 3 Controller (Red Hat QEMU xHCI) to be finished at the next restart of the computer." (A1, S3, N3, W1, W5) | 3 | query-remove (minor 1) to both device PDOs, the root hub's FDO and PDO and the controller, then cancel-remove (minor 3) to each of them; no start, no removal |
| refused again, the mark set | the same window, no restart of Windows between | the same confirmation, which says nothing of the mark; the same five lines and "Windows had marked xHCI98 USB 3 Controller (Red Hat QEMU xHCI) to be finished at the next restart of the computer before this request." (W6) | 3 | the same |
| the window closed, the mark still set | nothing (the window closed with its close box) | "Controller restart": "Windows accepted the restart request for ...", "It has started again.", "It is running.", the W6 line (A1, S1, N3, W6); AutoPlay's window on D: again after it | 3 | the removal and a new start |
| refused, after a restart of Windows | AutoPlay's Explorer window (the stick unplugged and plugged again) | as the first row (A1, S3, N3, W1, W5) | 3 | query-remove, then cancel-remove; no start |

The row "elevation allowed, an Explorer window on the stick" of the section "the legs still owed" (Vista x86, the
`release` driver, no trace) answered as the first row here: by its answer, the same refusal. The rows "a file held
open on the stick" on XP and 10 in stage 1's section answered alike (W1, W5, exit 3).

**What this shows, and what it does not.** On Vista x64, under emulation, this branch's driver package signed in the
guest with a throwaway certificate and a catalog made there installs and runs, and the Tree's restart answers as on the
other 64-bit systems: the restart, the hand-over with its exit code, R4, elevation declined (A14) and allowed, and A16.
When an Explorer window is open on a drive of the controller, Vista x86 refuses the stop in the session: the
controller sees a query-remove and then a cancel, no new start follows, and the call still returns success. The Tree
then says what it read - the request accepted, no new start seen, the controller running, Windows asking for a restart
of the computer and its mark - with exit code 3, and it never says that the controller restarted; with the window
closed the same request restarts it. On Vista x64 (the `release` driver, no trace) the same window gave the same answer
and exit code once; the trace and the request with the window closed were not read there. Not read: a refusal after which Windows sets neither the restart flags nor the
mark (every refusal read here and in the rows named above set both; such an answer would have no fourth line
and exit 2); a refusal by a program other than Explorer on Vista; Vista x64's window and tray items, a latched or
contained controller on it, and a standard user there; and real hardware.

### 50.32 revision 50: the hint after a restart Windows refuses in the session (2026-11-19)

**Emulation; each row is a single reading.** Design record 25 section 27 revision 50 (2c208c5ee) records the owner's
decision of 2026-11-19, given through the coordinator, on the refusal read in the section above: where Windows
accepted the restart request, no new start was seen and Windows asks for a restart of the computer or has marked the
controller (A1, S3, and W1 or W5), the answer ends with H1, "A program may be using one of its drives: close it and
try again, or restart the computer."; on 2000 and later only, never where a new start was seen, the exit code and the
title unchanged. 7cf4708c5: the line in the pure half (`tr_rst_answer`), the tray's balloon limit there too
(`tr_rst_in_balloon`, the same limit `rst_show` used), and host vectors for H1 in that combination and its absence
beside S1, S2 and S4, without W1 and W5, after A9, A18, R1, R10, a refusal before the call and on 98 SE and ME. The
settle is left as it was: it is not ended early when the flags or the mark read set, since neither shows that no start
follows (record 25 section 27 item 4).

**The gated build.** Gate H, 7cf4708c5, x86 `all` (`release` and `qemu`, the host tests among them) in the gate
worktree, `XHCI98_SELFTEST_SKIP_OK=1`: "BUILD + GATES PASSED (release qemu)", exit 0, the worktree clean, `test_trrst`
291 checks with no failure. `XHCITR.EXE` `152B63C7...`, `XHCITR64.EXE` `65CAB5A9...` (the 64-bit tool comes from the
x86 run); the drivers' sources did not change.

**Where and what ran.** As in the section above: Vista SP2 x86 (one processor) on a fresh overlay of the same
