## 50.32 (continued): the 98 SE hang at the Tree's restart with a USB audio device, taken apart (worker s98audrm, 2026-11-19)

**The lead.** 50.32's last legs (worker treerst3; this file's "50.32 stage 2: revision 49, the floppy letter; a hub; a USB audio device",
"A USB audio device on the controller") saw 98 SE stop responding in two of three restarts of the controller by the USB Tree with QEMU's
`usb-audio` on it: once after the answer "Controller restarted" (`release` driver; tablet, keyboard and the audio
device), once inside the removal (`qemu` flavour, the same three devices: the trace ends at "hcd: removed function
released, port/mask=07000003"), and the start between them, without the keyboard, passed. Asked here: is it the
Tree's restart or any removal with the audio device present; is this driver needed for it at all; if it is, what was
outstanding; and which of Windows' own, the Tree's route, or this driver's removal of an audio function it is. A
diagnosis by guest runs only: nothing in `src\` or `xhcitr\` changed, no build was made.

**Where.** Development host A, the emulator build of 50.32's legs
(`E:\xhci98-vm\q35-bases\bin\asm4242-20261110-docks`), TCG, headless, the q35 machine, one processor and 512 MB a
guest, at most three guests at a time (other work's guests ran on the host throughout, so no time here is a timing).
Every leg is a fresh overlay of a prepared image and a cold start. The system disk on `piix3-ide` (the PIIX IDE
wizard answered in the image), the transfer folder as D:. The USB controller is either QEMU's `qemu-xhci` behind a
`pcie-root-port` under this driver, or a PIIX3 UHCI (`piix3-usb-uhci`) under Windows' own driver. Devices plugged
after the desktop by QMP `device_add`: `usb-tablet`, `usb-kbd`, and `usb-audio` (UAC 1.0, Full Speed, `46F4:0002`,
`-audiodev none`) - on the xHCI controller at QEMU ports 1, 2 and 3 (Windows' ports 5, 6 and 7, as in 50.32), on the
UHCI controller the audio device at port 1 and a `usb-hub` at port 2 with the tablet and the keyboard behind it (a

**Which audio driver.** On both stacks the audio device's function is installed by Windows' own `WDMA_USB.INF` ("USB

Device"); under UHCI it is Windows' own "USB Composite Device". `MEDIA\0000` is the only device driver installed for
it (the other `MEDIA` keys are the kernel-streaming software devices).

**Two states of the audio device, found at the first legs.** 50.32's three starts installed the audio device in the

### What was outstanding at 50.32's stop inside the removal

Read from 50.32's trace (`treerst3\ev\s98b-c-debugcon.log`) against this item's passing ones, and from the source at
the branch's tip:

- **The audio function's REMOVE was received and its release begun; the trace shows no more.** Its client sent
  SELECT_CONFIGURATION through the controller thread ("thread URB done, function/status=00000000") before its REMOVE
  (98 SE's `usbaudio.sys` unconfigures at its removal), which succeeded and closed the function's pipes; the function
  PDO's REMOVE entered ("device PDO PnP minor=00000002" is printed on entry); the line where the trace ends, "hcd:
  removed function released, port/mask=07000003", is printed by the controller thread at the start of its release of
  a removed function (`hcd_cfg.c` `hcdCfgReleaseOne`), queued by the REMOVE (`hcd_pdo.c` `hcdPdoFunctionRelease`,
  `HcdCfgReleaseFunction`), which does not wait for it. Neither line shows that the REMOVE returned or the release
  finished. What the source leaves after them: in the REMOVE, the quiesce and the rundown had already returned (they
  come before the release is queued), then a reference count, bookkeeping under a spin lock (`hcdPdoRemoved`; a
  listed PDO's orderly removal sets one flag) and the IRP's completion; in the release, with no pipe of interfaces 0
  and 1 left open, the Configure Endpoint is "a success with nothing issued" (`hcdCfgSwitchConfigure`) and no
  SET_INTERFACE is sent (both interfaces at alternate 0). Neither path has a wait of its own there; the completion
  runs the upper drivers' completion routines, which are theirs. In every passing removal here the same line is
  followed by no command either.
- **No isochronous transfer, ever.** The start's trace holds no isochronous-transfer URB at all: the streaming
  interface was selected at alternate 0 at its start ("interface selected, number/alt=00000100") and never moved, and
  the isochronous bandwidth count went back to 0. The same holds for every first-install leg here (no "isoch URB" or
  "isoch published" line in any of their traces; `L26`'s and `L28`'s departures say "isochronous held
  released=00000000"); the only isochronous traffic in this item is `L01`'s and `L02`'s after a cancelled removal. So
  nothing was held under docs/issues/25's rule (which holds a *departed* device's isochronous requests; this was an
  orderly removal with nothing in flight).
- **No command outstanding.** The last command had completed; no command timeout or "commands the engine gave up on"
  line.
- **What stays pended at this driver** is the HID reads `hidclass.sys` keeps on the tablet and the keyboard, as at
  any idle moment; they are cancelled by each HID device's own removal, which never began (no transfer stopped or
  cancelled after the line).
- **What the removal waited for** is Windows' next step. In every passing removal with the audio device first in the
  walk (50.32's `u1` had the tablet first; here `L15`, `L19`, `L16`'s and `L20`'s and `L23`'s second restarts) the
  next line is the composite parent's REMOVE ("hub FDO PnP minor=00000002", "hub FDO removed, children let go"), at
  once. At 50.32's stop that REMOVE never came. Where the system was instead is not shown: somewhere between the
  audio function's REMOVE entering this driver and the next REMOVE, a span that holds the rest of this driver's
  REMOVE (above), the completion back through the audio function's stack, and 98 SE's own handling of that devnode's
  removal.
- **The registers at that stop** (50.32's `s98b-u2-regs.txt`): EIP `C000A881`/`C000A882` in ring 0, ESP `E2E5AE04`,
  EBX `E4520074`, EDI `E45202B0`, ECX `00000015`. `L09`'s stop after the restart (below) shows the same EIP with EBX
  `E4520074`, EDI `E45202B0`, ECX `00000015`; the stops at the audio device's arrival on Windows' UHCI driver with no
  package (`L03`, `L05`) and on `3.5.0.0` (`L04`) have EIP in the same addresses (`C000A881`, `C000A882`, `C000A700`,
  `C005335E`), and so did 36.41's and run 47's (`C000A4D8` to `C000A933`). That is VMM's own code; no driver's code
  was read. Run 47 reads that look as Windows 98 SE's configuration manager "blocked in a PnP operation, whichever
  one it is": it says that 98 SE waits, not what for, and it does not place the cause above or below this driver.
- **With the keyboard and without it.** Here the walk's order followed the plugging: plugged tablet first, the
  tablet's removal came first; plugged audio first, the audio function's came first; and every second restart of a
  start walked the audio function first. 50.32's `u1` (no keyboard, the tablet first) and `u2` (keyboard, after a
  restart, the audio function first) differ in that order as much as in the keyboard. Here the audio function first
  with the keyboard present passed in 13 removals; the keyboard changed no outcome.

### A fault after a restart (`L16`, `L36`): this driver's controller thread returns into its unloaded image

On 98 SE this driver's image is **unloaded at every removal of the controller** (`hcdUnload`'s "msg4.uninit" line
ends each one) and a new copy is loaded for the rescan. Where each copy lay was read by searching guest memory for
one of this driver's own strings (`tools\findimg.py`; nothing else of the saved memory is read), with the mapped
ranges from QEMU's `info mem`:

| Leg | at the boot | after restart 1 | after restart 2 | after restart 3 | after restart 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `L20`, `L23`, `L32` (tA+k) | `FF03EAC0` | `FF16A380` | `FF1E1D80` | - | - |
| `L22` (tAk) | `FF03EAC0` | `FF16A380` | `FF1E1D80` | `FF259D80` | `FF1DFD80` |
| `L36` (Atk) | `FF03EAC0` | `FF16C160` | `FF1E3D80` | `FF25BD80` | `FF1E1D80` (read at the fault) |
| `L16` (tA+k) | - | - | `FF1E45C0` (read after the fault) | - | - |

Each copy spans `0x79400` bytes.

**`L36`, restart 4** (taken with the registers and the image positions before any key): the removal ran to its end
(the audio function first), the controller stopped ("controller thread leaving its loop", "controller thread has
exited"), the image was unloaded, the new copy at `FF1E1D80` started the controller and answered its
QUERY_CAPABILITIES and QUERY_PNP_DEVICE_STATE, and the trace ends there; the screen: "A fatal exception 0E has
occurred at 0028:FF271C03." That address is `FF25BD80 + 0x15E83`, inside the copy that had been running until this
removal, and at the fault its pages were no longer mapped (`FF25C000`-`FF2D1000` unmapped, the new copy mapped at
`FF1E2000`-`FF25C000`). In the `qemu` flavour's own disassembly (`90233D9A`, read with its PDB; the project's own
binary), offset `0x15E83` is the instruction after the second `call ebx` near the end of the controller thread
(`hcd_ctl.c`, `hcdThread`'s exit), `ebx` holding `KeSetEvent`: the return address of `KeSetEvent(&hc->ThreadExited,
...)`, the line before `PsTerminateSystemThread`. So the controller thread had set the event its stop waits for and
had not yet returned from that call when the image was freed; when it was run again it returned into the freed copy.
The screen stayed (the harness's keys, through the USB keyboard in this leg, went nowhere) and the leg was ended.

**`L16`, restart 2** (the same sequence as 50.32's `u1` then `u2`): the same point in the trace (the new copy started
the controller, QUERY_PNP_DEVICE_STATE at 18:18:10.2, then 50 s of silence until the harness's key dismissed the
screen), and "A fatal exception 0E has occurred at 0028:FF181F83." `FF181F83` is `0x15E83` above `FF16C100`, and lay
in the range the copy after restart 1 occupies (`FF16A380`-`FF1E3780` in the three legs of the same sequence) and
that was unmapped at the reading after the fault (`FF16D000`-`FF1E2000`). `L16`'s own copy was not read before the
fault, so that it lay at `FF16C100` is inferred from the offset, not read. After the screen was dismissed the
re-enumeration completed and the tool answered "Controller restarted" (exit 0), the shell opened its Start menu and
shut down, but the taskbar clock had stopped at 6:21.

**What the source says about that window.** `hcd_ctl.c` above `HcdThreadReference`: on NT the stop waits on the
thread object; "Windows 98 and ME: on that event. ... The event leaves the thread's call into PsTerminateSystemThread
after it; a Windows 98 disable is QUERY_STOP and STOP, which unloads nothing, and the remove that would unload the
image has not been measured against that window on Windows 98". It is measured now: a removal of the controller (the
Tree's restart; Device Manager's Remove unloads the image too, `L31`) does unload it, and in `L36` the controller
thread was still inside that window when the image went; `L16`'s fault fits the same offset if its copy lay at
`FF16C100`, which was not read (the copy the other legs of its sequence read after restart 1, `FF16A380`, would put
it at `0x17C03`, inside an instruction of `hcdLedgerReturn`), so `L16` is compatible with it, not shown by it. **This
is a defect in this driver's teardown on 98 SE (and by the same code ME): the controller thread's exit (`hcdThread`,
its `KeSetEvent(&hc->ThreadExited)` and `PsTerminateSystemThread`) against the stop's wait on that event
(`hcdThreadStop`, its 98/ME branch, `HcdWaitEvent`) and the image's unload.** It is not the audio function's removal,
and not the stop inside the removal 50.32 saw (`u2` never reached the controller's stop). Both faults came with the
audio device on the controller and the audio function first in the walk; whether the device matters (for the timing)
was not read: no restart without it was made here. No fix is designed here.

### What it is

**Counts** (emulation; the first-install state unless named). Under this driver: **27 removals** of the controller
with the audio device on it, **none stopped inside the removal** - the Tree's restart 25 times (21 on 6dcd3e51f's
`qemu` flavour, 4 on `3.5.0.0`) and Device Manager's Remove twice (one each); 13 of the 22 traced ones walked the
audio function first, as `u2` did, all with the keyboard present; 4 stops by Device Manager's disable (3 on the
`qemu` flavour, 1 on `3.5.0.0`), 2 unplugs. After 24 of the 25 Tree restarts the audio device came back (`L36`'s
fourth ended before it): **1 stop** at that arrival (`L09`). **2 faults** (`L16`, `L36`) after the controller had
started again, in the 22 removals that unloaded the `qemu` flavour (none in the 5 of `3.5.0.0`); `L36`'s identified
as this driver's (point 3), `L16`'s compatible with it. Under Windows' UHCI driver with no package: 5 removals by
Device Manager's Remove (one of them installed earlier), none stopped; 5 stops by its disable; 2 unplugs. Installed
earlier: **6 of 9 starts stopped at the audio device's arrival**, before any route (3 of 4 under Windows' UHCI driver
with no package, 3 of 5 under this driver); of the 3 that went on, the Tree's removal was refused twice (`L01`,
`L02`, then the documented `usbaudio.sys` fault) and Device Manager's Remove under UHCI went through once (`L42`).
50.32 itself: 3 Tree restarts, 1 stop inside the removal, 1 stop after it.

1. **The stop after "Controller restarted" (50.32's `a1`) is the audio device's arrival, and 98 SE stops there
   without this driver too.** `L09` stopped the same way, its trace ending in the audio device's re-arrival at the
   point 36.41's stops end (its streaming interface selected at alternate 0, a QUERY_CAPABILITIES, then nothing), the
   clock still. The same device's arrival stopped 98 SE under Windows' UHCI driver with no package of this project
   (`L03`, `L05`, `L41`), under `3.5.0.0` (`L04`) and under 6dcd3e51f (`L39`, `L40`) in the "installed earlier"
   state, with the same look (VMM's wait, the clock still); 36.41 recorded the same on Windows' UHCI stack. A restart
   ends in an arrival of the audio device, so any route that brings it back can meet this. That `L09`'s and `a1`'s
   stops have the same cause as the UHCI ones is not shown, only that the same stop exists without this driver; no
   stack word at `L39`'s and `L40`'s stops pointed into this driver's image. `a1` showed no fault screen; whether
point 3's window played any part in it is not shown either way.
2. **The stop inside the removal (50.32's `u2`) was not reproduced, and its cause is not identified.** No removal
   stopped in 27 removals under this driver, 13 of the traced ones with the audio function first as in `u2`, nor in 5
   under Windows' UHCI driver, nor at the 9 stops by Device Manager's disable. At `u2`'s stop the trace shows this
   driver's part of the audio function's removal under way with nothing visible pending (above): the client's
   unconfiguring select done, no isochronous transfer at any time, no command outstanding; the source shows no wait
   of this driver's own left in that REMOVE or that release; what did not come is Windows' next REMOVE. That narrows
   the stop to the span from the audio function's REMOVE entering this driver to the next REMOVE, which holds the
   rest of this driver's REMOVE, the completion back up the audio stack and 98 SE's own handling of that devnode. It
   does not say which: the VMM look marks the configuration manager blocked, not what blocked it. `u2` never reached
   the controller's stop, so point 3's defect is not its cause.
3. **A defect of this driver, in every removal of the controller on 98 SE, not of the audio function's: the
   controller thread's exit races the image's unload** (section above): `hcdThread` sets `ThreadExited` and then
   calls `PsTerminateSystemThread`; on 98 SE and ME `hcdThreadStop` waits on that event only, the REMOVE then
   completes and `hcdUnload` lets the image go; in `L36` the thread had not yet returned from its `KeSetEvent` and
returned into the freed copy ("fatal exception 0E" at that copy's base + `0x15E83`, the base read before the
removal). `L16`'s fault, in the same sequence as 50.32's `u1` and `u2`, is compatible with the same return but its
copy's base was not read. Both came after the controller had started again, so a restart's answer can still read
"Controller restarted"; `L16`'s left the clock stopped. Read with the audio device on the controller only, 1
identified and 1 compatible in 22 removals.
4. **The Tree's route differs from Device Manager's in one property; no failure was seen to follow it.** The removal
   the Tree asks for (`CM_Query_Remove_SubTree`, then `CM_Remove_SubTree`, then a rescan of the parent:
   `xhcitr\tr_rst.c` `tr_rst_seq9x`) reaches this driver as QUERY_REMOVE to every devnode of the subtree first and
   then the REMOVEs, so that when the audio function is removed every other devnode is already query-removed and
   waiting; Device Manager's Remove (`L31`) sends each devnode its QUERY_REMOVE and its REMOVE together, bottom up.
   50.32's `u2` stopped in the Tree's order, but so did every passing Tree removal here (25), and Device Manager's
   order was read only twice under this driver (once traced). Device Manager's Remove also unloads the image (`L31`),
   so point 3 is not the Tree's alone. Device Manager's Remove and Refresh differs in that Windows forgets the
   controller and asks for its driver again (both stacks), so that route does not reach the re-arrival; its disable
   is no removal at all but a stop of the subtree (QUERY_STOP, STOP; the devnodes and this driver's image stay), and
   its enable a start.
5. **"Installed earlier" is a different case.** There the Tree's query-remove was cancelled, a sound then streamed,
   and 98 SE's `usbaudio.sys` faulted on its first isochronous transfer (`L01`, `L02`), lessons.md's documented
   failure of QEMU's `usb-audio` on 98 SE; who refused the removal was not read. The arrival stops of point 1 came in
   6 of 9 such starts on both stacks, quiet or not; under Windows' UHCI driver, made quiet, one start passed its
   arrival and Device Manager's Remove (`L42`).
6. **`3.5.0.0`**: restarted by the Tree 4 times (`L24`), removed by Device Manager (`L08`) and disabled once (`L37`)
   with the audio device on it, as 6dcd3e51f, each unloading removal moving its image as the `qemu` flavour's does
   (`L24`'s copies at `FF146360`, `FF1A7D60`, `FF209D60`, `FF1A5D60`); point 3's code is older than 50.32 (the
   source's own comment names the window), and no fault came in these 5.

**Answers.** (1) No removal stopped here on any route: the Tree's restart, Device Manager's Remove (whose order of
requests differs from the Tree's) and its disable (a stop, not a removal), the audio device or all devices unplugged;
the stop after the answer is the audio device's arrival, which 98 SE also makes on Windows' own UHCI driver with no
package; `3.5.0.0` behaved as 6dcd3e51f. (2) The device is served by Windows' own `USBAUDIO.SYS` (`WDMA_USB.INF`) on
both stacks; its arrival stops 98 SE with no package of this project. Whether its removal does, as `u2` stopped, was
not reproduced on either stack. (3) At `u2`'s stop: the audio function (interfaces 0 and 1) entering its REMOVE after
its client's successful unconfiguring select, no pipe of it open, no isochronous transfer ever, no command
outstanding, the HID reads pended as always; the removal waited for Windows' next REMOVE. The keyboard changed no
outcome here; the walk's order followed the plugging. (4) The stop after the answer: an arrival stop, of a kind 98 SE
also makes on Windows' UHCI driver with no package; that `a1`'s and `L09`'s have that cause is not established. The
stop inside the removal: not shown to be a property of the Tree's route (its subtree-first order is the one
difference from Device Manager's Remove, and no stop followed it here) nor a defect in this driver's removal of the
audio function (nothing of it visibly outstanding and no wait of its own left in its source there, though that its
work had finished is not shown; not reproduced in 27), and not shown to be Windows' either; it stays open at one
reading. A different defect of this driver was found on the way: the controller thread's exit against the image's
unload on 98 SE (point 3; `hcd_ctl.c` `hcdThread` / `hcdThreadStop`, `hcd_entry.c` `hcdUnload`), identified once
(`L36`) and compatible once (`L16`) in 22 removals. No fix is designed here.

**Not read.** A real USB audio device (the emulated one cannot stream on 98 SE); ME; a playing or recording stream at
the removal (docs/issues/25's wait, read by usb-wdm-free's work, needs one; none existed in these removals); the
`release` flavour of 6dcd3e51f (50.32's `a1` ran gate E's `release`; the stop it reached is an arrival stop, which 98
SE also makes with no driver of this project); restarts without the audio device, to see whether point 3 needs it;
the `release` flavour against point 3 beyond `3.5.0.0`'s 5 removals.

## The USB Tree while the controller thread is held: what waits, for how long, and what to do (2026-11-20)

From worker sdq's side finding in 50.20 leg 2 (L2a-2kb): `XHCITR /eject` was read as reading the tree through
the driver first, so that with the controller thread held its confirmation appeared only after the hold. In the
field the thread can be busy for many seconds: up to about 21 s in a recovery where the 50.30 handling applies, 5 s
otherwise. A reading of the tool and of the driver's side of every request it sends, a measurement on 98 SE and
2000, and a proposal. No product code changed, nothing committed.

**Branch read.** `3.5.1.0` at `9747cd96f` (the integration flag `INT-ABC-MERGED.flag` was absent when this began).
The flag appeared at 01:59 and `3.5.1.0` moved to `6372ce8cb` with 50.30 to 50.32 merged; the reading below was
checked again there. The merge adds fields to the recovery-status answer (50.30, 50.31) under the same door gate and
controller lock, and refuses a queued descriptor read for a frozen device; the tool's tree read sends the same
requests; the tray also reads the recovery status when the window is closed; the new path, the restart of a
controller (50.32), is described at the end.

### What each request waits on (the driver's side)

Three things decide whether a request of the tool waits for the controller thread:

- **The door gate** (`DoorGate`, `hcd_door.c` `HcdDoorGateEnter`): a synchronization event used as a mutex, held
  by a controller start and stop (`HcdStartController`, `HcdStopController`) and by each door request that reads
  the extension or the registers. The controller thread never takes it (`hcd_ctl.c`, above `HcdStartController`).
- **The power gate** (`PowerGate`, `HcdPowerGateEnter`): held by the controller thread across its service pass
  (`hcd_ctl.c` `hcdThread`: `HcdPowerGateEnter`, `HcdEnumService`, `HcdPowerGateLeave`), which runs the
  enumeration, the commands and EP0 transfers with their deadlines, the endpoint resets of `RESET_PIPE` and the
  cancels (`HcdCfgRetryService`, `HcdCfgCancelService`, `HcdCfgService`) and the hold service; and held again,
  separately, by an in-place recovery for its whole length (`hcd_ctl.c`, the recovery's `HcdPowerGateEnter` after
  `RecoveryRequested`), which the thread's poll (`hcdPoll`) runs before the service pass. Between the two the gate
  is free. Whatever holds the thread inside either holds the gate: a stalled command waiting out its deadline, a
  recovery, and in this test the rendezvous of fault 0x23 (`hcd_inj.c` `HcdInjRendezvous`, called from
  `hcd_cfg.c` between the device's clear and the recycle, inside the service pass).
- **The thread's door queue** (`hcdDoorPend`, task 36.45): a descriptor read the bus cannot answer from what it
  read at enumeration is queued for the thread and served in the service pass after `HcdCfgService`
  (`HcdDoorService`), so it waits for the pass under way, and for a recovery before it, to end.

None of the three has a time limit on NT: a gate wait returns only when the gate is free. `HcdWaitEvent`'s bound
counts unsatisfied returns, the undocumented `0xFFFFFFFF` Windows 98 can return: after 100 in a row the wait is
abandoned and the caller goes on **without** the gate, recorded as `gate.door.missed` / `gate.power.missed`
(`hcd_svc.c`). That is no time limit either, and was not seen here (the 98 SE waits below lasted the whole hold). A
queued descriptor read has no deadline until the thread takes it; from then the thread's own EP0 bound applies, and
the request can no longer be cancelled (`hcdDoorTake` clears its cancel routine).

| Request (who sends it) | Driver's side | Waits for the thread? |
|---|---|---|
| `IOCTL_XHCI98_QUERY` (XHQ, `0x222920`): version, failed flag, driver log, counters, storage poll | `hcdDoorQuery`: door gate, PCI configuration by `IRP_MN_READ_CONFIG`, controller lock | no, unless the door gate is taken (below) |
| `IOCTL_XHCI98_HOLDS` (XHH, `0x222928`): the held ports (3.5.1.0's tool) | `hcdDoorHolds`: door gate, memory only | no, unless the door gate is taken |
| recovery status (XHR, `0x22292C`): the window's controller line, the tray's menu, the restart (50.30 to 50.32) | `hcdDoorRecovery`: door gate, controller lock | no, unless the door gate is taken |
| ACPI tables (XHA, `0x222924`): `/acpi` on 98 SE and ME | `HcdAcpiRequest`: its own gate, waited for 10 s at most, then "busy" | no |
| `IOCTL_USB_USER_REQUEST` request 1 (controller information; Windows' Advanced tab) | door gate, PCI configuration | no, unless the door gate is taken |
| `IOCTL_USB_USER_REQUEST` request 3, the pass-through (`TR_SNAP_IOCTL`), with the snapshot request's signature: snapshot windows | `hcdDoorSnapshot`: door gate, **then the power gate**, held to the last register read | **yes**, and it holds the door gate meanwhile |
| the same request without the snapshot signature (`/probe`'s route checks, `tr_snap.c` `probe_call`) | refused `BAD_REQUEST` before the power gate | no, unless the door gate is taken |
| `GET_HCD_DRIVERKEY_NAME`, `GET_ROOT_HUB_NAME` (controller FDO) | names under `PdoListLock` | no |
| hub IOCTLs: node information, connection information (plain, `_EX`, `_EX_V2`), connection name, driver key, attributes, capabilities | `hcdDoorNodeIoctl`: copies under `PdoListLock` and the controller lock | no |
| `GET_DESCRIPTOR_FROM_NODE_CONNECTION`: device descriptor, configuration 0 | answered from the enumeration's copy | no |
| `GET_DESCRIPTOR_FROM_NODE_CONNECTION`: strings, device_qualifier, BOS, anything else | `hcdDoorPend`: queued for the thread | **yes** |
| `IOCTL_STORAGE_GET_DEVICE_NUMBER` (NT, the disks' letters) | the disk class driver, not this driver | not through this driver |

The cascade: a pass-through waiting on the power gate keeps the door gate, so while it waits every XHQ, XHH and XHR
request of any process, and Windows' own Advanced tab, waits behind it. `3.5.0.0`'s tool has no XHH request: its
tray's hold watch reads the held ports through the pass-through, every 10 s on a job thread, on every system
(`v3.5.0.0:xhcitr/xhcitr.c` `poll` calls `hold_poll` every tenth poll unconditionally; the removal warning and
`tr_hold_notice_on` decide only whether a hold is announced afterwards). Its installer starts that tray at login
("It starts at login", read in this work's 2000 install).

### What each action of the tool sends (`3.5.1.0`'s `xhcitr.c`)

Most actions read the tree again first (`refresh_model`): the device tree from the configuration manager (`walk`),
the NHIs' query (`CM_Q_IOCTL`, xhcicm, not this driver), each `XHCI98HC<n>` / `HCD<n>` door's driver key and root
hub name, each hub's node and connection requests (`usb_scan_hub`), XHQ for the running version (`hc_ver_read`), on
NT each disk's device number (`disk_letters_nt`), and the descriptor reads named after the table. Then, by caller:

| Action | Sends besides the tree | Waits for the thread when |
|---|---|---|
| `/eject id=` (a USB device) | the tree, then the confirmation (`usb_confirm`), then the eject (`CM_Request_Device_Eject` on NT, `CM_Query_Remove_SubTree` and `CM_Remove_SubTree` on 98 SE and ME) | the tree read queues a descriptor read, or the door gate is taken |
| The window opening, a first start | `WinMain`'s `refresh_model(0)` before any window or icon exists, then `open_window` -> `refresh_window` (the tree again, XHH and XHR per controller, `hold_read_all`) | as above: nothing at all shows while the first read waits; then a window that does not paint |
| The window opening from a running tray (Open, or a second start) | the tray's `open_window`: the tree, XHH, XHR (no `WinMain` read) | as above: a window that does not paint |
| The window's Refresh (F5) | the tree, XHH, XHR; the selected node's details | as above, plus strings and BOS with View > Descriptors on |
| Selecting "Driver log (xhci98)" | XHQ (`log_hcd`; the pass-through only for a driver before revision 12) | the door gate taken |
| Save Report (window) | no new tree read: every node's details with the descriptors fetched (`write_report` -> `details_of(..., 1)` -> `usb_fetch`: configuration, string 0 and the device's string indexes, BOS from USB 2.01; each only once, none for an index 0), the logs by XHQ, then a `/snapshot` child per controller (`report_snapshots`, 120 s each, then ended, at most 10 s more) | **yes**: the strings and BOS are queued for the thread, and the snapshot child waits on the power gate holding the door gate |
| `/report` | `refresh_model(1)`, then as Save Report | **yes**, as Save Report |
| `/dump`, `/snapshot /c N` | the pass-through with the snapshot signature, window after window (`tr_snap.c`) | **yes**, and it takes the door gate meanwhile |
| Save Snapshot (window), `/snapshot` without `/c` | `/snapshot` first reads the tree (`refresh_model(1)`); both then run a snapshot child per controller (`snap_all`, 120 s each, then ended, at most 10 s more), each the pass-through as above | **yes**: the children as above; `/snapshot`'s tree read as for the tree |
| `/probe` | the route checks: the pass-through without the snapshot signature, controller information | only the door gate taken |
| Quick save (tray menu or hotkey) | a job thread: `/report` (600 s), a snapshot set per controller (`snap_all`, 120 s each; 180 s for the fallback `/snapshot /c 0`), `/set /show` (120 s), each a child run ended at its limit (`snap_child`; one that cannot be ended in 10 s more is left) | **yes** (the report and the snapshots), on its own thread; the tray's own door reads then wait behind a snapshot's door gate |
| The icon's left-click menu (`tray_unit_menu`) | the tree on the tray's thread (`refresh_model(0)` when the window is closed), then the menu | as for the tree |
| The icon's right-click menu (`tray_context_menu`) | nothing: no refresh | no |
| The tray's timer (each second, `poll`) | the NHIs' query; every 5 s XHQ and, with the window closed, XHR (`red_hc_read`); each second XHQ with the drive notice on (`stor_poll`); the tree again on a device change | the door gate taken: the tray's thread then freezes |
| The tray's hold watch (3.5.1.0, every 10 s, only when switched on) | XHH on a job thread | the door gate taken (on the job thread only) |
| The restart of a controller (window, tray, `/restart id=`; merged tool) | the tree, on 98 SE and ME configuration descriptors, then the stop; see "What the merged tool adds" | the tree's and configuration reads as above; the stop's own wait for the thread |
| `/setlevel`, `/set` | the registry; `/set /show` the settings | no |
| `/acpi` | NT: the firmware interface only; 98 SE, ME: the device tree, the NHIs, the controllers' doors (no USB scan) and XHA | no (XHA's own 10 s gate) |
| `/selftest` | nothing | no |

When the tree read itself queues a descriptor read: `fast_qual` asks a device_qualifier of a Full-Speed device
behind a Full-Speed hub on this driver's controller (`tr_fast_wants_qual`); `fast_product` asks the product string
of a device the faster-port notice counts that has no specific name; the tray's drive notice (`stor_name`) asks the
product string of a drive with no specific name, once per drive; the details pane with View > Descriptors on fetches
the selected device's strings and BOS. None of these occurred in the measured guests.

**Time limits in the tool.** None on any `DeviceIoControl` (all synchronous, no overlapped I/O); none on the
window's or the tray's refresh. The snapshot children of a report, of Save Snapshot and `/snapshot` without `/c`,
and of the Quick save have the limits above (a child is ended at its limit and waited for 10 s more); the
eject's own lock (`ej_lock`) waits 10 s for another eject; the restart's limits are below; the 32-bit tool on 64-bit
Windows waits for `XHCITR64.EXE`'s one-shot run without a limit (`wow64_handoff`).

**The reading's prediction.** With only `3.5.1.0`'s tool running and none of the descriptor reads above arising, the
eject's confirmation, the window, its Refresh and the icon's menus do not wait for a held thread: their requests
take the door gate alone. Save Report and `/report` wait, for the descriptor reads and the snapshot child. Anything
taking the snapshot pass-through (a snapshot, a report, a Quick save, an older tool's tray) waits, and while it
waits every other door request waits behind it.

### The measurement: 98 SE and 2000, the thread held 20 s

**Build and rig.** The gated x86 `qemu` build of `779c6a5d2` (`E:\xhci98-wt\w50-startmenu`,
`out\gated-x86-qemu.txt`: `xhci98.sys` `783EF699...`, `xhciuas.sys` `ECDABE5D...`) and that tree's `XHCITR.EXE`
(`2e6bedee...`), as worker sdq used them; nothing under `xhcitr\` and none of `hcd_door.c`, `hcd_ctl.c`,
`hcd_enum.c`, `hcd_cfg.c`, `hcd_inj.c` and `xhci_qry.h` differs between `779c6a5d2` and `9747cd96f` (the merged
`6372ce8cb` is read below, not measured). Emulator `emu25c` (`aaf9768b...`, the 50.20 one, with `usb-uas
x-refuse-rw-every`). Guests: the q35 98 SE and 2000 bases, one vCPU each, the published `3.5.0.0` installed (98 SE
with NUSB 3.3's storage files), the gated build's `xhci98.sys` and `xhciuas.sys` put over it, the value layer
`XhciStreamDequeueAvoid` 1 and fault 0x21 arg 1 (the controller flagged, so the drive's streams open to the
contract), a UAS drive (`usb-uas` with a blank 64 MB `scsi-hd`, `x-refuse-rw-every=2`) attached after the desktop,
no other USB device. Prepared images `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\ejwait\p98` and `p2k`, each run a fresh overlay. Development
host A under the other workers' load (19 to 22 emulators running).

**The hold.** Rendezvous point 2 (fault 0x23 arg 2) armed; a single READ(10) sent until one is refused (2000:
`PTCANCEL`, SCSI pass-through; 98 SE: `ASPIRD`, ASPI - xhciuas sends an ATA PASS-THROUGH to the device once per
start, so the ATA refusal cannot be repeated); the recovery's `RESET_PIPE` then holds the controller thread at point
2 inside its service pass; the release (fault 0x23 arg 0) by `regedit /s`, started 20 s after the refusal by a
detached process; the action started about 2 s after the refusal. From QEMU's own trace (the refusal's Stop
Endpoint to the recycle's Configure Endpoint): 2000, 18 holds of 20.13 to 20.26 s; 98 SE, 18 holds of 21.1 to
27.3 s (on 98 SE the release is armed 1 to 7 s after the refusal, so the hold is longer than 20 s; every action
started inside its hold, at least 9.8 s before the release). On 98 SE the driver's log, read through the held
reports, has the rendezvous notes in pairs (`qemu.inj.rv.reached` / `qemu.inj.rv.released`, 201 to 213 polls of
100 ms).

**The probe.** `TRWAIT.EXE` (scratch, never tracked) starts or pokes the tool and times on the guest's clock: the eject
(`XHCITR /eject "id=USB\VID_46F4&PID_0003\27842-0000:00:1C.0:00.0-4"`) until its dialog "Stop a USB device" is
visible (then Cancel); `/report` until the program ends; the icon's left click (`NIN_KEYSELECT`, which runs
`tray_unit_menu`) and right click (`WM_CONTEXTMENU`) until a menu is visible; a plain start with the tray running
(the window opens in the tray's process) until the window is visible and until it answers a message; the window's
Refresh (`WM_COMMAND IDM_REFRESH` sent) until it returns; and the eject started 2 s after a `/dump` (the
pass-through). Before every run the installed `3.5.0.0` tray is closed and the gated build's tool started in the tray
(`XHCITR /tray`), as a `3.5.1.0` install has it. A first start with no tray was not measured.

**Readings** (ms, guest clock; B without a hold, H with the thread held). "Release" gives two times, counted from the
action's start as the probe measured it (the program's start for the eject, `/report` and the window; the posted
click or the sent Refresh for the menus and Refresh): the release process's due time, just before it starts
`regedit /s`, and the time `regedit` had ended. The value is written between the two, and the driver polls for it
every 100 ms.

| Action | System | B (three) | H (three) | Release after the action's start | Waited for the thread? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Eject: the confirmation shown | 2000 | 500, 510, 501 | 500, 511, 461 | 17,936-17,956 / 17,926-17,946 / 17,936-17,956 | no |
| | 98 SE | 576, 571, 483 | 585, 432, 503 | 17,689-18,499 / 18,220-19,105 / 18,005-19,635 | no |
| `/report`: the program ended | 2000 | 981, 971, 1,002 | 18,426, 18,467, 18,396 | 17,925-17,945 / 17,926-17,946 / 17,915-17,935 | **yes**: ended 0.46 to 0.52 s after the release's end |
| | 98 SE | 1,292, 1,335, 1,243 | 19,049, 19,015, 19,117 | 17,985-18,128 / 17,874-18,012 / 18,007-18,128 | **yes**: 0.92 to 1.00 s after |

The tray answered a message within 10 ms after every menu. With nothing waiting for the thread, every action ran as
fast held as unheld. The held `/report` cycles do not tell which of the report's two waits (the descriptor reads,
the snapshot child) met the hold first. The `/dump`, started detached with no console, ends with a result box
(`run_snap`) that nobody dismissed, so its end was not read (the probe's 30 s wait for it ran out in every cycle,
held or not).

**What the user sees, by action** (the readings above, and the reading for what was not run):

- The eject's confirmation, the window from the tray, its Refresh, both icon menus: no difference while the thread is
  held, in this configuration (no descriptor read arising, nothing taking the door gate).
- Save Report from the window: the window stops painting and answering from the moment the report starts until the
  thread lets go, then the file is there (it runs on the window's thread, `save_report_dialog`); `/report`: nothing
  until it ends. No message says why.
- Anything asked while a snapshot waits: whatever was asked (here the eject's confirmation) appears only once the
  thread lets go - nothing at all is shown meanwhile. A tray running at the same time also freezes at its next door
  read (reading; not run).

**Guest clocks** (the guest's `GetTickCount` at each unheld box and report cycle against the host's arrival time of
that cycle's first COM1 line): 2000 0.9999 over 530 s; 98 SE 1.0000 over 759 s (run `s98 a`) and 0.990 over 742 s
(run `r98 b`): the normal state, not the slow one of 50.20's L2a-98d.

**Runs, and the ones that do not count.** `r2k b` (2000) and `s98 a` (98 SE) are the readings above. Void: `r2k a`
(the drive's devnode was never made: the prepared image's wizard had been dismissed; fixed by installing the drive
through its wizard on the image, `PhysicalDrive2` then present); `r98 a` (98 SE gives every child a redirected
handle, so the release process held the cycle's output file and its lines were lost; the probe then wrote its own
file); `r98 b` (its "held" cycles held nothing - the drive-wait loop's `ASPI1` had spent xhciuas's one ATA
PASS-THROUGH at the drive's arrival, so no `RESET_PIPE` came after it, and QEMU's trace shows no hold; its unheld
readings agree with `s98 a`'s).

**Evidence.** `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\ejwait\r2k\` (`ts-b.txt` COM1 with host time, `tsd-b.txt` the debug port,
`qemu-b.out` QEMU's trace, screenshots), `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\ejwait\s98\` (the same, tag `a`); the kit

### The 50.20 observation

The measurement shows `3.5.1.0`'s confirmation does not wait for a held thread by itself in that configuration, so
L2a-2kb's wait, if it was one, came from something else. A plausible cause, not confirmed: the `3.5.0.0` tray. The
published `3.5.0.0` was installed in those guests, and its installer starts its tray at login; that tray's hold
watch reads through the pass-through every 10 s whatever its settings; a watch begun inside the hold takes the door
gate and waits on the power gate, and an eject's door requests then wait behind it -
the cascade cycles 34 and 35 measure. Whether that tray was running in L2a-2kb is not recorded, and the run did not
record when its hold began (its COM1 lines give the trigger's start, 20:56:55.9, and the eject's start, 20:57:58.6,
and its 60 s hold ran out, `rv.released=00020258`), so whether the eject started inside the hold at all is not read.

### What the merged tool adds (`3.5.1.0` at `6372ce8cb`, read, not measured)

The tree read sends the same requests. New is the restart of a controller (50.32, `rst_call`, from the window, the
tray's menu or `/restart id=`). Before the stop it reads: `/restart` reads the tree first (`refresh_model(0)`, with
the descriptor reads named above); on 98 SE and ME `rst_collect` -> `rst_scan9x` reads each device's configuration
descriptors, indexes 0 to 7 (any index above 0 is a queued read for the thread), before the confirmation and again
just before the call; and it takes the eject's lock (`ej_lock`, 10 s, shared with the eject). On 2000 and later it
calls the class installer's property change
(`DIF_PROPERTYCHANGE`) on the calling thread; on 98 SE and ME a query-remove, a remove and the parent's rescan. The
stop this causes waits for the controller thread to leave (`HcdStopController` -> `hcdStopBody` -> `hcdThreadStop`)
inside the door gate, so asked while the thread is held, the call returns only when the thread lets go, and every
door request of any process waits for that time too. The restart's own limits: 10 s for a hold-watch job to finish
(`rst_hold_quiet`), then recovery-status samples every 0.5 s for a nominal 30 s (`TR_RST_SETTLE_MS`), each a door
request that a taken door gate can make longer. A disable in Device Manager meets the same stop. Option 1 below does
not change this: the stop must wait for the thread.

### The options, with costs (recommendation first)

What is left to fix in `3.5.1.0` is two things: (A) a snapshot read (Save Snapshot, `/snapshot`, `/dump`, the
report's and the Quick save's snapshot children) waits for a busy thread **and keeps the door gate while it waits**,
so the eject's confirmation, the window's Refresh, the icon's left-click menu and the tray's own reads, in every
process, wait behind it; (B) Save Report and `/report` wait for a busy thread through the descriptor reads, with the
window frozen (Save Report runs on the window's thread). Each wait lasts as long as the thread is busy - up to about
21 s for one recovery where the 50.30 handling applies, 5 s otherwise, and more where a report meets several busy
periods in turn. Nothing anywhere has a time limit, and no aggregate bound for a report is established.

1. **Recommended: the snapshot pass-through stops waiting for the thread (driver and reader).** In
   `hcdDoorSnapshot`, try the power gate without waiting (`KeWaitForSingleObject` with a zero timeout, the form
   `hcd_enum.c` `hcdTimerFired` uses; on Windows 98 an unsatisfied `0xFFFFFFFF` return read as "busy") instead of
   waiting for it. When the thread holds it, answer the window from memory alone and say so: a new header status
   bit, "busy", with the register words not read (`XHCI_SNAPSHOT_S_NO_MMIO` for PORTSC, as today; the HCD region's
   register words and the routing record, which is copied under both gates, marked unavailable rather than zeroed).
   This is more than one line in the reader: `tr_snap.c` refuses every status bit but `TRUNCATED` and `PAST_END`
   for the slots, word and HCD regions, so the new bit must be admitted there and the unavailable words decoded
   and shown; an older reader meeting the bit will refuse those windows (a newer driver with an older tool only).
   Removes (A): the pass-through no longer waits and no longer blocks anything else, for every caller. It also
   removes the snapshot half of (B); the descriptor half stays, and so does any descriptor read of a tree read
   before a snapshot (`/snapshot` without `/c` reads the tree first). Changes: `src/hcd_door.c` (`hcdDoorSnapshot`), `src/xhci.h`
   (the bit and the unavailable marking), `xhcitr/tr_snap.c` (admit, decode, print), `snaptest.cmd` vectors,
   design record 13 sections 8.8 and 8.12, `docs/contributing/snapshot-reader.md`; no import change. Cost: a
   snapshot taken during a recovery has no register readings and no routing record - exactly when they would be
   interesting; one taken after the recovery has them. Proof: `snaptest.cmd` with the busy answers; this rig's
   cycles 33 to 35 on 98 SE and 2000 with the `/dump` given a console (so its result goes to the console, not a box)
   and its end read: the eject's confirmation under 1 s while the `/dump` runs inside a 20 s hold, the dump ending
   within seconds and saying the controller was busy; the same with Save Snapshot and `/snapshot` without `/c`
   (their children each ending within seconds); an unheld `/dump`, Save Snapshot, Save Report and Quick save on
   both, compared with the gated build's on the same guest (registers present, no busy bit).
   Rejected variant: releasing the door gate while waiting for the power gate. The stop takes the door gate and
   then the power gate; any other order risks a deadlock with it and needs its own proof.
2. **With 1: say it in the guide (documentation only).** `xhcitr/README.TXT` gets one sentence: Save Report and the
   Quick save wait while the controller is resetting a device. Covers (B) at no risk; it promises no length. No
   leg; `scripts\check-readme-text.ps1`.
3. **Save Report with a time limit (tool).** The report's descriptor reads (`usb_desc`) sent overlapped on a handle
   opened for it, with one overall budget for the report (say 3 s): a read still queued when the budget runs out is
   cancelled (`CancelIo`; the door's queued request has a cancel routine, `hcdDoorCancel`, while the thread has not
   taken it), every later read is skipped, and the report says the strings were not read. A read the thread has
   already taken cannot be cancelled and ends within the thread's EP0 bound, so the overlapped buffers must live
   until each request completes. Removes the descriptor half of (B) for the report and the details pane. Changes:
   `xhcitr/xhcitr.c` (`usb_desc`, an overlapped `open_device`), one report line. Cost and risk: overlapped
   `DeviceIoControl` and `CancelIo` to this driver through NTKERN on 98 SE and ME have never been read in this
   project; legs: Save Report held and unheld on 98 SE, ME and 2000 (strings present unheld, the line present held,
   the report's descriptor part ending within the budget plus one EP0 bound). Not recommended now: (B) is the wait
   of a user who asked for a report, and option 2 says it.
4. **A "busy" field in the query answer (driver and tool).** The thread stamps when its pass or a recovery began;
   XHQ serves "busy for N s"; the window's status bar says the controller is busy, and Save Report can skip the
   strings. Changes: `src/hcd_ctl.c` (the stamp), `src/hcd_door.c`, `src/xhci_qry.h` (a revision), `xhcitr`
   (status bar, report). Cost: a revision of the query request, both architectures' legs. Useful only if (B) is to
   be shown or avoided; option 3 does that with less.
5. **The eject asks before it reads the tree (tool).** Not recommended: in `3.5.1.0` the confirmation does not wait
   for the thread (measured, in the configuration above), and it cannot list what stops before the tree is read. It
   would put the confirmation ahead of the cascade (which option 1 removes) and of the tree read's own descriptor
   reads (`fast_scan`, `stor_scan`; which option 1 leaves), but the eject itself would then wait after the user's
   OK, with the same lack of any message.
6. **Leave it and document it.** Without 1, (A) stays: a Save Report or Quick save during a recovery freezes the
   eject's confirmation, the window's Refresh and the tray for as long as the recovery. Documentation alone cannot
   fix that.

**Recommendation: 1 and 2.**

**Wording drafted for the owner** (none is in the tree; each is the owner's to rephrase):

- Option 2, `xhcitr/README.TXT` (the guide's section on Save Report and the Quick save): "While a USB device that
  stopped answering is being reset, Save Report and Quick save wait until the reset has finished."
- Option 1, the snapshot reader's line where the busy bit is set: "The controller was busy: its registers were not
  read. Save the snapshot again in a minute."
- Option 3, the report's line under a device: "(Strings not read: the controller was busy.)"
- Option 4, the window's status bar: "The USB controller is busy: some details may come late."

**What the legs add beyond the rule.**

- **An eject carried out while the thread is held waits for the thread, on both systems.** The confirmation no longer
  waits (L2), but the stop it asks for does: on 2000 the result came with the release (16.7 s after the eject's
  start; the release ended at 15.9 s). On 98 SE it came 56.2 s after the eject's start, 62.5 s after the refusal.
  Measured there: the release helper, armed at the refusal and due 20.0 s later, logged its end 62.0 s after it was
armed - 41,974 ms for
  one `regedit /s` (the helper logs only before starting the program and after its wait, which is 30 s at most, and
  then the exit code, 0; it does not stamp when the program started or when the value was written). The driver's
  debug port has the rendezvous reached at 09:37:09.6, the thread's next lines at 09:38:11.0 and the release value
  read at 09:38:12.0. Inferred, not shown: the release was held up while the removal waited for the thread, and the
  thread left at the rendezvous's own 60 s limit (the timing fits it), after which the removal ended and the release
  ran. Not a change of this branch: section 8.8.1 leaves a stop's and a removal's wait for the thread as it was;
  reported, not investigated further.
- **98 SE's detached `/dump` started late.** In cycles 07-09 and 30 the helper was asked to start the `/dump` 2 s
  before the eject; its "started" stamp, printed when its `CreateProcess` had returned, came 4.1 to 4.4 s after it
  was asked on 98 SE (2000: 70 to 100 ms). Where in that time the delay lies (the helper's own start, the process
  creation) is not read. So on 98 SE the `/dump` and the eject started within 0.25 s of each other, both inside the
  hold; the confirmation came 756 to 1,068 ms after the eject's start, 0.3 to 0.6 s over the unheld 427 to 437 ms.
  That fits the door gate being kept up to 500 ms once per hold, but the reading does not separate it from the two
  programs starting together. L2's case as written (the eject 2 s after the `/dump`) is read on 2000 only.
- **The probe could not close the eject's result box.** A posted `WM_COMMAND IDOK` closed the confirmation but not
  the result box, on both systems, so the eject's process stayed until a key from the host closed the box (2000 at
  09:36:2x, just before cycle 31; 98 SE at 09:39:3x, before cycle 31); the probe's "NOT ENDED within 60000 ms" for
  cycles 30 and 31 is that.
- Refresh cycles 24 and 25 report "the window is already open" from their opening step, as in the earlier matrix:
  the window was open, and Refresh was timed.

## 50.35 98 SE: the Start menu that did not open with a USB HID device plugged, and the shutdown fault, both on an image never given this project's package (2026-11-18 to 2026-11-19)

Task 50.35 (owner, 2026-11-18) takes 50.26's first open item: a Start menu that did not open with a USB HID device
plugged, and the starts that then did not shut down by the ACPI power button (`P17`, `H23`, `U04`, `V14`), seen
under this driver and under Windows' own UHCI driver. To be settled: whether it occurs with no package of this
project installed, what conditions bring it, and whether any change in this project is called for. Diagnosis by
guest runs only: nothing in `src\` changed. Branch `w50-startmenu` from `3.5.1.0` at `779c6a5d2`. Development host
A, QEMU TCG (the emulator build of 50.26's readings), headless, one processor and 512 MB a guest, at most three
guests of this item at a time (other work's guests were running on the host, so no time here is a timing). The
runs stopped for a host restart in the night of 2026-11-18/19, between two starts (none of this item's guests was
running then; every start has its stop line), and resumed on 2026-11-19 with the same harness on fresh overlays.
The evidence is under `E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\startmenu\`: `pids.txt` (every start and stop) and `kit\` (the harness
in `tools\`, the configurations in `tools\cfg\*.env`, `results.txt` with one line a start, and one folder a start
with `sess.log`, `serial.log`, `debugcon.log`, `plug.log`, `cmdline.txt`; the screenshots in `shots\`).

**Build** (`779c6a5d2`, `dirty=0`; Windows' own directories first on `PATH`, `XHCI98_SELFTEST_SKIP_OK=1`): gated
x86 `all`, "BUILD + GATES PASSED (release qemu)". The guests ran its x86 images, each hash equal to the gated
record's: release `xhci98.sys` `87F5EDCE...` and `xhciuas.sys` `3046918B...`; qemu `xhci98.sys` `783EF699...` and
`xhciuas.sys` `ECDABE5D...`; and the build's `XHCITR.EXE` `2E6BEDEE...`.

### The guests

- **`prepN`, never given any package of this project.** An overlay of the q35 98 SE base
  (`E:\xhci98-vm\q35-bases\w98se\disk.qcow2`: read-only, its SHA-256 `ab1d4d65...` the one its record gives; the
  record says the base was made from a fresh 98 SE install with the emulator's xHCI controller left with no driver,
  that its checks with xHCI98 `3.2.0.0` installed were made on throwaway overlays, and "Nothing of xHCI98 is on
  it"). It was started once on a machine with a PIIX3 UHCI controller (`piix3-usb-uhci`) and no xHCI
  controller, its transfer drive holding only two batch files of the harness: 98 SE's wizards installed "Intel
  82371SB PCI to USB Universal Host Controller" (`USB.INF`) and a `usb-tablet`, a `usb-kbd` and a `usb-mouse`, each
  as "USB Human Interface Device" (`HIDDEV.INF`), from the disk with no prompt; all were then unplugged, and the
  ACPI power button on its desktop powered it off in 2 s. Checked in two starts of fresh overlays of it (`CHKN`,
  `CHKN2`; `kit\xferC\CHK.BAT` and `CHK2.BAT`, made of Windows' own `dir`, `regedit /e` and `find`, the results
  sent to COM1): no file name on C: contains `stor98`, `s98vsd` or `xhcipfw`, and no line of the registry export
  (the whole registry: 16909 `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE` keys and 512 `HKEY_USERS` keys) contains those or `usbmtp`; the
  only file name and lines containing `xhci` are this 98 SE install's own user and computer name, `xhci98`
  (`C:\WINDOWS\XHCI98.PWL`, and the values `RegisteredOwner`, `ComputerName`, `Comment`, `Current User`, `username`
  and one named `xhci98`); `C:\WINDOWS\INF\OTHER` is empty; `C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM32\DRIVERS` holds Windows' own drivers only
  (`UHCD.SYS`, `USBHUB.SYS`, `USBD.SYS`, `HIDUSB.SYS`, `HIDCLASS.SYS` among them), no `xhci98.sys` or
  `xhciuas.sys`. No tray of this project runs on it.
- `prepX` and `prepQ`: 50.26's chain (the legs' 98 SE guest: the same base, `3.5.0.0` by its Setup, the legs build
  by Device Manager, the probe driver), on a machine with the xHCI controller behind a root port and no UHCI; one
  start placed the tip's release (`prepX`) or qemu (`prepQ`) `xhci98.sys` and `xhciuas.sys` through

Every start is a fresh overlay of its image (for `prepX` and `prepQ` the first start after the update, as in 50.26).

### The session

50.26's "disturbed" session cut to the parts every Start-menu failure there shared: no `fc` of installed files, no
MTP probe, no stick, and `XHCITR /report` only where named; every Run dialog opened by Ctrl+Esc and R (no Win+R).
Each part a switch in the configuration's file:

- Window 1, `command /k D:\RDY.BAT`, opens COM1 (its marker on COM1). Then, where named: `WORK.BAT`
  (`start /w regedit /e` of the Run key, an `fc /b` and a `find`: Windows' own programs, a stand-in for 50.26's
  steps), or 50.26's own `TR.BAT` (`start /w D:\NT\XHCITR.EXE /report`, the build's `XHCITR.EXE` run from the
  transfer drive, not installed, its report then sent to COM1). On `prepN` that report reads "No USB controller is
  driven by xhci98" and lists Windows' UHCI controller ("Opened as: HCD0").
- The USB devices of the configuration hot-plugged, 25 s apart, after window 1 is up (the tablet first where both
  the tablet and the keyboard are plugged). With a USB keyboard plugged QEMU sends every key to it.
- **Hold**: window 2, `command /c D:\KB.BAT`, writes to COM1 while window 1 holds it and meets "Write fault error
  writing device COM1", answered F at each prompt (two every time). Without the hold (`NTh0`) window 1 is closed
  before the plugs and window 2's line reaches COM1.
- **The pointer**: two moves (`NTx`: and 40 more during the write-fault prompt and 40 after window 2 closes), 50 s,
  then window 1 activated by a click on its title bar and closed by `exit`. Through the tablet where one is
  plugged; otherwise relative events (the PS/2 mouse, or the `usb-mouse` where it is plugged); `NTni` sends no
  pointer input before the test (window 1 activated by Alt+Tab); its test's click is the tablet's, as in every
  start with a tablet.
- **The test**, every start: the Start menu by Ctrl+Esc (closed by Esc), by the Windows key alone (closed by Esc),
  and by a click on Start (the tablet where one is plugged, else relative events), 20 s each; then Shut Down,
  "Shut down", OK. A start whose menu opens to none of the three: two screenshots 70 s apart (the tray clock
  compared), the ACPI power button (QMP `system_powerdown`) and 150 s watched, then Ctrl+Alt+Del and a screenshot.
  `NTpb` and `XTpb`: the ACPI power button pressed instead of Shut Down, on the healthy desktop after the test (the
  power button's control).
- **The end**: QEMU's `SHUTDOWN` event with reason `guest-shutdown` is a completed shutdown; otherwise at 150 s a
  screenshot, and the guest stopped by QMP.

A start was counted when its session ran through the test with its COM1 markers in order and its shutdown (or the
power button) was asked for; a start stopped by a check is not counted, and was replaced by a start of a new
number. A first Ctrl+Esc after the desktop that opened nothing in 20 s was sent again (as 50.26's harness did).
Added on 2026-11-19, each after a reading of the runs before it: `NTr`, `NPr` and `NTw` from its fourth start on,
after the observation that every start of 50.26 ran `XHCITR /report` in window 1 and this session did not
(`NTr`'s first start, `NTrp1`, is counted with it); then `NTK` and `XTK`, the tablet and the USB keyboard plugged
together, after the observation that eight of 50.26's nine Start-menu failures had both and none of the first 170
starts here had.

or a click, the clock stopped, the power button without effect), on an image with nothing of this project.

**What the fault names.** All thirteen: "A fatal exception 0E has occurred at 0028:C029983B in VXD VWIN32(05) +
00002363. The current application will be terminated.", on the screen 45 s after the OK; the thirteen screenshots
taken at 150 s are byte for byte the same image. The same text, address and offset as all of 50.26's faults.

**Also seen**, beside the counts:

- A Start menu that opened to some of the three tries: `XP11`, Ctrl+Esc opened nothing in the test and the Windows

- A first Ctrl+Esc after the desktop that opened nothing in 20 s and worked when sent again: nine counted starts

  device plugged.
- A desktop whose background was never painted: 26 counted starts, in sixteen of the configurations; the session ran
  on it as on any other.
- The USB keyboard: under Windows' own UHCI driver (`NK`, `NTK`) every key of the thirty counted starts arrived, as
  far as the harness checks (no retry, no key seen held), `NTK17`'s three tries aside; under this driver (`XK`) two
  starts of eight were stopped for the U key above, as was `XP10` with no USB keyboard plugged; `XTK` had none.

### Reading

**The Start menu that does not open, with the power button then without effect, occurs on an image never given this
project's package.** `NTK17` showed it on `prepN`, with the tablet and the USB keyboard on Windows' own UHCI driver
and no program of this project run. This answers the first question of 50.35 and 50.26's "Not run: a guest never
given the xHCI98 package": this project's files are not needed for it. It came in 1 of 20 starts with the tablet and
the USB keyboard on `prepN` and in none of the 20 on `prepX` under this driver; in none of the 98 starts here with a
tablet and the hold but no USB keyboard (`NT`, `NTx`, `NTw`, `NTr`, `NTni`, `XT`, `QT`, `NTpb`, `XTpb`). In 50.26,
nine of the 151 starts it ran with the hold and a USB tablet (140 counted, 11 replaced) had a Start menu that did not
open to Ctrl+Esc, seven of them also resisting a click (`R06` and `Q07` had no click tried), and eight of the nine
had a USB keyboard beside the tablet (`P17`, the ninth, had the tablet alone). So, as far as these counts go, the
USB keyboard plugged beside the tablet goes with the failure: in eight of 50.26's nine, and in the one here. The
counts are small (here 1 of 40 with both); no rate is compared between rows or drivers, and nothing shows the
keyboard, the tablet or the hold to be needed in general. `XHCITR /report` run from
the transfer drive (`NTr`, 31 starts) did not bring it. The Close Program list names one program not responding,
`Msgsrv32`; that is what the dialog showed, not a cause read. On a healthy desktop the ACPI power button powered
the guest off in each of the four `NTpb` and `XTpb` starts and in `prepN`'s making, so the power button's failure
is seen only with the menu's.

**The shutdown fault occurs on the same image, with no program of this project run.** `NTp1`, `NT11`, `NTx03` and
`NTw12` faulted on `prepN`, with the tablet on Windows' own UHCI driver, the hold, the pointer moves, and nothing of
this project in the image or the session (`NTw12` ran only Windows' own programs in window 1); `NTr`'s seven ran
this project's `XHCITR.EXE` from the transfer drive as well; `XTK04` and `XTK10` faulted under this driver, the
tablet and the USB keyboard plugged. All thirteen came with a USB tablet plugged and moved and with the COM1 hold;
none in 10 starts with the tablet and no pointer input before the test (`NTni`), 10 without the hold (`NTh0`), 20
with the `usb-mouse` or the USB keyboard instead of the tablet (`NM`, `NK`), 24 with no USB device (`NP`, `NPr`),
or 20 with the tablet and the USB keyboard on `prepN` (`NTK`); none in the 22 with the tablet alone on this driver
(`XT`, `QT`). Those counts are small and no rate is compared between rows, nor between `NTr` (7 of 31) and the rows
on the same image without `XHCITR` (4 of 31). What the guest's own components do at that offset is not read.

**Change in this project.** None is called for by these readings: both the Start-menu failure and the shutdown fault
occur on an image with nothing of this project, with Windows' own USB driver serving the devices; no code path of
this driver is implicated. No driver change is proposed.

Not run: more starts with the tablet and the USB keyboard together (one failure is a single reading); 50.26's
session unchanged on `prepN` (its `fc` step compares installed files, which `prepN` has not); the `usb-mouse` under
this driver (`XM`, no driver in that image); real hardware. Guest memory and code were not read. Every guest of
this item is stopped (`pids.txt`; `prepQ`'s stop line is doubled); the run overlays are deleted; the three prepared
images and the kit stay until the item is closed.

## 50.36 Keys lost or held through a USB keyboard on 98 SE, compared under Windows' own driver (2026-11-18 to 2026-11-19)

The second open item of 50.26's last reading ("50.26", "The shutdown fault narrowed by its conditions", "Open
items"): on 98 SE in emulated guests, the Win key held after Win+R (`H01`, `H04`, `K06` and eleven more `X-kbd`
starts) and a lost key (`H20`), cause unresolved, not compared under Windows' own USB driver. Investigation only:
nothing in `src\` changed. Development host A, QEMU TCG (the emulator build of 50.26's reading, QEMU 11.1.0),
headless, one processor and 512 MB a guest (XP: 1 GB), at most three of this item's guests at a time, in two passes:
the night of 2026-11-18 to 2026-11-19 (starts `A` to `D` and `X`, three rounds of the script each) and, after a
restart of the host, the morning of 2026-11-19 (starts `E` to `L`, one round each). **Timing is the subject, so the
host's load is part of the record**: 32 logical processors; in the night about 91% CPU load at the pass's start and
4 to 23 QEMU processes in all at the starts (other work's guests; this item's at most three); in the morning 57 to
100% CPU load and 12 to 21 QEMU processes when each start's script began (its `sess.log`). The evidence is under
`E:\xhci98-vm\p50\keys\`: `pids.txt` (every start and stop), `results.txt`, `queue.txt`, the harness in `tools\`
(`v.sh`, `vnt.sh`, `sess.sh` with each start's own copy in `tmp\`, `sessxp.sh`, `slot.sh`, `keysend.py`,
`trace-events.txt`, `trace-events2.txt`) and the readings (`analyze.py`, `agg.py`, `firstwinr.py`, `span.py`,
`held.py`, `rep6.py`, `irqlat.py`; their outputs `E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\keys\agg-final.txt` and `first-final.txt`),
one folder a start (`sess.log`, `sent.log`, `serial.log`, `trace.log`, `debugcon.log`, `cmdline.txt`, `env.sh`) and
the screenshots in `shots\`; the recorder's source under `E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\keys\rec\`.

**Build**: gated x86 `all` of `779c6a5d2` (the `3.5.1.0` tip), "BUILD + GATES PASSED (release qemu)", `dirty=0`; the
guests ran its qemu flavour, `xhci98.sys` `134E41C5...426F` and `xhciuas.sys` `B9AEEB66...265A` (the gated record
`out\gated-x86-qemu.txt`), placed in the image by `WININIT.INI`; every `xhc` start's `debugcon.log` has the qemu
flavour's debug-port lines.

**The recorder** (`KEYREC.EXE`, throwaway, untracked, built with the repository's MSVC 6.0): a `WH_JOURNALRECORD`
hook, so it sees every keyboard event as USER takes it off the system queue whatever window has the focus, and
writes each with the guest's own event time and the time it saw it to COM1 (COM2 on XP, where the legs' agent holds
COM1) and to `C:\KEYREC.TXT`; every 50 ms it also writes the set of keys `GetAsyncKeyState` reports down when that
set changes, and, from the runs started after about 01:05 (its third build, `8F9BB953...`), the foreground window
when it changes. It records the event, not the window that gets it. Two kinds of key event never reach it: a key
USER turns into a hotkey (Win+R's R press when the Run dialog opens), and a key that 98 SE gives to an active MS-DOS
window's virtual machine (the Esc of `+pre` below).

**The sender** (`keysend.py`): one QMP `input-send-event` per key event, timed on the host. A round is: Win+R in QMP
`send-key`'s own order and spacing (Win press, 10 ms, R press, 10 ms, R release, 10 ms, Win release; `ui/input.c`
`qmp_send_key`), a screenshot 1.2 s later classed as the Run dialog, the Start menu or neither, five letters, Esc;
20 letters at 100 ms; Win+R again; 20 letters at 30 ms; 10 taps whose press and release go in one QMP command; one
key 10 times at 40 ms; six Shift chords; six Ctrl chords; eight overlapping pairs; four 300 ms holds; Win+R; Esc
between blocks. 278 events and 284 scan codes a round (three Win+R). Letters are only those with no Win+letter
shortcut and no Start-menu accelerator, so an opened Start menu or a held Win key does no harm.

**The comparison**, per event: sent against received by a longest-common-subsequence alignment on scan code
(`analyze.py`). An R press missing from a Win+R whose screenshot shows the Run dialog is USER taking it as the
hotkey and is not counted as lost. A received event the alignment leaves unmatched is an extra; a press of a key
already down, or followed by another press of it within 700 ms, is counted as a typematic repeat. Held: a key the
recorder's key-state lines show down for more than 1 s (no sent hold is longer than 300 ms). The emulator's side
from QEMU's trace (`-trace events=`): `hid_kbd_queue_full` (the usb-kbd model drops a key event when its 16-entry
scan-code queue is full, `hw/input/hid.c` `hid_keyboard_event`), every successful 8-byte keyboard report
(`usb_xhci_xfer_success` on the keyboard's endpoint, `usb_uhci_packet_complete_success` with its IN token), the PS/2
scan codes; in the `+t` starts also this driver's interrupter register writes and doorbells, UHCI's register writes
and the PIC's interrupt deliveries (`trace-events2.txt`). The guest clock's rate (`firstwinr.py`): the guest
event-time span from the script's first Win press to its last Esc press, as received, over the host time between the
two as sent.

**The arms**, all on the q35 98 SE guest unless named:

- `xhc`: the legs' 98 SE image of 50.26 (`3.5.0.0` by its Setup, the legs build), the gated qemu files placed
  through `WININIT.INI` with no registry value written (`prepX`); every start is the first after that update, as in
  50.26. qemu-xhci behind a root port; usb-kbd at `xh.0` port 2, high speed, `bInterval` 7.
- `uhc`: the q35 98 SE base, never given the xHCI98 package (**package absent**), with a PIIX3 UHCI controller and
  no xHCI controller; 98 SE's wizards installed Windows' own UHCI driver ("Intel 82371SB PCI to USB Universal Host
  Controller", `USB.INF`) and the keyboard ("USB Human Interface Device", `HIDDEV.INF`) (`prepU`). usb-kbd at
  `uhci.0` port 2, full speed, `bInterval` 10.
- `ps2x`, `ps2u`: the same two images, the USB keyboard never plugged; the keys go to the PS/2 keyboard.
- `+dos`: an MS-DOS Prompt window opened through the PS/2 keyboard (Win+R, "command", Enter) and active before the
  USB keyboard's plug, as 50.26's window 1 was. `+pre`: as `+dos`, with one Esc sent through the USB keyboard 5 s
  before the script. `+early`: the USB keyboard plugged with the desktop active and 30 s waited, then the MS-DOS
  window opened, then the script about 10 s later; `+early30`: the same with 30 s more before the script. In both,
  QEMU sent the harness's keys for the MS-DOS window (Win+R, "command", Enter) to the newly plugged USB keyboard,
  not to the PS/2 one (22 more keyboard reports than the script's scan codes in every such start), so the script's
  first Win+R was not the keyboard's first keys. `+t`: as `+dos`, with the wider trace.
- `xp`: 32-bit XP SP3, a fresh overlay of 50.26's NT5 legs image (its qemu xHCI98 package of those legs,
  `XhciCancelStatus` absent), usb-kbd on xHCI98; the US Dvorak layout handled by sending Win+R's R at the R key's
  Dvorak position.

Each start: a fresh overlay of its image, 150 s from the boot, the recorder started through the PS/2 keyboard

screen check) are named where they matter and not counted; `T02` to `T04` failed the harness's own checks and are
void.
