The columns: events sent and lost by the alignment; the extras (a Win press nobody sent, typematic repeats, other:
the four key releases recorded twice, below); the starts with a key held more than 1 s after the script began; every
Win+R by its screenshot; the script's first Win+R (in every arm but `+pre`, `+early` and `+early30` the USB
keyboard's first keys after its plug); `hid_kbd_queue_full` lines; the keyboard's successful reports against the
scan codes sent (`+pre` adds the Esc's two, `+early` and `+early30` the 22 of the harness's keys for the MS-DOS
window, below); starts whose guest clock ran at about a third of the host's (below). Not counted: `E18`, `G03` and
`K09`, void by the harness's own checks before the script (below).

**No event was lost, on any arm.** Every key event sent was received by USER, in the order sent: the alignment
leaves none unmatched in any counted start (59492 events in 132 starts). QEMU's keyboard queue was never full
(`hid_kbd_queue_full` 0 in every start), and on both USB drivers the device's successful 8-byte reports equal the
scan codes sent, one each, as the model gives one queued scan code per report (`hw/input/hid.c`
`hid_keyboard_poll`), so the emulator neither dropped nor merged a key. QEMU traced no xHCI transfer error
(`usb_xhci_xfer_error` 0); this driver's debug-port lines in the `xhc` starts show Transfer Events with completion
codes 1 (Success) and 13 (Short Packet) only, `transfers cancelled` 0, and `transfers submitted` two ahead of
`transfers completed` wherever they printed (the HID class's two reads, each resubmitted as it completed). The
extras in the table are of three kinds, none a key lost: the Win press nobody sent (below); typematic repeats of the
four 300 ms holds, in the starts where the guest's clock ran at the host's rate (next paragraph); and four key
releases recorded twice with the same event time (`A05`, `A06`, `B04`, `B05`, at the first Win+R, both drivers).

**The guest's clock ran at one of two rates.** Measured per start (`firstwinr.py`), the guest's event time advanced
either at about the host's rate (0.97 to 1.00) or at about a third of it (0.34 to 0.43), with nothing between: every
night start begun before 01:40 at about a third, every one after at about the host's rate, and in the morning `E10`,
`E11` and `F10` at about a third, the rest at about the host's rate; it went with the time of the start, not with
the arm, the PS/2 ones included. At a third, the guest saw a 300 ms hold as about 100 ms and gave it no typematic
repeat; at the host's rate it saw 300 ms and gave each hold one repeat, or two (35 of 520 held presses), the first
251 to 277 ms after the press (98 SE's own repeat of a USB keyboard's key; none on PS/2, whose repeat QEMU's
keyboard model does not make). Why the rate changed was not read; the table's last column counts the starts at a
third.

**The held Win key is reproduced, and it is not USB's.** With an MS-DOS Prompt window active, a Win+R was followed,
0 to 60 ms after its own Win release, by a Win press nobody sent; USER then kept Win down (the recorder's key-state
lines) until the next Win release, 3 to 33 s later, and every letter typed meanwhile was a Win+letter. It came after
the first Win+R of 91 of the 115 starts with the window (48 of 56 on this driver, 40 of 55 on the UHCI driver, 3 of
4 through the PS/2 keyboard), after the second one too where the first had not opened the Run dialog (the window
then still active), and never in the 17 starts without the window. It came the same on all three keyboards: through
the USB keyboard on this driver, on Windows' own UHCI driver with no xHCI98 package ever installed, and **through
the PS/2 keyboard with no USB keyboard plugged** (`C04`, `C06`, `C07`). In the PS/2 start `C04` the recorder's lines
read: Win press at 80304, R release 80319, Win release 80325, **Win press 80325**, Win down in the key state from
80345, the Run dialog foreground at 80455. 50.26's harness typed into the Run dialog with its first MS-DOS window
open, and its screenshots of `H01`, `H04` and `K06` (`E:\xhci98-vm\p50\s98diag\shots\`, `-wfault`) show the Run
dialog inactive behind a single-pane "My Computer" or "Recycle Bin" window: what a Win+M (the "m" of "command") and
then the command's other letters selecting a desktop icon and its Enter opening it would leave (a reading of those
shots, not shown in those starts).

**The lost key is a Win+R the system did not take as the hotkey; its four events arrived.** In every Win+R that did
not open the Run dialog, the recorder has Win press, R press, R release and Win release, in order, within 5 to 44 ms
of each other in the guest's time; the R press, which a working Win+R never shows, went to USER as a letter: `A02`'s
screenshot after its seventh Win+R (`A02-w07.png`) shows "Recycle Bin" selected on the desktop, and with an MS-DOS
window active the window stayed foreground with nothing typed in it (`E03-w01.png`). That is 50.26's lost R (`H20`;
in its own logs `V06` and `V19`, under Windows' own UHCI driver, had Win+R tries that opened the Start menu or
nothing, `results.txt` and their `sess.log`). After the script's first Win+R (next paragraph), it came in 5 of 226
later Win+R on this driver (`A02`, `A14`, `A16` twice, `E09`), 1 of 212 on the UHCI driver (`B15`), none of 56
through the PS/2 keyboard and none of 18 on XP; in the trials, `T05` on this driver and `T01` on the UHCI driver
(its R press recorded; no screen check). `G03` and `K09` (void: the harness's Win+R for the MS-DOS window, the USB
keyboard's first keys 30 s after its plug on this driver, the desktop active) failed the same way, their four events
received.

**One difference between the two configurations is established, and its cause is not found.** The script's first
Win+R with the MS-DOS window active, where it was the USB keyboard's first keys after its plug, failed more often
under this driver than under Windows' own UHCI driver, in every pass:

| The script's first Win+R, MS-DOS window active | xHCI98: not the Run dialog | UHCI driver: not the Run dialog |
|---|---|---|
| night, `+dos` (`A07` to `A14`; `B07` to `B14`) | 6 of 8 | 0 of 8 |
| morning, `+dos` (`E01` to `E21` without the void `E18`; `F01` to `F20`) | 7 of 20 | 1 of 20 |
| morning, `+t` (`I01` to `I10`; `J01` to `J10`) | 6 of 10 | 1 of 10 |
| all three (the keyboard's first keys after its plug) | 19 of 38 | 2 of 38 |
| night, `+pre` (`A15` to `A17`; `B15`), not the first keys | 0 of 3 | 0 of 1 |
| morning, `+early` (`G`, without the void `G03`; `H`), not the first keys | 0 of 6 | 2 of 6 |
| morning, `+early30` (`K`, without the void `K09`; `L`), not the first keys | 1 of 9 | 1 of 10 |

19 of 38 against 2 of 38 has a one-sided Fisher exact probability of about 0.00001 under no difference, and each
pass alone points the same way (0.003, 0.022, 0.029). The two configurations differ in more than the driver: the
controller model (qemu-xhci against PIIX3 UHCI), the keyboard's speed and polling (high speed, 8 ms, against full
speed, 10 ms), and the image (the legs image with the package against the base with none); which of these makes the
difference is not isolated here, since 98 SE has no driver of its own for the xHCI controller. The difference is
tied to the keyboard's **first keys after its plug**: once the keyboard had carried keys before the script, the
first Win+R with the window active failed in 1 of 18 starts on this driver and 3 of 17 on the UHCI driver (`+pre`,
`+early`, `+early30`; in `+early` and `+early30` those keys were the harness's own Win+R, "command" and Enter, at
the desktop). The same first keys at the desktop, with no MS-DOS window, failed twice on this driver, both in that
harness Win+R of `+early` / `+early30` (`G03`, `K09`, void for it), in 23 such first Win+R (`xhc` 6, `G` 7, `K` 10),
and in none of 22 on the UHCI driver (`uhc` 6, `H` 6, `L` 10), with the trial `T05` failing on this driver too: too
few to call a difference. Through the PS/2 keyboard no first Win+R failed (`ps2x+dos` 4, `ps2x` 2, `ps2u` 1), nor on
XP (2).

What the traces show of it:

- **The device's reports were the same.** The six keyboard reports of that Win+R (Win's prefix, Win, Win+R, Win, the
  prefix, none) had the same content and order on both drivers, 35 to 91 ms of host time from the first to the last
  on this driver and 38 to 76 ms on UHCI (`rep6.py`, the `+dos` and `+t` starts); no queue was full.
- **Each report's interrupt was taken and acknowledged at once, on both drivers, failing or not.** In the `+t`
  starts, for each of the six reports the PIC delivered the controller's interrupt to the guest's processor, and the
  driver's interrupt routine acknowledged it, within 2.4 ms of QEMU completing the report on this driver (its write
  of the interrupter's IMAN with IP set, `src/xhci_evt.c` `XhciIsr`, not the IE-only write that re-enables it) and
  within 2.1 ms on the UHCI driver (its USBSTS write); this driver's event-ring drain ended (its ERDP write) within
  8.0 ms. The same in the six `I` starts that failed and the four that worked (`irqlat.py`, `irqlat-final.txt`).
  When the HID class got each report and resubmitted its read is not in these traces. The guest's timer interrupts
  ran at about 200 a second in all twenty.
- **Above that, the four events reach USER closer together when it fails.** In the `+dos` and `+t` starts with the
  guest clock at the host's rate, the guest's event times of that Win+R, Win press to Win release, spanned 5 to 26
  ms in the 16 failures and 19 to 53 ms in the 48 that worked, 11 of those 26 ms or less (`span.py`), while the Win
  report and the Win-release report were 30 ms or more apart on the host. The overlap means the span is not the
  cause by itself.

So the reports reach the guest in order and their interrupts are handled at once on both drivers; the failure itself
is in the hotkey's recognition, with all four events received. Where the higher rate under this configuration comes
from is not localized: the report spacing and polling differ between the two (above and below) and may bear on that
recognition, and the stretch from this driver's completion of the HID class's read through the HID class to USER is
not timed by these traces; the guest's own components, which this project does not read, are part of it.

**The interval.** For the keyboard's interrupt IN endpoint this driver writes Interval 6, 8 ms, at both speeds:
`bInterval` 7 at high speed gives `bInterval - 1` (`src/xhci_pipe.c` lines 525-527), `bInterval` 10 at full speed
gives log2(10 x 8) = 6 (lines 531-539, a declared 10 ms rounded down to 8 ms); the shipped tuning values change
neither (`XhciFastPollFsLs` 0 and the interval caps, `src/xhci98.inf` lines 260, 267, 339). Successive reports while
keys were queued came 10.2 to 11.5 ms apart at the 10th percentile on this driver and 7.3 to 10.0 ms on UHCI: QEMU's
xHCI model starts each interrupt TD at its own kick time, aligned to the endpoint's interval (`hw/usb/hcd-xhci.c`
`xhci_calc_intr_kick`, `xhci_check_intr_iso_kick`). The poll rates differ between the two configurations and are
among the differences named above; the 16-entry queue was never full.

**This driver's interrupt IN path, read in the source** (`779c6a5d2`): one URB is one TD whose last TRB has IOC
(`src/xhci_xfer.c` line 896), the doorbell rung under the controller lock as it is placed (`src/hcd_io.c` lines
2208-2214); up to four records a pipe (`HCD_PIPE_XFERS`, `src/hcd.h` line 232), further IRPs waiting in order; the
IRP completed with `IoCompleteRequest` (`src/hcd_io.c` line 3144) after its record is released under the lock (line
3117), so a resubmission from the completion routine finds one. Nothing on that path drops, merges or reorders a
report in ordinary running on one processor. The paths that could lose one are the error and cancel paths (a TD
swept with `USBD_STATUS_INTERNAL_HC_ERROR` when a later TD's event arrives first, `src/xhci_xfer.c` lines 1932-1946;
a cancel; a refused completion code; an event ring full); none was entered in these starts (the completion codes and
counters above, no cancel before the guest was stopped, one processor).

**XP cross-check** (`X01`, `X02`; plus the trial `XT1`): 1668 events, none lost, 18 Win+R, 18 Run dialogs, no held
key, 1704 reports for 1704 scan codes.

**Reading.** The keys are not lost in this driver, and not in the emulator: every report the emulator made reached
the guest's input path whole and in order, and every event reached USER. The held Win key is 98 SE's own, with an
MS-DOS Prompt window active, and comes through the PS/2 keyboard the same. The lost key is a Win+R USER did not take
as the hotkey although its four events arrived in order, on both USB drivers. One difference goes with this driver's
configuration: the script's first Win+R with an MS-DOS window active, when it is the keyboard's first keys after its
plug, failed in 19 of 38 starts against 2 of 38 under Windows' own UHCI driver. The reports and their interrupts
reach the guest in order and at once on both; where the higher rate comes from is not localized, the controller
model, speed, polling and image are not separated from the driver, its cause is not determined, and no repair is
proposed here. For harnesses, not for the driver: open the Run dialog with no MS-DOS window active, or by a click,
send one key through a newly plugged keyboard before the first Win+R, and check the dialog's text before Enter.
Whether 50.35's Start menu that does not open is the same cause is not shown here: no Start menu failed in these
starts, which sent no Ctrl+Esc and no click.

**Side observations**, not followed: `E18` (void) showed a black screen with a text-mode cursor 150 to 240 s from
its start, so the harness never reached the recorder; its `debugcon.log` ends where every start of that image ends
before a USB device is plugged (the same 8043 bytes as the `ps2x` starts), so this driver's lines do not place the
stop; one of 71 starts of that image in this item. `G03` and `K09` above. Other work's guests shared the host
throughout, so each timing here may carry their load; the counts are given per pass, and each pass was repeated many
times over at loads from 57 to 100% in the morning.

Not run: real hardware; Windows 2000 (XP was the cross-check); 50.26's whole session with the shutdown; the tablet;
the keyboard at full speed on the xHCI controller. Guest memory and Microsoft binaries were not read. Every guest of
this item is stopped (`pids.txt`); the overlays are deleted.

## 50.36 (continued): the first Win+R's difference taken apart by its variables (2026-11-19)

The one difference the reading above left standing: the script's first Win+R with an MS-DOS Prompt window active,
when it is the USB keyboard's first keys after its plug, failed (no Run dialog) in 19 of 38 starts under this driver
against 2 of 38 under Windows' own UHCI driver, with the controller model, the keyboard's speed and polling and the
image differing between the two configurations as well as the driver. This pass changes one of them at a time.
Investigation only: nothing in `src\` changed. Development host A, the same emulator build (QEMU 11.1.0, TCG,
headless, one processor and 512 MB a guest), the same recorder, sender and script as the morning's `+dos` starts above
(one round; the MS-DOS window opened through the PS/2 keyboard, the USB keyboard then plugged and 30 s waited, then
the script), each start a cold start on a fresh overlay of its arm's image, at most three at a time. The five arms
took turns in one queue (`A01`, `B01`, `C01`, `E01`, `F01`, `A02`, ...), so each arm's starts are spread over the
whole pass, 11:17 to 14:16; 16 to 32 QEMU processes on the host and 71 to 100% CPU load when each script began (its
`sess.log`). The evidence is under `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\keys2\` as the first pass's is under `keys\` (`pids.txt`,
`results.txt`, `queue.txt`, `tools\` with each start's own copy of `sess.sh` in `tmp\`, one folder a start,
`shots\`); the run names in this continuation are this pass's own, not the first pass's starts of the same names.
The outputs the numbers below come from are in `E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\keys2\` (`first2.txt`, `sum2.txt`,
`agg2.txt`, `rgaps2.txt`, `qgap2.txt`, `pred-split.txt`). The guests ran the same gated qemu files of
`779c6a5d2` (`xhci98.sys` `134E41C5...426F`, `xhciuas.sys` `B9AEEB66...265A`), placed by `WININIT.INI` through the
first pass's `UPD.BAT`; every counted start is the first after that update.

**The keyboard's speed, established.** QEMU's `usb-kbd` (`hw/usb/dev-hid.c`) has a property `usb_version`, 2 by
default, which gives the device a full-speed and a high-speed descriptor set (`desc_keyboard2`); on a USB 2 port of
the xHCI controller it attaches at high speed with `bInterval` 7, on the UHCI controller at full speed with
`bInterval` 10. With `usb_version=1` it has the full-speed set alone (`desc_keyboard`) and attaches at full speed on
the xHCI root port too. Each start logged QEMU's `info usb` line after the plug: 480 Mb/s in all 20 `A` and 20 `F`
starts, 12 Mb/s in all 20 `B`, `C` and `E` starts. So the first pass's "high speed against full speed" was right:
its `xhc` keyboard was the default `usb-kbd`, at 480 Mb/s.

**The arms** (all with the MS-DOS window, `+dos`):

- `A`: the first pass's `xhc` image (`prepX`, copied unchanged), `qemu-xhci`, the keyboard at 480 Mb/s. The
  reference.
- `B`: the first pass's `uhc` image (`prepU`, copied unchanged): no xHCI98 package ever, a PIIX3 UHCI controller on
  Windows' own driver, the keyboard at 12 Mb/s. The reference.
- `C`, **the speed**: as `A`, the keyboard plugged with `usb_version=1`, so at **12 Mb/s on the xHCI root port**,
  the rest unchanged; this driver programs the same Interval for it, 6 (8 ms; `bInterval` 10 at full speed, above,
  "The interval"). Its image (`prepXF`) was made as `prepX` was, from the legs' 98 SE guest: one start in which the
  keyboard was plugged at 480 Mb/s (by mistake, before the property was set), unplugged and plugged again at 12 Mb/s
  (no wizard either time), then `UPD.BAT` and Shut Down.
- `E`, **the image with the driver taken out of the path**: the legs' 98 SE guest (the xHCI98 package installed) with
  `qemu-xhci` and a PIIX3 UHCI controller both present (`prepXU`). 98 SE's wizards installed its own UHCI driver
  ("Intel 82371SB PCI to USB Universal Host Controller", `USB.INF`) and, with the keyboard plugged on the UHCI
  controller, its "USB Human Interface Device" (`HIDDEV.INF`; a restart asked, given as a cold start); Win+R through
  the keyboard then opened the Run dialog; then `UPD.BAT` and Shut Down. In its starts this driver ran the xHCI
  controller with nothing on it (every `E` start's `debugcon.log` is the 8043 bytes the image writes before a USB
  device is plugged), and the keyboard was on the UHCI controller under Windows' own driver at 12 Mb/s. Against `B`:
  the same path, the package-free image.
- `F`, **the xHCI controller model**: as `A` with `nec-usb-xhci` (QEMU's NEC uPD720200, PCI `1033:0194`) in place
  of `qemu-xhci` (`1B36:000D`). In its image (`prepXN`) 98 SE's wizard installed this driver for it from the
  package's INF ("xHCI98 USB 3 Controller (NEC uPD720200)"), the keyboard was checked once (Win+R through it opened
  the Run dialog), then `UPD.BAT` and Shut Down. Every `F` start's `debugcon.log` reads "PCI vendor/device=01941033".
  The keyboard at 480 Mb/s. Both models are QEMU's one xHCI core (`hw/usb/hcd-xhci.c`) behind a different PCI
  identity (`hcd-xhci-nec.c`), so this arm separates the PCI model, not the controller's behaviour. This driver keys
  on `1B36:000D` in two places only, neither on a keyboard's path: the stream restart for UAS drives
  (`XhciTolQemuStreamQuirk`, `src/xhci_tol.c` line 115) and the port-switchover model, which also needs the test value
  `XhciQemuPswModel` (`src/hcd_ctl.c` lines 1193-1196), not written in these images; no quirk table of
  `src/xhci_quirk.c` lists either model.
- `D`, **the UHCI arm's polling interval on the xHCI controller, was not built.** The emulated keyboard's
  `bInterval` is fixed in QEMU (7 at high speed, 10 at full speed), the xHCI endpoint's Interval is a power of two
  (xHCI Table 6-12), this driver programs 6 (8 ms) at both speeds, and no value it reads changes this keyboard's
  interval (`XhciFastPollFsLs`, off by default, takes with 2 or 3 a root-port full- or low-speed device asking 16 to
  63 ms and with 4 a filter's code from 128; the interval caps take devices asking more than 32 ms, or a high-speed
  one more than 8 ms; `docs/using/tuning.md`). The premise did not hold either: the UHCI arm did
  not poll at 10 ms. Under the script its successive reports came 6 to 9, 14 to 17 or 22 to 25 ms apart
  (`rgaps.py`), multiples of 8 ms, and a report whose data was already waiting came a median 8.0 ms after the one
  before (`qgap.py`, below): Windows' own UHCI driver polled the keyboard every 8 frames. The nominal interval was 8
  ms in both configurations, and the "10 ms" of the reading above was the keyboard's declared `bInterval`. What does
  differ is how the reports follow the keys (below).
- An EHCI controller with UHCI companions was not tried again: 50.26's reading found no keyboard or tablet enumerated
  on the companions' ports (its `prepE`), and that path would not involve this driver.

| Arm | Changed against `A` | Keyboard on | Starts | The script's first Win+R not the Run dialog | Later Win+R not the Run dialog | Lost | Queue full | Keyboard reports / scan codes | Guest clock rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `A` | - | `qemu-xhci`, this driver, 480 Mb/s | 20 | 10 of 20 | 0 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 5680 / 5680 | 0.98 to 1.00 |
| `C` | speed | `qemu-xhci`, this driver, 12 Mb/s | 20 | 9 of 20 | 0 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 5680 / 5680 | 0.98 to 1.00 |
| `F` | xHCI PCI model | `nec-usb-xhci`, this driver, 480 Mb/s | 20 | 8 of 20 | 0 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 5680 / 5680 | 0.98 to 1.00 |
| `E` | the path (image kept) | PIIX3 UHCI, Windows' driver, 12 Mb/s | 20 | 0 of 20 | 0 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 5680 / 5680 | 0.98 to 1.00 |
| `B` | the path and the image | PIIX3 UHCI, Windows' driver, 12 Mb/s | 20 | 1 of 20 | 0 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 5680 / 5680 | 0.98 to 1.00 |

The columns as in the first table above: the script's first Win+R and its two later ones by their screenshots; events
lost by the alignment (5560 sent an arm); `hid_kbd_queue_full` lines; the keyboard's successful reports against the
scan codes sent; the guest clock's rate, per start (`firstwinr.py`). No start was void. The extras and held keys were
of the kinds above (typematic repeats of the holds; the Win press nobody sent after the first Win+R with the window
active, and the Win key held after it: every key held more than 1 s was Win, in 15 to 20 starts of each arm).

**The excess goes with the xHCI controller path.** The reference arms reproduced it: `A` 10 of 20 against `B` 1 of
20 (one-sided Fisher exact probability 0.0017). Each variable in turn, with 20 starts an arm:

- **Speed**: with the keyboard at 12 Mb/s on the xHCI root port, `C`, the first Win+R failed in 9 of 20 (`A` at 480
  Mb/s: 10 of 20), more often than in `B` (0.004).
- **Image and package**: the xHCI98 image with the keyboard on the UHCI controller, `E`, failed in none of 20 (the
  package-free image on it, `B`: 1 of 20), less often than the same image with the keyboard on the xHCI controller
  (`A`, 0.0002). The package-free image cannot run the keyboard on the xHCI controller (98 SE has no xHCI driver of
  its own), so that combination is not in the pass.
- **PCI model**: on the NEC model, `F`, 8 of 20 (`qemu-xhci`: 10 of 20), more often than in `B` (0.010).
- **Interval**: 8 ms nominal on both paths (above); not varied.

Pooled, with the keyboard on an emulated xHCI controller under this driver the first Win+R failed in 27 of 60 starts
(`A`, `C`, `F`), and on the UHCI controller under Windows' own driver in 1 of 40 (`B`, `E`), one-sided 7e-7. So the
excess does not need the high speed, the `qemu-xhci` identity or the package's image on the UHCI path; with 20
starts an arm these counts do not exclude a smaller part of any of them, or an interaction. After the first Win+R, no
Win+R failed in any arm (0 of 200).

**The guest clock's rate does not carry it.** Every start of this pass ran at the host's rate (0.98 to 1.00); none was
in the state of the first pass's night, where the guest's millisecond clock ran at about a third (that state came with
Windows' own UHCI driver and the PS/2 keyboard as well, and its cause is not part of this item). The first pass's 38
and 38 split by that rate (its `first-final.txt`; `pred-split.txt`): at the host's rate this driver 14 of 31 against
the UHCI driver 2 of 33 (0.0003), at about a third 5 of 7 against 0 of 5 (0.027). Both passes' reference
configurations at the host's rate together (the first pass's `xhc` and `uhc` starts, this pass's `A` and `B`): 24 of
51 against 3 of 53 (9e-7); with this pass's other arms too (`C` and `F` with the xHCI ones, `E` with the UHCI ones):
41 of 91 against 3 of 73 (5e-10).

**How the reports follow the keys on the two paths.** Under the script's keys the keyboard's reports reached the guest
mostly 10 to 13 ms apart, or 20 to 23 ms (3225 of the 3660 gaps under 30 ms in `A`, 3212 of 3657 in `C`, 3227 of 3659
in `F`), on both xHCI models and at both speeds, the median of each start's gaps under 30 ms 11.5 to 12.1 ms; and 6 to
9, 14 to 17 or 22 to 25 ms apart on the UHCI controller in both images, the multiples of its 8 ms poll (`rgaps.py`,
every start). The xHCI path is not the slower one. QEMU's keyboard logs `hid_kbd_queue_empty` when a poll takes its
last queued scan code (`hw/input/hid.c`), so a report whose poll did not log it left the next report's data waiting.
In those cases (121, 122 and 122 reports in `A`, `C` and `F`; 375 and 366 in `B` and `E`; `qgap.py`, `qgap2.txt`) the
next report came 0 to 11.5 ms later on the xHCI controller, the arms' medians 5.2 to 6.0 ms, with this driver's next
transfer already taken up by the emulated controller when the previous report completed (`usb_xhci_xfer_start` 0.0 ms
after it at the median, at most 2.7 ms); and 4.9 to 18.8 ms later on the UHCI controller, the medians 7.9 and 8.0 ms,
one poll. So nearly all of the xHCI path's 10 to 13 ms gaps (all but at most 122 of the gaps an arm) are reports whose
key came after the report before had emptied the keyboard's queue: they waited for their key, and most of the script's
key events come 10 ms or more apart (above, "The sender"; the `tap0` block's press and release go in one command). On
the UHCI path a report waits for the next 8 ms poll after its key. That is the timing difference measured between the
two paths; it is not measured how soon after its key event each report came, and the time from a report to USER's
event is not timed by these traces (above).

**Reading.** The higher failure rate of the first Win+R after the plug with an MS-DOS window active goes with the
keyboard on an emulated xHCI controller under this driver. It persisted at full speed and on the NEC model, did not
follow the package's image onto the UHCI path, and is there at the host's clock rate in both passes; the nominal
interval is the same on both paths. Within that path, this driver and QEMU's xHCI core are not separable on this rig:
98 SE has no other xHCI driver, and QEMU's two xHCI models are one core. The one timing difference measured, how the
reports follow the keys (above), is not shown to be what makes USER miss the hotkey, and neither the emulator nor
this driver has a setting that changes it alone. So whether this driver takes part is not decided on the emulator,
and nothing read points at it; the recognition still fails in USER with all four events received, as above. No
repair is proposed. Follow-ups that would narrow it, none decisive alone: the same first Win+R on a real xHCI
controller under this driver against a real UHCI or EHCI controller under Windows' own driver with the same keyboard
(a bench reading; controller and driver still change together), and an emulator change that makes the xHCI model or
the UHCI model deliver reports with the other's timing (which would test the timing, not assign it to the driver or
the emulator).

Not run: arm `D` (above); EHCI with companions (above); the wider `+t` trace in this pass; real hardware. Guest
memory and Microsoft binaries were not read. Every guest of this pass is stopped (`pids.txt`; three later processes
on the host that took over a stopped start's process number were checked by their command lines and are not this
pass's); the counted starts' overlays are deleted.

## 50.37: the 98 SE and ME thread ends against the image's unload (worker unload9x, 2026-11-19)

**The defect** (this file's "50.32 (continued)", worker s98audrm, legs `L36` and `L16`). On 98 SE this driver's
image is unloaded at every removal of the controller - the USB Tree's restart and Device Manager's Remove alike -
and a new copy is loaded for the rescan. The controller thread set `ThreadExited` with an ordinary call and then
called `PsTerminateSystemThread`; the 98 SE and ME stop waits on that event alone (a wait on the thread's object
faults there, 26-A.2). In `L36` the thread returned from its `KeSetEvent` into the copy that had just been unloaded
("A fatal exception 0E has occurred at 0028:FF271C03", the old base + `0x15E83`); `L16` is compatible. 1 identified
and 1 compatible in 22 removals. The same code is in `3.5.0.0`, and ME runs it too.

**The design** (design record 15 section 4.5.22, revision 17; reviewed and revised before the code). On 98 SE and ME
each thread of `xhci98.sys` builds on its own stack the frames of its two last calls and jumps to the first, so that
the signal routine (`KeSetEvent`, or the `__fastcall` `InterlockedExchange` for the threads joined by a flag)
returns straight into `PsTerminateSystemThread`: nothing of the image runs after the signal (`HcdThreadEnd9x`,
`hcd_ctl.c`, x86 only). The controller thread, the idle callback thread and the completion workers and grower (the
last two only with `XhciSelectiveSuspend` 1) end that way; the completion workers' 10 ms grace after their flag is
dropped. 2000 and later keep their endings and their joins on the thread object; the amd64 build compiles none of
it. No import is added. Weighed and not taken: the thread-object wait (faults on 98 SE), a bounded settle (no
synchronisation), keeping the image for the boot (changes the image's life on 98 SE and ME; the owner's option for
the residual windows the record lists).

**The qemu flavour's view.** A port-`0xE9` line at each 9x thread end, before the jump ("hcd: thread end 9x": the
thread and form, the signal routine's, the delay's and `PsTerminateSystemThread`'s addresses, an address of the
routine itself, the sleep, the chained frame's stack address); `XhciQemuThreadExitSleep` (machine-wide, ms, at most
10000) chains `KeDelayExecutionThread` between the signal and the end; `XhciQemuThreadExitOld` 1 is the control, the
controller thread ending as before with the sleep made inside the image.

**Where.** Development host A, QEMU (`E:\xhci98-vm\q35-bases\bin\asm4242-20261110-docks`), TCG, headless, the q35
machine, one processor and 512 MB a guest, at most three guests at a time on ports 59260-59289 (other work's
guests ran throughout, the host's processors at 60 to 100 %, so no time here is a timing). Every leg is a fresh
overlay of a prepared image and a cold start; QEMU's `qemu-xhci` behind a `pcie-root-port`, the system disk on
`piix3-ide`, the transfer folder as D:, `usb-tablet` and `usb-kbd` (bound to the VGA console, so the harness's keys
go to the PS/2 keyboard) plugged after the desktop at QEMU ports 1 and 2, and in the legs marked "A" QEMU's
`usb-audio` at port 3 with its Add New Hardware wizard answered in that start (50.32's "first install" state).

**The images.** `P98P`: the 98 SE q35 base with `3.5.0.0` installed by its Setup and NUSB 3.3 (devfault9's
`p98`), the PIIX IDE wizard answered and the tablet and keyboard installed (98 SE on its AHCI disk was refused by
the Tree, "The tool could not tell which controller drive C: is on", so the PIIX disk as in 50.32); `MEK`: the ME
base with `3.5.0.0` (cancelst's `mb`), tablet and keyboard installed. From each, one prepared image a flavour, made
in one start by `SWAP.BAT` (the built `xhci98.sys` copied over the installed one, `fc /b`: no differences) and
`QREG.BAT` (the qemu-only values written under `Services\USB`), then shut down and kept read-only: `-G2Q` (the
`qemu` flavour), `-G2R` (`release`), `-G2QS` (`qemu`, `XhciQemuThreadExitSleep` 10000), `-G2QC` (the same and
`XhciQemuThreadExitOld` 1, the control), `-G2QSS` (`qemu`, the sleep and `XhciSelectiveSuspend` 1). The USB Tree is
the gated build's `XHCITR.EXE`, run as `XHCITR /restart "id=<the controller>"` from a batch file that writes its
exit code to COM1; Device Manager's Remove is followed by its Refresh and the wizard that finds the controller
again answered.

**What each removal is read for.** The answer (the batch file's exit line) or the Device Manager step, a screenshot
checked for a text-mode fault screen after each, this driver's image found in guest memory by one of its own
strings (`findimg.py`; each copy's span from its own PE header) with QEMU's `info mem` after each removal; at the
end of the leg the taskbar clock compared over 70 s and a Start-menu shutdown. In the `qemu` flavour, from the
port-`0xE9` trace (`check.py`): before every `msg4.uninit` (the unload) a "hcd: thread end 9x" record of the
controller thread, and every routine address the records name outside every span of this driver's copies read in
that start. In the sleep legs a second QMP monitor (`watch.py`) read, as soon as each `msg4.uninit` line reached
the host, `info mem` and the six stack words at the address the end record names, and read them again after the
sleep; the trace and serial lines are stamped with host time as they arrive (`stamp.py`). Each start's guest clock:
`TICK.EXE` (`GetTickCount`) three times, host-stamped (`rate.py`).

**The builds.** Two gated x86 builds of the change, each `BUILD + GATES PASSED (release qemu)`: `5ea280359` on
`224cd4328` (w50-int1 before 50.32 was merged; `qemu` `29918898...`, `release` `cfb89a73...`), used by the early
legs below, and the same change on `319f8b6aa` (50.30, 50.31 and 50.32 merged), `6c6a557a6` (`qemu` `fa4fa428...`,
`release` `898d8652...`, `XHCITR.EXE` `07f10616...`), used by every other leg. This project's own disassembly of
`HcdThreadEnd9x` (dumpbin `-disasm` of `hcd_ctl.obj`, both flavours, both builds, the same code apart from string
labels): the routine addresses are loaded from the import table into the frame's locals first (in the `qemu`
flavour the interval and the trace record are prepared and written then too); each of the endings is then
`mov esp,[ebp-4]`, pushes of constants and of the frame's own locals, `mov eax,[ebp-..]` (and ECX and EDX from the
frame in the flag form), `jmp eax`; nothing of the image is read or executed after the jump.
The control's two return addresses in the `qemu` image of `6c6a557a6`, from the same disassembly and a
search of the image for its bytes: after `KeSetEvent` RVA `0x16FCB`, after the sleep's call RVA `0x16FDD`.

### The legs

One line a start. A **removal** is one removal of the controller's devnode that unloaded this driver: the Tree's
restart (`XHCITR /restart`, a remove and a rescan on 98 SE and ME; its answer and exit code read) or Device
Manager's Remove (followed by its Refresh and the wizards that find the controller and its devices again). Devices:
`t` tablet, `k` keyboard, `A` QEMU's `usb-audio` with its wizard answered in that start, in plug order. Clock: the
guest's `GetTickCount` against host time over the start (every counted start at full rate; the two harness trials
before them, not counted, ran at about a third, 50.36's slow state). "Traced": in the `qemu` flavour, the unloads
`check.py` found, each with a controller-thread end record before it and every routine it names outside every copy
of this driver read in that start.

has occurred at 0028:FF041C14 in VXD USBAUDIO(01) + 00002ED4" - lessons.md's "Windows 98 SE cannot play USB audio
here", the fault 50.32's `L01` and `L02` met, in Windows' own driver. **Stops:** `F03` and `F10`, each after its first
restart's answer "It has started again", at the audio device's re-arrival, EIP `C000A882` (VMM's wait), the stop

device plugged first, as in 50.32's `u2`) went through all eight. A plain unplug (`F13`: the tablet and the keyboard
deleted and plugged again) and a shutdown with the devices plugged (`F14`, and the end of every leg that passed; the

removes no controller, so no unload and no end record.

### What the qemu flavour showed

- **Every removal, in order.** In every 98 SE and ME `qemu` leg, before each `msg4.uninit` (the unload) the trace
  holds a "hcd: thread end 9x" record of the controller thread written just before its jump, and every routine
  address the records name lies outside every span of this driver's copies read in that start (`check.py`: ALL OK
  in every leg; 78 unloads, the control's one among them). On 98 SE `KeSetEvent` resolved to `C002C4D3`, `InterlockedExchange` to `C002F6A0`,
  `KeDelayExecutionThread` to `C002C6E2` and `PsTerminateSystemThread` to `C029748D`; on ME `C002B9FE`, `C002BF7A`
  (the delay) and `C02A3172` (the end); this driver's copies lay at `FF03EAA0` upward.
- **The exited thread still in its chain while its image is gone** (the sleep legs, `XhciQemuThreadExitSleep`
  10000). The proof is the delay's length, as design record 15 section 4.5.22 sets it out: the 10000 ms delay
  cannot have ended before 10 s of host time after the end record (these legs run QEMU with TCG and no `-icount`,
  where the guest's timers follow the host's clock; the starts' `GetTickCount` ratios, 1.00, agree), and the
  readings below were taken 0.01 to 5.31 s after the record - so at each the thread had not yet reached
  `PsTerminateSystemThread`'s end and had nothing of the image ahead of it; which of its two system routines it was
  in is not read. In every removal read, the page of the old copy's `HcdThreadEnd9x` (the record's own address) was
  **unmapped** at the unload line's reading or at the one 2 s later, on both systems - the proof rests on those
  samples (the rest of that copy's pages likewise, but for the few the next copy or a neighbour occupies; in `F10`
  that page was mapped again at the 5 s reading, by memory given out again after the unload, so a later sample says
  nothing of which image holds it); the six words at the stack address the record names read, at each, `C029748D 00000000 00000000
  <the interval's address> 00000000 00000000` on 98 SE (`C02A3172 ...` on ME), the chained frame's layout as built
  (a layout check, not a state); 13 s after the record the stack page itself was gone (released), and no fault
  followed.
  `F05` (98 SE, the second removal read in full: the watcher had stopped at that reading on a page it could no
  longer read, then fixed), `G03` (ME, 4 of 4 removals), `F09` (98 SE with selective suspend: five end records before
  the first unload - the controller thread in the event form, the idle callback thread, two completion workers and
  the grower in the flag form, `InterlockedExchange` - the watcher sampling the last record's frame, read at 0.4, 2
  and 5 s, its stack page released by 13 s; the joins no longer wait the 10 ms grace), and `F10`
  (98 SE with the audio device, its one removal before the arrival stop).
- **The control** (`F06`, `XhciQemuThreadExitOld` 1 with the sleep): the controller thread's end record (form 3,
  written before its signal), the unload, and "A fatal exception 0E has occurred at 0028:FF055A7D": the old copy's
  base `FF03EAA0` + `0x16FDD`, the return address of the control's own sleep call inside the image, its pages
  `FF03F000`-`FF0BB000` unmapped at the unload reading and at the fault, the new copy at `FF0D8860`. So with the
  ending in the image the sleep reproduced 50.32's `L36` window in the control's one run, and the chained ending
  survived the same sleep at every removal of the sleep legs.

### Windows XP (the NT ending unchanged)

`X01`: the XP SP3 guest of 50.26's legs (a `release` install of this project), the gated `qemu` image of `6c6a557a6`
copied over the installed file (`fc /b`: no differences), the tablet plugged, three restarts by the Tree: the first
loaded the copied image ("Windows accepted the restart request ... The tool cannot tell whether it was restarted. It
is running."; the installed release image has no state the tool reads), the second and third on it ("It has started
again. It is running."). The trace: "stopping the controller thread", "controller thread leaving its loop",
"controller thread has exited", `msg4.uninit`, the new start - twice - and no "thread end 9x" line: on 2000 and later
the thread ends as before and the stop joins its object. Alive after; ended by QMP quit.

### Harness slips (none changes a reading above)

`D01`: 98 SE on its AHCI disk, the Tree refused ("could not tell which controller drive C: is on"); the 98 SE images
moved to the PIIX disk as in 50.32. `XP0`: a first XP start without the emulator option its image needs (STOP 0xA5),
a second powered off by stray keys while the controller's id was read; the id was taken from 50.26's logs instead.
The first build's `P98-QS` image was not used (its preparing start's shutdown keys went to a window left open).
`leg3.sh` started no watcher for the second build's `qemu` images until fixed during `F05` and `F06` (started by
hand before their second and first readings), and the watcher stopped once on a stack page it could no longer
read (`F05`, then fixed). In the Device Manager legs the image readings after each removal were taken but not
all kept apart: the wizard loop reused the leg's loop variable, so `F07` and `F08` wrote each removal's reading to
`img-post14.txt` and `G05` reused `img-post1.txt` and `img-post3.txt`; the copies `check.py` compared against are
those that survived, and the removals' trace records and unloads are complete. A second pipeline started a preparing start on the slot of the hand-driven `X01`: its boot
was refused ("port busy") and its processes stopped by pid before they sent any key.

### Not run, and what stays

- **Real hardware.** Every reading here is QEMU's (TCG, one processor). On a bench the change is exercised by any
  restart of a controller from the USB Tree or Device Manager's Remove on 98 SE or ME; nothing of it is specific to
  the emulator.
- **A callback context abandoned at a teardown** (design record 15 section 4.5.22's legs, as in 50.27): no client in
  these guests holds its idle callback in progress at a removal and no injection holds one. The idle callback
  thread's ordinary end, which is the same code, was read in `F09`.
- **The windows the change does not close** (record 15 section 4.5.22, the siblings' table: the work items, the
  PASSIVE_LEVEL completion and dispatch tails that release a teardown's count, `xhcicm.sys`'s and `xhcinet.sys`'s
  threads on 98 SE and ME): none was seen in these legs; none was provoked.

### 50.37 (continued): xhcicm.sys and xhcinet.sys on 98 SE and ME - can their images unload? (worker unload9x2, 2026-11-20)

Record 15 section 4.5.22 lists `xhcicm.sys`'s and `xhcinet.sys`'s threads among the windows 50.37 does not close.
Both end their threads as `xhci98.sys` did before 50.37: `KeSetEvent` and then `PsTerminateSystemThread` from the
image, the stop waiting on the event alone on 98 SE and ME (`src\cm\cm_thr.c`, `cmThread`'s end and `CmThrStop`;
`src\net\ndis5\n5_main.c`, `netWorker`'s end and `netStopWorker`); `xhcicm.sys`'s CONFIGMG worker (`cm_cfgwk.c`)
and call workers (`cm_callwk.c`) may by design run on after their NHI's stop, which the stop does not wait for. The
source takes `xhcicm.sys` to be resident for the boot on 98 SE and ME because `DriverEntry` registers no
`DriverUnload` there (`cm_entry.c`; `stor98cm.h` R4, whose stand-in also names a device object made at
`DriverEntry`, which the code does not make; `cm_cfgwk.c`, `cm_callwk.c`, `cm_nvlinkos.c`). Whether the images
actually unload there was read in emulated guests. No product code was changed; no qemu-only delay exists in either
driver's thread ends, so the thread tails themselves were not stretched.

**The rig.** The `qemu` images of `6c6a557a6`'s gated build (`xhcicm.sys` `af3850ff...`, `xhcinet.sys` `3c320c3e...`,
`xhci98.sys` `fa4fa428...`; `80ddbf28b`'s code, as above) copied over the installed files (`fc /b`: no differences) in
copies of 50.27's Thunderbolt guests (98 SE on the AHCI disk, ME on the PIIX disk; the package of 50.27's branch
installed with Thunderbolt support), with QEMU's TB3 Alpine Ridge host router (`usb4-host`, profile
`tb3-alpine-ridge`, the firmware connection manager) and `xhcicm.sys` on its NHI (`PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_15BF...`). For
`xhcinet.sys` each guest's package was run again with `/thunderbolt /tbnet` (`XhciCmNet` 1; the adapter
`XHCICM\TBNET` installed after the restart Windows asked for). Each image was found in guest memory by a string of
its own (`findimg2.py`; the span from its own PE header) and its span's mapped bytes read in QEMU's `info mem`; the
NHI or the adapter was removed with `DEVCYCLE remove` (SetupAPI `DIF_REMOVE`, as Device Manager's Remove; on the NHI
the trace's `cm.stop=00000002`, `IRP_MN_REMOVE_DEVICE`). Times below count from the script's request (the Run
box's Enter) unless named otherwise. `xhcicm.sys`'s `cm.ms` clock starts at its `DriverEntry` (one per image,
`cm_log.c`), so a reload would show as the clock starting again. Before each removal the span read fully mapped
(98 SE `0x962C0` of `0x962C0`; ME `0x95BE0`, the last partial page of its span, past `FF163000`, not mapped
from the start).

| Leg | System | What | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| `B98a` | 98 SE | `DEVCYCLE cycle` of the NHI (disable, 60 s, enable) | 98 SE's disable reached the NHI as `IRP_MN_STOP_DEVICE` (`cm.stop=00000004`), not a removal: the image stayed at `FF03EAC0`, mapped, and its `cm.ms` ran on through the second `cm.start` (no reload). Not a removal reading |
| `B98c` | 98 SE | the NHI removed | `xhcicm.sys` at `FF03EAC0`: as before at 26 s; at 68 s its string gone, `0x52C0` still mapped (the edge pages it shares with its neighbours) |
| `BMEa` | ME | the NHI removed | at `FF0CD420`: as before at 26 s; at 68 s its string gone, `0x4BE0` mapped |
| `BMEb` | ME | the NHI removed, `info mem` every ~2.7 s | the removal done by 6 s (`cm.stop`, `DEVCYCLE`'s answer); as before through 35 s, `0x4BE0` from 38 s |
| `B98n` | 98 SE | the adapter removed, then the NHI, `info mem` every ~2.7 s | `xhcinet.sys` not in `FF000000`-`FFFF0000` (searched there only); after the NHI's removal `xhcicm.sys` as before through 40 s, `0x52C0` from 43 s |
| `B98m` | 98 SE | the adapter removed (`DEVCYCLE remove TBNET`), `info mem` every ~2.7 s; then the NHI | `xhcinet.sys` at `C2A071C0` (span `0x4AE0`); its halt (`net.close`) 3.4 s after the batch file's first serial line; the span as before through 115 s, `0x1AE0` (its edge pages) from 118 s, its string gone; then the NHI: `xhcicm.sys` as before through 22 s, `0x52C0` from 25 s |
| `BMEn` | ME | as `B98m` | `xhcinet.sys` at `C2A04620` (span `0x4AE0`); its halt 2.9 s after the batch file's first serial line; the span as before through 100 s, `0xAE0` from 103 s, its string gone; then the NHI: `xhcicm.sys` as before through 18 s, `0x4BE0` from 21 s |
| `B98d` | 98 SE | the link-state key (below) | `xhcicm.sys` gone by the 70 s reading (string gone, `0x52C0`); the key's read then faulted |
| `BMEd` | ME | the link-state key (below) | gone by the 70 s reading (`0x4BE0`); the key's read then faulted |

Every leg alive after its removals (the taskbar clock moving over 60-70 s) and shut down from the Start menu, but
for `B98d` and `BMEd`, which ended at their fault screens.

**The link-state key outlives the image - a fault, on both systems** (`B98d`, `BMEd`). On 98 SE and ME
`xhcicm.sys` publishes the stor98 link-state channel's proof as a dynamic registry key,
`HKEY_DYN_DATA\Stor98LinkState`, whose query handler is `cmNvProofQuery` in its own image (`cm_nvlinkos.c`), made at
the first exposure of a tunnel in the boot and deleted only by an unload routine 98 SE and ME never get. The legs
plugged QEMU's TB3 NVMe enclosure (`usb4-device`), so that the trace read `cm.nvlink.9x.record=80000000` (the key
made); `regedit /e` of the key then exported `BootCookie` and `TableLinear`. After the NHI's removal, with the image
gone by the 70 s reading, the same export stopped the guest: 98 SE "A fatal exception 0E has occurred at
0028:FF0BC0E2" (the old base `FF03EAC0` + `0x7D622`), ME "Error: 0E : 0028 : FF14AA42" (`FF0CD420` + `0x7D622`).
`0x7D622` is the first byte of `cmNvProofQuery` in this `xhcicm.sys` (its bytes, from this project's own
`dumpbin -disasm` of `cm_nvlinkos.obj`, found at that offset of its own image): the registry called the handler in
the freed image. So once a tunnel has been exposed in a boot and the last NHI is removed, any read of the key after
the image's pages have gone - stor98 at its next `HwFindAdapter`, Regedit browsing `HKEY_DYN_DATA` - calls into
freed memory; between the removal and the pages going (the deferral above) the handler still answers, and these
legs read only the case after. The published `3.4.0.0` to
`3.5.0.0` images carry the same key.

**Harness slips** (no reading changed): `B98a`'s script stopped after its readings when the script file was edited
while it ran; the guest was then checked alive and shut down by hand. `B98b` never started a guest (its port was
still `B98a`'s); its combination ran as `B98c`. `B98n` searched for `xhcinet.sys` in the wrong range; `B98m`
repeated it with the right one.

**The verdict.**

- `xhcicm.sys`, 98 SE and ME: **its image unloads** after its last NHI's removal, with no `DriverUnload` (98 SE in
  four removals, ME in four). The residency the source relies on does not hold. Consequences: (1) the link-state
  key's handler is left behind - a fault, read on both systems; (2) the controller thread's end races the unload as
  `xhci98.sys`'s did - the pattern is in the code. Where readings bracket it, the pages went 18 to 43 s after the
  removal was asked (98 SE 22-25 and 40-43 s, ME 18-21 and 35-38 s, by the ~2.7 s readings; between 26 and 68 s in
  `B98c` and `BMEa`), and no fault came at any of the eight NHI removals; but what defers the unload is not read (the
  image has no trace at its unload), so these readings set no minimum, and the window is not shown to be closed;
  (3) the detached CONFIGMG worker and the call workers, which the stop does not wait for, run this image's code for
  as long as a CONFIGMG call blocks: past the unload they would fault; not provoked here.
- `xhcinet.sys`, 98 SE and ME: **its image unloads** after its adapter's removal (one reading each: between 115 and
  118 s on 98 SE, between 100 and 103 s on ME). The worker's end races it in the code as above; no fault was seen,
  and the same caution about the deferral applies.

**Fix options** (for the owner; recommendation first; nothing built):

1. *(Recommended for `xhcicm.sys`.)* Make R4's stand-in true: on 98 SE and ME, `DriverEntry` makes one unnamed,
   non-PnP device object and never deletes it, failing the load if it cannot. 46.20's test images (`w98se-tS2`,
   `-tS3`) showed such an object keeps `xhci98.sys`'s image through a controller's Remove on 98 SE: the Refresh
   brought no second `DriverEntry` and the controller started again on the first image. It closes every tail at
   once - the key's handler, the thread ends, the detached workers, any DPC or callback - which the code already
   assumes; the cost is the residency the design already intends (an update on 98 SE and ME already needs a
   restart). Owed with it: the same reading on ME, where 46.20 did not read it, and here with the NHI removed and
   added again (its second start on the resident image, the key still answered by it).
2. Delete the key in the last NHI's removal and chain the thread ends out of the image as 50.37 did: narrower; it
   leaves the detached workers and any other callback, and it changes the channel's lifetime, which R4 sets. Two
   cases follow. An NHI added again before the image goes starts on the same image, whose publication state
   (`cm_nvlinkos.c`, `cmNvEnsure`: `cmNvRecordTried` 2 and `cmNvRecord` 1) says the key exists, so it would report
   the channel up with no key: the deletion would have to reset that state, and R4 asks a withdrawn table to be
   written no more. An NHI added after the image has gone loads a new image, which publishes again only under R4's
   rules for a reload (a new cookie, every endpoint under its bridges retired before its first UP), while a stor98
   instance bound before keeps polling the old table. Ending the channel for the rest of the boot instead is simpler
   in rule, but a new image keeps no state, so that end would need a mark that outlives the image (in the registry,
   for example), at the cost of the channel after any NHI removal.
3. For `xhcinet.sys` (an NDIS miniport: NDIS, not this driver, owns its driver object): *(recommended)* the 50.37
   ending for `netWorker` - the frames built on the thread's stack so `KeSetEvent` returns straight into
   `PsTerminateSystemThread`, as `HcdThreadEnd9x` does, x86 and 98 SE / ME only; or a 9x residency for the
   miniport, which NDIS's ownership makes harder to do and to read.

Evidence: `E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\unload9x\ev\` (`B98a` ... `B98n`, `BMEa`, `BMEb`, `BMEd`, `BMEn`, and the prepared
images `P98T`, `MET`, `P98N`, `MEN`: `leg.log`, `prep.log`, `imgcm-*.txt`, `imgnet-*.txt`, `mem-*.txt`, `fast*.txt`,
`pk2.png`, `pk2-regs.txt`), `tools\findfn.py`, `tools\spanmap.py`, `tmp\disasm-cm_nvlinkos.txt`; the guests' traces
and host-stamped logs under `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\unload9x\vms\`.

## 50.39 The USB Tree's window and Save Report within their widths (2026-11-20)

The owner's decision of 2026-11-19: the widths of the USB Tree's window and of its Save Report are swept in this
release, after tasks 50.30 to 50.32 (merged on branch 3.5.1.0 at `319f8b6aa`). The rule is design record 25's own
(sections 3.6, 6.5 and 20 item 6): every line within 79 columns; section 7.3's addendum lets Save Report's tree lines
pass it at depth. Task 50.30 brought the snapshot engine's report within it and left this tool's texts. Design record
25 revision 52, section 28, is the design (revision 53 after the owner's answers); branch `w50-trwidth` from
`319f8b6aa`.

### The sweep

**From the source.** A static sweep of every text call in `xhcitr\` (each format split at its line ends, each number
at the most digits it can hold, each string at its longest: a literal, a table's longest entry, a buffer's bound),
then the functions the details pane and Save Report reach. In the details pane - which Save Report repeats node by
node - 21 line formats pass 79 columns with their words and numbers alone, and 105 more with long values. Among the
first: the recovery requests' `reset requested:` line (up to 223 columns), the descriptors' SuperSpeed companion and
SuperSpeedPlus lines (99 to 131), the Thunderbolt router's tunnels line (106), the PCI and bridge diagnostics' counts
(86 to 105), the network link's logins (99), the qlog's refused value (87), the PCI walk's bound (97), the
Thunderbolt unit's mark and stop lines (85, 91) and the report's header (93); among the second: the transport line
(`  Transport:     ` and up to 86 more), the controller's version and settings lines, the Settings rows (`now` and
`default` texts), the stopped controller's "involved" line, the driver keys' notes (task 50.29, up to 149). The list:
`E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\trwidth\sweep-pane.txt`; the whole sweep, `sweep1.tsv`.

**In guests, the dialogs.** A measuring program of this task's own (never tracked, never run on the host;
`E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\trwidth\meas\meas.c`) took each dialog's texts at their longest in the dialog's font (MS Sans
Serif 8, DrawText at the control's width) and the tray's items in the menu font, on the q35 98 SE base (640 x 480,
MS Sans Serif menus) and the q35 XP base (1024 x 768, Tahoma menus); no package installed. Every text fits its
control - the restart dialog's heading with the Run As line and a 63-character name (3 of 4 lines) and its note with
every warning (4 of 5), the Settings heading's other texts, the range line (43 characters), the hotkey note, the
Logging level dialog's "Now:" lines (2 of 2), the stop with administrator rights (6 of 6, a 159-character label),
About (8 of 9) - but two: the Settings heading when six or more settings wait for a restart (3 or more lines in 2)
and a tray item for a device with a long label (a four-slot card reader's item: 817 pixels on 98 SE, wider than its
640-pixel screen; 797 on XP, within its 1024 but wider than an 800-pixel screen once the menu's margins are added; a
159-character label with a reason, 1083 to 1097). The status bar at its longest is 546 pixels. Balloons are bounded already (an answer of 250
characters or more goes to a message box) and message boxes wrap their own text.

| Step | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 98 SE, the q35 base (one processor), `meas.exe` over 48 cases | as above; the Settings heading clipped at 6 and 8 names; the two long tray items wider than the screen | `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\trwidth\ev\meas-98se.txt`, `meas-cases.txt`, `m98-boot1.png` |
| XP SP3, the q35 base (two processors), the same | the same for every dialog text; tray: the card reader's item 797 pixels, the 159-character one 1083; the status bar 546 | `ev\meas-xp.txt`, `mxp-boot1.png` |

### The change (`cf871bd9a`)

`tr_fit_text` (`xhcitr\tr_core.c`, the pure half) writes a line within the width as it is and breaks a wider one
between words: after a clause's end (the space after a `,`, `;`, `.` or `:`) in the line's second half by column,
else at the last space that fits; never inside a quoted string, the label or before its first word; its further
lines under its first value (a short "Label:" and its spaces) or its indent, never further in than half the width. A
word or a quoted string wider than a line stays whole, and a line that begins with `TR_FIT_WHOLE` - a value read as
it is: a name, an id, a path, a version, a serial number, a device's or Windows' string - is written whole, the mark
dropped. Only spaces and line ends change. It runs on the details pane and Edit > Copy (79 columns); Save Report's
header, Logging levels and Settings blocks (79) and each node's details, the driver keys' block heads and notes at 79
less the node's lead (`tr_report_width`; `TR_REG_KEY`'s `Width`), so that with the lead every line stays within 79;
the Logging level dialog's list, `/set /show` and `XHCISET.TXT`, a block that no longer fits its caller ending with
the cut mark. Settings' heading is three lines high (230 x 26 dialog units; the list one line shorter, the tool's own
tab 8 units lower; the dialog keeps its 262), so six of the longest names waiting for a restart fit. Not fitted: a
registry value's line, the logs' records (no space in them), the tree's labels (record 25 section 7.3), the snapshot
engine's text (50.30's), the console's answers (already wrapped at 79), message boxes and balloons. No word of a
user-visible string changed. Design record 25 revision 52, section 28.

Fitting each report node to 79 less its lead, rather than keeping the pane's 79 under the lead (79 + 6 + twice the
depth), was taken as the recommended choice under the 79-column rule; the owner kept it (2026-11-20).

| Step | Result | Evidence |

### The change (`5d0cd980d`)

Design record 25 revision 53, section 28 items 4 and 5. **Settings' heading** (`IDC_S_HEAD`) is a read-only
multi-line edit with no border in the label's place and size (230 x 26 dialog units, three lines). Its vertical scroll
bar, and a stop of the Tab key, are there only while its text needs more lines than the box shows: the lines are counted
with the bar shown (`EM_GETLINECOUNT` against the formatting rectangle's height in lines of its font), so that a text
that fits at that width fits without the bar too; `ShowScrollBar` is looked up at run time, so the import table keeps
to `xhcitr-imports.allow`. Its margins are none, so its words start where the label's did, and its text holds every
row's name (`TRS_NAME_MAX`, held by `test_trset`; it was cut at 600 bytes). **The tray menu's** "Safely remove" items
cut the device's label to `tr_tray_label_chars`: 60 characters on a 640-pixel-wide work area and in proportion to the
width (75 at 800, 96 at 1024, 120 at 1280, and from 1696 the 159 it was held to before), and no more than leaves the
item with its reason within the width at 6 pixels a character after 48 for the menu's margins (with the longest reason
a USB device gives, 43 characters, 38 at 640); never under 24, and 159 for a width not read. The width is the work area
of the monitor at the cursor, where the menu opens. `tr_tray_label` is `tr_unit_label` at that length, the letters kept
whole, with a cut name ending in "..." too; `tr_unit_label` and every other place a label is shown are unchanged. No
user-visible word changed.

levels deep keeps 20 columns (`tr_report_width`'s floor), so its lines can pass 79 with their lead (section 28 items 3
and 6).

### Addition, 2026-11-20 (afternoon): the same-version line in the owner's words, and the tree's own label cut at a whole character (`bca3bd074`)

Two changes to the USB Tree, decided by the owner on 2026-11-20 for this release; branch `w50-trline` from
`be50285c0`. Design record 25 revision 55 (section 18 item 4; section 28 items 7 and 9).

**The same-version line.** Where the running driver is the installed one, the controller's and the NHI's "Driver
version:" line in the details, Edit > Copy, Save Report and `/report` read "3.3.0.0 running, the installed file's"; it
now reads in the owner's words, "3.3.0.0 running; the installed file is the same." (`tr_ver_line`). The line that says
the versions differ is unchanged. A driver that does not say its version (a running 0, shown as "older than 3.3.0.0")
is never the same (`tr_ver_state` gives differs or not known for it, and is the line's only source), so the widest
version in a same line is 15 digits and dots long, and the line 74 columns with its label `  Driver version: `,
within the details pane's 79; in Save Report it is fitted at the node's width like every other details line (section
28 items 2 and 3). The run record of task 44.8 (`run-44.md`, leg T.17) quotes what the tool of `3.2.0.0` showed then and stays as it was.

window's Action menu, the confirmations, the notices and Save Report, now takes the same lead-byte test as the tray's
cut (`tr_tray_label`, `fd4b9637d`), and XHCITR passes `IsDBCSLeadByte` to both; the tray's rounding down to a

letters, and disks whose letters leave no room. On a double-byte code page a cut label can be a byte shorter; with no

shown) and the storage refusal's list (1,600 bytes, past the refusal's 600); a text that overflows its whole buffer
is a bound of the text, not of a name. Design
record 25 revision 57 (section 28 item 11).

## 50.40: `xhcicm.sys` resident on 98 SE and ME, and `xhcinet.sys`'s worker end (worker cmres, 2026-11-20)

The fix of the defect section "50.37 (continued): xhcicm.sys and xhcinet.sys on 98 SE and ME - can their images
unload?" read (worker unload9x2): `xhcicm.sys` went 18 to 43 s after its last NHI's removal, and the link-state key
`HKEY_DYN_DATA\Stor98LinkState` it publishes for Stor98 then answered from freed memory. Design record 21 section
7.9 and record 35 section 19 (`d40d7273d`, on the release branch at `7129d517a`): on 98 SE and ME `DriverEntry`
makes one device object that is never deleted, and `xhcinet.sys`'s worker ends by record 15 section 4.5.22's
event form. Read in emulated guests; no real hardware.

**Build.** One gated build of `d40d7273d` (`git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` empty before and after,
one commit on the branch): x86 `all` "BUILD + GATES PASSED (release qemu)", amd64 `release` "BUILD + GATES PASSED
(release)". Packages staged by `make-package.ps1` from it (x86 `release` and `qemu`), the release one laid out by
family as the kit. The images: `release` `xhcicm.sys` `49c9c7dc...`, `xhcinet.sys` `754bd9a7...`, `xhci98.sys`
`5310674f...`; `qemu` `xhcicm.sys` `18c4f91b...`, `xhcinet.sys` `2048419e...`, `xhci98.sys` `da6a20fa...`.
This project's own disassembly of its linked `xhcinet.sys` (both flavours): `netWorkerEnd9x` loads its two targets
from the import address table's `KeSetEvent` and `PsTerminateSystemThread` slots (RVA `0x324`, `0x310`), and its
last instruction is `jmp eax` after the frames are pushed; in the qemu image the control's
`KeDelayExecutionThread` call returns to RVA `0x3B64`.

**The rigs** (development host A, QEMU TCG, one processor, 512 MB a guest, cold starts of fresh overlays, the
host-stamped serial and port-`0xE9` logs and `info mem` readings of the section above; the emulator's TB3 Alpine
Ridge host router with `xhcicm.sys` on its NHI `PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_15BF`, 98 SE on the AHCI disk and ME on the PIIX
disk, copies of 50.27's guests). `P98K` and `PMEK`: the published `3.5.0.0` installed over them by its console
installer (`XHCIINST /dir 98-me /yes /nopause /thunderbolt /tbnet /force`: "Setup will replace
C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM32\DRIVERS\xhcicm.sys at the next start. Restart Windows to load it."), a restart, a second run,
a restart: `xhci98.sys`, `xhcicm.sys` and `xhcinet.sys` equal to the published files (`fc /b`). `P98N` and `PMEN`:
this build's release kit installed over those the same way (the version string is unchanged, hence `/force`): the
same line for `xhcicm.sys` and `xhcinet.sys`, "xhci98.sys: run Setup again after the restart"; after one restart
all three equal to the kit's. `P98Q` and `PMEQ`: those, with this build's `qemu` images copied over the three
(`fc /b`). Each image was found in guest memory by its own version string and its span read as unload9x2 did.

**The reproduction on the published `3.5.0.0`** (`tools\bkey.sh`, the release images of `P98K` and `PMEK`; the
emulator's TB3 NVMe enclosure plugged so that a tunnel is exposed and the key made; the key exported with
`regedit /e` before and after the NHI's removal by `DEVCYCLE remove` (`IRP_MN_REMOVE_DEVICE`); `info mem` every
~3 s for 90 s from just after the removal's answer; the times below count from that answer, as the stamped serial
line gives it):

| Leg | System | Before the removal | After it | The second export |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `V98a` | 98 SE | `xhcicm.sys` at `FF03EAA0`, span `0x90BE0` mapped; the key: `BootCookie`, `TableLinear` | the span mapped at 15 s, `0x4BE0` (its edge pages) at 18 s; the image's string gone | "A fatal exception 0E has occurred at 0028:FF0B6EB0" |
| `VMEa2` | ME | at `FF0B0D00`, `0x90300` mapped (the last page never) | `0x90300` at 37 s, `0x4300` at 40 s; string gone | "Error: 0E : 0028 : FF129110" |

Both are the old base + `0x78410`, where this project's own reading of the published `xhcicm.sys` finds the bytes
of `cmNvProofQuery` (`tools\findfn.py`, the pattern from this project's own object): the section above's fault, on
the published release. `VMEa`, the first ME start of the same leg, ended with no screen: its QEMU ended by itself
between 12:06:26 and 12:08:20, after the second export was asked and before its batch file wrote its first serial
line, with no screenshot in between (the harness then took one only at the end of its wait); read as a reset of the
guest under `-action reboot=shutdown`, not counted, and the leg run again as `VMEa2` with a screenshot every 2 s.

**The same with this change.** The release images (`P98N`, `PMEN`) and the `qemu` ones (`P98Q`, `PMEQ`), the NHI
removed four times a start (each followed by Device Manager's Refresh, below) and the key exported after every step:

| Leg | System | Image | After the NHI's removal (and three more, below) | The key |

| `V98b` | 98 SE | release | the span (`0x95C60`) fully mapped at every reading, the last about 90 s after each removal's answer, the image found at the same base `FF03EAA0` after each, still there 26 min after the first removal | 9 exports, the same `BootCookie` and `TableLinear` each time; no fault |
| `V98c` | 98 SE | qemu | the same (`0x963C0` at `FF03EAC0`), 27 min; one `cm.start` and one `cm.stop` in the trace, the `cm.ms` clock of one `DriverEntry` | 9 exports, all the same; no fault |
| `VMEb` | ME | release | the same (`0x95C60` at `FF0B9140`), 24 min | 9, all the same; no fault |

Only the first removal of each start removed a running NHI: after each Refresh the NHI stayed at Code 29 (the next
paragraph), so the later three removed a devnode this driver was not running, and the readings after them are of the
same resident image, kept 24 to 27 min after the first removal. Each guest ran on after its last reading (the
taskbar clock moving over 60 s) and shut down from the Start menu.
The device list (`DEVCYCLE list`, every present devnode) was the same entry for entry on `3.5.0.0` and on this
change, on each system (`V98d` against `V98b` and `V98c`, 71 entries; `VMEd` against `VMEb` and `VMEc`, 73): the
object makes no devnode.

**The NHI added again: Code 29 on 98 SE and ME, with or without this change.** After Device Manager's Refresh the
Add New Hardware wizard installed "xHCI98 TB3 Controller (Intel Alpine Ridge)" again, but the NHI did not start: no

object alone, so `AddDevice` was never asked. The configuration manager's devnode table (Regedit's export of
`HKEY_DYN_DATA\Config Manager\Enum`, `tools\cme.py`) gave the reason: the NHI's new devnode at Problem `0x1D`
(Code 29, `CM_PROB_HARDWARE_DISABLED`), Status `08000620`, an empty `Allocation`, where before the removal it had
Problem 0 and its resources - Windows had given it nothing to start with:

| Leg | System | Image | The Refresh, after the removal's answer (the harness's wait, then its readings) | The NHI's devnode after it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `D98a2` | 98 SE | this change, qemu (resident) | 68 s (a 5 s wait) | Code 29, empty `Allocation`; the driver object: the resident object alone |
| `D98b2` | 98 SE | the same | 182 s (120 s) | the same |
| `D98k2` | 98 SE | published `3.5.0.0` (its image not found 152 s after the removal) | 183 s (120 s) | the same; no image loaded again. Its export before the removal failed (`no CMEEND 1`), so this leg has no devnode reading of its own before it |
| `DMEq` | ME | this change, qemu | 180 s (120 s) | the same |
| `DMEk` | ME | published `3.5.0.0` (image not found 150 s after) | 183 s (120 s) | the same |
| `A98` | 98 SE | this change, qemu, with the emulator's Intel host on the root bus (`-Usb4 adl`'s devices: `PCI\VEN_1B36&DEV_00F4` at 00:04.0) | about 100 s | the same; the driver object: the resident object alone |

So an NHI removed in Device Manager does not come back in the same Windows session on 98 SE or ME in these guests,
whatever this driver does: its devnode is left at Code 29 before any driver is loaded for it, as it was with the
published release. That the image stays and its key answers across the removal is what this change can show; an NHI
started again on the resident image could not be read this way. (`D98a`, `D98b` and `D98k` are void: a finished
batch window held COM1, and `D98k`'s script file was edited while it ran.)

**Windows 2000** (`W2K1`: 50.27's 2000 SP4 guest with the TB3 rig and Thunderbolt networking installed, its
`release` package; this build's `qemu` `xhcicm.sys` and `xhcinet.sys` copied over, `fc /b`, a restart): the NHI
disabled and enabled twice (`DEVCYCLE cycle`), then removed and found again twice (`DEVCYCLE remove`, Device
Manager's "Scan for hardware changes", the Found New Hardware wizard for the network adapter answered): each of the
four stops of a running adapter `cm.stop=00000002` with `net.close` before it, and each start after them
`cm.start=00000001`, the adapter's `net.init` following once it was installed again; no `net.end9x` line (the NT
ending, joined on the thread object); the `cm.ms` clock running on through all of it (the image stays on NT, as
before); the network adapter back in Device Manager after each; the guest alive and shut down from the Start menu.
After each rescan the wizard's install of the network adapter's driver brought one more `cm.stop`/`cm.start` pair of
the NHI (12:38:38 and 12:43:22), with no adapter initialised yet and so no `net.close` before it. On 2000 this change makes no resident object and keeps the NT ending.

**The NHI stopped and started again on the resident image** (`C98`, 98 SE, `qemu`, `tools\bcyc.sh`: the tunnel
exposed, the key exported, then four times `DEVCYCLE cycle` of the NHI - disable, 8 s, enable, which 98 SE delivers

again (`cm.nvlink.9x.proof-read` up by two each time); the five exports the same `BootCookie` and `TableLinear`; the
image at the same base throughout; no fault; shut down from the Start menu. This is the way back for an NHI in the
same session on 98 SE; the removal above is not.

**Setup's update and the uninstall.**

- *Published `3.5.0.0` to this change* (the `P98N` and `PMEN` preps): "Setup will replace

- *This change to this change, other bytes* (`F98` on 98 SE, `FME` on ME: the release kit with `/force` over the

- *The uninstall* (`U98`, `UME`, on the release `P98N` and `PMEN`, `XHCIINST /dir 98-me /uninstall /yes /nopause`):

  (`FF03EAA0`; ME `FF0B9140`) and the key still answered with the same values; after the restart neither file
  existed and Regedit found no key ("no export file").

**`xhcinet.sys`: the worker's end** (`tools\bnet2.sh` and its variants; the `qemu` images of `P98Q` and `PMEQ`; the
network adapter removed on its own - `DEVCYCLE remove TBNET`, its NHI running - and found again by Device Manager's
Refresh; `xhcinet.sys` found by its own string between `C0000000` and `D0000000`; its end record read from the
connection manager's trace, host-stamped as it reached port `0xE9`; `tools\ananet.py`):

| Leg | System | Removals with an end record | What was read |
|---|---|---|---|
| `N98a` | 98 SE | 4 of 4 | each record 2 to 4 s after the removal's Enter, form 1 (the chain), the routine at the image's base + `0x3A56` (its RVA in this image), `KeSetEvent` at `C002CCEF` and `PsTerminateSystemThread` at `C02A148D`, outside every copy of the image; the adapter initialised again after each Refresh in a new copy; the first copy's pages went about 120 s after the removal (`0x1DC0` of `0x4DC0` left, its edge pages); no fault, alive, shut down |
| `NMEa`, `NMEb`, `NMEs3`, `NMEs5` | ME | 1, 3, 1 and 2 | the same: form 1, base + `0x3A56`, `KeSetEvent` `C002B9FE`, `PsTerminateSystemThread` `C02A3172`, outside; the first copy's pages went 17 to 114 s after the removal; no fault. On ME the Refresh's new network adapter asks "To finish setting up your new hardware, you must restart your computer"; `NMEa`'s harness answered Yes (QEMU ends at a reset here), so it has one removal; `NMEb` answered N (No) and went on |
| `N98s3` | 98 SE | 1, with the sleep | below |
| `N98c3` | 98 SE | 1, the control | below |
| `NMEs6` | ME | 1, with the sleep | below |

- **With the sleep** (`N98s3`; `XhciQemuThreadExitSleep` 200000 and `XhciQemuThreadExitOld` 0 written into the
  adapter's key, `HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\Class\Net\0001`, then the adapter disabled and enabled so that
  it read them): the removal's Enter at 15:12:34, the end record at 15:12:38 (form 1, the sleep `0x30D40` ms, the
  delay's target `KeDelayExecutionThread` at `C002CEFE` and the end's at `C02A148D`, outside the image; the chained
  frame at stack `E4356E1C`); the image's pages gone at the reading of 15:13:45. The worker's signal came after the
  Enter, so at that reading it had slept at most 71 s of its 200 s: it was alive, in the delay, with nothing of the
  image ahead of it, and the image it had run in was gone. The guest then ran on with no fault through the readings
  every 30 s to 15:16:54 and at the end, past the end of the sleep (the guest's clock ratio about 1), and shut down.
- **The control** (`N98c3`: the same with `XhciQemuThreadExitOld` 1 - the old two calls, the sleep an ordinary call
  between them): the end record at 15:17:12 (form 3, the same sleep); the image's pages gone at 15:17:56; then "A
  fatal exception 0E has occurred at 0028:C2A0AC84" - the old base `C2A07120` + `0x3B64`, the return address of the
  control's `KeDelayExecutionThread` call in this image (this project's own reading of its linked image): a worker
  that returns into its image after the signal faults once NDIS has let the image go, and the chain does not.

- **ME with the sleep** (`NMEs6`): ME's `DEVCYCLE` disable does not reach the adapter (`NMEs3`: no halt, so the
  values were not read), and the adapter found again by the Refresh did not read them either (`NMEs5`: its second
  removal ran with no sleep), so a guest with the values written (`PMEV`, `PMEQ` with them, shut down) was
  started and its adapter read them at its first start. The removal's Enter at 16:04:00, the end record at 16:04:06
  (form 1, the sleep `0x30D40` ms, the delay's target `C002BF7A`, the end's `C02A3172`, outside; the frame at
  `E3494E1C`); the image's pages gone at the reading of 16:04:31 (`0xDC0` of `0x4DC0` left), when the worker had
  slept at most 31 s of its 200 s; no fault through the readings every 30 s to 16:08:23, 257 s after the end record,
  and the guest alive after it.

**Harness slips and voids** (no reading above rests on them): `VMEa` (above); `P98N`'s first start (a fatal
exception 0E at `0197:BFF8713B`, a ring-3 selector, on the desktop before any step; the prep run again on a fresh

**Not read, and what stays.** Real hardware. An NHI started again on the resident image after a removal (Code 29 on

disassembly). Windows 2000's network adapter removed on its own (its NHI's stops halted it, joined on the thread
