## Setup after the driver was removed by hand: the exit 4 and the `C:\WIN98` prompt on 98 SE, and ME, 2000, XP (2026-11-20)

Development host A, the q35 w98se base (`E:\xhci98-vm\q35-bases\w98se`) as fresh overlays, the pinned emulator
`bin\asm4242-20261110-docks`, one vCPU and 512 MB a guest, `qemu-xhci` (`p2=4,p3=4`) behind its root port, no USB
device plugged. Kit, scripts, logs and screenshots: `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\inst4\` (`pids.txt` has every start and
stop; `logs\cell-<cell>.txt` each cell's steps, `logs\<cell>-inst-*.txt` each Setup log, `logs\<cell>-<what>-<tag>.txt`
the exports). Packages: `3.5.0.0` as published (`releases\3.5.0.0`, `xhci98.sys` `b3ea6650...`), and the gated build
of `7cf4708c5` (2026-11-19, clean; `xhci98.sys` `e54f6644...`), whose `xhciinst\`, INFs and packaging scripts are the
same bytes as `3.5.1.0` at `9747cd96f` (no gated build of that commit exists); `xhciinst\inst_eng.c` is the same file
in `v3.5.0.0` and `9747cd96f`. Setup ran as `INSTALL.BAT /console /yes /nopause /log` from a copy of the package on
`C:`.

The question: the cells TD2, TD3 and TD3R of "50.17 (old device entries)" deleted `xhci98.sys`, `xhciuas.sys` and
every key and value naming xhci98, cancelled the controller's wizard at the next start, and then saw
`INSTALL.BAT` of `3.4.3.0` (TD2) and `3.5.0.0` (TD3, TD3R) exit with 4. In TD2 and TD3R, whose wizards were then
answered, the controller's second wizard asked for `xhci98.sys` with `C:\WIN98` offered and found it only when
given `C:\XHCI98`; in TD3 the wizard was dismissed and no xHCI98 ran.

### The prepared state, and one thing the base carries

`P0` (`cfg\P0.qcow2`): a fresh overlay of the base, `3.5.0.0` installed (exit 3), a cold start: the controller
(`Class\USB\0000`) and its root hub (`Class\USB\0001`) on `xhci98.sys` and started, `INF\OTHER\YEOKHE~1.INF` with
its `SetupX\INF\OEM Name` record, `C:\XHCI98` on `DevicePath`.

The base also carries an `Enum\PCI` entry of an ASMedia ASM4242 xHCI controller (`1B21:2426`) with no driver, left
from the base's making (it was booted once with that controller, `w98se\README.txt` step 2). No such controller is
in these machines, so the entry has no devnode. Setup lists such an entry as "Recorded in the registry, but with no
driver and not running now" (design record 23 sections 6.3 and 6.4): it cannot tell an old entry from a controller
whose New Hardware wizard was cancelled, so it prints the hand steps for it and ends with exit 4 whenever its helper
did not run (a run where the helper installs a device leaves the entry unlisted, as P0's own install did, exit 3).
On this base that makes exit 4 the answer to every run that has nothing to install, a hand cleanup or not (cell CZ
below).

### One piece at a time

Each cell: a fresh overlay of `P0`; the piece deleted from a DOS box (`regedit /s` of a `.reg` file with `[-key]`
lines, `del` for the files); the state exported; a cold start and a screenshot of what 98 SE shows; a hardware
wizard on screen cancelled (as in the TD cells); the state exported again; Setup.

| Cell | Deleted | At the cold start | Setup (`3.5.0.0`) |
|---|---|---|---|

cleanup as CA: at the cold start no wizard; ME installed the controller by itself from the `INF\OTHER` copy, put

unanswered by the cell). Setup then: the controller "Keep (same version)" at problem code 2, and the two

running on `xhci98.sys`. In this cell ME needed no wizard step and no disk, and its exit 4 came from leftover
entries.

### What the code says (`xhciinst\`, `v3.5.0.0` = `9747cd96f` for `inst_eng.c`)

- **Exit 4** is `INST_EXIT_STEPS` (`inst_core.h`; `tools\xhciinst\readme.txt`, "Exit codes": "done as far as
  Setup can; it said what is left for you"). On 98 SE and ME `run_install_9x` returns `inst_exit_code(0, flagFailed, flagRestart, steps || flagSteps)`, where
  `steps` is set by any present device of the package's INFs that is planned to run or refused (`d->Runs ||
  d->Refused`) and that the helper did not do (`inst_eng.c`, the loop before `steps_9x`).
- **The controller after a cancelled wizard is invisible.** The tree comes from the configuration manager
  (`walk_cm`), and a controller whose wizard was cancelled has no devnode until the next start (record 23 section
  6.3, read again here: after CE's and CA's cancel, no devnode and, with its key deleted by hand, no `Enum\PCI` key
  either). `registry_controllers_9x` adds an xHCI `Enum\PCI` entry with no driver and no devnode as `RegOnly`; the
  helper's passes skip every `RegOnly` entry (`pass_takes`), and `steps_9x` prints its hand steps ("Recorded in the
  registry, but with no driver and not running now ...") and counts it.
- **The leftover decides the code.** With the base's ASM4242 entry the run has a `RegOnly` controller to list, so
  `steps` is 1 (CE, CA, CI, CZ, CW2, CA3). Without one (CN), no device of the package is listed:
  `steps_9x` prints "No supported device found." and, since `controller_listed()` is false, the "Windows lists no
  USB 3 controller now ... restart: the wizard comes back ..." paragraph, and the run ends "No changes were made.",
  exit 0. With a leftover listed, that paragraph is not printed; the leftover's own paragraph says the same thing
  in other words ("After a cancelled New Hardware wizard, restart: the wizard comes back and finds the driver
  itself; finish it ...") and its step 5 names the disk prompt and `C:\XHCI98`.
- **A missing driver key refuses the run (CK).** `dev_driver_values` cannot open the key the devnode's `Driver`
  value names; on 98 and ME it prints "unreadable: the driver key of <id>" and counts a walk error ("its owner is
  unknown, never 'no driver'", record 23 section 6.3), and any walk error stops the run before a change (exit 1).
  `walk_cm` calls it for every live devnode, not only this package's, so by the code a hand-deleted driver key of
  any device would stop Setup the same way (not run for another device). A key that does not exist and a key that
  exists but cannot be opened are the same to it.
- **The file alone is repaired (CF).** 98 SE keeps no `DriverVersion` for the controller, so the group's binary
  speaks for it (`plan`, record 23 section 6.3); with the file gone the version is absent, `inst_versioned`
  (`inst_core.c`) plans "Update" for an absent version, and the helper reinstalls the controller. An
  *unreadable* version (`INST_VS_UNREADABLE`) is planned "unknown" and refused instead: that is 2000's and XP's
  case below, where the key the version would be read from is the one deleted.
- **Why `C:\WIN98`.** The helper brackets each of its jobs with `CtlSetLddPath` to the install folder and back
  (`xhciinst\di\di_sys.c`, `LDID_SRCPATH`; its lines in the Setup logs above); Setup's own installs of the
  controller asked nothing here. Windows' own wizard at the next start has no such help and offers its setup folder (`SourcePath`, `c:\win98\` on this base), as record 26
  section 5.0 (drafts 39 and 40) read and the owner kept (W9XPROMPT.1).

### What this shows

- **The exit 4 is not the hand cleanup's.** On these bases it comes from a registry-only xHCI entry the base
  carries, listed whenever Setup's helper does not run (CZ: nothing deleted, exit 4). What the cleanup does is
  take the controller out of Setup's reach: deleting its `Enum` entries brings back the New Hardware wizard, and
  once that is cancelled the controller has no devnode and no entry until the next start, so there is nothing
  to install (record 23 section 6.3). Without a leftover entry the same run ends exit 0, "No changes were made.",
  with the paragraph that says to restart and finish the wizard (CN).
- **The `C:\WIN98` prompt** is the controller's wizard asking for the "xhci98 xHCI Host Controller Disk" with
  Windows' setup folder offered (CA2), the prompt the owner kept (W9XPROMPT.1). `C:\XHCI98` answers it, as
  Setup's step 5 says.
- **The way out today** of the cleanup as the reporter described it (CA): run Setup, restart, finish the wizard
  (Next to Finish; `C:\XHCI98` if asked for the disk), restart when asked; then Setup finds the controller and
  root hub current (CA2, CA3). On ME, in CAme, no wizard step was needed: ME reinstalled the controller and asked
  for a restart (CAme2).
- **Two worse states**, both a driver key deleted while its `Enum` entry stays: on 98 SE (CK) Setup refuses every
  run, install and uninstall alike, until the devnodes are removed in Device Manager; on 2000 and XP, where the
  administrator's `regedit /s` left `Enum` in place, the whole cleanup left that state, and Setup skips the controller as of
  unknown version (exit 4) with no step that gets out of it.
- **The cleaner.** `XHCICLN` (2.4.0.0 to 3.2.0.0, dropped in 3.3.0.0) only listed or removed the old `XHCI98\`
  devnodes of releases before 2.4.0.0, and on 98 SE and ME only listed them (its `readme.txt`); it neither makes
  nor repairs these states. Setup's own uninstall is the supported removal (release notes, "Uninstalling"); it was
  not run here on an intact install.

### Slips

- P0's first start did not happen (a variable of the launch script named `OS`, which Windows already sets); no
  guest started; run again at once.
- CF, CK and CE: the state export after Setup timed out ("Write fault error writing device COM1": the install's
  DOS box still held COM1); those three exports are missing, the cells' results stand; fixed from CI on.
- CW: after the walked wizard, the restart question appeared late and the next step's keystrokes answered it;
  98 SE restarted (QEMU ended, as `-action reboot=shutdown` makes it), which the step meant to do anyway; CW2 went
  on from that disk.
- CAK: the cold start was refused (the script saw the just-stopped QEMU as still running); the guest had powered
  off cleanly, and the cell went on from its disk as CAK2.
- CKU: a "Yes" meant for a restart question fell on the desktop (no question had come), so Setup ran in the same
  session (recorded so above); the uninstall's log did not reach COM1 (a damaged `cd` line in `UN.BAT`), its
  screen and exit code did.
- The ME guests (P0me, CAme, CAme2) did not finish the ACPI power-off in 240 s and were ended by QMP `quit`.
- QEMU deletes its pid file at exit; one `pids.txt` STOP line with no pid is annotated there.

### What this shows

- A deleted driver key of the package's own devices no longer stops Setup on 98 SE and ME: the controller is
  installed where its `Enum` entry proves it the package's, and the root hub follows (G1, M2); after the restart
  Setup finds both current (G1). On XP the same state is reinstalled as an update (X5), where it was skipped as of
  unknown version.
- Where the entry does not prove the device the package's, Setup leaves it, says so, and gives the step (G7); the
  uninstall removes what is proven and says what it leaves (G7), and is not stopped.
- A stale bus entry with no devnode is removed through the helper and only that entry (G2). In G1 and M2 the root
  hub's own stale entry was not removed: the controller's install brought the root hub back with a devnode, and
  Setup installed it in the same run instead - the design's other path. So the path where Setup removes the real
  root hub's entry and Windows makes it afresh after the restart was not read: G2's removed entry was a second,
  made-up one beside the live root hub's.
- A gone key of another device does not stop or change Setup and is not touched (G6); the eject still refuses on it
  (G6).
- The fresh install is unchanged (F3, X5). The update over `3.5.0.0` (U4) plans the controller "Replace files
  (same version)" where `3.5.0.0`'s own run on the same machine planned "Keep (same version)" (CZ above): the kit's
  other bytes under the same version number, not this change; the root hub's plan and the state after the restart
  are as before.

### ME: a start that faulted

M2's last cold start, the sixth start of its disk (each disk was ended by QMP `quit` after ME's 240 s ACPI off had
not finished, as at every ME cold start of these cells; this was after the fifth) showed "Error: 0E : 0177 :
BFF7B018" on the blue screen (`shots\c-M2-c0.png`, taken by the cell 140 s after the start). The cell's Esc keys
then left a black screen, and Enter, pressed by hand later, changed nothing: the guest took no input (registers
read as data: `logs\M2-c0-registers.txt`, the CPU in the VMM). The guest was stopped by `quit`. Not attributed;
M3 repeated M2's chain on a fresh overlay with one more cold start before the confirming Setup run: no fault at its
five starts, and the confirming run found both devices current; a sixth start of M3's disk, after its fifth
`quit` as in M2: ScanDisk's "Improper shutdown detected. Checking disks for errors..." (as after every such
`quit`), then the desktop with the USB Tree in the tray, no fault (`shots\c-M3-c6.png`, `c-M3-c6b.png`). Not
reproduced.

  one after the gate, the final check) (`logs\G7-inst-G73.txt`). Cosmetic.
- The console wraps the orphan's plan line: "INF xhci98.inf; driver none (driver entry missing); Skip (driver

## 50.34: the Intel port switchover held while Windows Setup runs - the code, its gated builds and its emulator legs (2026-11-18)

Branch `w50-pswhold`: `3.5.1.0` merged in at `0610124ab` (`990970a30`, no conflict), then `4ebe4b2d6` (record 16
section 21 carried to the owner's answers: Alternative A, the decided image-state rule kept, the exception for
`ReadyAtStart`; decisions 34 to 36), `6d1755640` (the pure half and `test_psw`), `07ffe0476` (the INFs, the INF
gate, `tuning.md`, the Settings and Setup rows), `0eabcf53c` (the driver, the snapshot, the shutdown predicate and
the Tree's words), `04b062445` (the `qemu` flavour's verdict line under a shorter label), then this section.
Design record 16 section 21 is the design. Development host A. Everything below is the emulator's (the `qemu`
flavour's stand-in for a listed controller, `XhciQemuPswModel`, record 16 section 20) or the host's; no real board
has run any of it, and the bench on a listed Intel board follows the cut (owner, decision 32).

### Order of the commits

The planned order was the pure half, the driver, then the INFs. `test_trset` holds every value the code reads to
a Settings row, a `tuning.md` row and the INFs' default in the same tree, so the INFs and rows (`07ffe0476`) come
before the driver that reads the new values (`0eabcf53c`). At `6d1755640` and `07ffe0476` the driver's step has no
readings wired, so a start on 2000 and later with the switchover on holds (every reading unread), which is the
safe direction while the INFs write 1; 98 SE and ME route at the first start, as decided.

### Gated builds

Each commit's tree was gated before it was committed, in a second worktree of the branch with a clean PATH,
x86 `build-driver.cmd all` and amd64 `all -amd64`, each "BUILD + GATES PASSED (release qemu)", exit 0:

| Commit | Tree gated as | x86 `all` | amd64 `all -amd64` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `6d1755640` | `a4c0b0cbe` (a work-tree commit of the same tree) | PASS | PASS |
| `07ffe0476` | `6cd70b253` | PASS | PASS |
| `0eabcf53c` | `0ddb389e4` | PASS | PASS (a first amd64 run, made beside the x86 run, failed one VM-matrix self-test that counts `qemu-slow.cmd` processes host-wide; run again alone, PASS) |
| `04b062445` | the commit | PASS | PASS |

Failures on the way, each fixed before the commit: the setting read before its rows existed (`test_trset`);
the packager self-test's upload set, which gates this tree's own INF at the version the tree still carries
(`3.5.0.0`, not yet bumped) against the gate's history of `XhciIntelPortSwitch` (0 before `3.5.1.0`) - the gate
now accepts, at exactly that version, either the history's default or the current one, and every other version
keeps the history's alone (the published `3.5.0.0` INF still passes at `3.5.0.0`, and this tree's INF fails at
`3.4.3.0`; withdrawn before the merge, "The merge items" below); `test_snap`'s header sizes; `XHCI_VER_PACKED` (from `xhci_verpk.h`); the amd64 import allowlist's row
for `ZwCreateKey` (`nt52-amd64-export`).

Host suites in the gated builds: `test_psw` 920 checks, `test_trpsw` 52, `test_trset` 8466, `test_inst` 9200,
`test_snap` 583, each 0 failures. `test_psw` covers every cell of section 21.3's tables, the 1296 Setup value
combinations against a rule stated in the test, the PE tests and the boot options' token spellings, the hive and
image state, the setting at absent, another type, 0 to 3 and all-ones on both families, the step reached only
where the mode is on and the board passes, the guard over a modelled registry (every disposition, the volatility
test's outcomes, `ReadyAtStart`'s write and read-back, G at absent, 0, 1, 5 and another type, its write failing)
through every failure-then-recovery sequence within one boot, the helper never answering, a stable key of the
name, the update and deployment rows of section 21.5.3, a held lifetime's no access at `D0h` to `DCh`, the
shutdown predicate, the latch and the record.

At XP's and 10's boot with `SystemSetupInProgress` set by hand, Windows itself did not complete the logon; the held verdict was read before it. The legs' x86 files: `xhci98.sys` qemu `8287F494...0B8F` (`0eabcf53c`; XP, 7 and Vista), qemu `3A6F2279...4DBE`
(`04b062445`; 10), release `22AB73C8...EF57` (`04b062445`; the release smoke).

### The legs (headless QEMU, the q35 bases, overlays, QMP ports 58501 to 58506)

Each NT leg: `devcon update` of the staged family folder's `nt-x86\xhci98.inf` from an elevated prompt with
`XhciQemuPswModel` 1 machine-wide, `devcon reboot`; then a batch run at each logon steps through the boots - (1)
a restart of the controller in the session (`devcon restart`), Restart; (2) the same, then
`XhciIntelPortSwitchSetup` 2, Restart; (3) the setting removed and the injection 4 (the session key's
create refused), Restart; (4) the injection cleared and the controller restarted, then injection 1 (the hive
read as not loaded), Restart; (5) `SystemSetupInProgress` set to 1 by hand, Restart; (6) the setting's 1 and
the controller restarted, then the value put back. The trace on port `0xE9` is the reading. Verdict codes are
`XHCI_PSW_V_*`: 1 route, 2 bypass, 4 held by the setting, 5 Setup in progress, 12 image state not loaded yet,
13 first session, 14 session not known. The injection was the value `XhciQemuPswInject` in the build these
legs ran; it is now `XhciQemuInject`'s fault 2C, read only by a start that reaches the step.

Each base ran one sequence, once. On XP, Vista and 7 the build's verdict line carried a label so long that
the line kept only its first word (the verdict) and, on its second line, the image word: the guard's words
(G, the outcome, S, the key's disposition) were not printed there, so what the table says of them on those
three bases is inference from the verdict codes and the order of the starts, not a reading. The 10 leg ran
the shorter label (`04b062445`) and read every word.

| Base (SHA-256 of the read-only base) | What the trace read, in order |
|---|---|
| XP SP3 x86 (`64ada103...d5f0`) | install session: 14 (inferred: the helper not yet running, so no routine and no arming); boot 1: 13, the restart in session 13 (inferred: G armed, S 0); boot 2: 1 (`USB3_PSSEN now=0000000F`), restart in session 1; boot 3: 4; boot 4 (injection 4): 14, restart in session with it cleared 1; boot 5: 1 (the hive is not read before Vista); boot 6 (`SystemSetupInProgress` 1): 5 - and XP refused the logon ("The system is not fully installed. Please run setup again."), so step 6 did not run on XP |
| 7 SP1 x86 (`95893177...2a7d`) | boot 1: 13, restart in session 13; boot 2: 1, restart in session 1; boot 3: 4; boot 4: 14, restart in session 1; boot 5: 12; boot 6: 5, then the setting's 1 and a restart in session: 2 |
| Vista SP2 x86 (`4d1aa775...1e2890`) | boot 1: 12 (the image word 3: not loaded at the boot's first start, as the probe read), restart in session 13 (inferred: first session, armed); boot 2: 12, restart in session 1; boot 3: 4; boot 4: 12 (the image check comes before the guard in the verdict's order), restart in session 1; boot 5: 12; boot 6: 5, then bypass 2 |
| 10 22H2 x86 (`ac361c39...0ca1ae`), on `04b062445`'s build (the six words whole: verdict, value, setting with its key, guard, image, system) | boot 1: 12 with the guard armed (G 0 to 1, outcome 13's "first session", S 0, the session key created), restart in session 13 (G 1, S 0, the key opened); boot 2: 12 with the guard permitting (S 1, a new key: the volatile key did not survive the restart), restart in session 1; boot 3: 4, the setting read from the machine-wide key; boot 4 (injection 4): 12, the guard's outcome "key failed" with S unknown and G kept at 1; restart in session with the injection cleared: 1 (a new key, S = G = 1); boot 5: 12; boot 6 (`SystemSetupInProgress` 1): 5 - and 10 did not reach a desktop (a black screen), so step 6 did not run on 10 |

The shutdown lines: every restart of a held lifetime printed `shutdown hand-back held: no access`, and every
restart of a routed one `shutdown hand-back: D8h and D0h written 0`, on all four bases. These lines come from
the model's own branch, taken before the real quirk's decision: they show the lifetime's predicate
(`XhciPswShutdownAllowed`) answering as designed for each held and routed lifetime; they do not show the real
`XhciIntelShutdownToEhci` path running - that quirk is not enabled on QEMU's controller, so its enablement and
readiness checks, its writes and its outcome are not exercised by these legs (the host vectors are their
evidence so far; a listed board's reading is owed, after the cut). A held start printed no route line, and its stop no release line; a
routed lifetime's stop released (`released, step=00000000`).

Release-flavour negative smoke, 7 SP1 x86, the release `xhci98.sys` above from the same family folder by
`devcon update`, read with `reg query` after the restart: the controller's driver key holds
`XhciIntelPortSwitchSetup` 0, `XhciIntelPortSwitchReady` 0 and `XhciIntelPortSwitch` 1 as the INF writes them,
and no `XhciIntelPortSwitchResult` (QEMU's controller is not Intel: nothing of the step is read or written).
`XhciQemuPswModel` 1, which the kit writes machine-wide, is read by no release build.

### Not run here, and why (owed)

- **2000 SP4.** WDK 7.1's `devcon` does not run on 2000 ("not a valid Win32 application"), and the package's

- **98 SE and ME** (the INF's 1 routing at the first start, the setting's 2 holding, the shutdown hand-back):

### The installed-guest legs, second set (2026-11-19)

<!-- DRAFT for runs/run-50.md, task 50.34, to be placed by the worker who commits on w50-pswhold. Supersedes
     RUNSHEET-DRAFT.md (the draft of 2026-11-19 01:55): none of that night's readings counts below. -->

The legs of record 16 section 21.10 that the first installed-guest legs left open: sleep, hibernation and Fast
Startup; two controllers; a crash and a power loss in each phase; both update rows and the stale value; the
remaining guard cases (the volatility proof on each NT system, failure then recovery, the helper never
answering); devices actually moved; 98 SE and ME through `SETUP.EXE`. Development host A, headless QEMU 11.1.2
(`asm4242-20261110-docks`), TCG, overlays of the read-only q35 bases (`E:\xhci98-vm\q35-bases`); guests in
`E:\xhci98-vm\p50\pswlegs2`, tools, kits, expected lists and every check's output in
`E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\pswlegs2`. No Windows was installed: every image is an overlay of an existing base with
this build's package installed on it (`qemu-img info --backing-chain` of each).

**Every reading here is emulation, with the model standing in.** The `qemu` flavour's `XhciQemuPswModel` 1 makes
QEMU's `1B36:000D` read as `8086:1E31` for the switchover's own reads, with `D0h` to `DCh` as four dwords in the
controller's extension; no write reaches QEMU's configuration space. Each sequence ran once: every reading is a
single reading.

**The build.** `w50-pswhold` at `bd96ea618` with the debug channel's whole-line writer of `w50-dbgline`
`a2d5317eb` (gated there, x86 and amd64 `all`, exit 0), the `qemu` flavour staged by `make-package.ps1`:
`xhci98.sys` x86 `16EC34D6...D342`, amd64 `F6911B37...B32B`; `xhcihlpr.sys` x86 `0052E39A...EC03`; `xhci98.inf`
x86 `6C8794B0...197B` (equal to `bd96ea618`'s), amd64 `201C4639...FC68`; `XHCITR.EXE` `3C49D90D...E4DD` (the gated
build of `bd96ea618`; `a2d5317eb` changes no tool). The switchover's code is `bd96ea618`'s; only
`src\xhci_dbg.c` differs. Each image compared the installed `xhci98.sys` (and on x86 `xhcihlpr.sys`) with the
package's (`fc /b`, "no differences encountered").

Readings on two earlier builds are not counted and are named only so the record is whole: on `bd96ea618` the XP
guard leg ran to its end with the expected tokens and 7 lines torn by a second writer (`vxp-bd96`); on the first
whole-line commit `1a91b5c48` (superseded by `a2d5317eb` the same morning) `vxp`, `frxp` and `vw7` passed
(`*-wl1`). Every leg in the table below ran on `a2d5317eb`.

**How they ran.** Images first, each read-only once made: on a fresh overlay of a base, the model's value written
machine-wide by a `.REG` file, UAC off, the Run key pointing at a batch that copies whichever leg kit is mounted
and runs it, the package installed by `UpdateDriverForPlugAndPlayDevices` (the scratch `PSWTOOL.EXE`), the files
compared, a power-off. Vista to 10 ask for a restart at that install: a second stage installs the root hub, sets
`XhciIntelPortSwitchReady` back to 0 by hand (that stage's own start armed it) and powers off, so every leg's
first boot finds G 0 and no session key. XP x64 does not ask for the restart, but its install's own start found the
routine (no separate helper on x64), held 13 and armed G; the first leg on that image (`vxp64`) therefore routed at
its first boot, and the same second stage, with the 64-bit tool, was then made for it (`ixp64f`, G 1 read and set
back to 0); the legs on it are `vxp64b` and `pwhxp64b`. Images: XP SP3 (one controller; two controllers; one with
`XhciQemuInject` 2Ch bit 1 written before the install, for the helper that never answers), XP x64, 2000 SP4
(ACPI), Vista, 7 (one and two controllers), 8, 8.1 and 10 22H2, all 32-bit except XP x64. Where an image's fixed
keystrokes missed the desktop (7 and 7 with two controllers at one vCPU) or the elevated prompt (8, 8.1, 10: UAC's
secure desktop under TCG), the steps were driven by hand over QMP with a screenshot before each; every such step
is a `hand` line in that image's `leg.log`. Legs: an overlay of an image; the batch at each logon steps through the
leg's boots (`C:\PSW\N.TXT`) and sends every reading to COM1 (`reg.exe`; 2000 `regedit /e`), so an absent key or
value prints reg's own error line. On 2000 (no `reg.exe` on the base) the guard leg reads with `regedit /e`;
the hibernation leg `pwhw2k`'s batch called `reg` and printed "not recognized" for each reading, so its PASS is the
trace alone, with no registry reading. 2000, XP and XP x64 guests ran with one vCPU, Vista to 10 with two: on one vCPU
7's first start read the image state "not loaded" (verdict 12) where the lists, written for two, expect 13 - a
timing of the hive's load that the design names (section 21.2), not a fault. Leg 4's resets and power losses were
made by `crash.py` beside the leg, on the leg's own `CRASHME` requests.

**How they were judged.** Two scripts. `pswcheck2.py` parses the trace with the strict prefix rule (a line that
does not begin with the producer prefix `xhci98: `, or holds it twice, fails the leg) and matches the leg's token
string whole against its list (`spec\<leg>.json`), written before the leg ran; two controllers: `ctl2check.py`.
`pswcheck2.py` imports the whole-line classifier but does not call it, so every capture was also put through
`wlscan.py`, which classifies each line by `wholeline.classify`: one whole line of a producer form of
`src\xhci_dbg.c` with its text or label one of the source's literals at `a2d5317eb` (`white-a2d5317eb.json`, the
same 1793 literals as `1a91b5c48`). Every capture of every leg in the table: 0 lines not whole, 0 unfinished last
lines (`wlscan.txt`; the same scan finds the 7 torn lines of `vxp-bd96`). One mechanical change was made to three
lists after the checker's "off" token gained its value field (`S:model-off:ips=<v>`: the checker's off token
carries the value its start printed, a change made to the checker on 2026-11-19 before these legs were judged):
`specfix.py` rewrites the bare `S:model-off` to accept the field and nothing else (`spec2\`: `u35xp`, `u35w7`,
`ui35w7`).

**What the failures are.**

- `crxp` (a reset and a power loss in each phase, XP): every segment equals its list except the power loss "at the
  release": the routed lifetime's release (D8h, D0h written 0 and read back, "released"), the shutdown hand-back
  and the guest's reset all reached the trace before the power loss landed (`debugcon-c` ends with the hand-back
  line; QEMU's reset and the host's quit both at its last byte). They follow each other within one 50 ms look of
  `crash.py` and the QMP round trip, so a loss inside the release cannot be placed by watching the trace. The
  next boot read routed 1. The other segments are as listed: after the losses with G persisted the next boot
  routed; after the loss at the verdict line (G's write lost) the next boot held 13 and armed again and routed only
  after a further Restart. The list stays as written: FAIL on that segment.
- `crw7` (the same on 7): after the first power loss, 120 s after the arming start, the next boot held 13 and armed
  again where the list expected it to route with G persisted (`b:32`); the boot after the following Restart held 13
  as well (`b:273`; COM1 states C1a/C2a: G 1, ReadyAtStart 0), and the first routed start came only at the boot
  after the next power loss, the one at the first driver line (`c:32`). Why the arming did not carry over those two
  boots is not analysed here: a reading to explain before the leg is run again. The power
  loss "at the release" landed after the release, the hand-back and the reset, as on XP. After the power loss at
  the verdict line, 7 started Startup Repair ("Your computer was unable to start", `h1.png`) and the driver did not
  load in 20 minutes; the leg was stopped there. FAIL, incomplete.
- `stxp` (the stale value, XP): `SystemSetupInProgress` 1 by hand and a restart: the start held with verdict 5 and
  G armed (01010101), as listed; then Windows XP refused the logon ("The system is not fully installed. Please
  run setup again."), so the leg's batch could not go on to the setting's 1 and 2 and the Tree's line. FAIL,
  incomplete; a stale-value leg on XP needs a way to act without a logon.
- `u35uxp` (an update over 3.5.0.0 with a user's 1 in the controller key, XP): its list was copied from the
  update over 2.2.0.0 and expected the update's own start to hold 14 with no routine; 3.5.0.0 installs
  `xhcihlpr.sys`, whose helper runs in that session, and the start read 13 (the routine answered), armed G and the
  next boot routed. FAIL against its list; the list was wrong on the helper. `u35uxq` is the same sequence with a
  list written before it ran from section 21.5's rule for a session whose routine answers.
- `pwhxp` (hibernation, XP with no display adapter, the only arrangement in which XP offers S4): the held
  lifetime stayed held across the hibernation and the in-session restart after the resume held 13/02000201, as
  listed; then XP's restart request hibernated instead, and every later resume hibernated again within five
  minutes with no logon (launches c to e). FAIL, incomplete.
- `pwhvista` (hibernation, Vista): every start as listed - held 12 (first boot, image state not loaded) across a
  hibernation and its resume, held 13/02000201 at the in-session restart, routed only after the Restart, the routed
  lifetime hibernated and resumed with its route (RESUME, REL:4 at the next stop) - but each restart or shutdown
  request made in a resumed session hibernated once more first (QMP: SUSPEND_DISK), and the restart or shutdown
  completed after the next resume (HB:held RESET; REL:3 HB:written SHUTDOWN). FAIL against the list, which has no
  such extra hibernation; the same happened on XP (`pwhxp`, where it never ended) and not on 2000 (`pwhw2k`).
- `c2w7` (two controllers, 7): its image's second stage set G back to 0 in the first controller's key only
  (`fix86` finds one driver key); both controllers' starts in that stage had armed G (verdict 12 held, guard
  01000200 at each), so at the leg's first boot the second controller routed at its first start. The checker

- `c2xp` (two controllers, XP; controller 1 tagged by its key's `XhciIntelPortSwitchSetup` 3, which reads as 0):

  list, the image's state not the driver's; `vxp64b` runs the same list on the image with G set back to 0.

### The installed-guest legs, second set, continued (2026-11-19, from 15:32)

The same build (`a2d5317eb`'s packages, above), the same images and tools; a replacement worker took the set
over at 15:32 with 12 legs passed, 10 failed and the rest not run. The owner's rule of 2026-11-19 applies: every leg
of section 21.10 passes before the merge, so each failure above was first read again from its evidence and each
ended as a pass, a driver finding, or a leg that cannot run as written (a question for the owner). None of the ten
is a driver defect. Two readings of the legs run here may be, and are left unresolved: standby on Vista and 7 (the controller surprise-removed after every S3 resume) and leg 2's first check after an in-session route (below). Where a failure looked like Windows' own behaviour, a control was run first: the same kit on
the same image with `-NoXhci` (no xHCI controller, so `xhci98.sys` never loads: no port-0xE9 line in any launch).
Every list was written before its leg ran; an arrangement changed after a control kept its leg's list unchanged.
Every capture of every leg here was also put through `wlscan3.py` (`wlscan.py`'s classifier, writing
`wlscan3.txt`): 0 lines not whole.

**The ten failures, read again** (`notes-pswlegs3.md` has the lines):

- `pwhxp`, `pwhvista` - Windows' own, decided by the controls `kpwhxp` and `kpwhvista` (no controller): both
  repeated the failure exactly. On this emulated machine a resume with no user input goes back to sleep after a
  few minutes (Vista about 2.4 min: the extra hibernation came before the restart request, not because of it -
  `pwhvista` serial-b ends at the controller restart and the request is in serial-c), and on XP with no display
  adapter (the only arrangement in which XP offers S4) a restart asked with `ExitWindowsEx` after a resume never
  completes. The driver saw no shutdown request before those hibernations (no S5 query in the trace) and answered
  every power request. The power legs now move the PS/2 mouse every 30 s while the guest runs (`leg2.py`
  "nudge", never while suspended), and XP's restart and power-off after a resume go through
  `shutdown -r/-s -f -t 0` (kits `pwhxpf`, `pwhxp64f`); the lists are unchanged.
- `crw7` - two matters, neither the driver's. (1) The held boots after the first power loss: G's write, made at the
  boot's first start and visible in the session (`XhciIntelPortSwitchReady 0x1`), was not on disk 2 to 4 minutes
  later, so each boot after a power loss or a reset read G 0, held 13 and armed again, and only a clean restart
  carried G 1 to the next boot (`b:48`, `b:289`, `c:54`). That is the state record 16 names for a power loss with
  G's write lost (section 21.5.1 step 6, section 21.10), and the driver held and armed as designed. The rework
  `crw7b` meant to flush the SYSTEM hive first, but its call (.NET `RegistryKey.Flush` on a key opened for it) does
  nothing unless that object wrote a value, so it repeated `crw7` (G lost, the same session's `bcdedit` change
  lost too). The control `crk7` decided it: in the arming session two values written by `reg.exe` at logon and
  read back 120 s later were both gone after a power loss 30 s after that, and G with them, while a file written in
  the same session was intact - on 7 here a session's registry writes, whoever makes them, are not yet on disk
  minutes later (on XP, `crxp`, G was). `crw7c` (`crw7`'s list; the SYSTEM and BCD hives flushed by `RegFlushKey`
  in the arming session, each return 0, then the power loss 30 s later): the next boot read G 1 and routed.
  Every segment of `crw7c` equals its list except the power loss "at the release", which landed after the release,
  the hand-back and the guest's reset, as on XP (`crxp`; owner question Q-A); with the BCD change flushed too,
  Startup Repair did not appear. (2) Startup Repair
  after the power loss at the verdict line is Windows 7's own boot-failure recovery (`h1.png`, `crw7b` `e1.png`).
- `crxp`, `crw7` - the power loss "at the release" cannot be placed (owner question Q-A).
- `c2xp`, `c2w7` - the checker's and the image's, not the driver's. `ctl2check.py` gave each release to the first
  routed lifetime still open in its table whichever controller had stopped; every routed lifetime has exactly one
  release (`c2xp` boot 3: four routed lifetimes, four releases, each stop's release followed by its own device
  object's removal record, `M86 L <fdo> ... 00000008`). The setting's 2 written into controller 2's own key makes
  that controller's starts read tag 2, which the list did not admit. `c2w7`'s image had G armed in the second
  controller's key (the second stage reset the first key only), so that controller routed at the leg's first boot,
  as section 21.5.3 says for G 1 with a new session key.
- `stxp` - the leg's: XP refuses the logon while `SystemSetupInProgress` is 1. `u35uxp` - its list (copied from
  the update over 2.2.0.0) did not allow for 3.5.0.0's helper; `u35uxq`, the same sequence with a list written
  before it ran, passed in the first part. `vxp64` - its image's G was armed; `vxp64b` passed in the first part.

**What changed in the arrangements** (each before the leg that uses it):

- Two controllers: lists `c2xpb`, `c2w7b` with the per-controller hold's tag (spec `ctl`: tags 0 and 2 name
  controller 2, tag 3 controller 1) and a checker, `ctl2check2.py`, that gives a release made while both
  controllers' lifetimes are routed to the controller whose removal record follows it (the device object's serial
  tied to its controller by the `M86 S` record after that object's start decision), fails a start or a removal of
  a controller whose routed lifetime is unreleased, and requires each release to be exactly W D8h 0, R D8h 0,
  W D0h 0, R D0h 0 with step 0 (checked on mutated copies of `c2xpb`'s capture: a release's D0h lines removed, a
  removal record naming the other controller or an earlier boot's device object, a whole release removed,
  each fails; `scratchpad\mut` of the worker). `c2xp`'s and `c2w7`'s own captures pass the new
  checker against the new list (not counted). `c2w7b` ran on a new image stage `iw72g` (kit `fix2`: G set back to 0
  in both controllers' keys, then a clean power-off).
- The stale value: three routes that need no logon were tried before one worked - a start-up task
  (`stxpb`: it never ran while `SystemSetupInProgress` was 1), Setup's own `CmdLine` with `SetupType` 2 (`stxpc`:
  it ran, but no restart could be asked from it) and with `SetupType` 1 (`stxpd`: Windows restarted after it, then
  cleared `SetupType`, and the next boot showed "The system is not fully installed" again). `stxpe`: Setup's
  `CmdLine` with `SetupType` 1, each step setting `SetupType` 1 and `CmdLine` again before it ends; the last step
  puts `SystemSetupInProgress` and `SetupType` back to 0. `SetupType` is a secondary Setup value: in automatic
  mode `SystemSetupInProgress` 1 still gives verdict 5 (the primary first), and the setting's 1 and 2 give 2 and 4
  before Setup is looked at, so `stxp`'s list stands unchanged. On 7 (`stw7e`, `stw7f`) the same route read all five
  starts as listed and the Tree's line at the three Setup-mode boots, but after those boots 7 no longer logged on by
  itself (a password prompt; re-importing the Winlogon key did not bring it back), so the last step's logon batch
  could not run; `stw7g` runs that step from a service started at the boot (`SVCW.BAT`), with no logon.
- 98 SE and ME through `SETUP.EXE` (the coordinator's choice of the earlier runs' arrangement): the `release`
  package of `a2d5317eb` in its family layout (`kits\ins98`, `mkinstkit.ps1`: `xhci98.sys` `564CEE29...5D28`; tools
  of the gate worktree at `1a91b5c48` - `a2d5317eb` changes no tool) installed by its `SETUP.EXE` window, driven by
  hand (Welcome, Components with its defaults, Summary, Install, Finish with "Restart Windows now"; `w1`-`w4`,
  `mw1`-`mw4`), then at the next logon the installed file compared with the package's (`fc /b`, equal) and the
  `qemu` flavour's `xhci98.sys` of the same commit copied over it (equal), then cold starts. The kit's own start of
  `SETUP.EXE` failed (its batch changed directory on C: without changing drive), so the window was started from
  the Run box by hand (`hand` lines). Each guest's clock was read against the host's in the timed boot (59.1 s
  guest over 59 s host on 98 SE, 60.1 s over 61 s on ME).
- Devices moved (leg 2): the stick was never given a volume by 7 because the stick and the transfer disk, both
  made by QEMU's `vvfat`, carried the same MBR disk signature (`BE1AFDFA`); the probe `stkprobe2` (the stick as a
  FAT image file) still showed no volume, and `stkprobe3` (the same image with its signature changed to
  `50535731`, `stickimg\stick-fat16b.raw`) gave it a drive letter and read its files under 7's own EHCI driver.
  `l2w7b` (the predecessor's `l2w7.sh` on `iw7f` with that stick, two vCPUs) passed nine of its ten checks - the
  keyboard typed and the stick read (786 to 795 KB counted by QEMU) on the controller the routing rules expect at
  each held, routed and bypass boot - and failed C05, the check typed 77 s after the in-session move: no drive held the
  stick's files and QEMU counted no read. The driver had enumerated both moved devices on the xHCI in that
  lifetime (the stick at its SuperSpeed port: slot enabled, addressed, its device objects created and started, its
  configuration selected and its endpoints opened). `l2w7c` (C05 300 s after that start's verdict, nothing else
  changed) failed C05 the same way, the check typed 321 s after the move. Probes, each looking for the stick's files on COM1 with
  no check of the harness: `l2p7` (only the in-session route), `l2p7c` (the stick read on the EHCI first), `l2p7d`
  (also a held in-session restart first), `l2p7e` (also a routed boot before) found the moved stick and read it from
  their first look to the end of an 8-minute poll - the first look typed 76 to 79 s after the move (`l2p7`: 204 s,
  the first typing having been lost with the moved keyboard); `l2p7f` (`l2w7c`'s own steps to C04, all four checks
  passing) looked once, typed 75 s after the move - no stick drive, while `diskpart` in the same batch already
  listed the stick's disk (online) and its volume D: (FAT, healthy) - and then, 240 s later (the poll typed about
  330 s after the move), found and read it at every look. (Times are from the harness's own record of the move and
  of each typed command; a look runs a few seconds after its command is typed.) `stkprobe4` (no `xhci98` in the path: the read stick unplugged and
  plugged back on the same EHCI port) found it again within 35 s. **The cause of C05's failure is not resolved and
  may be the driver's.** For Windows' side: in each run the driver presented, configured and opened the moved
  stick, every probe found it in the end, and in `l2p7f` its volume was listed while its files could not yet be
  read. Against closing it there: `l2w7b` and `l2w7c` themselves never showed the stick usable after the move
  (each lifetime ended soon after C05), the probes are other runs (and called `diskpart`, which the leg does not),
  their first good looks bound the time only from above, and the EHCI control did not reproduce the failure at
  all. `l2w7d` runs C05 after `WAITSTK.BAT` (a look every 20 s until the stick's files are there, at most 8 min),
  every other step and check `l2w7.sh`'s: it reads whether the stick becomes usable in the leg's own path, and
  cannot by itself explain the earlier failures. It passed, all ten checks: `WAITSTK`'s first look (typed 74 s after
  the move) found the stick, and C05 read it on the xHCI (786432 bytes counted by QEMU).
- Standby: a control with no controller on each system first. Vista offers S3 and resumed (`kpwsvista`); 8.1 and
  10 do not offer S3 with no display adapter (`kpwsw81`, `kpwsw10`; with the standard VGA 10 disables it too, the
  predecessor's probe); XP x64 entered S3, was woken and never came back (`kpwsxp64`); 7 resumed in the
  predecessor's probe `pw7n` (no project driver); 8 does not offer S3 either (`kpwsw8`). Legs run only where the
  control resumed: Vista `pwsvista` and 7 `pwsw7`. **Both stopped on a possible driver defect**: after every S3
  resume Windows surprise-removed the controller (its D0 line, then no driver line at all, then only
  `QUERY_DEVICE_RELATIONS` and `SURPRISE_REMOVAL` to the root hub and the controller, `pwsvista` `a:246-256`,
  `pwsw7` `a:248-259`; the controller was then enumerated and started again), so the leg's restart of the
  controller 60 s after the resume found no device. After an S4 resume the same D0 line is followed at once by the
  driver's re-initialisation (`pwhw7` `b:2-8`). The control `kpwsvista2` (Vista, the controller present, xhci98's
  service disabled) kept the controller's device row unchanged before, right after and 60 s after the resume. In
  both legs, and in the control, the power-off asked after a resume ended as a guest reset (the control's next
  power-off, after a fresh boot, powered off): that part is Windows' or the emulator's, and made the leg's last step
  repeat. The first standby of each leg was in a held lifetime, which makes no routing access; nothing in the trace
  places the failure in the switchover's code.
- Fast Startup on 8 (`pffw8`, `pffw8-r2`) and hibernation on 8 (`pwhw8`): the first QEMU launch after the
  hibernation's power-off ended within 14 s with empty logs, and the next launch did not resume the session (a
  reset before any driver line, then a fresh session). A 30 s gap before the relaunch did not change it. Never seen
  on Vista, 7, 8.1 or 10. The control `kpwhw8` (`pwhw8`'s kit, no xHCI controller) did the same - the first
  launch after the power-off ended at once and the next booted fresh - so 8's resume from a hibernation fails on
  this rig without the driver too: hibernation and Fast Startup on 8 cannot be read here (Q-C).

### The two unresolved readings, diagnosed (2026-11-20)

The coordinator asked, with the owner away, whether each of the two readings left unresolved above is new with
50.34 or older, and to narrow each; diagnosis only (no fix). Builds: 50.34 (`a2d5317eb`, the `qemu` package used
above), the release branch tip `6372ce8cb` (its source equals `319f8b6aa`'s; the gated `qemu` build of gate ABC,
`xhci98.sys` `CBAA26D3...5488`, `xhcihlpr.sys` `CC43A6D1...`, hashes equal to the gate's record), and the released
3.5.0.0 (`release` flavour, `nt-x86`); in each leg the build's two `.sys` files were copied over the installed ones
on the leg's image and compared (`fc /b`) before the leg's boot. Nothing was built.

**Standby on Vista and 7: the emulator's firmware, not the driver, and not new.** The same standby step (two
S3 cycles, the controller's device row read 0, 20, 60 and 120 s after each resume; `tools\mks3arm.py`) on 7 with
each build (`s3w7534`, `s3w76372`, `s3w7350`) and on Vista with each (`s3vi534`, `s3vi6372`, `s3vi350`): all six
lost the controller after the resume - five with the row still present at the first look right after the resume
and gone from +20 s on, `s3vi534` with it gone already at that first look; on the `qemu` builds the trace shows the
power dispatches down to the D0 set-power, then no driver line, then the PnP surprise removal and removal - as in
`pwsvista` and `pwsw7`. In each of the six only the first standby reached S3 (one SUSPEND event); the second
returned at once. So it is already in 3.5.0.0. The cause is outside the driver: launch2.ps1 starts QEMU with
`-L` usb4-emu `vms\qemu-baseline\share`, whose `bios-256k.bin` is the stock SeaBIOS rel-1.17.0
(`rel-1.17.0-0-gb52ca86e094d-prebuilt`, SHA-256 `ae6f6aa9...`), and no `-bios`. That firmware has the q35 S3
resume fault of task 48.35 (run-48 "48.35 (the vehicle)"; usb4-emu `docs/Q35-S3-RESUME.md`): QEMU wakes the
machine with a full reset (`pc_machine_wakeup()` -> `pc_machine_reset(RESET_TYPE_WAKEUP)` -> every device reset;
on the PCI side the reset clears Command, the BARs and the PM state of each device and the root port's bus
numbers and windows, and `xhci_reset` clears the controller - nothing in the PCI, xHCI or root-port code treats a
wake reset differently), and the reset also disables the MCH's `PCIEXBAR` (MMCONFIG) and the ICH9 PM block;
SeaBIOS's resume path then writes the chipset back through the dead MMCONFIG window, so Windows resumes with no
MMCONFIG and no ACPI PM block. Windows' PCI bus driver then fails the controller's D0 (run-45 45.63 read
`STATUS_NO_SUCH_DEVICE` from the bus below at this point, before 48.35's fix existed), the driver's failed-D0 path
(`hcdD0Refused`, task 45.63) ends what the bus holds, and PnP removes the device. The emulator folder's own
`bios-256k.bin` is the fixed image (`e5dc0550...`, `rel-1.17.0-1-g7a5a6afa-usb4emu`; its README: "the S3 resume
fix needs -bios"). Controls with it (`tools\mks3bios.py`, `-bios` added, nothing else): 7 with 50.34 (`s3b7534`)
and with the release tip (`s3b76372`), Vista with 50.34 (`s3bvi534`): both standbys reached S3, the D0 went
through, the driver re-initialised the controller ("init complete", "slots invalidated by a resume, keeping
devices"), and the device row was present at every look. Hibernation differs because its resume starts a new
QEMU process: the firmware's power-on path sets MMCONFIG and the PM block up as at any boot, so the D0 at the
resume reaches a configured device and the driver re-initialises (`pwhw7` `b:2-8`). A control with Windows' own
xHCI driver across S3 is not available on this rig's 8 to 10 images (no S3 offered with no display adapter);
run-45's 45.63 has one on 10 x64 (Windows' `USBXHCI` controller removed after the wake and found again), on the
same stock firmware.

### The installed-guest legs, second set, after the host's restart (2026-11-20, from 09:08)

A replacement worker took the set over at 09:08 after the host was restarted; everything running at 08:49 was
stopped then and is void (`l2w7e`, `crxp2`). The same build (`a2d5317eb`'s `qemu` packages), images and tools; the
owner's answers of 2026-11-20 applied (Q-A, Q-B, Q-C option 1 each, `QUESTIONS-pswlegs3.md`). At about 10:25 the
coordinator reported the host's processors at about 90 % and limited this set to two guests: no guest was started
above two from then on, while the three running at the notice ran down (`p2knb` stopped at 10:32). The runs that
ended after 10:25 ran under that load: `l2w7s2` to `l2w7s4`, `stk5`, `pwsxp64d`, `pwsw7c`, `p2knb`, `crxp3`, `crxp4`,
`crw7d`, `crw7e`. Every list was written before its leg ran; where an arrangement had to change after a run, the list
was copied unchanged under a new leg name.

**Leg 2's C05, run again.** The path known to fail is the leg itself (`l2w7b`, `l2w7c`); the probes
`c5r6372`, `c5r534c` (release tip and 50.34, route form) and `c5h350`, `c5h6372` (a plain hot move, no routing) found
the moved stick in 20 of 20 cycles, 16 to 28 s after the move (`c5read.py`). So the leg was run again, as written,
with readings around C05 (`l2w7e.sh`: `PRE5.BAT`, typed about 45 s before C05 - the
device rows and `mountvol`, touching no volume; `POST5.BAT` right after it - `vol` of every letter, the stick's file
looked for again, `diskpart`'s disks and volumes, `mountvol`, the device rows, then a look every 20 s for 8 minutes)
and, from the second run on, QEMU's own record of the stick (`l2w7s.sh`, made by `mkl2w7f.py` and `mkl2w7s.py`: the
trace events of every SCSI command the stick receives and of its xHCI slot and endpoints, with QEMU's timestamps;
the leg cut after `POST5` - boots 4 to 8 had passed in every earlier run - so that one run takes about 30 minutes).
Times below are from the stick's leaving the EHCI in QEMU's record (`stktrace.py`) where it exists, else from the
harness's record of the move. Runs, one at a time (`l2seq.py`):

- `l2w7e2` (`l2w7e.sh`, all ten checks): C05 typed 313 s after the move - passed (QEMU 786432 bytes on the xHCI);
  `POST5`: `D:` the stick, `diskpart` Disk 2.
- `l2w7s1`, `l2w7s2`, `l2w7s3` (C01-C05): C05 typed 313, 314, 314 s after the move - passed; QEMU's record: the
  arriving disk's first commands (INQUIRY) 2.7 to 3.0 s after the stick left the EHCI, the FAT volume's 4 KB reads (35
  in each run) from 3.5 to 4.5 s after it, C05's 15 READ(10) and 3 WRITE(10); Disk 2.
- `l2w7s4` (C01-C05): **C05 failed again**, typed 314 s after the move, and this time with the readings. QEMU's
  record (`stktrace-l2w7s4.txt`): 0.66 s after the stick left the EHCI the arriving disk was asked INQUIRY, READ
  CAPACITY and the partition table (READ(10) of 512 and 2048 bytes; every command answered, the check conditions the
  same as in the passing runs), the last of them at 0.97 s, and then nothing at all until 337 s. `PRE5` (about 270 s
  after the move) and C05 itself: the disk's device row started (`USBSTOR\DISK...`, problem 0, service `disk`) but
  no `STORAGE\VOLUME` row for its partition, `mountvol` listing no volume of it, `vol D:` "The system cannot find
  the path specified". `POST5`'s `diskpart` (337 s): the disk was numbered 3 (number 2 was still taken when it
  arrived), and `diskpart`'s own commands read the disk again (TEST UNIT READY, MODE SENSE, READ CAPACITY, the
  partition table); the volume row and `D:` appeared at once, and the next look read the stick.

What the driver's own trace shows (`lifesum.py`, `lifecnt.py`, the in-session routed lifetime): in all three failures
every transfer the driver submitted completed or was cancelled at the shutdown as in the passing runs (`l2w7b` 218 =
216 + 2 cancelled, `l2w7c` 214 of 214, `l2w7s4` 212 = 210 + 2 cancelled), no URB, selection or endpoint was refused,
and after the disk's first burst (about 117 transfers) nothing more reached the driver until the run's own `diskpart`
(`l2w7s4`) or the shutdown but the keyboard's few transfers per typed command; in the passing runs two more bursts
follow (about 60 and 50 transfers, the volume's mount) and the lifetime ends at 290 to 301. A difference in timing
goes with the failures in the leg's own runs: the root hub's first answer to Windows' relations query after the
controller's restart waited for the moved devices' enumeration in all three failures (`l2w7b` 343 ms, `l2w7c` 436 ms,
`l2w7s4` 436 ms; both devices reported in that first answer) and came at once in all five passes (`l2w7d` 31 ms,
`l2w7e2` 62 ms, `l2w7s1` to `l2w7s3` 31 ms; the devices reported in a later answer). It is not the whole story: the
probe `l2p7f` (the leg's path to the route) answered at once (31 ms) and its look 75 s after the move still found no
stick before its `diskpart` (which listed the disk as number 3), and the probes `l2p7c`, `l2p7d` answered after 436
and 343 ms with the disk numbered 2 (their looks came after a `diskpart`). What every run with readings shares is the
disk number: wherever the moved disk was numbered 3 (`l2w7s4`, `l2p7f`, and `l2p7e`, whose first look came after a
`diskpart`) its volume was missing until the disk was read again, or was seen only after a `diskpart`; in every pass
since the host's restart (no `diskpart` before C05) it was numbered 2 and its volume was there (`l2p7c` and `l2p7d`,
numbered 2, looked only after a `diskpart`). The two older failures recorded no disk number.

This is the outcome this rig already showed for two disks with one MBR signature: `stkprobe2`, under 7's own EHCI
driver with the transfer disk and the stick both made by `vvfat` (signature `BE1AFDFA` on both), gave the stick no
volume until its signature was changed (`stkprobe3`). A control with no `xhci98` in the path (`stk5`, `mkstk5.py`,
written before it ran: 7 with two EHCI controllers both run by 7's own `usbehci`, the stick read on one and moved
to the other at once by QMP, five cycles, looks every 10 s with no `diskpart`) found the stick at the first look 16 s
after each of the five moves to the second controller, and at the next cycle's first look after four of the five
moves back (the fifth was not looked at). It did not reproduce the missing volume, so it neither shows nor excludes
the outcome without `xhci98` (how soon 7's own hub reported the arriving disk, and its number, were not recorded).

**Reading of leg 2's C05:** reproduced and narrowed, not closed. Shown: in the failing runs the driver had presented,
configured and served the moved disk, answered every command asked of it and held nothing pending, and Windows had
made no volume for the disk, which it made at once when `diskpart` read the disk again. Indicated, not proven: that
Windows held the volume back because the same disk (one MBR signature) was still present on the EHCI when it
arrived - the disk numbers and `stkprobe2`'s behaviour point there, but no run captured the departing disk's row at
the arrival; and that the driver's quicker report of the moved devices (the first answer that waits for them) makes
that overlap more likely - in the leg's eight runs it goes with every outcome, in the probes it does not. Not shown:
whether the same outcome occurs without 50.34 - the code paths involved (the root hub's settle, in the driver since
2.1.0.0, and the in-session route, in the release tip) predate it, but the release-tip probes never met the overlap
and the leg's harness cannot run the older builds. Counts on the leg's own path: C05 failed in 3 of 8 runs (`l2w7b`,
`l2w7c`, `l2w7s4`); every other check of every run passed. What it means for a user (on a real board, a USB disk on a
switchable port when the controller is restarted in a session - an update or a disable and enable - and the route
happens then), whether the driver should report moved devices later, and whether 50.34 waits for either, is the
owner's question Q-D (`QUESTIONS-pswlegs4.md`).

  routed; Q-A's cut 6 s after the restart request before the release, the next boot G 1 and routed; the verdict-line

  request; the same list): passed (10 starts, 34 tokens, 0 failures) - the "G persisted" loss 30 s after the

### Leg 2's C05 held for its cause (2026-11-20, from 13:1x)

The owner held 50.34 until C05's failure is explained (Q-D option 3). Four questions, in the coordinator's order:
is it there without 50.34; what Windows holds of the departing EHCI disk at the arrival, and does a disk that cannot
collide, or a later arrival, avoid it; does 7 miss the volume with its own drivers only; and the cause and whether it
is ours. Up to four guests again, six from 16:4x. Every script, kit and list below was written before the runs that
use it; the per-run readings are in `legsum-final.txt` (`legsum.py`) and `mvsum-final.txt` (`mvsum.py`).

**What the event log and the registry keep.** The failing run's own disk booted once more (`evq`, `evq2`;
`mkevq.py`, `mkevq2.py`; the disk only read): the System log holds no event of the disk, partition, volume or mount
managers at all. `Enum\USBSTOR` keeps both instances of the stick's disk - the EHCI one (`...\1-0000:00:1d.0-3&0`)
and the xHCI one (`...\1-0000:00:1c.0:00.0-3&0`), each with its own partition-manager disk id - and `MountedDevices`
maps `D:` to the stick's MBR signature and offset (`31575350`, `7E00`): one identity for the two instances.

**Without 50.34: yes.** The leg's own path on the release tip `6372ce8cb` (`l2w7r.sh`, `mkl2w7r.py`; kit `k2w7r`
copies the release tip's `qemu` build over the installed driver at boot 1). What differs from the 50.34 leg: the
release tip has the switch model but no Setup guard and prints no register-access lines, so the harness moves the
devices at the driver's "XUSB2PR now" line (a few lines after the D0h write it uses on 50.34), and the hold before
the routing restart is the setting's 0 instead of 50.34's image-state fault. C05 failed in 3 of 4 runs (`l2w7r1`,
`l2w7r2`, `l2w7r3`; `l2w7r4` passed). On 50.34 the leg's path failed C05 in 5 of 13 (`l2w7b`, `l2w7c`, `l2w7s4`,
`l2w7k4`, `l2w7k5`). 3.5.0.0 cannot take the leg's path in the emulator: it has no model of the switch and never
routes there; the hand move below gives it the same move.

**The same move by hand, on every build - 3.5.0.0 as released included.** `mkmv.py`, `fmover.py`: the in-session move
with the switch code idle on every build (`XhciIntelPortSwitch` 0), the batch restarting the controller and the rig
moving the keyboard and the stick from the EHCI to the xHCI 46 ms after the start's controller reset (QEMU's trace),
the look 45 s after, then every 30 s to 300 s, with no `diskpart`; then back to the EHCI and the next cycle. Of the counted cycles (`mvsum-final.txt`), every one whose
disk arrived within a second of the move failed - the stick not found in 300 s, its volume only after a `diskpart`
(or not yet at the look after it) - and every one that arrived later passed: 50.34 (`mv534d`) 3 early arrivals
(0.49-0.54 s), 3 failures; the release tip (`mv6372d`) 3 early (0.56-0.59 s), 3 failures; 3.5.0.0 as released
(`mv350d`, `mv350e`, the release flavour, which prints nothing of its own) 3 early (0.51-0.64 s), 3 failures, and
5 later (2.8-3.6 s), 5 found. The disk capture shows the overlap in all 9 early cycles (the departing PhysicalDrive2
and the arriving PhysicalDrive3 in one look, both attribute 0) and in none of the 5 later ones. `mv534d`'s cycle 2
with the capture loop's rows: 12:06:56.80 the EHCI and the xHCI disk and device rows together; 12:06:58.50 only the
xHCI ones, the departing volume and `D:` still listed; 12:07:10.45 that volume and `D:` gone - and no volume for
the arriving disk. On the qemu builds the counted early arrivals had the waiting first answer (374-499 ms). So the hand move
reproduces the leg's failure on every build, and 3.5.0.0 has it.
The first cycle of each run is the stick's first arrival on the xHCI in that image (a driver install, 9 to 15 s) and
is not counted. (The first hand-move runs, `mv534b`, `mv6372b`, `mv350b`, `mv534c` and the controls `mvctlb`,
`mvctlc`, are void after their first cycle: the mover left its QMP connection open, every move back timed out and the
later cycles re-plugged the stick on the bus it was already on. Fixed - `fmover.py` closes both - before the `d` and
`e` runs.)

**What decides each run: an overlap of the two instances.** The leg with a capture loop started 10 s before the
routing restart (`l2w7k.sh`, `mkl2w7k.py`): `CAP.BAT` (about one look in two seconds: the stick's device and disk
rows of both instances, every `STORAGE\VOLUME` row, the volumes and mount points `mountvol` lists, `MountedDevices`)
and `DSK.PS1` (twice a second, every PhysicalDrive's number and the partition manager's attributes, by documented
IOCTLs only; no sector read). In every failure with the capture (`l2w7k4`, `l2w7k5`, `l2w7r1`, `l2w7r2`, `l2w7r3`)
both disks were present at once - e.g. `l2w7r1` 12:17:34.50 and `l2w7k4` 12:18:09.04: PhysicalDrive2 (the departing
EHCI disk) and PhysicalDrive3 (the arriving one), both with attribute 0, online and not read-only, and a second or
two later only PhysicalDrive3; the volume never came until `diskpart` read the disk again. The moved disk's number
tells the same in every run: 3 where it arrived while the departing one still held 2, 2 where it did not. All six
failures with readings since the host's restart (`l2w7s4`, `l2w7k4`, `l2w7k5`, `l2w7r1`, `l2w7r2`, `l2w7r3`) had
Disk 3; every pass with the stick's own signature had Disk 2. Whether the arrival overlaps goes with how soon the disk
arrives, and in the runs of the unchanged path that went with the driver's first answer to Windows' relations query at
the routing restart: where it waited for the moved devices' enumeration (343 to 842 ms) the disk arrived 0.56 to
1.12 s after the stick left the EHCI and C05 failed; where it came at once (31 to 78 ms) the devices were reported in
a later answer, the disk arrived 2.7 to 3.6 s after, and C05 passed - all 17 runs, on both builds (`l2w7b`, `l2w7c`,
`l2w7d`, `l2w7e2` recorded no arrival time, `l2w7b`, `l2w7c`, `l2w7d` no disk number). This is a correlation, not the
whole mechanism: `l2w7vs2` (below) had the immediate first answer and still an early arrival (0.85 s) and an overlap
(Disk 3). (The capture loops ran in the failures as in the passes; two findstr patterns in `CAP.BAT` waited on their
input until 15:05 - the captures of the runs before that are `DSK.PS1`'s only.)

**The direct tests** (`tools\harness3`, `mkharness3.py`, `l2w7v.sh`, `mkl2w7v.py`: test-only options acting at the
routing restart only):
- A stick whose MBR signature cannot collide (`sigswap`: the same files, signature `32575350`; it arrives on the
  xHCI with that image, goes back with its own): `l2w7vs7` (first answer 546 ms, first command 0.79 s, Disk 3) and
  `l2w7vs9` (686 ms, 1.17 s, Disk 3) - the failing timing, the twin still present - both passed; `l2w7vs2` (31 ms,
  but 0.85 s and Disk 3: an overlap with the immediate answer) passed; `l2w7vs1` (31 ms, 3.1 s, Disk 2) passed. 4 of
  4, 3 of them overlapped. `l2w7vs9`'s capture shows it: at 12:18:14.03 the EHCI and the xHCI disk and device rows
  together, at 12:18:18.15 only the xHCI ones, a new volume (the other signature's) and `D:`.
- A later arrival: a 0.5 s delay in the move (`l2w7vd05a`, one run) let the first answer come before the devices,
  which then came in a later answer (31 ms, 3.3 s, Disk 2) - passed; since the harness's delay acts before the
  controller is even initialised, a longer one is expected to do the same - not tested: `l2w7vd2a` was stopped at its
  first boot (void) and no 5 s run was made. The arrival after the EHCI instance has left the device tree (`l2w7vg1`, "EGONE"): its
  capture loop hung (the findstr fault above), so the devices arrived after the 60 s limit (first command 60.5 s after
  the stick left the EHCI) - passed; not a test of that condition.
- Not run: the driver itself delaying its report (a test-only setting in a build of this branch). A later arrival
  passed every time it happened, but a driver-side delay is untested as such; it is part of an owner's option.

**Windows' own drivers** (`mvctld`: 7 with two EHCI controllers, both run by 7's own drivers, the stick moved from
one to the other by QMP in 3 to 6 ms and back each cycle, the same batch, capture and looks as the hand moves):
4 of 4 counted cycles found at the first look, no overlap in the capture. 7's own hub reported the arriving disk 3.2 to 3.7 s after the move - never as early as the xHCI driver's
early reports - so it never met the overlap; whether 7 would miss the volume with only its own drivers given an
arrival within a second cannot be produced here.

**The cause, as far as shown.** Windows 7 does not bring up a volume for a disk that arrives while another disk with
the same MBR signature is still present (here: the same stick's departing EHCI instance), not in the 5 minutes the
runs waited; a `diskpart` brought it up at the next look in some failures and not yet in others; with a signature that cannot collide the same overlap costs nothing (3 of 3). The overlap
happens when the moved disk is reported within about a second of the in-session route, before 7 has finished removing
the EHCI instance; in the unchanged leg that early report went with the root hub's first answer waiting for the moved
devices (17 of 17), though one swapped-signature run arrived early without it. It is not new with 50.34: the release
tip fails on the leg's path (3 of 4) and, like 50.34, on every early arrival of the hand move; 3.5.0.0 as released
fails on every early arrival of the hand move too (3 of 3 early arrivals). 50.34's own code only decides that the route is taken; how
soon the moved devices are reported is older code (the root hub's settle, 2.1.0.0). The missing volume is Windows' behaviour; the
in-session move of a mounted disk and its early report are the driver's. Not shown: what 7 does on a real board,
where the stick has one serial number on both controllers (QEMU gives the two instances different ones) - a bench
reading. The owner's question is Q-E (`QUESTIONS-pswlegs4b.md`).

### What brings the missing volume back (2026-11-20, from 18:0x)

The owner chose to state the limit with no code change, and asked for the remedies to be read before they are
worded. Two runs on the kept Windows 7 rig (not keyed), on the build the cut carries: the merged tree's gated qemu
x86 images, commit `30fca1928` (its gate record `gated-x86-qemu.txt`, dirty 0), copied read-only from that tree's
build output to `pkg\merge-qemu-x86` - `xhci98.sys` SHA-256 `f098b31ee8de03d042cb300b377fd52a3ed7a7767e891f585928543eac495eed`,
`xhcihlpr.sys` `b9b7532a59f3f4713cbb06441e9622b3565ddd71b3160bc1f465ee1dd294d0d0`, both equal to the record.

**How.** `mkrm.py` (written before the runs) makes two legs of the hand move above (`mkmv.py`, `fmover.py`), 7 cycles
each: the stick and the keyboard moved by QMP from the EHCI to the xHCI as soon as QEMU's trace showed the
controller's start reset (the latency varies; in `rmA` 3 the stick was attached to the xHCI - QEMU's first
`usb_msd_reset` - about 64 ms after the controller's reset), one look 45 s later. Found: no failure. Not found: a failure; the state is read (mountvol, the device rows, `MountedDevices`,
`vol D:`), then one remedy, in rotation over the failures, and a look every 2 s for 120 s (the stick's drive letter
with its file on it = the volume and its letter back):

- **Scan for hardware changes**: `devcon rescan` (WDK 7.1's `devcon.exe`, run in the guest). Device Manager's
  "Scan for hardware changes" itself was not clicked. They are documented for the same purpose - DevCon Rescan
  "uses Windows Plug and Play features to update the device list", Device Manager's item scans for hardware
  changes - but no document found says they make the same request or the same call, and that is not verified.
- **Unplug and plug in again**: `fmover.py`'s "REPLUG": QMP `device_del` of the stick on the xHCI, then
  `device_add` on the same port with the same disk, 2 ms after it was gone (a person takes seconds).
- **`diskpart`** (`list disk`, `list volume`), for comparison with the earlier runs.

`rmB` also had a display: at its first failure, before any remedy, it opened Explorer's Computer view and then Disk
Management, with a screendump of each (`rmB\uv2explorer.png`, `rmB\uv2diskmgmt.png`; `ppm2png.py`).

**Results** (`rmread.py rmA rmB`; arrival = the arriving disk's first SCSI command after the stick left the EHCI):

| Run, cycle | Arrival | 45 s look | Remedy | Volume and letter back |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rmA` 1 | 7.24 s | found | - | - |
| `rmA` 2 | 0.49 s | missing | `devcon rescan` | no, not in 120 s |
| `rmA` 3 | 0.59 s | missing | unplug and plug in | yes, `D:`, 3 s after |
| `rmA` 4 | 0.52 s | missing | `diskpart` | yes, `D:`, 5 s after |
| `rmA` 5 | 2.87 s | found | - | - |
| `rmA` 6 | 0.49 s | missing | `devcon rescan` | no, not in 120 s |
| `rmA` 7 | 3.15 s | found | - | - |
| `rmB` 1 | 9.80 s | found | - | - |
| `rmB` 2 | 0.62 s | missing | opening Disk Management | yes, `D:`, found 34 s after it was started |
| `rmB` 3 | 0.48 s | missing | `devcon rescan` | no, not in 120 s |
| `rmB` 4 | 0.45 s | missing | unplug and plug in | yes, `D:`, 3 s after |
| `rmB` 5 | 0.51 s | missing | `diskpart` | no, not in 120 s |
| `rmB` 6 | 0.58 s | missing | `devcon rescan` | no, not in 120 s |
| `rmB` 7 | 0.53 s | missing | unplug and plug in | yes, `D:`, 3 s after |

Every arrival within a second failed (10 of 10) and every later one passed (4 of 4), as in the runs above.
By remedy: unplugging and plugging in again 3 of 3, each back at its old letter 3 s after it began (the second
look); the scan (`devcon rescan`) 0 of 4 - it printed "Scanning for new hardware. Scanning completed." and the
stick's volume and letter did not come back in 120 s; `diskpart` 1 of 2; opening Disk Management 1 of 1.

**What the user sees in the failed state** (`rmB` 2, the screendumps; the other failures' state readings agree):
Explorer's Computer view shows the other drives but not the stick's, while the tray balloon says the device is
ready to use and its driver software was installed. In all 10 failures Windows has the stick's disk (its xHCI
instance present, with no problem code) but no volume and no letter for it, and `vol D:` answers "The system
cannot find the path specified."; `MountedDevices` still maps `D:` to the stick's signature and offset. Disk
Management was not seen showing the failure: in `rmB` 2, `D:` was missing, then Explorer and after it Disk
Management were opened, and Disk Management's window, 30 s after it was started, listed the stick's volume as `D:`
(the look 34 s after found the stick). That opening Disk Management brought it back is inferred from that order (one
trial; Explorer was opened first). `diskpart`'s two listings differ: in `rmA` 4 it listed the stick's disk and
volume `D:` (and the look 5 s after found it); in `rmB` 5 it listed the stick's disk with all its 504 MB free and no
volume, and nothing came back in 120 s. Whether those were two different failures before `diskpart` ran is not
known: no listing was taken before it.

**Observed and inferred.** Observed: the outcomes and times above, on QEMU, with the moved stick at its old letter
after each remedy that worked. Inferred, not run: that Device Manager's own "Scan for hardware changes" does what
`devcon rescan` did (documented for the same purpose; not shown to be the same request); that opening Disk
Management brings the volume back (one trial, above); that a person's unplug and plug in, seconds rather than 2 ms,
works the same (by then the departing instance has long gone, which is what the earlier runs make the condition);
that Disk Management, opened on a failure like `rmB` 5's, would show the stick's disk as unallocated with no volume
(from `diskpart`'s listing; not seen in Disk Management) - and that initializing or formatting it there would
destroy the stick's files, so a statement should not send the user there. Not shown: a real board.

- Windows 2000 has no shutdown command: the controller-restart tool gained a restart and a power-off of the computer.

  guest's power-off; twice more with every power-on a new emulator process and the tools floppy swapped in by hand.

  every start; a fresh disk cannot carry them, so a small boot CD applies them and hands on to the next boot device.
  Setup must be given the computer type "Advanced Configuration and Power Interface (ACPI) PC" (F5): with the type
  it detects, it restarted every 11 seconds. A warm reset after text mode left the first GUI-mode boot hanging before
  any driver ran (3 of 3); a cold power-on did not (2 of 2), so the 2000 legs power on cold each time.
- Key-less proofs only: the plain and the integrated 2000 CDs reach "Welcome to Setup"; F6 loads the xHCI98 driver
  in text mode and the first GUI-mode boot starts it (with the answer-file template that carries no key).

| L3C-eject | ACPI | files from CD; A: emptied 0.3 s after boot 2's power-on (kept empty from boot 3 on) | 4.7, 4.3, 7.7 | loop (timing) |

- Observed: on the ACPI test machine, with the F6 service as the description sets it (boot-start) and with either
  F6 entry, GUI-mode Setup restarted after 4-8 minutes of each GUI-mode boot; on the pc machine (no ACPI, a different
  HAL, no shim, warm restarts) it ran once (11.5 minutes) and the system then stayed up; the integrated-CD route (L4)
  finished on the ACPI machine; with the service made demand-start in text mode, one GUI-mode boot of 9.3 minutes,
  one restart, and a boot that stayed up 15 minutes. Not observed: the Setup page at which it restarts (no capture
  under the key lock), a completed Setup or a desktop in any of these runs, and whether L3C-eject's boot 4 (7.7
  minutes) repeated the same stage; L3C-eject's boot 4 reset at 1202.2 s, boot 5 began at 1203.8 s and the run was
  stopped at 1205.8 s, so boot 5 was not observed.
- Reading (inference): the repeated restarts happened with the unmodified F6 service configuration on the tested ACPI
  rig, with either F6 entry; they did not depend on the files from CD, and the F6 disk staying in A: after the first
  0.3 s of boot 2 was not needed for them. The comparison with the pc machine changes the machine, the HAL, the shim
  and the restart mode together, so it does not isolate ACPI. One run with the service demand-start from text mode
  did not show the pattern while watched - that points at the boot-start F6 service on this rig; its 9.3-minute
  GUI-mode boot (556.5 s) misses the 10-minute full-pass criterion set for these reruns and is shorter than the
  completed passes seen (11.5-12 minutes), so it is not shown to be a full pass.
  One run each, in the emulator only; not read on real hardware. The published 3.5.0.0 behaves the same as 50.34's
  driver here, so this is not new with 50.34.

### The F6 disk's demand start for the driver - tried and dropped (2026-11-20, 21:52-22:22)

  instead of the boot start text mode gives it; the installed system's end state (the INF's `Start` 3) and text
  mode itself are the same either way. Branch `w50-f6start` (`cdfbeade9`, on `0b3eb827b`), not merged. The legs ran
