## 50.30 (device isolation): 8086:1E31 listed by the owner's decision, read in emulated guests (2026-11-20)

Branch `w50-isol7` at `abad4be5f` (from `be50285c0`): the Intel 7 Series xHCI, `8086:1E31`, listed in
`xhciIsolationTable` by the owner's decision of 2026-11-20, without the reading of its abort on real hardware that
design record 17 section 4.15.10 makes the entry criterion (record 17 revision 38). **Emulation only**: no reading
below is of an Intel controller. The emulated controller is QEMU's `qemu-xhci` programming model given the PCI
identity `8086:1E31` revision 04 (or `8086:1E30` for the control); its abort behaviour is the injection layer's
(record 17 section 4.15.9). What the legs show is the driver's table and its gating at work, on the image the gated
build made.

**The emulator.** The 50.30 legs ran QEMU's own controller, `1B36:000D`, which the qemu flavour's own table lists,
so no earlier rig showed the release table. usb4-emu's `usb4-dock-xhci` (a `qemu-xhci` with a settable identity,
built until now only by the dock presets) was made creatable on its own: usb4-emu branch `w50-isol7`, commit
`4b6c581` (its QEMU tree `f239bc9` = `76e89a5` plus that one change), not merged. Built with the usb4-emu
toolchain (`src\build-qemu.sh`), `qemu-system-x86_64.exe` sha256 `4E001501...6CF`; checked headless first (`E:\xhci98-scratch\w50\isol7\emu-check.txt`): `info
pci` reads "USB controller: PCI device 8086:1e31" with the identity set and "1b36:000d" without. The legs replaced
`-device qemu-xhci,id=xh,...` by `-device usb4-dock-xhci,id=xh,pci-vendor-id=0x8086,pci-device-id=0x1e31,
pci-revision=4,...` and kept every other option of the 50.30 legs' launchers (7 and XP: `launch-q35.ps1`, q35, the
controller behind a PCIe root port; 2000: the two-processor `-machine pc` image of the 50.30 legs). The subsystem
stayed QEMU's (`1AF4:1100`).

**The images.** One gated build of `abad4be5f` (x86 `all`, amd64 `all -amd64`, clean PATH,
`XHCI98_SELFTEST_SKIP_OK=1`; the four records `out\gated-*.txt` say `commit=abad4be5f`, `dirty=0`). `xhci98.sys`:
x86 qemu `8BA39809...884FB100`, x86 release `AD8D3916...D8FC35`, amd64 qemu `16C794C5...57613`, amd64 release
`79881F62...793A2`; `XHCITR.EXE` `AEBA33F4...` (this build). Each guest's running `xhci98.sys` compared identical
with the kit's (7: `CMP.BAT` "SAME"; XP and 2000: T5 "cmp: identical, 573047 bytes"); the snapshot's "driver
file" line reads the version resource, `3.5.0.0`. The leg-only recovery-status client `XHRQ.EXE` `895D9E83...`
(step 1's). On 7 the swap also put the 50.30 legs' `xhciuas.sys` in place (`AD2DEDAD...`; no UAS device in these
legs). Development host A, QEMU TCG, headless, at most two guests at once; starts and stops with their pids in
`E:\xhci98-vm\p50\isol7\pids.txt` (11 START, 11 STOP), evidence under `E:\xhci98-vm\p50\isol7\vms\`.

**Getting the identity onto a prepared image.** The prepared images (the 50.30 legs' `gone-ev` 7 and XP images, the
2000 SMP image) had the driver bound to `1B36:000D`; with the new identity each saw new hardware. 7 installed the
controller from the driver store at once ("Device driver software installed successfully", restart asked), and the
kit's qemu image was then copied over the installed and store copies and the guest cold-started. XP's and 2000's
wizards found no driver (XP problem 28; 2000 problem 1 with the root hub's wizard stuck until a restart); the
staged x86 qemu package of this build (`make-package.ps1 -Flavor qemu`) was installed on the device with T5
`/force` (`UpdateDriverForPlugAndPlayDevices`), which wrote the INF's `XhciDeviceIsolation` 1. On 7 the value
stayed absent (the image's older INF), so 7 reads the default from absence and XP and 2000 from the written 1.

**The legs.** As the 50.30 R legs: a `usb-mouse` plugged by QMP at a root port, code `26` armed at that port,
outcome 1, persistent (`0xSS26PP1F`), the mouse disabled and enabled (7: `DC.EXE`; XP and 2000: T5 `/dis` `/en`),
so its SET_CONFIGURATION and then its Address Devices meet the withheld doorbell; a Bulk-Only stick copied and
compared in a loop throughout (`TRAF.BAT`, 8 MiB, each pass "SAME" or not); the tablet left plugged. L1: the listed
id at the default. C0: the listed id at `XhciDeviceIsolation` 0 (machine-wide, then a disable and enable of the
controller). C1: the unlisted neighbour `8086:1E30` at the default. R: the release flavour on the listed id at the
default (no forcing values in that flavour: the decision only).

The identity-dependent policies, read in the start notes on both ids (7): the switchover off on both (`psw.mode=0`,
`XhciIntelPortSwitch` 0); `quirk.deqavoid` and `quirk.shuttoehci` `00010061` on `1E31` and `00010001` on `1E30`
(the stream-dequeue avoidance and the shutdown routing switched on by the listed id, neither reached by a HID device
and a Bulk-Only stick, and no shutdown compared); `pirq.decision` 4 on `1E31` (a reviewed id, the function not at
00:14.0) and 3 on `1E30` (not reviewed); QEMU's own stream quirk off on both (it keys on `1B36:000D`).

**Slips.** On XP, T5 `/restart VEN_8086&DEV_1E31` was split at the `&` by the command line, so `/restart VEN_8086`
restarted every Intel-id function of the guest (the xHCI first, then the LPC, SATA, SMBus, host bridge and IDE
functions; three disables were refused and every enable succeeded); the guest kept running and C0 was taken after it.
The first launch of the 2000 guest was given a malformed folder argument and never started (no pid; its folder
removed). 7's first boot ended by a QMP quit after the restart dialog held the power-off.

**Not run here.** 98 SE and ME (read in the next section, on the images of `5f1f6d04a`), XP's and 2000's C1 (the unlisted neighbour, read on 7 alone), 7 x64 (the field report's
system; the same code as 7 x86, signing in the guest not reached), the hub and composite rows of the 50.30 legs, and
every item of record 17 section 4.15.10, which only a real controller of this kind can show.

The owner's cut of `3.6.0.0` and the install legs run on its three zips. **The renumbering.** The tree was renumbered
to `3.6.0.0` with the driver date 2026-11-20 in `fed93547d`. The first pre-cut (both gated builds and the check-only
pass) passed at `fed93547d` on 2026-11-20 at 23:35. usb-wdm-free v0.1.12 (release commit
`e3b3ad7732011fcb20de93435c42b9c1dc30e1ce`; network changes only: `rtl815x` 0.2.4.0 and the `cdcnet` INFs 0.1.6.0,
every other file 0.1.11's) was pinned in place of v0.1.11 at `e681d5438`, and the second pre-cut passed there on
2026-11-21 at 00:46. Three documents-only commits followed (`8b6a34fec`, `374e076df`, `b9f62d53c`), which the cut's

named above.

### Windows ME's base download

- **The first runs.** Both failed. The console route: the installer's list did not return in the start after the
  install, Windows still running. The `SETUP.EXE` route: the desktop froze in the start after the install.
- **The second runs.** Both passed; the console one then hung at power-off after the uninstall.
- **Six more fresh runs.** 4 passed; 2 froze in the first start after the install.

**A control series** on the same rig, a fresh starting point for each run, each run the install, the first start and
the check:

| Package on the guest | Runs | Frozen | Pass | Other |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `3.5.0.0`'s published base zip | 8 | 0 | 5 | 2 hung at power-off after the install; 1 hung in a step of the harness |
| `3.6.0.0` | 8 | 0 | 6 | 2 hung at power-off after the install |
| no xHCI98 installed | 4 valid | 2 (below) | 2 | a fifth run hung at power-off |

Of the two frozen runs without xHCI98, one froze at the first start with the same screen (the guest's instruction
pointer the same in two samples 10 s apart, the processor not halted), and one froze at its own cold start.

**Judgment.** The freeze at the first start and the hang at power-off occur on this emulated ME guest without
xHCI98. The one list that did not return was not seen again in 21 runs and is not attributed.

The owner, 2026-11-21, on these facts: "Tick it, with the facts noted".

### The XP STOP 0x7E with the free `uac2` driver

The XP STOP 0x7E with the free set's `uac2` driver is a stated limitation of this release. A series on the v0.1.10
images gave 222 plugs with no STOP on 2026-11-20 and 21, which at the rate seen with v0.1.11 (5 in about 400)
happens about 1 time in 16.

The owner closed 50.final on 2026-11-21, after these legs, and Phase 50 with it. The pushes of usb-wdm-free's `main`
and tag `v0.1.12`, the xHCI98 tag and its push, and the publishing are his, not recorded here.
